assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism
assessments.quote:
Aligned Delegates must safeguard the security of the Sky Protocol through the Executive Vote process. To deal with emergencies related to Executive Votes, ADs are required to sign up for the approved emergency contact mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5).

ADs must strictly adhere to all onboarding procedures and usage instructions associated with this emergency contact mechanism. ADs that fail to do so will be considered in misalignment and will be derecognized.

The high operational security requirements applicable to ADs extend to their use of the emergency contact mechanism.
assessments.description: Requires Aligned Delegates to sign up for the approved emergency contact mechanism and follow its onboarding and usage procedures, or be derecognized.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The enrollment obligation and the derecognition consequence are concrete and checkable, but the operative onboarding and usage procedures are delegated to the referenced document. The 'high operational security requirements' clause is qualitative and has no criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph states derecognition as a consequence, but no enforcer, detection process, or escalation path is defined here. Reaching it depends on the misalignment catch-all (c6c6f595), which alone is weak, and no catalog mechanism such as artifact review or emergency spells is shown to reach this rule.

assessments.title: Protocol Security Workstream Lead Requirements
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead role must be held by an individual with demonstrated expertise in protocol security, smart contract security, and operational security practices. The individual must not have involvement in any business, political, or governance-related activities that could create a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to have security expertise and be free of conflicting business, political, or governance involvement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named role and two concrete requirements are stated, but 'demonstrated expertise' and 'could create a conflict of interest' have no criteria, thresholds, or verification method. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain mechanism, penalty, or review path is tied to the role's qualifications or conflict-of-interest status; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Emergency Response System
assessments.quote: This Article defines a general emergency response protocol for managing emergencies or urgent situations outside of the standard Weekly Governance Cycle and Monthly Governance Cycle.
assessments.description: Defines a general emergency response protocol for urgent situations outside the regular governance cycles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a scope statement that introduces a protocol without stating any trigger, threshold, deadline, or actor obligation. There is nothing operative to comply with at this level.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph imposes no violable obligation; the escalation machinery it introduces (Emergency Response System, 1d940c6d) would be the enforcing mechanism for the protocol's content in its sub-articles, not for this scope statement.

assessments.title: Definition Of Emergency Situations
assessments.quote:
An emergency situation is any situation that would require immediate intervention to prevent initiation of Emergency Shutdown, severe peg divergence, or harm to members and users of the Ecosystem.

Pursuant to [A.0.1.2.1 - Core Council’s Broad Discretionary Capacity](f18229fe-fbc3-4dc8-ad84-4bca2915f6c4), the Core Facilitator has broad discretion to apply the emergency-situation processes defined in [A.1.9.1 - Emergency Response](20dcf582-8862-48b3-9ca9-c3703871bd14) to urgent situations. Urgent situations are defined as any situation that involves a time-sensitive matter that would need an expedited governance process, where following a standard governance cycle would be too slow, risk a larger problem, or constitute an important missed opportunity.
assessments.description: Defines what counts as an emergency or urgent situation that may trigger expedited Emergency Response processes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The definition relies on judgment terms such as 'severe peg divergence', 'harm to members and users', and 'too slow, risk a larger problem', with no thresholds, metrics, or verifiable criteria. The Core Facilitator's 'broad discretion' makes compliance arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This paragraph classifies situations rather than binding an actor to an action, and no mechanism polices misclassification. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) are what this definition gates, but they do not enforce the definition itself, so only the misalignment backstop reaches it.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group
assessments.quote: Emergency response is coordinated by the Emergency Response Group ("ERG"). The Emergency Response Group is a group of Facilitators, Aligned Delegates, and Ecosystem Actors that include domain experts in different areas of the Sky Ecosystem. The Emergency Response Group is tasked with reacting to emergency scenarios that are critical to the survival of the Sky Protocol.
assessments.description: Defines the Emergency Response Group's composition and its mandate to react to emergency scenarios critical to Sky Protocol survival.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actors (Facilitators, Aligned Delegates, Ecosystem Actors) and a real tasking, but gives no membership criteria, size, response deadlines, or measurable trigger for what counts as an emergency. Compliance is arguable on any given facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) is the defined escalation protocol that this group operates within, so it plausibly reaches failures to respond to emergencies. The consequence is unquantified for the ERG itself, and escalation depends on someone invoking the process, so mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Membership Criteria
assessments.quote: The membership of the Emergency Response Group may change at the discretion of Core GovOps, and as circumstances require. Generally, the Emergency Response Group should contain domain-expert Ecosystem Actors as well as governance decision-makers. The group must be able to diagnose a situation, suggest a short-term mitigation and act on such mitigation. The group should also be able to define the path forward for a long-term solution to the problem and act on it.
assessments.description: Sets discretionary, largely unquantified membership and capability expectations for the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Core GovOps) and enumerates capabilities (diagnose, mitigate, act, define long-term path), but membership changes are left to discretion and composition is only 'should contain' with no criteria, counts, or verifiable test. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Core GovOps sets membership at its own discretion, so enforcement is self-policing. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs escalation, not group composition, and no penalty, spell, or artifact review reaches the membership expectations.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Membership
assessments.quote:
The membership of the Emergency Response Group is defined as Active Data in [A.1.9.1.2.2.0.6.1 - Emergency Response Group Current Membership](e9807449-fdc3-4860-8d53-c56181311618).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is Core GovOps.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.description: Defines Emergency Response Group membership as Active Data, updated by Core GovOps via the Direct Edit process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names a responsible party (Core GovOps) and a named update procedure (Direct Edit), but states no membership size, eligibility criteria, cadence, or deadline. The membership content itself is deferred to another Active Data document, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, contract-enforced role, or independent review in the catalog targets membership changes. Core GovOps both updates the membership and is the sole named party, so enforcement is self-enforcement only, and the catch-all misalignment backstop alone is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Team Members
assessments.quote:
Where an Emergency Response Group Member is a team, that team should assign two (2) of its own team members to be responsible for incident response.

A team may assign more than two (2) of its team members to be responsible for incident response at the discretion of Core GovOps.

To the extent possible, the selected team members should be in different timezones and jurisdictions for maximum operational and regulatory resilience.

The team members assigned to the Emergency Response Group should not be disclosed publicly under any circumstances as this could make them targets.
assessments.description: Sets staffing and disclosure expectations for team members assigned to the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The two-member assignment is a concrete number, but it is phrased as "should" and can be expanded at Core GovOps' discretion. Timezone and jurisdiction diversity is qualified by "to the extent possible", and the non-disclosure rule has no measurable test.
metrics: Each Emergency Response Group team assigns two (2) team members for incident response
Additional assignments are permitted at the discretion of Core GovOps
Team members should be in different timezones and jurisdictions to the extent possible
Assigned team members are not disclosed publicly under any circumstances
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a staffing expectation with no penalty, reversion, or review path tied to it. The parent Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs incident escalation, not team composition or disclosure, so it does not clearly reach this rule.

assessments.title: Additional Emergency Response Team Members
assessments.quote: Soter Labs is permitted to assign more than two (2) of its team members to the permissioned Emergency Response Communication Channels defined in [A.1.9.1.3 - Emergency Response Communication Channels](18418289-ada8-401d-a992-7e38b235c866), as well as any Emergency Response calls.
assessments.description: Permits Soter Labs to assign more than two team members to Emergency Response channels and calls.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a numeric baseline of two members and a permission to exceed it, but sets no upper bound, cap, or measurement. The operative magnitude is open-ended, so the rule says what is permitted without saying how much.
metrics: more than two (2) team members assigned to Emergency Response Communication Channels and Emergency Response calls
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a permission rather than a constraint, and no cited mechanism enforces a membership count. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs escalation, not team sizing, so it does not reach any violation mode here.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegate Membership In Emergency Response Group
assessments.quote:
Aligned Delegate membership in the Emergency Response Group is not automatic based on amount of delegated SKY or Ranked Delegate status. An Aligned Delegate seeking to participate in emergency response must be reviewed and approved by Core GovOps prior to joining the Emergency Response Group.

Core GovOps has discretion to approve or deny Aligned Delegate participation in the Emergency Response Group based on their assessment of the Aligned Delegate's competence and reliability.
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to review and approve Aligned Delegates before they join the Emergency Response Group, at its discretion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Core GovOps) and a sequencing requirement (approval before joining), but the approval criteria are judgment-based ('competence and reliability') with no thresholds or verifiable standards. A defender could plausibly argue compliance on any approval decision.
metrics: Core GovOps review and approval required prior to joining the Emergency Response Group
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Core GovOps both grants and polices the approval, so enforcement is self-enforcement. No on-chain role gate or artifact review is stated for ERG membership, and the Emergency Response System only governs escalation, not who joins.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Signal Group
assessments.quote:
A unique Signal "Emergency Response" Group will be used for all incident response coordination.

TechOps Services will create the Signal Group and assign its administrators.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead shall manage access to the Signal Group. All Emergency Response Members must be added to the Group.

Where an Emergency Response Group Member is a team, the two (2) team members responsible for incident response are required to join the Signal Group.

The Signal Group should not be used for any purpose except communications concerning a potential emergency situation. The Group must be configured to have a four-week message retention.
assessments.description: Requires a dedicated Signal emergency group with defined administrators, membership rules, two-member team coverage, and four-week message retention.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states concrete parameters: two team members per team, a four-week retention period, and named administrators (TechOps, Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead). Gaps remain: the "should not be used" restriction is soft, "Emergency Response Member" is defined elsewhere, and there is no verification cadence.
metrics: Two (2) team members responsible for incident response must join the Signal Group for each team member group
Four-week message retention configured on the Signal Group
All Emergency Response Members must be added to the Group
A unique Signal Group used for all incident response coordination
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No on-chain mechanism applies to Signal group membership or retention. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could catch a misconfigured group, and the Emergency Response System provides an escalation path for incident coordination. Neither quantifies a penalty for this specific rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism
assessments.quote: Emergency Response Group Members must use an emergency contact mechanism to deal with emergencies. This emergency contact mechanism is selected and validated by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Group Members to use a contact mechanism chosen and validated by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation and the named actors are clear, but the contact mechanism is never specified and no response time, testing cadence, or availability metric is stated. Compliance is arguable because "use an emergency contact mechanism" can be satisfied by almost any channel.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, contract control, or named remedy attaches to failing to use the selected channel. The parent Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) defines escalation but does not state a consequence for non-use, and the Workstream Lead's validation is self-referential rather than an enforcement path.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism Selection Criteria
assessments.quote:
A suitable emergency contact mechanism should meet the following criteria:

- The mechanism should use enterprise grade infrastructure with correspondingly high levels of uptime.
- The mechanism should not require personal information or KYC from users.
- The mechanism should allow segmenting of target user groups, so that required individuals are only notified when necessary.
- The mechanism should be able to bypass silent / do not disturb mode on devices to achieve an immediate response any time of day.
- It is recommended, but not required, that the mechanism minimizes data tracking of individual users.
- It is recommended, but not required, that the mechanism is open source.
assessments.description: Lists selection criteria for the emergency contact mechanism: enterprise uptime, no KYC, audience segmentation, do-not-disturb bypass, and recommended privacy and openness.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The criteria are enumerated and name concrete attributes, but the operative standards are judgment language such as 'enterprise grade' and 'correspondingly high levels of uptime' with no numeric uptime target or measurement. Privacy and openness are explicitly non-binding recommendations.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a selection guideline with no violation mode that a control or escalation path reaches. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs response to incidents, not the choice of contact tool, and only generic misalignment reporting would apply.

assessments.title: Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms
assessments.quote: The currently approved emergency contact mechanism is PagerDuty.
assessments.description: Designates PagerDuty as the currently approved emergency contact mechanism.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names one concrete, verifiable tool (PagerDuty) as the approved channel. It gives no response time, escalation sequence, contact cadence, or obligation on who must use it, so the operative requirement is thin.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph designates a channel but attaches no consequence to using another channel or failing to contact through PagerDuty. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is a general escalation process and does not specifically enforce this designation, and no catalog mechanism reaches it.

assessments.title: Changes To Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may recommend changing the approved emergency contact mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5), but they must do so in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. The Core Facilitator’s recommendation is subject to a poll through the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator recommend changing the approved emergency contact mechanism, after consulting the Security Lead, subject to a weekly poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Core Facilitator), the consultation step (Protocol Security Workstream Lead), and the poll via the Operational Weekly Cycle are named, but the consultation has no defined criteria or outcome and no quorum or threshold for the poll. Compliance can be judged only on whether the steps occurred, not on their substance.
metrics: Recommendation is subject to a poll through the Operational Weekly Cycle (weekly cadence)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The poll is an approval step rather than a consequence for non-compliance, and no penalty, contract control, or escalation attaches to skipping the consultation. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would reach a violation.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism Fire Drills
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator may run firedrills to test the preparedness of individuals that have been added to the emergency contact mechanism. This will be done at the discretion of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator. The results of firedrills shall be published to maintain transparency.
assessments.description: Lets the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator run discretionary fire drills on emergency contacts and publish results.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors and a publication obligation exist, but the drills are optional ("may") and at the actors' discretion, with no cadence, threshold, or deadline. Not running any drill arguably complies, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The drills and publication are self-policed by the same actors who run them, with no distinct enforcer, penalty, or automatic mechanism reaching this discretionary rule; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is empowered to declare an emergency situation.

After an emergency situation has been declared, Core GovOps is responsible for coordinating emergency-situation processes to ensure they are civil, consistently applied and aligned. The Core Facilitator is responsible for publishing Polls and Executive Votes.

Any participant in the Sky Ecosystem, including Ecosystem Actors, Aligned Delegates or other community members, can request that the Core Facilitator declare an emergency. The Core Facilitator is granted broad discretion in handling such requests.
assessments.description: Assigns Core Facilitator authority to declare emergencies and publish votes, gives Core GovOps coordination duties, and allows requests for declarations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Core Facilitator, Core GovOps) and their roles, but has no thresholds, deadlines, or criteria for declaring an emergency. Terms like "empowered", "civil, consistently applied and aligned", and "broad discretion" are judgment language, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is the defined escalation process this paragraph operates within, and it is the general mechanism that would address a failure to declare or misuse of discretion. Its firing depends on someone raising the escalation, and no quantified consequence attaches to these specific role duties, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Considerations Before Expediting Protocol Changes
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is required to consider several important factors before expediting changes to the protocol:

- Potential for SKY holders to miss a poll or Executive Vote due to departure from the standard governance cycles.
- Expedited votes may not allow for sufficient discussion, leading to a sub-optimal solution.
- Increased governance burden on community and increased workload for domain teams.
- Frequent expedited votes may signal a lack of appreciation for a consistent and predictable governance process.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to weigh four listed factors before expediting protocol changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real obligation and four enumerated considerations, but gives no threshold, criteria, or documentation requirement for how the factors must be weighed. Whether the Facilitator complied is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The duty to consider factors is a deliberative step the Facilitator performs on itself, so the rule is self-enforced. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs the expedited process but does not police whether these considerations were made, and no review or penalty targets this duty.

assessments.title: Incident Validation
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator is responsible for determining whether a reported incident is a valid emergency; where possible, this can be done in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to determine whether a reported incident is a valid emergency, with optional stakeholder consultation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named actor and a real determination duty exist, but there is no criteria for what makes an incident a valid emergency, no deadline, and consultation is hedged with "where possible". Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The Facilitator is self-determining, so the duty is policed only by the actor itself. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is the surrounding context but does not attach a consequence to an invalid validation decision, and only the catch-all misalignment backstop remains.

assessments.title: Incident Categorization
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator is responsible for categorizing emergencies according to their severity and other pertinent criteria.
assessments.description: Assigns the Core Facilitator responsibility for categorizing emergencies by severity and other unspecified criteria.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named actor and a real categorization duty exist, but the only criteria are "severity" and "other pertinent criteria," with no severity levels, thresholds, or category definitions. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) is the escalation protocol that consumes these categories, so miscategorization plausibly affects whether and how it fires. Its consequence for a categorization error is not defined, and firing depends on someone invoking the escalation path.

assessments.title: Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger
assessments.quote: Upon receiving notification from the Core Facilitator of a validated and categorized emergency situation, TechOps Services must trigger a notification in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2 - Emergency Contact Mechanism](3efb0238-aaae-4351-9ec9-31902f3a1394). All Emergency Response Group Members are required to acknowledge the incident in a timely manner through the Emergency Contact Mechanism. The notification must include a link to the official Emergency Response video call ("war room").
assessments.description: Requires TechOps to trigger emergency notifications and members to acknowledge them, with a war-room link included.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and required content are concrete: TechOps must trigger the notification, members must acknowledge, and the notice must include the war-room link. However, acknowledgement is only required 'in a timely manner' with no interval, so the timing is qualitative.
metrics: TechOps triggers notification upon receiving Core Facilitator notice of a validated, categorized emergency
Members acknowledge the incident 'in a timely manner' (no interval specified)
Notification must include a link to the official Emergency Response video call ('war room')
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System defines an escalation protocol outside the standard governance cycle that plausibly reaches a failure to trigger or acknowledge notifications. No penalty is quantified for this rule, and escalation depends on someone raising the failure.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Video Call Coordination
assessments.quote: Emergency Response Group Members are required to promptly join the Video Call to coordinate incident response.
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Group Members to promptly join the emergency Video Call to coordinate incident response.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A defined actor (Emergency Response Group Members) and a real obligation to join the call are stated, but 'promptly' is undefined, with no deadline or time window. Compliance is arguable on the same facts, so the score is capped at 2.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System defines the escalation protocol under which this call runs, so it plausibly reaches a member's failure to join. No consequence is quantified for non-attendance, and firing depends on someone raising the matter.

assessments.title: Known And Uncontentious Remedies
assessments.quote: If a remedy is known and uncontentious, the Core Facilitator shall coordinate with the necessary Ecosystem Actors to expedite an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to coordinate with Ecosystem Actors to expedite an Executive Vote when a remedy is known and uncontentious.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named actor (Core Facilitator) and a defined action (coordinate to expedite an Executive Vote) are stated, but the trigger 'known and uncontentious' is undefined and no threshold, deadline, or measurable criterion is given. Whether the duty was met is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) defines the escalation protocol this paragraph operates within and plausibly reaches a failure to expedite the vote. No quantified consequence attaches to this specific duty, and firing depends on someone escalating a non-compliance.

assessments.title: Emergency Declaration Procedure
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is empowered to declare an emergency situation at their discretion, either on their own initiative or in response to a request from a community member.

When declaring an emergency, the Core Facilitator should create a formal post on the Sky Forum, providing sufficient detail regarding the issue and explaining why immediate action is required. If the situation allows, the Core Facilitator should post the emergency declaration on the Sky Forum before taking action. If the urgency of the situation requires immediate intervention without delay, the Core Facilitator should create the Forum post as soon as possible after, or simultaneously with, the emergency action.

There may be situations in which a public Emergency Declaration would be counterproductive to security objectives; the Core Facilitator is granted discretion in these matters.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator declare emergencies at discretion and sets soft expectations for Sky Forum posting around them.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is a real posting duty with a timing sequence (before action where possible, otherwise as soon as possible after or simultaneously), but it uses 'should' and grants broad discretion, including exemption from public declaration. No numeric deadline, content criteria, or measurable threshold is stated, so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Forum post should precede emergency action where the situation allows
Forum post should be created as soon as possible after, or simultaneously with, urgent emergency action
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph's operative duty (posting on the Sky Forum) is self-policed by the Core Facilitator, and no citable mechanism such as the Emergency Response System or Emergency Spells reaches a failure to post; only the catch-all Reports of Misalignment would apply.

assessments.title: Record Retention
assessments.description: Recommends retaining post-incident emergency response records, with external sharing left to Core Facilitator discretion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names record categories (template, artifacts, chat transcripts) but uses 'should' and 'may include but are not limited to'. It sets no retention period, review cadence, or deadline, and the incident template is deferred to a future iteration.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, penalty, or review mechanism reaches record retention or the discretionary sharing decision; the Emergency Response System defines the response process but not retention obligations.

assessments.title: Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness
assessments.quote: Emergency preparedness is a critical priority. Core GovOps, in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, must regularly evaluate the emergency preparedness of the Emergency Response Group. This can be done through running fire drills or through extensive postmortems after an actual incident.
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps, with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, to regularly evaluate the Emergency Response Group's preparedness via drills or postmortems.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actors and the permitted methods (fire drills or postmortems), but "regularly" has no cadence and no evaluation criteria or metric are defined. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The obligated actor is Core GovOps, which evaluates its own compliance, so enforcement is self-enforcement. None of the catalog mechanisms, including the Emergency Response System, reaches a failure by Core GovOps to run the evaluation.

assessments.title: Accountability Measures for Ecosystem Actor Individuals And Teams
assessments.quote:
For Ecosystem Actors appointed to the Emergency Response Group, fulfilling the responsibilities of this role is as critical to their overall performance evaluation as their customary deliverables.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are required to document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members’ failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements. Given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are granted the discretion to evaluate emergency-preparedness deficiencies. Generally, they are required to take swift action to address non-negligible emergency-preparedness deficiencies in the following manner.

If the deficient Emergency Response Group Member is an Ecosystem Actor individual, the individual should be removed from the Group.

If the deficient Emergency Response Group Member is part of an Ecosystem Actor team, the specific member who has failed to meet requirements should be removed from the Group.

If different Emergency Response Group Members from the same Ecosystem Actor team consistently fail to meet requirements, the Ecosystem Actor team as a whole should be removed from the Group.

The removal of a Member from the Group is done at the discretion of Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. However, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead may not proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation.

When an Ecosystem Actor is removed from the Emergency Response Group for deficient performance, Core GovOps must transparently announce this action via a post to the Sky Forum. Further, the removal must be incorporated into the evaluation of the Ecosystem Actor’s overall performance.

Core GovOps has the discretion to decide if documentation supporting the removal should be retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to document and act on emergency-preparedness failures by removing deficient Emergency Response Group members.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The removal path is structured by actor type, but key triggers are judgment terms: "non-negligible", "consistently fail", "clear documentation", and "swift action". No numeric threshold, cadence, or deadline is stated, and the "should" and discretion language lets a defender argue compliance either way.
metrics: Removal of an individual Ecosystem Actor member for an emergency-preparedness deficiency (no numeric threshold)
Team removal when different members from the same team "consistently" fail requirements (no count or period given)
Forum announcement required upon removal of an Ecosystem Actor (no deadline stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) supplies a defined escalation protocol reaching emergency-preparedness failures, and the paragraph names an enforcer (Core GovOps) distinct from the actors removed, with concrete remedies of removal and a performance-evaluation consequence. However, removal is discretionary ("should", "at the discretion of") and no penalty is quantified, so it does not reach strong.

assessments.title: Accountability Measures For Alignment Conservers
assessments.quote:
For an Alignment Conserver who has been appointed to the Emergency Response Group, the requirements of this role become as critical to the assessment of their overall performance as their customary obligations.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are required to document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members’ failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements. Given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are granted the discretion to evaluate emergency-preparedness deficiencies. Generally, they are required to take swift action to address non-negligible emergency-preparedness deficiencies in the following manner.

Where the deficient Member is an Alignment Conserver, that Member should be derecognized pursuant to [A.1.5.9 - Adjudication Process](560e1024-0897-4f1e-ae71-3ba31e29ed57).

Where the deficient Alignment Conserver is the Core Facilitator, the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps must reach consensus in order to initiate a derecognition proceeding against the Core Facilitator. Once this threshold is met, the procedure defined in [A.1.5.9 - Adjudication Process](560e1024-0897-4f1e-ae71-3ba31e29ed57) should be followed. In the interim, Core GovOps selects an Operational Facilitator to step in temporarily and assist with coordinating emergency response.

The initiation of derecognition is done at the discretion of the Core Facilitator (or Core GovOps) and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. However, the Core Facilitator and Protocol Security Workstream Lead may not proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation.

When an Alignment Conserver is removed from the Emergency Response Group and derecognized for deficient performance, the Core Facilitator must transparently announce this action pursuant to [A.1.5.10.1 - Derecognition Notice](9c05207d-5e11-43ae-a8a3-1b61734d6ef9).

The Core Facilitator has the discretion to decide if documentation supporting the Alignment Conserver’s derecognition and removal should be retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed).
assessments.description: Requires documentation and discretionary derecognition of Emergency Response Group members who fail emergency-preparedness requirements, with special consensus rules for the Core Facilitator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named (Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead, Core Facilitator), but the trigger is qualitative: "non-negligible" deficiencies, "discretion", "should be derecognized", and "swift action" with no numeric thresholds, deadlines, or cadence. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Core Facilitator derecognition proceeding requires consensus between the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps
Removal of a member requires clear documentation supporting the removal
Core GovOps selects an Operational Facilitator on an interim basis while a Core Facilitator derecognition is pending
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Removal from the Emergency Response Group is a concrete remedy with a named enforcer distinct from the member, which goes beyond the catch-all. However, initiation is at the discretion of Core GovOps or the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, so the escalation depends on someone volunteering it. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) supplies the escalation context, and the Adjudication Process (560e1024) is catch-all and cannot carry the rating alone.

assessments.title: Sky Core Governance Security
assessments.quote: This Article governs the correct and secure execution of Sky Governance processes for deploying and reviewing Executive Votes. This Article must protect against all forms of attacks, disruption and accidental failure by maximizing the transparency and resilience of the Sky Executive Process.
assessments.description: Scopes Sky Governance processes for deploying and reviewing Executive Votes, with a goal of resisting attacks, disruption, and failures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a scope and posture statement with no thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or defined actors. Its only operative language is 'must protect against all forms of attacks' and 'maximizing transparency and resilience', which cannot be verified against any criterion.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states a goal without a consequence attached, and no cited mechanism is triggered by a violation of this scope statement. Emergency Spells and other security machinery exist elsewhere in the atlas but are not linked to this text.

assessments.title: Spell Team Anonymity
assessments.quote: The Spell teams need not share their identities. Therefore, it is no longer a requirement that Spell crafting teams publish the deployer of a smart contract. The Spell Checklists have been amended accordingly.
assessments.description: Removes the requirement for Spell crafting teams to publish the deployer of their smart contracts, and states the Spell Checklists were amended to match.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a clear actor (Spell crafting teams) and a concrete change (publishing the deployer is no longer required), so compliance is checkable. It contains no thresholds, deadlines, or formulas, and the operative change depends on Spell Checklists that are not quoted.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph removes a disclosure requirement and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Penalty Mechanisms, artifact review, etc.) reaches a violation of it; only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Audit Recognition Requirements
assessments.quote:
An audit that Sky did not commission through the process specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) is a recognized audit where all of the following are satisfied:

- The audit was performed by an audit firm recognized by Sky, as specified in [A.1.10.1.3.3 - Recognized Audit Firms](4a6e09e6-9e9d-45f0-923a-9c842faa7708).
- The audit report provenance is independently verifiable. For example, the report is hosted on or linked from the auditor's website, or found in the auditor's official code repository. Files uploaded to the audited codebase do not satisfy this requirement.
- The audit report contains a scope statement identifying the contracts, scripts, or artifacts reviewed.
- The audit report contains the exact commit hash at which the audit was concluded. A linked pull request addressing findings, without that commit hash, does not satisfy this requirement.
- The audit report records the severity and resolution status of any findings.
- The audit report documents the trust assumptions of the audited system, or the audited codebase documents them at that commit hash.
assessments.description: Sets six conditions an off-protocol audit must meet to count as a recognized audit: firm, provenance, scope, commit hash, findings, trust assumptions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Most conditions are objectively checkable: a named firm list, a commit hash, a severity and resolution field, and a scope statement. Gaps remain: 'recognized by Sky' is delegated to A.1.10.1.3.3, 'independently verifiable' is illustrated by examples rather than defined, and the required depth of trust-assumption documentation is unspecified.
metrics: Audit performed by an audit firm recognized by Sky (per A.1.10.1.3.3)
Report hosted on or linked from the auditor's website or official code repository; files uploaded to the audited codebase do not qualify
Report contains a scope statement identifying the contracts, scripts, or artifacts reviewed
Report contains the exact commit hash at which the audit concluded; a linked PR without the hash does not qualify
Report records severity and resolution status of any findings
Report documents trust assumptions, or the audited codebase documents them at that commit hash
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check whether a relied-upon audit meets these conditions and assess penalties, and Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) prices poor security practice. Neither quantifies a consequence specific to this rule, and the review must be triggered, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Audit Coverage Requirements
assessments.quote:
These requirements apply to smart contracts whose audits Sky did not commission through the process specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) and that are materially relevant to the security of the assets Sky holds or transacts through them.

Contracts materially relevant to that security include the contracts in which the assets are held, the contracts the assets pass through on deposit, redemption, and withdrawal, the implementation of any of those that is a proxy, and the contracts that can alter the behavior, parameters, or price sources of any of them.

The deployed code of those contracts must satisfy all of the following:

- It is covered by at least two (2) recognized audits, as specified in [A.1.10.1.3.1 - Audit Recognition Requirements](c4258c16-c199-4d5b-86f8-9acb74b7e40c).
- Each of those audits is performed by a different audit firm.
- Each of those audits targets the deployed commit, or every difference between the commit at which each audit was concluded and the deployed code is covered by two (2) recognized audits performed by different audit firms.
- Any finding of medium severity or higher identified in an audit used to satisfy these requirements has been confirmed by the auditor as resolved.

Sky may rely on contracts that do not meet these requirements only with the approval of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.description: Requires non-Sky-commissioned contracts holding or transacting Sky assets to have two recognized audits by different firms, with medium-plus findings resolved.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: at least two recognized audits, each by a different firm, and a commit-difference coverage rule, plus medium-or-higher findings marked resolved. Supporting terms are deferred to other paragraphs ("recognized audits", A.1.10.1.3.1) and "materially relevant" is not objectively bounded.
metrics: At least two (2) recognized audits per deployed contract
Each audit performed by a different audit firm
Each audit targets the deployed commit, or differences are covered by two (2) recognized audits from different firms
Findings of medium severity or higher confirmed by the auditor as resolved
Exception only with approval of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled, independent review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could catch missing audit coverage. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and firing depends on the review being run, and no mechanism directly blocks use of a non-compliant contract.

assessments.title: Recognized Audit Firms
assessments.quote:
The documents herein specify the audit firms recognized by Sky and the tier to which each belongs. The Protocol Security Workstream Lead must review this categorization on a regular basis and update it as necessary.

A firm is recognized under any name it publishes audits under. Audits published under different names by the same firm, or by firms under common ownership or control, count as one (1) audit firm.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to periodically review and update the recognized audit firm list, and counts same-owner audit firms as one.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The review duty names an actor but only says "on a regular basis" with no cadence or criteria for updating the tier list, so compliance is arguable. The counting rule for firms under different names or common ownership is concrete, but it has no threshold and the recognition criteria themselves are only referenced.
metrics: review the audit firm categorization "on a regular basis" (no cadence defined)
audits under different names by the same firm, or firms under common ownership or control, count as one (1) audit firm
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches the Workstream Lead's review duty or the firm-counting rule; Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers agent artifacts rather than this list, and the only remaining path is the misalignment catch-all, which is weak alone.

assessments.title: Audit Firm Tiers
assessments.quote: Audit firms are divided into two (2) tiers: top-tier and mid-tier.
assessments.description: Divides audit firms into two tiers, top-tier and mid-tier, without stating tier criteria.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete count of two tiers but gives no criteria for assigning firms to either tier and no obligation attached to the classification. Compliance cannot be verified from the text beyond the tier count.
metrics: Two (2) tiers: top-tier and mid-tier
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph attaches no consequence to tier membership or to any audit-firm obligation, and no catalogued mechanism reaches it.

assessments.title: List Of Top-Tier Audit Firms
assessments.quote:
The top-tier audit firms are:

- ChainSecurity
- Cantina
assessments.description: Names ChainSecurity and Cantina as the firms designated top-tier audit firms.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete, checkable enumeration of two named firms, so membership can be verified from the text. It states no criteria for what makes a firm top-tier and no review cadence or update process, so the category is undefined beyond the list.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a reference list that imposes no obligation on a named actor, and no citable mechanism reaches it. Artifact review (d4bf73e7) could in principle check audit-firm use, but nothing in the text ties the list to that review, and the misalignment backstop alone is weak.

The mid-tier audit firms are:

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The list names 33 specific firms, so membership is objectively checkable. However, the paragraph states no inclusion criteria, review cadence, or consequence for relying on an unlisted firm, and those operative terms are delegated to the parent section.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph only defines a recognition list and states no obligation whose violation a mechanism would reach; the catch-all backstops alone are weak.

assessments.title: Short-Term Transitionary Measures
assessments.quote:
The standards specified in [A.1.10.1.3 - Standards For Audits Not Commissioned By Sky](38057336-8638-49b6-85f6-cabcc27a74c4) apply as follows:

- Contracts Sky first relies on after October 22, 2026, must meet the standards before Sky relies on them.
- Contracts Sky already relies on as of October 22, 2026, must meet the standards by January 1, 2027. After that date, Sky may only continue to rely on such a contract that does not meet the standards with the approval of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.description: Sets dates by which contracts Sky relies on must meet external audit standards, and requires Workstream Lead approval for continued reliance on non-compliant contracts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Concrete dates (October 22, 2026 and January 1, 2027) and a named approver are stated. The substantive audit standards are incorporated by reference from A.1.10.1.3, so the threshold a contract must meet is defined elsewhere, and the approval criteria are unspecified.
metrics: Contracts relied on after October 22, 2026 must meet the standards before reliance
Contracts relied on as of October 22, 2026 must meet the standards by January 1, 2027
After January 1, 2027, non-compliant reliance requires approval of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Workstream Lead approval gate has no cited penalty, reversion, or review mechanism, and no catalog mechanism is tied to audit-standard compliance for reliance on external contracts.

assessments.title: Executive Sheet
assessments.quote:
The Executive Sheet serves as a planning instrument and documentation for the agreed content of the Spell. It is therefore one of the foundational documents in the Executive Process. Each Spell has a dedicated Executive Sheet. The Governance Point creates a new Executive Sheet for each Executive Vote cycle, listing every executive item intended for inclusion in that cycle along with the provenance of each item. In this way, the Executive Sheet helps ensure transparency and verification in the Executive Process. Past Executive Sheets are preserved in order to provide a record of Executive Votes and their provenance.

The Executive Sheet (also referred to as the "exec sheet" or "sheet") is maintained on a large Google Sheets spreadsheet with several tabs. Each Executive Vote has its own tab, whose title is the designated Target Date for each Spell.

The Executive Sheet provides a publicly visible list of plain-English instructions outlining the executive actions performed in a given Spell. Each executive action is populated in the Executive Sheet under a column and broken down into input actions (high-level actions) and derived actions (resulting from input actions).

The Executive Sheet is used by several actors in the Executive Process. It is managed and populated by the Governance Point, used by stakeholders, who are required to provide confirmation for proposed executive items, and by the Spell Team. The Executive Sheet is the source of truth for the Spell Crafter who crafts the Spell based on its content. Only the Core Facilitator has write access to the Executive Sheet.
assessments.description: Defines the Executive Sheet as a per-Spell planning record, its tab structure, and Core Facilitator-only write access.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Several checkable parameters are stated: one sheet per Spell and per Executive Vote cycle, tabs titled by Target Date, and write access limited to the Core Facilitator. The paragraph is mostly descriptive, though, and sets no cadence, completeness standard, or verification step for the sheet's contents.
metrics: One Executive Sheet per Spell / per Executive Vote cycle
Each Executive Vote has its own tab titled with the Spell's designated Target Date
Write access restricted to the Core Facilitator
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Google Sheet is off-chain, so its write restriction is not contract-enforced, and no penalty, review, or emergency mechanism is tied to sheet creation or unauthorized edits; only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Target Date
assessments.quote: The Target Date refers to the planned date when the Spell is expected to be made available to be voted on. The Target Date is decided by the Governance Point in collaboration with the Spell Crafter. Spells are usually deployed following a two-week cadence. Normally, the Target Date falls on Thursdays.
assessments.description: Defines the Target Date for Spell voting availability, assigned by the Governance Point with the Spell Crafter, usually on a two-week Thursday cadence.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete cadence (two weeks) and weekday (Thursday), but both are hedged with "usually" and "normally", so a party could argue it does not bind them. It is also primarily a definition, and the deciding parties are named without any decision criteria.
metrics: Spells usually deployed on a two-week cadence
Target Date normally falls on Thursdays
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a scheduling norm for Spell Target Dates; the rule is a non-binding definition and its only soft cadence has no enforcement path.

assessments.title: Executive Document
assessments.quote:
The Executive Document (also referred to as the "Executive Copy," "executive," "Executive Proposal," or "exec doc") is a formal, plain-English Markdown document that serves as the primary communication tool for presenting the contents of an Executive Vote to the community. Created after the Executive Sheet is finalized, it provides a detailed breakdown of the actions proposed in the Executive Vote. Unlike the Executive Sheet, which organizes actions in a cell-based format, the Executive Document expresses these actions in sentence format for improved readability.

Each Executive Document corresponds to a specific Spell and describes the actions that the Spell will perform if executed. It is a critical tool for ensuring transparency, clarity, and alignment among stakeholders. The document serves as a proposal that can be voted on and either approved or rejected by Sky Governance. The Core Facilitator is responsible for producing and finalizing the Executive Document; and any changes must be made by them.

The Executive Document is designed to be accessible to both technical and non-technical members of the Sky Ecosystem. It enables Aligned Delegates and SKY holders to understand the actions that will be executed when the Spell is cast. Its contents are publicly visible on the Voting Portal, where Aligned Delegates review it before voting on the Spell. In addition to serving as a reference for voters, the Executive Document also guides the Spell Team in developing and finalizing the Spell, ensuring that the proposed actions are accurately implemented. The contents of the Executive Document are hashed and included within the Spell code to provide an additional layer of verification.
assessments.description: Defines the Executive Document as the Core Facilitator-produced, hashed Markdown explaining a Spell's actions for an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete actor (Core Facilitator) and a concrete step (contents hashed and included in Spell code), but gives no cadence, deadline, or format criteria. The 'accessible' and 'critical tool' language is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The hash inclusion is a verification aid with no on-chain consequence for a mismatch, and no penalty, review, or escalation path is tied to the Core Facilitator's duty to make changes. Only the Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Ecosystem Spell Validation
assessments.quote: Ecosystem Spell Validation (also referred to as "Spell validation" or "validation") refers to the process of performing a set of checks and high-level review of a specific Spell’s code as it exists on the blockchain (referred to as a "deployed Spell"). This process applies only to the deployed Spell and is not as comprehensive as the reviews conducted during the Spell development process by the Spell Reviewers. The purpose of Spell validation is to validate the safety of the current Spell in respect to its security impacts in relation to Sky Protocol smart contracts.
assessments.description: Defines Ecosystem Spell Validation as high-level checks of a deployed Spell's security impacts on Sky Protocol contracts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real process (checks and high-level review of deployed Spells) but gives no check list, criteria, thresholds, cadence, or pass/fail outcome. It is a definition, so a defender could argue it imposes no testable obligation yet.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no consequence for failing validation, and none of the catalog mechanisms is tied to Spell validation here. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could reach it.

assessments.title: Spell Team
assessments.quote: Each Executive Vote has a dedicated Spell Team, made up of Spell Crafters and Spell Reviewers. The Spell Team must include one Crafter, who is responsible for crafting the Spells. The Spell Team must also include at least two Reviewers, responsible for reviewing and confirming that the Spells are ready for the Executive Vote, at least one of whom should be a member of a different Ecosystem Actor than the Spell Crafter. A Crafter cannot serve as a Reviewer for the same Spell. The Spell Team is a set of technical contributors working on developing all technical and smart-contract-related aspects of a particular Executive Vote, based on instructions set out by the Governance Point.
assessments.description: Requires each Executive Vote to have a Spell Team with one Crafter and at least two Reviewers, with cross-actor review.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Crafter count (exactly one), minimum Reviewer count (two), and the rule that a Crafter cannot review the same Spell are concrete and checkable. The cross-Ecosystem-Actor reviewer requirement is phrased as "should", which softens an otherwise quantified rule, and no cadence or verification method is given.
metrics: Exactly one Spell Crafter per Spell Team
At least two Spell Reviewers per Spell Team
At least one Reviewer should belong to a different Ecosystem Actor than the Crafter
A Crafter cannot serve as a Reviewer for the same Spell
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain check verifies Spell Team composition or Crafter/Reviewer identity, and the penalty and artifact-review mechanisms target Primes, Operational Agents, and agent artifacts rather than Spell Team makeup. Only the generic misalignment backstop would reach a violation.

assessments.title: Spell Crafter
assessments.quote: The Spell Crafter (the Crafter) is the person or entity who parses the written instruction set of a proposed Executive to Solidity code in order to develop the Spell in the first instance. Every addition, modification, or removal of code or content within the Spell must be performed by the Crafter. The designated Spell Crafter must be rotated, such that the same person does not craft the Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes. The Spell Crafter is a member of the Spell Team for a particular Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Defines the Spell Crafter role, requires that only the Crafter make Spell code changes, and mandates rotation between consecutive Executive Votes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rotation rule is objectively checkable: the same person may not craft Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes, and the sole-crafter requirement is clear. Gaps remain: the Crafter may be 'person or entity' with no criteria, and 'Spell Team' is undefined in this paragraph.
metrics: The same person does not craft the Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no penalty or escalation for a rotation or sole-crafter breach, and no catalog mechanism (rate limiter, role-based access, penalties, conservatorship, artifact review) clearly reaches Spell authorship in the text. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Spell Reviewer
assessments.quote: The Spell Reviewers (the Reviewers) are the people or entities responsible for reviewing the draft Spell as parsed by the Spell Crafter. The Reviewers are responsible for verifying the Spell, finding issues and catching bugs and mistakes in the Spell, and otherwise ensuring its quality. There is an important delineation between the function of Spell Crafters and Spell Reviewers: the Reviewers may not perform any addition, modification or removal of code or content within the Spell, although they may suggest changes to the Spell Crafter. Spell Reviewers are members of the wider Spell Team for a particular Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Defines Spell Reviewers' role and bars them from editing Spell code or content, though they may suggest changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The prohibition on adding, modifying or removing Spell code is concrete and checkable, but the core duties (verifying the Spell, finding issues, ensuring quality) are judgment language with no review depth, checklist, or sign-off requirement. Membership in the Spell Team is also undefined.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a reviewer editing a Spell, and the separation of duties is self-policed within the Spell Team. Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers Agent artifacts, not the Spell Reviewer role.

assessments.title: Governance Point And Governance Backup
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point is the Core Facilitator. Currently, the only Core Facilitator is JanSky. Each Spell also has a designated Governance Backup. The Governance Backup is required to assume the responsibilities of the Governance Point if the original Governance Point becomes unavailable, effectively stepping into the role as needed. The Governance Point is responsible for coordinating the Executive Vote and ensuring that the information in the Executive Sheet accurately reflects the progress of the Spell.

The Technical Point has domain expertise as the crafter of the smart contracts, but the Governance Point also has crucial context and should serve as a cross-check to the extent they can. The Governance Point is expected to ask questions where needed.
assessments.description: Defines the Governance Point role, its designated backup, and its coordination and cross-check duties for Spell execution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Core Facilitator as Governance Point) and a backup, but its duties are judgment language: coordinate the Executive Vote, ensure the Executive Sheet 'accurately reflects' progress, cross-check 'to the extent they can', and ask questions 'where needed'. No thresholds, cadence, or deadlines are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches the Governance Point's coordination or Executive Sheet duties; Emergency Spells cover security-rule violations rather than this role's duties, and the backup substitution is a structural continuity measure, not an enforcement consequence.

assessments.title: Role Of Governance Point And Backup
assessments.quote: The role of Governance Point and Governance Backup alternates from within the Core Facilitator. The positions rotate, following an internal schedule.
assessments.description: Assigns the Governance Point and Governance Backup roles to Core Facilitator members, rotating them on an internal schedule.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Core Facilitator) and an obligation to rotate the two roles are named, but no rotation cadence, term length, or schedule is given; 'internal schedule' is undefined and delegated, so compliance cannot be verified from the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rotation is not contract-enforced, and no penalty, conservatorship, or artifact review in the catalog is shown to reach a missed or irregular rotation; the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops alone make this weak.

assessments.title: Responsibilities For Governance Point
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point has the following responsibilities in the Executive process:

- Gather the proposed content for the Executive sheet and prepare a draft of the Executive Vote.
- Align on Executive Vote contents with the relevant teams, and coordinate technical details.
- Ensure the contents of each Executive Vote are justified by processes or structures ratified by Sky Governance.
- Produce the text (Executive Document) that accompanies each Executive Vote and verify that the delivered code matches the code reviewed and approved on GitHub and that it contains all expected actions from the sheet.
- Publish the Executive Vote on the official Voting Portal.
assessments.description: Lists the Governance Point's duties in the Executive process, including drafting votes, verifying code against GitHub, and publishing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The duties are real and identifiable, but they are expressed in judgment language such as 'ensure', 'align', and 'coordinate'. The one checkable item, that delivered code matches the GitHub-reviewed code, names no verification method, tooling, or sign-off record.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Governance Point largely self-verifies its own deliverables, which is self-enforcement. Emergency Spells could react to a security violation after the fact, but nothing in the text or the catalog specifically reaches a mismatched Executive Vote or a missed step.

assessments.title: Technical Point
assessments.quote:
The Technical Point role is filled by the Spell Team or the Spell Crafter from that group. For each Executive Vote, a Spell Team is selected from the Spell Roster to steward the Spell development process.

Within the Spell Team, the Spell Crafter serves as the primary point of contact for the Governance Point and any external parties. If the Spell Crafter is unavailable or if disagreements arise, the Governance Point’s secondary point of contact is the Spell Reviewers.

Input or opinions from external parties on technical details should be treated as informational and should not influence the Spell decision-making process.
assessments.description: Defines the Technical Point role as the Spell Team or Spell Crafter, and treats external technical input as informational.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named (Spell Team, Spell Crafter, Spell Reviewers, Governance Point), but selection criteria, availability conditions, and the meaning of 'disagreements arise' are undefined. Obligations like 'treated as informational' rely on judgment language with no verifiable test.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Role assignment and point-of-contact duties are not tied to any on-chain control, capital at risk, penalty, or named enforcer. The Liquidity Layer role definitions only reach controller roles, and the catch-all mechanisms alone yield weak.

assessments.title: Spell Team Configuration
assessments.quote:
The Spell Team consists of the Crafter(s) and Reviewers for a designated Spell.

Currently, Sky has two teams of technical contributors for Spell development, Dewiz, and Sidestream. They rotate the responsibility of crafting and reviewing as follows:

- When Dewiz is crafting:
    - Crafting: one Dewiz member
    - Reviewing: one Dewiz member, one Sidestream member
- When Sidestream is crafting:
    - Crafting: one Sidestream member
    - Reviewing: one Sidestream member, one Dewiz member.

assessments.title: Office Hours
assessments.quote:
Office hours are set to "Yes" if a Spell introduces major changes that can affect external parties, or if a stakeholder makes a specific request for the office-hours modifier to be switched on. Typical examples include collateral offboarding, onboarding new modules, oracle changes, and other actions that may have a significant impact on the protocol or its users.

While stakeholders can request that Office Hours be switched on, the final decision and responsibility for setting this parameter rests with the Spell Crafter. If the office hours modifier is on, the Spell can only be executed between 14:00 and 21:00 UTC, Monday - Friday. The purpose of this modifier is to ensure that Ecosystem Actors are available to address any issues that may arise during or shortly after the execution of the Spell. The Spell will have an extra restriction on top of the GSM Pause Delay, meaning it can only be cast during that timeframe, regardless of when it was approved.
assessments.description: Sets when a Spell may be cast if the office-hours modifier is on: 14:00–21:00 UTC, Monday–Friday, with Spell Crafter setting the flag.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The execution window (14:00–21:00 UTC, Monday–Friday) is concrete and verifiable. The trigger for switching the modifier on relies on qualitative terms such as "major changes" and "significant impact", with no defined criteria, so whether the flag was set correctly is arguable.
metrics: Spell execution window: 14:00–21:00 UTC
Execution days: Monday–Friday
Extra restriction applied on top of the GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog mechanism reaches the office-hours timing constraint or the Spell Crafter's flag-setting decision. The paragraph's text cites no UUID. Any on-chain timing check is not a catalogued mechanism, so none found.

assessments.description: Defines the global debt ceiling flag, set to Yes when a collateral line change requires modifying the global Line.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives a binary flag and a trigger, but the key test, whether a collateral line change 'necessitates' a global Line change, has no formula or criteria. No global Line value or calculation is stated, so compliance depends on judgment.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph governs an executive-vote flag, and no catalogued mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Role Definitions, Penalty Mechanisms) reaches a mis-set Yes/No flag. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Order Of Operations
assessments.quote: The Order of Operations parameter is relevant when actions within a Spell, or across multiple Spells, must be executed in a specific order to ensure that the correct final value is set. This applies to cases where dependencies, conflicting changes, or timing-sensitive modifications require precise sequencing to achieve the intended outcome. The Order of Operations parameter is set to "Yes" when actions must be executed in a specific order.
assessments.description: Defines the Order of Operations executive-vote parameter, set to Yes when Spell actions must execute in a specific sequence.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a binary parameter with a Yes setting, but the trigger is judgment-based ("dependencies, conflicting changes, or timing-sensitive modifications") with no criteria for when sequencing is required. A defender could plausibly argue the parameter is or is not triggered on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain mechanism enforces the order of Spell actions, and the only candidates are the catch-all Reports Of Misalignment and Adjudication Process, which alone are weak.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a module deployed without the required verification. The penalty size is unquantified here and imposition is discretionary, so it is mid rather than strong.
