assessments.description: Lists possible penalties for a Prime Spell Security Incident, without specifying triggers, magnitudes, or when each applies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names enumerated penalty categories but gives no amounts, thresholds, or criteria for which penalty applies. The discretionary wording ("may include, without limitation") leaves compliance and enforcement largely to judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Risk-Capital Incident Response framework (12b7d480) provides a defined incident path with penalties up to conservatorship, and risk-based insurance pricing (fd1f682c) makes poor spell security practice costly for a Prime. Neither quantifies the penalties listed here, and imposing them depends on a discretionary "may" decision.

assessments.title: Prime Agent And Operational Executor Agent Produce Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.quote: After a Prime Spell Security Incident has occurred, the Prime and its Operational Executor Agent must promptly produce a Prime Spell Security Incident Report using the designated template.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime and its Operational Executor Agent to promptly produce a standard Prime Spell Security Incident Report after an incident.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and the triggering event are defined, but 'promptly' has no deadline or time window and 'the designated template' is not specified in the text. Compliance on the same facts is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Risk-Capital Incident Response framework lets Sky Core impose penalties up to conservatorship after an incident, and the report is part of that response, so failing to file plausibly falls within it. Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry adds a priced incentive for weak security handling. Neither mechanism names this reporting duty, and the consequence is not quantified for it.

assessments.title: Delay In Submitting Or Failure To Thoroughly And Accurately Complete Report
assessments.quote: Unreasonable delay in submitting the Report, or failure to thoroughly and accurately complete it (including omission of relevant facts), as determined by the Core Council, constitutes a separate Prime Spell Security Incident and may result in additional penalties.
assessments.description: Makes unreasonable delay or an incomplete or inaccurate Prime Spell security report a separate security incident that may be penalized.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real but expressed in judgment terms: "unreasonable delay" and "thoroughly and accurately" have no deadline, threshold, or criteria, and the Core Council's determination is the only test. A defender could plausibly argue that a timely, reasonably complete report satisfies the rule, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) are the quantified financial penalty machinery for Primes, and the paragraph's "may result in additional penalties" plausibly routes through them. The consequence is unquantified for this rule, and firing depends on the Core Council volunteering the determination and escalation.

assessments.title: Core Spell Teams Review Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.quote: The relevant Core Spell Team, on behalf of the Core Council, must review this Incident Report for completeness and accuracy.
assessments.description: Requires the relevant Core Spell Team, for the Core Council, to review a Prime Spell Security Incident Report for completeness and accuracy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names an actor (the relevant Core Spell Team) and a document, but gives no deadline, cadence, or criteria for what counts as complete or accurate. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The review duty of a Core Spell Team is not policed by the penalty, conservatorship, rate-limit, or role-based mechanisms in the catalog, which target Primes and Operational Agents. Artifact review (d4bf73e7) covers agents rather than Core Spell Team review of incident reports, so only the catch-all misalignment backstop remains.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Records Prime Spell Security Incident Report In Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.quote: All Prime Spell Security Incidents must be recorded by the Core Facilitator in the Incident Registry at [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 - Prime Spell Security Incidents](7bcaaa37-c914-41a4-b61b-cf3a7eb5438f). Each Registry entry must identify the Prime Agent and its Operational Executor Agent, the incident date(s), a short description of the violation, the penalties imposed, and a link to the corresponding Prime Spell Security Incident Report.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to record every Prime Spell Security Incident in the Incident Registry with specified fields.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actor (Core Facilitator), the registry, and four required entry fields, which makes compliance checkable as to content. It gives no recording deadline or cadence, and the scope of "all" incidents depends on a term defined elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator is both the recorder and the obligated party, so the duty is self-enforced. The Risk-Based Pricing mechanism (fd1f682c) uses the same registry but prices Prime conduct, not omitted or incomplete Core Facilitator entries, so it does not reach this rule's violation modes.

assessments.title: Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Prime Agent Credit Rating System
assessments.quote: The Registry shall serve as a critical input to the Prime Agent Credit Rating system and will determine Primes’ Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate when variable pricing is activated pursuant to [A.3.1.2.5.1 - Relationship To Base Rate](4659cbf0-78c2-469b-8432-883e5c931dd1).
assessments.description: Makes the Prime Spell Security Registry a critical input to Prime credit rating and to Prime borrow rates once variable pricing is activated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the Registry, the credit rating system, and the borrow rate, but states no formula, threshold, or metric for how the Registry score maps to the rate. The magnitude is delegated to A.3.1.2.5.1, and 'critical input' is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The borrow-rate effect applies only once variable pricing is activated, so it is not live today. The live priced incentive, Risk-Based Pricing of Insurance (fd1f682c), is not created by this paragraph, and no mechanism citable here reaches the rule's current operation.

assessments.title: Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance
assessments.quote: Insurance‑related fees charged by a Prime’s Operational Executor shall also be calculated using risk‑based pricing informed by the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry, including the severity, frequency, and recency of incidents.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Operational Executors to price insurance fees by risk, using Prime Spell Security Incident Registry severity, frequency, and recency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actor, the pricing basis, and three incident-based inputs, but gives no formula, weighting, fee magnitude, or update cadence. A Prime could argue it complied by making any risk-informed adjustment, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Incident severity from the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry (no scale or threshold stated)
Incident frequency from the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry (no window or threshold stated)
Incident recency from the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry (no lookback period stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance (fd1f682c) creates a priced incentive in which poor security practice raises insurance fees, and this paragraph directly governs that pricing. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could catch a failure to price by risk, but the consequence is unquantified for this rule and firing depends on review.

assessments.title: Review Of Prime Spell Security Registry By Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are expected to review the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry on an ongoing basis and to independently incorporate mitigations and controls based on relevant prior incidents into their Spell-development related processes.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to review the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry ongoing and incorporate relevant mitigations into spell development.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real but expressed in judgment language: "expected" and "ongoing" give no review cadence, and "relevant prior incidents" and the required incorporation standard are undefined. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, distinct-enforcer review with penalty assessment that could check whether spell-development processes reflect registry mitigations. Risk-Based Pricing of Insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) prices poor security practice, but the consequence is not quantified for this specific review duty.

assessments.title: Escalated Penalties For Similar Prime Spell Security Incidents
assessments.quote: Where a new Prime Spell Security Incident reflects the same or a substantially similar circumstance as a previous Incident in the Registry, the new Incident shall be subject to an escalation multiplier applied to its financial penalty, as determined by the Core Council. This applies regardless of whether the earlier Incident involved the same Prime.
assessments.description: Applies a Core Council-determined escalation multiplier to financial penalties for Prime Spell Security Incidents that repeat a prior Registry incident.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a penalty multiplier and the Registry, but gives no multiplier value, no definition of 'substantially similar', and no timing. The magnitude is delegated to the Core Council, so a Prime could reasonably argue no binding amount exists yet.
metrics: escalation multiplier applied to the financial penalty (value determined by Core Council, not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The escalated penalty is a financial penalty within the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which the Core Council administers, and repeat incidents raise Prime insurance fees via Risk-Based Pricing (fd1f682c). Neither quantifies the multiplier for this rule, and the Core Council must act to set it, so the consequence is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.quote:
Prime Spell Security Incidents are recorded as Active Data in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 - Prime Spell Security Incidents](7bcaaa37-c914-41a4-b61b-cf3a7eb5438f).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is the Core Facilitator.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Spell Security Incidents to be recorded in an Active Data registry, updated by the Core Facilitator via Direct Edit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a responsible actor (Core Facilitator) and a defined registry, but gives no criteria for what constitutes a reportable incident and no deadline or cadence for recording. The update process is delegated to the 'Direct Edit' protocol, defined elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Core Facilitator updates its own record, which is self-enforcement. No cited mechanism reaches the accuracy or timeliness of the recorded incidents. The Prime Spell Security Registry pricing mechanism (fd1f682c) is not referenced in the paragraph and would only plausibly depend on this data.

assessments.title: Interim Deployments
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are allowed to deploy a new Allocation Instance on-chain and allocate capital through it under constrained testing conditions, prior to completing a full risk assessment. Such deployments are termed "Interim Deployments". Interim Deployments are otherwise subject to the customary requirements of the Sky Core Executive Spell and Prime Proxy Spell process.
assessments.description: Permits Prime Agents to deploy new Allocation Instances and allocate capital before a full risk assessment, under undefined constrained testing conditions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph grants a real permission and requires standard Executive and Prime Proxy Spell process, but 'constrained testing conditions' is never quantified or defined. No caps, durations, deposit limits, or exit criteria are stated, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The undefined 'constrained testing conditions' give no operative standard that a mechanism could enforce, and the Rate Limiter, PSM, and penalty machinery do not reach this paragraph. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Forum Post By Prime Agent
assessments.quote: The technical implementation of Interim Deployments must successfully complete all required external audits as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) before the Prime can post its Interim Deployment proposal to the Forum.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to complete all required external audits for Interim Deployments before posting the proposal to the Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The gating condition is concrete: audits must be completed before the Forum post. However, the set of 'all required external audits' is delegated to A.1.10.2.7 and no auditor, scope, or deadline is stated here.
metrics: All required external audits completed before Interim Deployment proposal is posted to the Forum
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review by a separate enforcer that could check whether audits were completed before posting, with penalty assessment. The consequence for this specific gate is not quantified, and the review must surface the violation.

assessments.title: Specification Of Testing Parameters By Core Council Risk Advisor
assessments.quote: Once posted to the Forum, the Core Council Risk Advisor must respond on the Forum thread specifying testing parameters that will govern the Interim Deployment, including maximum exposure and rate limits. The Prime must maintain 100% Instance Capital Ratio Requirement for all Interim Deployments.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council Risk Advisor to set Interim Deployment testing parameters on the Forum and requires Primes to hold 100% Instance Capital Ratio.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 100% Instance Capital Ratio Requirement is a concrete, verifiable magnitude, but the Instance Capital Ratio is defined elsewhere. The Risk Advisor's duty to specify maximum exposure and rate limits states no values, deadline, or cadence.
metrics: Instance Capital Ratio Requirement = 100% for all Interim Deployments
Testing parameters must include maximum exposure and rate limits (values not stated)
Advisor response triggered once posted to the Forum (no deadline stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A breach of the Prime's capital requirement reaches the Penalty Mechanisms and escalates to Conservatorship, with Sky Core taking direct control of the Prime. The Risk Advisor's Forum-response duty has no citable mechanism, so it is weak on its own.

assessments.title: Submission Of Artifact Edit Proposal By Governance Actor
assessments.quote: Subsequently, the appropriate Governance Actor must submit an Artifact Edit Proposal incorporating the approved testing parameters into the Prime’s Artifact.
assessments.description: Requires a Governance Actor to submit an Artifact Edit Proposal incorporating approved testing parameters into the Prime's Artifact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is clear, but the actor is only "the appropriate Governance Actor" and there is no deadline, cadence, or verifiable standard for what the edit must contain. Compliance is arguable, since the defender could dispute which actor is appropriate and when the submission was due.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps' scheduled Agent Artifact Review (A.1.14.2.10) is a named enforcer distinct from the actor and would plausibly catch a missing or mismatched Prime Artifact edit. However, no consequence or escalation is specified for this particular omission, and the review does not fire automatically.

assessments.title: Artifact Update
assessments.quote: Upon successful conclusion of the Artifact Edit Poll, the Prime's Agent Artifact is updated with a new Instance Configuration Document codifying the Deployment’s approved interim testing parameters and other basic data.
assessments.description: After a successful Artifact Edit Poll, the Prime's Agent Artifact is updated with a new Instance Configuration Document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is a real, identifiable process step (poll outcome triggers artifact update), but "successful conclusion" is undefined and "approved interim testing parameters and other basic data" is never specified. No thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable values are stated, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review by a party distinct from the Prime that can assess artifact contents and penalties, so it plausibly catches an artifact that does not match the approved Instance Configuration Document. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the review must surface the mismatch, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Inclusion Of Interim Deployment In Sky Core Executive Cycle
assessments.quote: The approved Artifact Edit Poll and resulting Instance Configuration Document serve as provenance authorizing the inclusion of the Interim Deployment into the Sky Core Executive Cycle.
assessments.description: States that an approved Artifact Edit Poll and its Instance Configuration Document authorize adding an Interim Deployment to the Executive Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: It names specific governance artifacts and a defined outcome, but gives no approval threshold, deadline, or criteria for what counts as valid provenance. A party could argue either that the poll-and-document chain was satisfied or that the authorization condition was never defined.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a procedural authorization link with no consequence for misuse. Executive Cycle inclusion is gated only by the general governance process, and the catch-all mechanisms alone keep it weak.

assessments.title: Creation Of Public Information Dashboard
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent must create a publicly available information dashboard through a platform such as Dune showing, at a minimum, the current exposure to the Interim Deployment. This requirement is waived if the Core Council Risk Advisor has already included the Interim Deployment in the publicly available information dashboard at https://info.skyeco.com.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to publish a dashboard showing current Interim Deployment exposure, waived if the Risk Advisor already publishes it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, the required content (current exposure to the Interim Deployment), and the waiver condition are concrete and checkable. However, 'current' has no defined update cadence or metric, 'at a minimum' leaves the content open, and 'such as Dune' does not fix the platform.
metrics: Dashboard must show, at a minimum, current exposure to the Interim Deployment
Waived if Core Council Risk Advisor has included the Interim Deployment in the dashboard at info.skyeco.com
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or contract mechanism reaches a public-disclosure duty. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could plausibly check for the dashboard, but nothing in the text schedules or requires that check, so only the misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Usage Of Interim Deployment
assessments.quote: Once the Interim Deployment has been deployed and all requirements above have been satisfied, the Prime Agent may begin using it subject to the approved testing parameters.
assessments.description: Permits a Prime Agent to begin using an Interim Deployment once deployment and prerequisite requirements are met, subject to approved testing parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is a usage gate with a named actor, but its operative conditions are delegated to "the requirements above" and "the approved testing parameters," neither of which is quantified here. A defender could plausibly argue either compliance or that the gate does not yet bind, so the score is capped at 2.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a permission gate with no stated contract-enforced access control, and no penalty, conservatorship, or artifact-review path is tied to use outside the approved testing parameters. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Completion Of Full Risk Assessment
assessments.quote: Following the Interim Deployment, the Prime will work with the Core Council Risk Advisor to complete a full risk assessment. Once the means to calculate an official Capital Ratio Requirement for the deployment has been determined, the Prime can request that Core GovOps propose a subsequent Atlas Edit Proposal to lift the testing constraints and reduce the RRC to the Atlas-calculated value.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime to complete a full risk assessment with the Core Council Risk Advisor before requesting lifting of testing constraints and RRC reduction.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to work with the Risk Advisor on a full risk assessment is real but has no deadline, scope, or completion criteria. The trigger, 'once the means to calculate an official Capital Ratio Requirement has been determined', is undefined, and the reduced RRC is only referenced as 'the Atlas-calculated value' without a figure.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or review mechanism is tied to completing the assessment or to the RRC-reduction request. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could reach a violation, and the Prime and Advisor police their own compliance.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Process Breakdown
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define the Prime Spell Process, the end-to-end procedure through which Prime Agents bring proposed actions through governance and into Sky Core Spells for on-chain execution. The Prime Spell Process spans four (4) weeks, from initial proposal through publication of the Sky Core Spell that includes the Prime Spell payload.

Two governance paths are accommodated. The Sky Governance path applies to Prime Agents whose Root Edit Primitive is not yet operational; in this state, Prime Spell content is ratified through the Sky Core Atlas Edit Proposal process as specified in [A.2.2.6.2.3.2 - Atlas Edit Proposal Process For Prime Agents](364e52eb-4529-46a9-9852-edaaab88baeb). The Independent Governance path applies to Prime Agents whose Root Edit Primitive is operational; in this state, Prime Spell content is ratified through the voting process defined in the Prime Agent's [A.2.2.6.2 - Root Edit Primitive](78488c6b-d77f-4344-b954-476e415a2c7d). Any divergences between the governance paths are specified in the relevant sections.

The Prime Spell Process is organized into four (4) phases, one per week, specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the four-week, four-phase Prime Spell Process and the two governance paths used to ratify Prime Spell content.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: States concrete parameters: a four-week total duration and four phases of one week each. Path selection is a binary condition (whether the Root Edit Primitive is operational), but any divergences between the two paths are deferred to unspecified sections.
metrics: Prime Spell Process spans four (4) weeks, from initial proposal through publication of the Sky Core Spell
Four (4) phases, one per week
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain or institutional mechanism reaches the four-week timeline or phase schedule; it is a procedural description with no stated consequence for overrunning it.

assessments.title: Step 1: Propose And Prioritize (Week 0)
assessments.quote: During week 0 of the Prime Spell Process, the Prime Agent's proposed Prime Spell content for the upcoming Executive Vote cycle is submitted, prioritized, and approved, as specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to submit, prioritize, and get approval for proposed Prime Spell content in week 0 of each cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actor (Prime Agent) and a timing anchor (week 0 of the Prime Spell Process). The operative steps (submitted, prioritized, approved) are defined only by reference to subdocuments, with no criteria, thresholds, or deadlines within the paragraph itself.
metrics: Submission, prioritization, and approval occur during week 0 of the Prime Spell Process
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No cited mechanism reaches a missed week-0 submission or a failed prioritization step; only the generic Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Submits Prime Spell Form
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent submits a Prime Spell Form to the Executive Process Liaison by Monday, 16:00 UTC of week 0. The Prime Spell Form initiates the Prime Spell Process for the upcoming Executive Vote cycle and specifies the proposed Prime Spell content. The Prime Agent must include the complexity score calculation for the proposed Prime Spell content in the Prime Spell Form. Items that introduce new code must have a completed audit as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) before submission.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit a Prime Spell Form by a fixed weekly deadline, including complexity score and completed audits for new code.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The submission deadline is exact (Monday 16:00 UTC of week 0) and the audit requirement is binary before submission. The complexity score must be included, but its formula is defined elsewhere and no value or method is given in this paragraph, and the audit standard is delegated to A.1.10.2.7.
metrics: Prime Spell Form submitted to the Executive Process Liaison by Monday, 16:00 UTC of week 0
Complexity score calculation included in the Prime Spell Form
Completed audit (per A.1.10.2.7) for any items introducing new code, before submission
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can review Prime Spell submissions and assess penalties for missed deadlines or unaudited code, with an enforcer distinct from the Prime. Risk-Based Insurance Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry makes skipping security audits raise a Prime's fees, but neither mechanism quantifies a consequence specific to this paragraph's deadline or complexity-score requirements.

assessments.title: Delivery And Pre-Risk Review
assessments.quote: During Wednesday of week 0, the Executive Process Liaison delivers proposed Prime Spell items to the Core Council Tracker and the Core Council Risk Advisor conducts a pre-risk review of the items submitted on Monday. Both must be completed by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0 so that the Strategic Team's scope approval that follows is informed by the Core Council Risk Advisor's findings.
assessments.description: Sets a Wednesday 16:00 UTC week-0 deadline for the Liaison's Prime Spell delivery and the Risk Advisor's pre-risk review of Monday submissions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is quantified by a concrete deadline (Wednesday 16:00 UTC of week 0) and names defined actors and steps. Gaps remain: "completed" and the depth or content of the "pre-risk review" are not defined.
metrics: Delivery of proposed Prime Spell items to the Core Council Tracker during Wednesday of week 0
Pre-risk review of items submitted on Monday (week 0) by the Core Council Risk Advisor
Both completed by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism reaches a missed delivery or review deadline. Only the misalignment-reporting and adjudication catch-alls apply, which are weak on their own.

assessments.title: Executive Process Liaison Delivers Items To Core Council Tracker
assessments.quote: The Executive Process Liaison reviews the submitted Prime Spell Form for completeness and clarity, and discusses possible Prime Spell content and potential blockers with the Prime Agent. The Executive Process Liaison must verify the Prime Agent's complexity score calculation. The Executive Process Liaison must deliver the items, including the verified complexity score, to the Core Council Tracker by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0.
assessments.description: Requires the Executive Process Liaison to review Prime Spell Forms, verify the complexity score, and deliver items to the Core Council Tracker by a Wednesday 16:00 UTC deadline.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, the deliverable, and a concrete deadline (Wednesday 16:00 UTC of week 0) are stated, which gives a checkable obligation. The completeness and clarity review and the complexity score verification have no stated criteria or method, so compliance on those steps is open to interpretation.
metrics: Deliver items to Core Council Tracker by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0
Verify Prime Agent's complexity score calculation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers Prime Agent artifacts rather than the Liaison's own delivery timing or verification, and no penalty or escalation is stated for a missed deadline. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Core Council Risk Advisor Conducts Pre-Risk Review
assessments.quote: The [A.1.8.1.1 - Core Council Risk Advisor](d80c8f64-b3f6-430d-bf62-8e50a3783e73) conducts a pre-risk review of the proposed Prime Spell content. The pre-risk review identifies any preliminary risk concerns that should inform the Strategic Team's approval of Spell scope. The pre-risk review must be completed by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0, before the Strategic Team approval specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.1.3 - Strategic Team Approves Spell Scope](05e33459-9ee6-430c-af72-13db2004c505).
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council Risk Advisor to complete a pre-risk review of Prime Spell content by Wednesday 16:00 UTC of week 0.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor is named and the deadline (Wednesday 16:00 UTC, week 0, before Strategic Team approval) is concrete and checkable. The review's content and what counts as a completed review are unspecified, only that it identifies 'preliminary risk concerns'.
metrics: Pre-risk review completed by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0
Completed before Strategic Team approval (A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.1.3)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism is tied to a missed pre-risk review. The Strategic Team sequencing is a process gate, not an enforcement mechanism, and only the generic misalignment and adjudication catch-alls would apply.

assessments.title: Strategic Team Approves Spell Scope
assessments.quote: The Strategic Team reviews the items and approves the scope of Prime Agent content to be advanced through the Prime Spell Process for the upcoming Executive Vote cycle. The approval reflects the Strategic Team's assessment of business needs and strategic alignment with the Sky Ecosystem's broader objectives. Approval must be completed by end of Friday of week 0.
assessments.description: Requires the Strategic Team to approve Prime Agent spell scope for an Executive Vote cycle by end of Friday of week 0.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Strategic Team) and a concrete deadline (end of Friday of week 0) are stated. The approval criteria, business needs and strategic alignment, are qualitative and have no measurable test.
metrics: Approval completed by end of Friday of week 0
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain, or emergency mechanism is tied to a missed approval deadline or to the scope decision. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Communication Of Approved Scope
assessments.quote: Following the Strategic Team's approval as specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.1.3 - Strategic Team Approves Spell Scope](05e33459-9ee6-430c-af72-13db2004c505), the Executive Process Liaison should communicate the approved scope to the Prime Agent and the Core Council Risk Advisor.
assessments.description: Requires the Executive Process Liaison to communicate approved spell scope to the Prime Agent and Core Council Risk Advisor after Strategic Team approval.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actor, the trigger (Strategic Team approval), and the recipients, but gives no deadline, cadence, or required content for the communication. The word "should" leaves compliance arguable even with the communication made.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain control, penalty, or escalation path reaches a communication duty; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops and self-policing by the Liaison apply.

assessments.title: Step 2: Finalize Scope (Week 1)
assessments.quote: During week 1 of the Prime Spell Process, the scope of approved Prime Spell content is finalized through Forum publication, risk review, and Atlas Edit Proposal submission, as specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Spell scope to be finalized in week 1 via Forum publication, risk review, and Atlas Edit Proposal submission.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete deadline (week 1) and three enumerated steps, but defines no criteria for the risk review and defers all procedural detail to unspecified subdocuments.
metrics: Finalize Prime Spell scope during week 1 of the Prime Spell Process
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, rate limit, or automatic mechanism is tied to missing the week 1 scope deadline; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Pre-Publication Review Of Forum Posts
assessments.quote: Prior to publication of Forum posts as specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.2.2 - Prime Agent Publishes Spell Actions On Sky Forum](2c577553-830f-4b9f-ab5f-dddd0fd62cfa), the Prime Agent must complete an internal review of the draft posts by at least one member of the Prime Agent's team independent of the action's author. The Executive Process Liaison then reviews the draft posts and verifies that the internal review has been completed. For actions involving Allocations, the Executive Process Liaison must validate the destination deposit addresses using offchain systems.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to have draft forum posts independently reviewed internally, then verified by the Executive Process Liaison before publication.

Executive Process Liaison verifies the internal review is completed before publication
for Allocation actions, destination deposit addresses are validated using offchain systems

assessments.title: Prime Agent Publishes Spell Actions On Sky Forum
assessments.quote:
Each proposed Prime Spell action must be included in a Forum post on the Sky Forum. Each Forum post must contain the Technical Scope, as specified in [A.1.10.2.5.2.1 - Technical Scope Template](b9ba6658-87a9-4421-9d20-386df8cea450), the Financial Risk Assessment, and, if relevant, a Technical Risk Assessment.

Each Forum post must be published under the Prime Agent's own category on the Sky Forum. The title of the Forum post must consist of the target Spell date in square brackets, followed by "Proposed Changes to", the Prime Agent's name, and "for Upcoming Spell".

Under the Sky Governance path, the Forum posts must be published by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 1.

Under the Independent Governance path, the Forum posts must be published by end of Friday of week 1.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to publish proposed Spell actions in Sky Forum posts with prescribed content, title format, and publication deadlines.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Concrete deadlines (Wednesday 16:00 UTC of week 1 under Sky Governance; end of Friday of week 1 under Independent Governance), a title template, and enumerated required post components are all stated. Gaps remain: the Financial Risk Assessment's content is undefined, and the criteria for "if relevant" Technical Risk Assessment are not given.
metrics: Sky Governance path: Forum post published by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 1
Independent Governance path: Forum post published by end of Friday of week 1

assessments.title: Risk Assessment Review
assessments.quote:
The items included in the Prime Agent's Forum posts must undergo a financial risk assessment.

Under the Sky Governance path, the financial risk assessment is conducted by the [A.1.8.1.1 - Core Council Risk Advisor](d80c8f64-b3f6-430d-bf62-8e50a3783e73). The assessment must be posted on the Forum thread by Thursday, 16:00 UTC of week 1.

Under the Independent Governance path, the financial risk assessment is conducted by an independent risk assessor designated by the Prime Agent. If the Prime Agent has no designated independent risk assessor, the financial risk assessment is conducted by the Core Council Risk Advisor.
assessments.description: Requires financial risk assessment of Prime Agent Forum items by a designated assessor, posted by a deadline.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Sky Governance path sets a concrete deadline (Thursday 16:00 UTC of week 1) and names the assessor. However, the deadline is stated only under the Sky Governance path, the Independent path has no timing, the content or depth of the assessment is undefined, and "designated" independent assessors have no qualification criteria.
metrics: Financial risk assessment posted on the Forum thread by Thursday, 16:00 UTC of week 1 (Sky Governance path)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, emergency, or contract-enforced mechanism reaches a failure to conduct or post the assessment on time. Only the Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication backstops could apply, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Atlas Edit Proposal Drafting And Submission
assessments.quote:
The Edit Proposal codifying the Prime Spell content for the cycle is drafted and submitted.

Under the Sky Governance path, Core GovOps drafts the Atlas Edit Proposal codifying the Prime Spell content into the Atlas and shares it with the Prime Agent for sign-off by Thursday, 18:00 UTC of week 1. The signed-off Atlas Edit Proposal should then be submitted by Friday, 08:00 UTC of week 1, in accordance with [A.1.11.2 - Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle](14e99d92-71fc-44d9-9dbf-933bce2e1b32).

Under the Independent Governance path, the Operational Facilitator prepares and submits the Agent Artifact Edit Proposal codifying the Prime Spell content into the Prime Agent's Artifact, in accordance with the process defined in the Prime Agent's [A.2.2.6.2 - Root Edit Primitive](78488c6b-d77f-4344-b954-476e415a2c7d).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to share the Atlas Edit Proposal with the Prime Agent by Thursday 18:00 UTC and submit it by Friday 08:00 UTC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named and both deadlines are stated to the minute in UTC, which makes the timing objectively checkable. The submission deadline uses "should" rather than "must", and the Prime Spell content and the Edit Weekly Cycle it defers to are defined elsewhere.
metrics: Sign-off to Prime Agent by Thursday, 18:00 UTC of week 1
Submission of signed-off Atlas Edit Proposal by Friday, 08:00 UTC of week 1
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain mechanism reverts a late or missing edit proposal, and no penalty or escalation path is tied to these deadlines. Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers agent artifact contents rather than submission timing, so it does not clearly reach a missed deadline; only the catch-all misalignment backstop remains.

assessments.title: Step 3: Governance (Week 2)
assessments.quote: During week 2 of the Prime Spell Process, the Edit Proposal is voted on, the Prime Spell payload is reviewed and delivered, and approved content is ratified into the Atlas or applicable Agent Artifact, as specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Specifies that during week 2 of the Prime Spell Process, the Edit Proposal is voted on, payload reviewed, and content ratified.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The week-2 deadline and the enumerated steps (vote, payload review and delivery, ratification) are concrete. The operative detail is deferred to 'the subdocuments herein', so no approval thresholds, vote criteria, or review standards are stated in this paragraph.
metrics: Timing: during week 2 of the Prime Spell Process
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph sets a process timeline with no stated consequence for missing week 2. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) reviews artifact content rather than process timing, so it does not clearly reach this rule's violation modes.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Delivers Signed-Off Prime Spell For Review
assessments.quote: By Monday, 08:00 UTC of week 2, the Prime Agent must deliver a signed-off Prime Spell Pull Request ready for external review. The internal review by the Prime Agent's team must be completed before this delivery.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to deliver a signed-off Prime Spell pull request for external review by a Monday 08:00 UTC deadline in week 2, after internal review.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, deliverable, and deadline (Monday 08:00 UTC of week 2) are concrete and checkable. The internal review precondition is stated only as 'completed', with no criteria or sign-off standard defined.

Precondition: internal review by the Prime Agent's team completed before delivery

assessments.title: Morpho Verification Report Requirements For Delivery
assessments.quote: Morpho Verification Report requirements applicable at this stage are specified in [A.1.10.2.5.2.3.3 - Morpho Verification Report Requirements](99d75e24-5ee2-4171-bc75-3cafa0170995).
assessments.description: Points to a separate section that specifies the Morpho Verification Report requirements for executive-vote delivery.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states no threshold, metric, deadline, or actor. It only cross-references another section (99d75e24) for the substantive requirements, so there is nothing to comply with at this level.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a pointer with no operative consequence, and the referenced requirements document is not an enforcement mechanism in the catalog. Only the catch-all backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Governance Vote
assessments.quote:
The governance vote on the Edit Proposal is published on Monday, 16:00 UTC of week 2 and runs through Thursday of week 2.

Under the Sky Governance path, the Core Facilitator publishes the Governance Poll on the Sky voting portal, in accordance with [A.1.11.2 - Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle](14e99d92-71fc-44d9-9dbf-933bce2e1b32). Aligned Delegates vote on the Governance Poll.

Under the Independent Governance path, the Operational Facilitator initiates the vote in accordance with the voting process defined in the Prime Agent's Root Edit Primitive. The Prime Agent's token holders vote in accordance with that process.
assessments.description: Sets the publication time and voting window for the Edit Proposal governance vote under the Sky and Independent paths.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Sky path gives exact timing (Monday 16:00 UTC of week 2, running through Thursday of week 2), but the Independent path defers its voting process to the Prime Agent's Root Edit Primitive with no values stated. The Sky timing is also referenced to the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle without restating its parameters.
metrics: Governance vote published Monday 16:00 UTC of week 2
Governance vote runs through Thursday of week 2
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism in the catalog reaches vote publication or timing violations; the only available routes are the catch-all Reports Of Misalignment and Adjudication Process, which are weak by definition.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Review
assessments.quote: The Prime Spell delivered in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.1 - Prime Agent Delivers Signed-Off Prime Spell For Review](b7e93d92-b433-40dd-bf6b-86a49b7ce9c6) must be externally reviewed during week 2, before the Prime Spell payload delivery specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.6 - Prime Agent Delivers Prime Spell Payload](d5223f2c-264f-47da-9e59-2574bdf9cfc2). The reviewer must be either a member of a Core Spell Team that is not also serving as the Crafter for the Sky Core Spell of the same Executive Vote cycle, or an external reviewer engaged for the purpose.

The 'external reviewer engaged for the purpose' alternative and the review's required depth or pass criteria are left undefined.
metrics: Prime Spell external review occurs during week 2
Review completes before Prime Spell payload delivery (A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.6)

assessments.title: Morpho Verification Report Requirements For Review
assessments.quote: Morpho Verification Report requirements applicable at this stage are specified in [A.1.10.2.5.2.3.3 - Morpho Verification Report Requirements](99d75e24-5ee2-4171-bc75-3cafa0170995).
assessments.description: Cross-references another section that specifies Morpho Verification Report requirements for executive review.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a pure cross-reference with no operative text, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limiter, role gating, or artifact review) is shown to reach a failure to produce a Morpho Verification Report at this stage.

assessments.title: Vote Outcome And Atlas Or Artifact Update

If the governance vote passes, the approved Edit Proposal must be incorporated into the Atlas or applicable Agent Artifact by Thursday, 23:59 UTC of week 2, establishing the provenance for the Prime Spell to be included in the Sky Core Executive Vote.

Under the Sky Governance path, the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps incorporate the approved Atlas Edit Proposal into the Atlas.

Under the Independent Governance path, the Operational Facilitator incorporates the approved Agent Artifact Edit Proposal into the Prime Agent's Artifact.
assessments.description: Requires approved Edit Proposals to be incorporated into the Atlas or Agent Artifact by Thursday 23:59 UTC of week 2.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A concrete deadline (Thursday 23:59 UTC, week 2) and named actors for each governance path are stated. Minor gaps remain: "week 2" is not anchored to a defined start, and "applicable Agent Artifact" is not fully specified.
metrics: Incorporation deadline: Thursday, 23:59 UTC of week 2, after a passed governance vote
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review by an enforcer distinct from the actor that can assess penalties, which plausibly reaches a missed Prime Agent Artifact update under the Independent path. No quantified consequence attaches to the deadline, and under the Sky Governance path the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps police their own incorporation, so that path is effectively weak.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Delivers Prime Spell Payload
assessments.quote: By Friday, 16:00 UTC of week 2, the Prime Agent must deliver the final Prime Spell payload in the govops channel in Slack. The delivery must include the Prime Spell address, codehash, and execution type. The execution type must be specified in accordance with [A.1.10.2.3.2.3 - Execution Of Agent Spells](5b0fd894-094e-4b0c-91ca-c5b59b710c0c).
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to deliver the final Prime Spell payload by a Friday deadline, with address, codehash, and execution type.

metrics: Deadline: Friday, 16:00 UTC of week 2
Delivery channel: govops channel in Slack
Required fields: Prime Spell address, codehash, execution type
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps is a scheduled review by an enforcer distinct from the Prime Agent that can surface a missing or late payload delivery and assess penalties. No consequence is specified for a late or incomplete delivery, and the review must be triggered, so the rating stays mid.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Recorded In Executive Sheet
assessments.quote: By Friday, 16:00 UTC of week 2, the Core Facilitator must record the Prime Spell address, codehash, and execution type in the Executive Sheet for the corresponding Executive Vote. The Executive Process Liaison must confirm the recorded Prime Spell address against the address delivered by the Prime Agent in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.6 - Prime Agent Delivers Prime Spell Payload](d5223f2c-264f-47da-9e59-2574bdf9cfc2). Before giving this confirmation, the Executive Process Liaison must make sure that each Prime Spell action is authorized in the Atlas. If any Prime Spell action lacks this authorization, the Executive Process Liaison must notify the Prime Agent and the Core Facilitator in the govops channel in Slack.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to record Prime Spell details in the Executive Sheet by a set deadline, and the Liaison to verify them.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The deadline (Friday 16:00 UTC of week 2) and the required recorded fields (address, codehash, execution type) are concrete and checkable. The 'authorized in the Atlas' test and the 'execution type' values are not defined in this paragraph.
metrics: Record Prime Spell address, codehash, and execution type in the Executive Sheet by Friday 16:00 UTC of week 2
Liaison confirms recorded address against the address delivered in A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.6
Each Prime Spell action must be authorized in the Atlas before confirmation
Notify Prime Agent and Core Facilitator in the govops Slack channel if any action is unauthorized
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled, separately-run review with published outcomes and penalty assessment, and it could catch a recorded address or codehash that does not match the delivered payload. The consequence is not quantified for this specific deadline or recording step, and firing depends on the review being run.

assessments.title: Step 4: Crafting And Publication (Week 3)
assessments.quote: During week 3 of the Prime Spell Process, a retrospective on the cycle is held and the Prime Spell payload is incorporated into the Sky Core Spell and published, as specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Requires a retrospective and publication of the Prime Spell payload in week 3 of the Prime Spell Process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule fixes a timing anchor (week 3) and names concrete steps (retrospective, incorporation into the Sky Core Spell, publication). It delegates the operative content to subdocuments and gives no criteria for what a retrospective must cover or what publication requires.
metrics: During week 3 of the Prime Spell Process
retrospective on the cycle is held
Prime Spell payload is incorporated into the Sky Core Spell and published
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No listed mechanism reaches a missed week-3 retrospective or publication step; Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers agent artifacts rather than this executive-spell timeline, and the catch-all misalignment and adjudication paths alone are weak.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Retrospective
assessments.quote: A retrospective on the Prime Spell Process for the cycle is held on Monday of week 3, attended by the Executive Process Liaison, the Prime Agent, and the Prime Spell reviewer designated in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.3.3 - Prime Spell Review](d09636ee-de88-4134-9a00-0c3de80ca060). The Prime Spell reviewer scores the review for purposes of evolving the complexity scoring system. The Executive Process Liaison must follow up on any discrepancy between the Prime Agent's complexity score calculation and the reviewer's assessment.
assessments.description: Requires a weekly Prime Spell retrospective on Monday of week 3 and follow-up on complexity-score discrepancies between the Prime Agent and reviewer.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The meeting has a concrete cadence (Monday of week 3) and named attendees, but the discrepancy that triggers follow-up has no threshold or tolerance, and the complexity scoring method is not specified here. The follow-up duty is therefore qualitative.
metrics: Retrospective held on Monday of week 3 of each cycle
Any discrepancy between the Prime Agent's complexity score and the reviewer's assessment must be followed up
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or artifact-review path is tied to a missed retrospective or unresolved score discrepancy. The Executive Process Liaison polices its own follow-up, which is self-enforcement only.

assessments.title: Sky Core Spell Crafting And Publication
assessments.quote: The Sky Core Spell that includes the Prime Spell payload is crafted, reviewed, and published during week 3, as specified in [A.1.10.2.4.7 - Spell Crafter Crafts Spell Week 2 Monday (Step 7)](60aac647-4fa3-4c1c-b9d4-8ababf001958) through [A.1.10.2.4.13 - Spell Execution Process And Retro (Step 13)](761cd866-17a9-47f5-8ae6-ab1788371be1) of the Sky Core Executive Process Breakdown.
assessments.description: Requires the Sky Core Spell containing the Prime Spell payload to be crafted, reviewed, and published during week 3 of the executive cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete timing window (week 3) but gives no day, deadline, or cadence within it. The operative crafting, review, and publication steps are delegated to linked process steps A.1.10.2.4.7 through A.1.10.2.4.13.
metrics: Sky Core Spell with Prime Spell payload published during week 3
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, penalty, or escalation mechanism reaches a missed spell-publication timeline. Only the misalignment-report and adjudication catch-alls cover it, which are weak on their own.

assessments.title: Execution Of Agent Spells
assessments.quote: The execution of Agent Spells is described in the subdocuments herein. Two methods are available: direct execution in a Sky Core Spell and execution through StarGuard. Execution through StarGuard is the preferred method and any exceptions require valid reasoning.
assessments.description: States that Agent Spells can execute directly or via StarGuard, with StarGuard preferred and exceptions requiring valid reasoning.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The two execution methods and the StarGuard preference are named, but "valid reasoning" for exceptions has no criteria, and the operative details are deferred to subdocuments not included here. Compliance with the exception requirement is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches the choice of execution path or the adequacy of exception reasoning. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could plausibly examine spell execution, but the paragraph does not tie the review to this rule, so the link is speculative.

assessments.title: Execution Through StarGuard
assessments.quote: When the execution through the StarGuard method is used, the Agent Spells are whitelisted in Sky Core Spells and later executed using the StarGuard contract. The Sky Core Spell includes a whitelist of approved Agent Spells, which allows them to be executed via separate transactions. This enhances resilience and scalability, ensuring robust handling of payloads from multiple active Agents while minimizing risks to Sky Core.
assessments.description: Describes executing whitelisted Agent Spells through the StarGuard contract after Sky Core Spell whitelisting.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete two-step process (whitelist in Sky Core Spell, then execute via StarGuard), but gives no criteria for whitelisting, no limits on which Agent Spells qualify, and no deadlines. Its closing sentence about resilience and scalability is posture, not an operative obligation, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog mechanism reaches the whitelist-then-StarGuard execution path: the Rate Limiter and Role Definitions do not cover StarGuard, and the Liquidation Penalty and PSM are unrelated. Whitelisting is set by the Sky Core Spell's governance vote, so enforcement rests on the generic misalignment and adjudication backstop only; none found.

assessments.title: StarGuard Deployment
assessments.quote: For each new SubProxy, the StarGuard contract should be deployed and initialized in the same Spell and added to the keeper job, StarGuardJob.
assessments.description: Requires StarGuard contracts for each new SubProxy to be deployed, initialized, and added to StarGuardJob within the same Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The deadline ('in the same Spell') and the required steps (deploy, initialize, add to StarGuardJob) are concrete and checkable. However, 'should' is non-mandatory language, and initialization parameters and the keeper-job registration criteria are not specified.
metrics: StarGuard deployed and initialized in the same Spell as each new SubProxy
StarGuard added to keeper job StarGuardJob
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain control reaches a missed StarGuard deployment in an executive spell; the only available backstops (misalignment reports, adjudication) are catch-alls and so weak.

assessments.title: StarGuard Functionality
assessments.quote: When initiated in a Sky Core Spell, the StarGuard whitelists relevant Agent Spells, enabling their secure execution. This whitelisting allows Agent Spells to run independently, supporting arbitrary complexity and custom features like office hours or expiration times. StarGuard also supports dropping a whitelisted Agent Spell, providing a mechanism to revoke access if needed for security or error correction. This is done via the `drop()` function.
assessments.description: Describes StarGuard whitelisting Agent Spells from Sky Core Spells and revoking them via drop().
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Sky Core Spell, StarGuard) and a concrete function (drop()), so a real process exists. It gives no thresholds, criteria for whitelisting or dropping, deadlines, or verifiable conditions, and relies on 'if needed' judgment language.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The catalog's Liquidity Layer Role Definitions cover the Diamond PAU, not StarGuard, and no catalog mechanism reaches a StarGuard whitelisting or drop decision. Governance executing its own whitelist is self-enforcement, which is weak.

assessments.title: Responsibilities For Agents
assessments.quote: The Agents are required to include logic for the public view method `isExecutable()` in their Spell. This function is used to signal if the Spell is ready to be executed in a particular block or not. StarGuard cannot execute an Agent Spell if `isExecutable()` returns `False`. The value that must be returned for execution to be possible is `True`.
assessments.description: Requires Agent Spells to implement a public isExecutable() method that must return True before StarGuard can execute them.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The function name and the required return value (True) are exact and a third party can check them from the text. Gaps: the required logic inside isExecutable() is unspecified, and the paragraph does not say how the check is verified before execution.
metrics: Spell must include public view method isExecutable()
isExecutable() must return True for StarGuard execution
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. StarGuard's refusal to execute a Spell that returns False is a real execution gate, but no catalogued mechanism or UUID in the paragraph covers it, and only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: StarGuard Whitelisting Authority
assessments.quote: Only the owner, the Pause Proxy, is able to whitelist new Agent Spells via a Sky Core Spell.
assessments.description: Restricts whitelisting of new Agent Spells to the Pause Proxy as owner, executed through a Sky Core Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a single authorized actor (the Pause Proxy as owner) and a defined execution path (a Sky Core Spell), which a third party could check against the whitelist contract's owner. It gives no cadence or further detail on what counts as an Agent Spell or how whitelisting is recorded.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Liquidity Layer role-based access control is an analogous contract-level restriction: a non-owner call should revert, and the rule is an only-the-owner-may-call constraint. The rating is capped at mid because the catalog mechanism is scoped to Diamond PAU roles, and the Sky Core Spell route runs through the executive vote, which is not separately cited.

assessments.title: StarGuard Max Delay
assessments.quote: A configurable `maxDelay` sets the maximum duration between the whitelisting of the Agent Spell in the Sky Core Spell and the execution of the Agent Spell. This feature ensures Spells do not linger indefinitely, enforcing timely processing and reducing risks from delayed or forgotten actions. The recommended value for `maxDelay` is seven (7) days.
assessments.description: Sets a configurable maximum delay between whitelisting an Agent Spell and executing it, recommended at seven days.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The parameter `maxDelay` is named and a concrete value (seven days) is stated, but the value is only 'recommended' and the parameter is configurable, so the binding magnitude is not fixed. It also lacks an enforcing actor, measurement point, or breach consequence.
metrics: maxDelay: maximum duration between whitelisting of the Agent Spell in the Sky Core Spell and its execution
Recommended maxDelay value: seven (7) days
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a spell execution delay breach: the Rate Limiter and Liquidity Layer roles govern different controller actions, and Emergency Spells require a security rule violation that is not defined here. The paragraph states no consequence for exceeding maxDelay.

assessments.title: Requirements For Whitelisting
assessments.quote:
The requirements for whitelisting are:

- The address of the Agent Spell.
- The codehash of the Spell's bytecode.
- Confirmation that direct execution is not needed. If direct execution is needed, a valid reason must be provided.

This information must be provided by the Agent Spell reviewers to the Governance Point.
assessments.description: Lists the information Agent Spell reviewers must provide to the Governance Point to whitelist a spell: address, bytecode codehash, and direct-execution justification.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates three concrete required items (spell address, bytecode codehash, direct-execution confirmation), so presence is checkable. However, "a valid reason" is undefined, and no deadline, format, or review cadence is stated.
metrics: Required items: spell address, codehash of spell bytecode, direct-execution confirmation or valid reason
Information provided by Agent Spell reviewers to the Governance Point
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps is a scheduled, enforcer-distinct review with staged findings and penalty assessment, which could catch missing or inaccurate whitelisting submissions. assessments.title: Permissionless Execution

- Verifies that the Spell meets custom requirements (e.g., office hours) by confirming the `spell.isExecutable()` view function returns true.
- Verifies that StarGuard retains access to the SubProxy, ensuring no loss of control during the Agent Spell execution.

In some cases, the Spell Crafter may request the removal of certain items if the Spell is deemed high risk, too big or contains novel code. Such removals typically affect non-critical items, such as internal payments. Content being removed from the Executive Sheet is added to the Executive Vote queue to be included in the next Executive Vote cycle.

Onboarding of sensitive modules is considered increasing the Spell's complexity in such a manner that the Spell Reviewers should only focus on this; therefore, non-crucial items should be removed from the Executive Sheet and included in the Executive Vote queue.

Where consensus cannot be reached, the procedure specified in [A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3.1 - Core Facilitator Final Inclusion Decision](4cbe3ee7-a64f-4e44-8cf5-25a09a87e233) applies.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Final Inclusion Decision
assessments.quote:
Where consensus cannot be reached on whether to include an item in the Spell, the disagreement must be raised in the govops channel in Slack so that the Spell Teams, Core GovOps, the Core Facilitator, and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead have visibility into the disagreement and the reasoning behind it. The Core Facilitator must hear all positions and make the final decision on whether to include the item. The Core Facilitator's decision is binding for the Executive Vote in question.

Routine coordination among the Spell Teams in their own working channels is expected. A disagreement over whether to include an item must not, however, be resolved in a way that excludes the Core Facilitator or that settles the matter privately and reports only the outcome. The positions of each party, and the reasoning through which the disagreement is resolved, must be visible in the govops channel in Slack.

Where a security or confidentiality concern makes it necessary to discuss such a disagreement in a private channel, the parties to that discussion must afterwards provide a substantive accounting in the govops channel in Slack, setting out the positions of each party and how the settled position was reached.

Where there is credible suspicion that the Core Facilitator is compromised, Core GovOps makes the final inclusion decision for the Executive Vote in question in the Core Facilitator's place, and the adjudication process specified in [A.1.7.6 - Acting Against Misalignment](7aafa61e-8649-41fb-8c3f-64e5714f9f18) applies.

assessments.title: Provenance
assessments.quote:
All actions in the Executive Sheet require sufficient provenance for their inclusion in the sheet and later in the Executive Vote. The legitimacy of a provenance is assessed on the basis of its mutability, visibility and resistance to compromise by external malicious actors. There are different ways of providing sufficient provenance, including "strong comment type" provenance, "onchain" provenance and "strong document type" provenance. These types of provenance are defined in the subdocuments herein.

If Executive actions and items do not have sufficient provenance, for example, "weak comment type", they cannot be included in the Executive Vote. If the Governance Point has any question whether a proposed Executive action has sufficient provenance, they must resolve that question of validity before including that action in the Executive Process.
assessments.description: Requires executive actions to have sufficient provenance before inclusion in the Executive Sheet and Vote, and bars those lacking it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is clear, but sufficiency is judged on qualitative criteria (mutability, visibility, resistance to compromise) with no thresholds, and the provenance types are deferred to subdocuments not included here. The only concrete element is the exclusion of "weak comment type" provenance from the Executive Vote.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No citable mechanism reaches this gate. The Governance Point polices its own sufficiency judgment, which is self-enforcement. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers agent artifacts rather than Executive Sheet provenance, and no penalty or on-chain check is stated for it.

assessments.title: Weak Comment Type Provenance
assessments.quote: The provenance type "weak comment type provenance" refers to informal or editable comments made by stakeholders, which lack the security and visibility needed for Executive actions. For example, Discord messages, forum posts, or unverified social media comments are considered weak comment provenance, even if they relate to an action affecting the commenter (e.g., confirming a payment). Weak comment types are highly mutable, as they can often be edited or deleted without a public trace, and may not be visible to all ecosystem participants (e.g., requiring platform-specific accounts or access to private channels). They also have low resistance to compromise, relying on accounts without strong security protocols, making them vulnerable to malicious edits or takeovers by bad actors. As such, weak comment provenance does not qualify as sufficient and must not be used to authorize Executive actions.
assessments.description: Defines weak comment provenance (informal or editable stakeholder comments) and prohibits using it to authorize Executive actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The prohibition is clear and examples are enumerated (Discord, forum posts, unverified social media), but the qualifying criteria ('informal', 'lack sufficient security', 'unverified') are judgment language with no objective test. A defender could argue a verifiable or archived forum post falls outside the definition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain control or named enforcer reaches the use of weak comment provenance to authorize an Executive action. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) targets agent artifacts rather than the authorization basis of Executive actions, and only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies otherwise.

assessments.title: OnChain Provenance
assessments.quote: The provenance type "onchain provenance" is one of the most legitimate types of provenance. Onchain information refers to information obtained from Sky Protocol-associated smart contracts and is considered practically immutable and publicly visible. Due to the design of these decentralized storage providers such as IPFS, information referred to by on-chain values or content hashes but stored on IPFS or other similar services is also considered practically immutable. The compromise resistance of on-chain values is very strong and relies on a compromised controller of a Sky Protocol-associated smart contract or severe supply chain attack to manipulate information.
assessments.description: Defines onchain provenance as highly legitimate and characterizes the immutability and compromise resistance of onchain and IPFS-referenced information.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a definitional posture statement with no operative obligation, threshold, actor, or deadline. It describes how onchain provenance is regarded but tells no regulated party what to do or maintain.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph imposes no obligation that a mechanism could enforce; it only characterizes a provenance type, and no citable mechanism reaches it.
