The increase and decrease guidance uses judgment language ('should be considered', 'especially high', 'extreme market volatility'), so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The pre-change delay is a self-referential timelock, but no catalog mechanism covers GSM Pause Delay changes. Emergency Spells cover pauses, not parameter changes, and no UUID in the paragraph text applies.

assessments.title: Executive Drop Exception
assessments.quote:
The MCD_PAUSE contract manages the general governance timelock of the GSM Pause Delay; however, it also contains an in-built exception to its own rule.

The executive drop functionality allows a successful governance proposal to cancel a previous governance proposal that has not yet passed the GSM Pause Delay period and been executed. As in any other situation, the new Executive proposal must be the hat proposal, meaning more SKY is voting for it than is voting for any other Executive proposal.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to prevent a malicious attack on the protocol if they are able to exceed the attacker’s SKY weight before the GSM Pause Delay expires.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that a malicious attacker may be able to delay or permanently block a legitimate governance proposal.
assessments.description: Lets a successful executive proposal cancel an earlier unexecuted proposal still inside the GSM Pause Delay, if it is the hat proposal.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The hat test is objective (more SKY votes than any other executive proposal), but the paragraph gives no GSM Pause Delay value, no definition of 'successful', and no timing or cadence. It mainly describes the exception rather than stating a verifiable obligation.
metrics: New executive proposal must be the hat proposal (more SKY voting for it than any other Executive proposal)
Cancellation only for proposals that have not yet passed the GSM Pause Delay period and been executed
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The hat-vote condition is contract-checked in the governance machinery, but no catalog mechanism or document UUID reaches the stated risk of a legitimate proposal being blocked. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Oracle Freeze Exception
assessments.quote:
The OSM_MOM contract manages the freezing of Sky’s oracles. The freeze functionality allows a successful governance proposal to immediately freeze the oracle price for any or all of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. Once frozen, the oracle price will remain at its current value.

The oracle cannot be unfrozen without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay as part of a regular governance proposal.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that the oracles may be frozen by an attacker in order to either:

- Prevent an expensive liquidation.
- Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS.
assessments.description: Governs the OSM_MOM oracle freeze, allowing governance to freeze vault oracle prices and requiring the GSM Pause Delay to unfreeze them.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the OSM_MOM contract, the freeze scope (any or all vault types), and an unfreeze condition tied to a regular governance proposal. The operative delay is only the named 'GSM Pause Delay', which has no value in this paragraph, so the magnitude is delegated.
metrics: Unfreezing requires waiting for the GSM Pause Delay as part of a regular governance proposal
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The GSM Pause Delay timelock is not in the catalog and has no UUID in this text, so it cannot be cited. No catalog mechanism directly reaches an attacker-initiated oracle freeze or the unfreeze delay, and the rule's only enforcer is governance itself.

assessments.title: Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The LINE_MOM contract manages the breaker for the Debt Ceilings of a configurable subset of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. This Debt Ceiling Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to reduce the debt ceilings of a pre-configured whitelist of vault types to zero without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay to expire.

The Debt Ceiling Breaker affects both the Debt Ceiling and the Maximum Debt Ceiling of a given vault type when activated, disabling the Dynamic Debt Ceiling functionality for that vault type if enabled. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected vault types must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.

The whitelist may be configured via a successful governance proposal, but must wait for the GSM Pause Delay before changes come into effect. The whitelist is defined in [A.1.10.3.2.3.1 - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception Whitelist](4937205a-5be0-4def-9b7f-00f9f3bff421) and can be changed via the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.description: Lets LINE_MOM reduce whitelisted vault debt ceilings to zero via governance proposal, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The action is concrete (debt ceiling and maximum debt ceiling set to zero, Dynamic Debt Ceiling disabled), but the whitelist is delegated to another paragraph and the GSM Pause Delay has no stated value here. Who may change the whitelist and how often is only partly specified.
metrics: Debt Ceiling and Maximum Debt Ceiling of a whitelisted vault type reduced to zero
Whitelist changes take effect only after the GSM Pause Delay expires
Reversal requires an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph is an exception that permits a fast-path action rather than a constraint on an actor. The GSM Pause Delay timelock is not in the mechanism catalog, and no citable mechanism reaches misuse of the breaker or an improper whitelist change.

assessments.title: Liquidations Circuit Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The CLIPPER_MOM contract manages the circuit breaker for vault types using Liquidations 2.0. The circuit breaker functionality allows a successful governance proposal to impose Sky Governance’s choice of limitations on liquidations for any or all of the vault types in the Sky Protocol.

- Level 0 - Liquidations Enabled - The breaker is not tripped, new vaults can be liquidated and old liquidations can proceed.
- Level 1 - New Liquidations Disabled - No new liquidations can take place.
- Level 2 - New Liquidations and Resets Disabled - No new liquidations can take place. No existing auctions can be reset if they expire.
- Level 3 - All Liquidations Disabled - No new liquidations, no resets, no bidding in active auctions.

This functionality is exceptional because liquidations at non-market prices have the potential to be irreversibly damaging to both users and the Sky Protocol. The circuit breaker allows Sky Governance to attempt to limit the damage in the event of an issue affecting liquidations without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay.

Additionally, the contract allows for permissionless activation of the circuit breaker, if the price decrease in a collateral exceeds a preset percentage value between oracle price updates. The permissionless activation triggers the circuit breaker at Level 2 because both new auctions and resets reference the current oracle price.

When Level (0, 1, 2, 3) of liquidations circuit breaker is altered via Executive Vote, Sky Governance has the ability to set locked time, which is a specified duration which needs to pass before the liquidations circuit breaker can be triggered again via permissionless activation.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that liquidations may be halted by an attacker in order to either:

- Prevent an expensive liquidation.
- Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS.
assessments.description: Defines CLIPPER_MOM circuit breaker levels that limit liquidations, permissionless Level 2 activation on a price drop, and governance-set locked time.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The four breaker levels are enumerated with exact effects, but the permissionless price-drop trigger uses an unstated 'preset percentage' and the locked time is set by governance with no value given. The core trigger magnitude and cooldown are delegated, so the rule is not fully quantified.
metrics: Permissionless activation when collateral price decrease exceeds a preset percentage between oracle price updates (value not stated)
Locked time before permissionless re-triggering, set via Executive Vote (value not stated)
Permissionless activation triggers Level 2
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The breaker is a pause-type intervention and the Emergency Spells mechanism covers pre-authorized executive freezes and pauses, which plausibly reaches misuse of the breaker. The CLIPPER_MOM contract's automatic Level 2 trigger and locked time are contract-enforced in principle but no catalogued mechanism is cited for them, so the rating stays mid.

assessments.title: Liquidations Circuit Breaker Exception Price Tolerance
assessments.quote:
Breaker Price Tolerance is a parameter which determines the condition for the permissionless activation of circuit breaker. Adjusting the Breaker Price Tolerance requires an Executive Vote, which is subject to GSM Pause Delay.

The Breaker Price Tolerance is expressed as a number between zero and one, and works with the following equation: `next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance`.

In instances where the price oracle model does not support the price delay function, the permissionless activation of the liquidation circuit breaker ceases to function, since there is no next oracle price.
assessments.description: Defines the Breaker Price Tolerance parameter and the oracle-price condition that permissionlessly activates the liquidation circuit breaker.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger formula (next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance) and the 0-1 bounds are fully specified and checkable. Gaps: no current tolerance value is stated, and the GSM Pause Delay duration and the oracle delay mechanics are defined elsewhere.
metrics: Breaker Price Tolerance is a number between zero and one
Trigger when next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance
Adjusting the tolerance requires an Executive Vote subject to GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The circuit breaker is an on-chain trigger, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph reaches it; the GSM Pause Delay is a governance-timing control not listed in the catalog, and the only applicable path is the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: Direct Deposit Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The DIRECT_MOM contract manages the breaker for Direct Deposit Modules (D3Ms). The breaker functionality allows a successful governance proposal to disable any or all of the active D3Ms. In practice, this will set the bar parameter to zero, which (contrary to intuition) disables the module by setting the allowed Debt Ceiling to zero. At this point, no further USDS can be minted through the Direct Deposit Module. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected Direct Deposit Modules must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that a given line of USDS credit is unexpectedly shut down. This has the potential to disrupt the protocol in question, which may impact Sky indirectly.
assessments.description: Lets a successful governance proposal disable Direct Deposit Modules by setting their bar to zero, with reversal requiring a delayed Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The contract, parameter (bar), resulting debt ceiling (zero), and reversal path via Executive Vote are named, but the GSM Pause Delay has no stated value and the paragraph sets no thresholds or conditions for when the breaker may be used.
metrics: bar parameter set to zero disables the D3M
allowed Debt Ceiling set to zero
reversal subject to GSM Pause Delay (value not stated in paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The breaker is triggered by governance vote and reversal is gated by the GSM Pause Delay, but neither is a penalty, on-chain rate limit, or role-gated enforcement that reaches misuse of the breaker itself; Emergency Spells are not cited in the text and would only loosely apply.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The SPLITTER_MOM contract allows for the disabling of the Smart Burn Engine without the GSM Pause Delay.

This functionality is available so that Sky Governance can react to emergencies regarding the Smart Burn Engine.

Since the Splitter contract also allocates USDS from the Surplus Buffer to USDS Staking Rewards, the activation of SPLITTER_MOM also disables these rewards. To reverse the effect, the `hop` parameter must be reconfigured, either with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay, or directly through the SBE-BEAM within its bounds, as specified in [A.3.5.2.4 - Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module](b57ac61b-f6b1-4025-bd44-569d0f2afe2f).
assessments.description: Permits disabling the Smart Burn Engine via SPLITTER_MOM without the GSM Pause Delay for emergencies, and specifies how to reverse it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the contract, the bypassed delay, and the `hop` parameter, and enumerates two reversal paths. The emergency trigger is undefined and the GSM Pause Delay value is not stated here, so the operative criteria are qualitative.
metrics: Disabling the Smart Burn Engine is allowed without the GSM Pause Delay
Reversal requires reconfiguring the `hop` parameter via Executive Vote (subject to GSM Pause Delay) or via SBE-BEAM within its bounds
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a delay exemption, and no mechanism constrains misuse of SPLITTER_MOM beyond the generic misalignment backstop. Emergency Spells would apply to threatened security rules rather than to misuse of this exception. The SBE-BEAM bounds only the reversal path and do not deter an unjustified disable.

assessments.title: PSM Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The LITE_PSM_MOM contract manages the breaker for swaps through the LitePSM. The PSM Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to halt swaps through the LitePSM.

The PSM Breaker can halt selling, buying, or both, independently. To reverse the effect, the halted parameter or parameters — `tin`, `tout`, or both, depending on which was halted — must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.description: Lets a successful governance proposal halt buying and/or selling through the LitePSM, and requires an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay to reverse it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the controlling contract (LITE_PSM_MOM), the independently haltable parameters (tin, tout), and the reversal path via Executive Vote. The operative delay is delegated to the GSM Pause Delay, whose value is not stated here.
metrics: Reversal requires reconfiguring tin and/or tout via an Executive Vote
Reversal is subject to the GSM Pause Delay (value not stated in paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The breaker is a pre-authorized governance halt of PSM swaps, which falls within the Emergency Spells class of executive interventions that reach security-relevant violations. The consequence is not quantified for this paragraph, and the GSM delay that gates reversal is a timelock with no catalog entry.

assessments.title: Bounded External Access Modules
assessments.quote:
Bounded External Access Modules (BEAMs) are contracts that allow whitelisted operators to manage parameters in the Sky Ecosystem without needing to use the standard Executive Vote process. Thus, parameter changes enacted via these modules are not subject to the GSM Pause Delay.

The actions of BEAMs are limited by risk parameters, which are set by Sky Core Governance. Changing these risk parameters typically requires an Executive Vote, unless the BEAM authorizes a standing actor to change them directly.
assessments.description: Lets whitelisted operators change Sky parameters via BEAM contracts, bypassing the Executive Vote and GSM Pause Delay, within risk-parameter limits.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (whitelisted operators, Sky Core Governance) and a delay exemption, but states no numeric limits, cadence, or verifiable criteria. 'Typically requires' and 'unless the BEAM authorizes a standing actor' leave the scope of permitted changes open.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The stated limit on BEAM actions by risk parameters is plausibly implemented by the Rate Limiter reverting out-of-bound controller calls, and the whitelist by Liquidity Layer role checks reverting non-whitelisted callers. Neither is stated in the paragraph and no quantified penalty applies, so this is implicit and mid at most.

assessments.title: Bounded External Access Module Risk Disclosure
assessments.quote:
BEAMs allow whitelisted operators greater flexibility to respond to market movements when setting parameters in the Sky Ecosystem. This flexibility introduces additional risk since operators are able to bypass the Executive Vote process when changing the parameters relevant to the BEAM that they operate.

This risk can be mitigated by limiting the frequency and size of modifications that can be made by operators in parameters controlled by Sky Core. All BEAMs should also have a related MOM contract that can deactivate the relevant BEAM in the event of an operator acting in a misaligned manner.

Any operator that fails to follow the defined procedures for a BEAM they are operating should be considered misaligned.
assessments.description: Describes BEAM operator risk; requires rate and size limits, a MOM deactivation contract per BEAM, and treats procedure violations as misalignment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete structures, such as a MOM contract per BEAM and a misalignment trigger tied to defined procedures, but gives no frequency, size, or other numeric limits. Key terms like 'should' and 'limiting the frequency and size' are judgment language, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter reverts operator calls above their limits, which reaches the frequency and size mitigation if limits are configured. Emergency Spells can freeze or pause a BEAM, which reaches the MOM deactivation path, but the consequence depends on someone invoking it after a misalignment finding.

assessments.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.quote:
The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) manages the parameters of the stUSDS system. Whitelisted operators can use the stUSDS BEAM to modify certain stUSDS parameters without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The stUSDS BEAM modifies stUSDS parameters within specified ranges. See [A.4.4.1.3.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module](37f8f82e-7239-4cfb-8f95-d2cc40515cd9).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update stUSDS parameters more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting stUSDS parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the stUSDS BEAM parameters and the STUSDS_MOM.
assessments.description: Lets whitelisted operators modify certain stUSDS parameters within specified ranges, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay, with mitigation via the BEAM and STUSDS_MOM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (whitelisted operators), the module, and the bypass of the GSM Pause Delay, but gives no parameter names, range values, or delay duration. The operative limits are delegated to the cross-referenced BEAM doc, and 'certain parameters' and 'specified ranges' are judgment-level language.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The stUSDS BEAM doc (cited verbatim) is the mechanism that bounds parameter changes to specified ranges, which plausibly reaches out-of-range settings. Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) could freeze or pause the module, which is the likely role of STUSDS_MOM, but this paragraph does not quantify any consequence or define the MOM's escalation, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.quote:
The Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module (SBE-BEAM) manages certain parameters of the Smart Burn Engine. See [A.3.5.2 - Smart Burn Engine Parameters](ddb90fee-2851-4bf0-b924-f1d73e30ce7a). Whitelisted operators can use the SBE-BEAM to modify the `kbump`, `burn`, and `hop` parameters without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The SBE-BEAM modifies these parameters, up or down, within specified bounds. See [A.3.5.2.4 - Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module](b57ac61b-f6b1-4025-bd44-569d0f2afe2f).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update Smart Burn Engine parameters more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting Smart Burn Engine parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the SBE-BEAM parameters and the SPLITTER_MOM, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.8 - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception](5247c795-7f9d-4d3f-a040-6bc9b070e2d4).
assessments.description: Lets whitelisted operators change Smart Burn Engine kbump, burn, and hop parameters within bounds, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (whitelisted operators) and the three parameters, but gives no numeric bounds, step sizes, or cadence. It defers the operative limits to referenced documents ("within specified bounds"), so the magnitudes are not stated in the text.
metrics: Modifiable parameters: kbump, burn, hop
Bypasses the GSM Pause Delay (duration not stated here)
Parameter adjustments are bounded 'up or down, within specified bounds' (bounds not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph cites the Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (5247c795), whose SPLITTER_MOM breaker can halt malicious parameter settings, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can freeze the system when security rules are threatened. Neither is quantified for this rule, and firing depends on escalation, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Configurator Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.quote:
A Configurator Bounded External Access Module (cBEAM) is a whitelisted Operator. It can use a chain's Configurator to adjust a Diamond PAU's rate limits or execute enabled controller actions, within the bounds that chain's BeamState sets, without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The Configurator's mechanism is the same on every chain's PAS, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.4 - Configurator](45840a10-6c7c-453a-8218-4ab4d705012d).

This functionality allows Diamond PAU parameters to be adjusted more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by cBEAMs setting rate limits to undesirable values, whether by raising them excessively or lowering them to zero.

This risk is partially mitigated: BeamState's `hop` and `maxChange` parameters bound how far and how often a cBEAM can raise a rate limit; they do not bound decreases, which take effect immediately. The Core Council Multisig can immediately unpair a specific misbehaving cBEAM from its `RateLimits` contract or Controller to stop it from acting, and can separately remove its registration entirely, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.4 - Immediate Function Calls](2c82cfd0-7a9a-464f-844d-ebc43b31c2a6). Sky Governance can halt Configurator operations for all cBEAMs on Ethereum Mainnet at once, through the PASMom contract, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71).
assessments.description: Defines cBEAM whitelisted operators' bounded authority to adjust Diamond PAU rate limits and controller actions, and the Core Council and Sky Governance halt paths.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the concrete parameters `hop` and `maxChange` in BeamState and the immediate-unpair and PASMom halt paths, but gives no values or formulas for the bounds, and says decreases take effect immediately with no limit. The operative magnitudes are delegated to per-chain BeamState.
metrics: BeamState `hop` parameter bounds how far a cBEAM can raise a rate limit
BeamState `maxChange` parameter bounds how often a cBEAM can raise a rate limit
Rate-limit decreases (including to zero) take effect immediately, with no bound
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Core Council Multisig can immediately unpair or deregister a misbehaving cBEAM (Immediate Function Calls, cited in text), and Sky Governance can halt all cBEAM Configurator operations via PASMom; both are named enforcers distinct from the cBEAM. The escalation is discretionary rather than automatic, so it is mid, and the Rate Limiter reaches the rate-limit states this paragraph governs.

assessments.title: Core Council Multisig Exception
assessments.quote:
The Core Council Multisig — deployed separately on each chain on which the PAS runs, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.2.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](5d26be25-bddc-4ede-8fa4-a092c610103e) — can act on a given chain's BeamState without a separate Executive Vote for each change, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754). Its immediate functions take effect directly, with no delay; its delayed functions take effect only after that chain's Timelock's minimum delay has passed.

This functionality allows the Core Council Multisig to respond to cBEAM misbehavior, and to adjust a chain's BeamState parameters, more quickly than waiting for a separate Executive Vote.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by the Core Council Multisig itself.

The Core Council Multisig's immediate functions are bounded: they cannot register a new cBEAM, but can re-pair an existing one to a different `RateLimits` contract or Controller, or disable/halt existing PAS (Parallelized Allocation System) functionality on that chain.

The Core Council Multisig's delayed functions, once a given chain's Timelock is unpaused, are subject to that Timelock's minimum delay. On Ethereum Mainnet, Sky Governance can additionally halt them by triggering `pause()` through the PASMom contract, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71); other chains have no PASMom equivalent, so pausing their Timelock instead requires a direct Sky Core Spell.

A chain's PAS may launch with its Timelock paused, as a transitional measure specified for that chain's own deployment; until unpaused, none of that chain's delayed functions can take effect, and they must instead go through an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. For the Ethereum Mainnet PAS, see [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.5 - Transitional Measures](d5240aa5-72c1-4f92-b22c-7a80a35d733c); for the Arbitrum PAS, see [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.2.5 - Transitional Measures](a819637b-04b7-4e1d-9e91-227a29ed6761); for the Base PAS, see [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.5 - Transitional Measures](9f398df8-0484-4c16-8cb9-8d7b04a8b531).
assessments.description: Governs the Core Council Multisig's immediate and delayed actions on each chain's BeamState, and the Timelock transitional pause.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete functions (cBEAM re-pairing to a RateLimits contract or Controller, disabling PAS functions, pause() via PASMom) and distinguishes immediate from delayed actions. The operative magnitude, the Timelock's minimum delay, is never stated, and the transitional launch state is deferred to per-chain sections.
metrics: Delayed functions take effect only after the chain's Timelock minimum delay has passed (value not stated)
Timelock launches paused until unpaused, then delayed functions take effect
assessments.enforcementReasoning: On Ethereum Mainnet, Sky Governance can halt delayed functions by calling pause() through PASMom, a named enforcer distinct from the multisig (PASMom Exception). Emergency Spells could plausibly pause misuse, but no consequence is quantified and other chains need a full Sky Core Spell, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The SPBEAM_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the SP-BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the SPBEAM_MOM is activated, the SP-BEAM will not be able to change any rates in the system, though Sky Governance retains the ability to modify rates directly through the usual Executive Vote process. To reverse the effect, the SP-BEAM's `bad` parameter must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance bypass the GSM Pause Delay to disable the SP-BEAM module, halting its rate changes, and sets the reversal path.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the contract, the bypassed delay, the `bad` parameter, and the Executive Vote reversal path, so the mechanism is concrete. However, it states no numeric thresholds or timing, and the GSM Pause Delay it depends on is referenced without a value.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SPBEAM_MOM is a pre-authorized emergency kill switch that Sky Governance, a distinct enforcer, can trigger to halt a misbehaving SP-BEAM operator, which maps to Emergency Spells and the Emergency Response System. It is not automatic, so firing depends on Governance volunteering the escalation, which keeps it at mid.

assessments.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The STUSDS_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module or set the `cap` or `line` stUSDS parameters to zero.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the stUSDS BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the STUSDS_MOM is activated to disable the stUSDS BEAM, the stUSDS BEAM will not be able to change any stUSDS parameters in the system, though Sky Governance retains the ability to modify stUSDS parameters directly through the usual Executive Vote process. Reversing a disabled stUSDS BEAM requires reconfiguring the rate setter's `bad` parameter with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay. Reversing a `cap` or `line` set to zero requires reconfiguring both the stUSDS parameter and the rate setter's corresponding `maxCap` or `maxLine` parameter, likewise with an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.description: Permits Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay to disable the stUSDS BEAM or zero its cap/line parameters, and sets reversal conditions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the contract (STUSDS_MOM), the exact parameters (cap, line, bad, maxCap, maxLine), and the permitted actions (disable, set to zero). The GSM Pause Delay is referenced but its duration is defined elsewhere without a value in this text, which is a minor gap.
metrics: STUSDS_MOM may disable the stUSDS BEAM or set `cap` or `line` to zero, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay
Reversal of a disabled BEAM requires an Executive Vote reconfiguring the rate setter's `bad` parameter, subject to the GSM Pause Delay
Reversal of a zeroed `cap` or `line` requires reconfiguring the stUSDS parameter and the rate setter's `maxCap` or `maxLine`, subject to the GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The bypass is a pre-authorized executive intervention analogous to Emergency Spells, which are the defined path for freezing or disabling a component when security is threatened. Nothing in the text quantifies a consequence for misuse of the bypass itself, and firing depends on governance invoking it, so mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: PASMom Exception
assessments.quote:
The PASMom contract (`PAS_MOM`) allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay to halt Configurator operations or pause the Timelock governing changes to the PAS. This is a Sky Governance action taken independently of both the Core Council Multisig and cBEAM; neither can trigger the PASMom contract itself. PASMom is deployed on Ethereum Mainnet only. For PASMom's on-chain relationship to BeamState and the Timelock, see [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.6 - PASMom](88e11076-5fe1-42a5-b2ba-bdb1bc929ec8).

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency. If a cBEAM is compromised or acting maliciously, Sky Governance can trigger `stop()` through the PASMom contract, preventing all cBEAMs on Ethereum Mainnet from executing any action through the Configurator; restarting is done via the Core Council Multisig proposing `start()` through the Timelock once it is unpaused, or otherwise via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.5 - Restart After Halt](e049feea-5af3-4a8d-8766-36e348fd5d7b).

If the Core Council Multisig is compromised or acting maliciously, Sky Governance can trigger `pause()` through the PASMom contract, preventing the Timelock from scheduling or executing the Core Council Multisig's delayed proposals; reversing this requires an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance bypass GSM delay to halt Configurator or pause Timelock, independent of Core Council Multisig and cBEAM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actors (Sky Governance, Core Council Multisig, cBEAM), the functions (stop(), pause()), the chain (Ethereum Mainnet only), and the restart path. However, the GSM Pause Delay it bypasses has no stated value here, and the trigger condition ("compromised or acting maliciously") is judgment-based.
metrics: Bypasses the GSM Pause Delay (value defined elsewhere, not stated)
Deployed on Ethereum Mainnet only
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is itself an emergency pause power, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) and the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) plausibly reach misuse of it by Sky Governance. The escalation is not quantified for this rule, and the restart and reversal path requires an Executive Vote, which is structural but not a penalty for misuse.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Features
assessments.quote: The `lerp` must be activated in an Executive Vote but can thereafter change the value of the designated parameter without additional Executive Votes. Each `lerp` instance is defined in terms of a `start` value, representing the desired starting value, an `end` value, representing the desired ending value, and a `duration` over which the parameter will be adjusted between the starting value and the ending value. Any user can then permissionlessly call `tick` to set the governance parameter to the appropriate value based on the time elapsed.
assessments.description: Describes how a linear interpolation module activates parameter changes via Executive Vote and then updates the parameter over a duration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the operative parameters (start, end, duration) and the permissionless tick function, and describes linear interpolation over time. No numeric bounds, maximum duration, or allowed parameter ranges are stated, so the magnitudes are left undefined.
metrics: start value (desired starting value, unspecified)
end value (desired ending value, unspecified)
duration over which the parameter is adjusted (unspecified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes the module's mechanics rather than a constraint on an actor, and no cited mechanism reaches a violation such as a parameter changed outside an Executive Vote-approved lerp. The tick function's determinism is not an enforcement mechanism for this rule.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Parameters
assessments.quote:
Each `lerp` instance has the following parameters:

- `target` - The target contract in which a parameter is being changed
- `what` - The name of the parameter being changed
- `startTime` - The starting time of this `lerp` instance
- `start` - The starting value of that parameter
- `end` - The ending value of that parameter
- `duration` - How long this `lerp` instance will run for
- `done` - Indicates whether this given `lerp` instance is completed or not
assessments.description: Defines the seven fields that each Linear Interpolation Module (lerp) instance carries when changing a contract parameter.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete fields (target, what, startTime, start, end, duration, done) but states no values, formulas, or limits. It defines a data structure rather than an operative obligation, so compliance is hard to judge from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a field definition, and no catalogued mechanism reaches it. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Authorization
assessments.quote: The Facilitators responsible for the Scope that governs the parameter to be adjusted by the Linear Interpolation Module, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, may recommend deploying the Linear Interpolation Module for parameter adjustments.
assessments.description: Allows Scope Facilitators, consulting the Core Council Risk Advisor, to recommend deploying the Linear Interpolation Module for parameter adjustments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Defined actors (Scope Facilitators, Core Council Risk Advisor) and a consultation step are named, but the permission is discretionary ("may recommend") with no criteria for when a recommendation is appropriate, no thresholds, and no deadlines. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph only grants a discretionary recommendation right and states no rate limit, access-control role, or penalty; the only available backstops are the generic Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication Process catch-alls.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Consideration
assessments.quote: The Facilitators must take into consideration the benefits and costs with using the Linear Interpolation Module. A longer `duration` has the benefit of adjusting the parameter more slowly, giving users more time to adjust. However, the drawback of a longer `duration` is that the parameter will not reach its desired `end` value for a longer period of time. When the cost of a parameter not being at its desired value is high, use of the Linear Interpolation Module is not appropriate, and the parameter should be adjusted to its desired value following the required process.
assessments.description: Requires Facilitators to weigh benefits and costs before using the Linear Interpolation Module, and to avoid it when parameter delay is costly.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names an actor (Facilitators), but it relies on judgment language such as "take into consideration" and "cost ... is high" with no threshold, metric, or cadence. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain control or named enforcer reaches the Facilitators' duty to weigh costs; the only general backstops (Reports of Misalignment, Adjudication) are catch-alls.

assessments.title: Governance Process For Linear Interpolation Module
assessments.quote: The process to utilize the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust a parameter must follow the same governance process required to modify the designated parameter. If the parameter can be updated directly through an Executive Vote, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust it may also be included directly in an Executive Vote. If modifying the parameter requires a prior Governance Poll, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module for that parameter must also be preceded by a Governance Poll.
assessments.description: Requires Linear Interpolation Module adjustments to follow the same governance path, Executive Vote or Governance Poll, as the target parameter.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete governance steps (Executive Vote, Governance Poll) and a conditional mapping from the parameter's process to the module's process. It gives no thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria for what counts as the 'same' process, so compliance is partly interpretive.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a governance-process sequencing rule: artifact review and penalties target agents and Primes, and the rate limiter and role definitions do not cover governance votes. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.1 - Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig](21fa6749-6209-4280-9b5f-b2a73d400421)) can freeze SkyLink bridges deployed in the Sky Ecosystem without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function.
assessments.description: Lets the Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig freeze SkyLink bridges outside Spell process and requires reporting each action on the Sky Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The freeze authority and the Sky Forum reporting channel are named, but the reporting deadline is only "a reasonable time frame" and the reporting content is not specified beyond "each action". Whether a given post was timely is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could check whether the multisig's freeze actions were reported and stage findings with penalty assessment, which plausibly reaches the reporting duty. The review is scheduled rather than triggered by each action, and no penalty is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.2.3.1.1 - Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig](8e618196-257a-49d8-834d-665dba345fcd)) can freeze the Solana SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function.
assessments.description: Allows the Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig to freeze the bridge without a Spell and requires reporting each action on the Sky Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (the Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig) and the freeze action are concrete, but the reporting deadline is only 'a reasonable time frame' with no value or cadence. The reporting duty is therefore delegated and not verifiable from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism reaches the reporting duty or the freeze exception: the paragraph names no penalty, review or on-chain check, and the only available mechanisms are the catch-all misalignment and adjudication processes.

assessments.title: Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.3.3.1.1 - Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig](0b1162f6-6a30-4a30-b693-68e077093e7c)) can freeze the Avalanche SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function.
assessments.description: Lets the Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig freeze the bridge without a Spell and requires reporting its actions on the Sky Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Freezer Multisig), the freeze authority, and the reporting channel (Sky Forum) are concrete. The reporting deadline is only "a reasonable time frame," and no measurable threshold or cadence is given, so the timing is delegated.
metrics: Each multisig action must be reported within a reasonable time frame
Reporting channel: post on the Sky Forum
Reportable actions include activating or disabling the freeze function
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, enforcer-distinct review with penalty assessment that could catch missing or late Forum reports. No consequence is quantified for this reporting duty, and firing depends on the review reaching it.

assessments.title: Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.4.3.1.1 - Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig](f833edaa-9f5f-4445-afcb-a9cfc3620b10)) can freeze the Plasma SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function.
assessments.description: Lets the Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig freeze the bridge without a Spell and requires forum reporting of its actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, the freeze scope (Plasma SkyLink Bridge), and the reporting channel (Sky Forum) are concrete. The reporting deadline is only 'a reasonable time frame', and no cadence or threshold is given, so compliance on timing is arguable.
metrics: Each multisig action reported on the Sky Forum within a reasonable time frame
Actions include activating or disabling the freeze function
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with penalty assessment that could catch missing or late forum reports and multisig configuration mismatches. No quantified consequence is stated for this rule, and the review is not automatic.

assessments.title: Multisig Freeze Of SparkLend
assessments.quote:
In addition to the SparkLend Freezer Mom contract defined in [A.1.10.3.2.7 - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception](645443f1-9004-48d3-868c-139b608bb1f9), an external SparkLend Security Access Multisig has been established that allows for pausing and/or freezing SparkLend markets. The SparkLend Security Access Multisig can enable or disable the SparkLend Freezer Mom contract without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the pause or freeze function.
assessments.description: Establishes an external SparkLend multisig able to pause or freeze markets and requires public forum reporting of its executed actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, scope of powers, required report contents (function calls and parameters) and the Sky Forum venue are concrete. The reporting deadline is only "a reasonable time frame", so the operative timing is delegated.
metrics: Each multisig action, including function calls and parameters, must be reported on the Sky Forum
Reporting must occur "within a reasonable time frame" (no numeric deadline)
Reportable actions include activating or disabling the pause or freeze function
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can review Spark Agent artifacts and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches a missed or late forum report. The consequence is unquantified for this rule and depends on the review being scheduled and triggered.

assessments.title: SparkLend Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote:
The SparkLend Security Access Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or SparkLend users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit).

The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior.

The Multisig can also be used in cases where a vulnerability or exploit is discovered in other protocols using the same codebase as SparkLend, and a timely action can prevent or mitigate the damage.

The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with the requirements defined herein.
assessments.description: Restricts use of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig to urgent or emergency situations threatening the ecosystem, and requires Core Council oversight.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives two conjunctive conditions for emergency use, but both rely on judgment terms such as 'potential to harm' and 'preparation time would leave the ecosystem vulnerable.' Enumerated use cases lack criteria, and no thresholds, cadence, or measurable tests are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review by a separate enforcer with staged findings and penalty assessment, and plausibly reaches multisig misuse. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the Core Council duty to ensure alignment has no defined escalation path.

assessments.title: Facilitators Must Exercise Due Caution In Reviewing Use Of Multisig
assessments.quote: The list of instances justifying use of the multisig in the Target Document is not intended to be exhaustive. However, the Core Council must exercise due caution in reviewing and validating use of the multisig in edge cases, i.e., use of the multisig that falls outside of the examples provided in the Target Document. In such "edge cases," the Core Council must ensure that a postmortem is publicly published on the Sky Forum which justifies the use of the multisig. The Core Council should also consider proposing an edit to the Target Document so that the edge case is explicitly included in the examples provided in the Target Document.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council to publish a public Sky Forum postmortem justifying any multisig use outside the listed examples.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The postmortem obligation is concrete and checkable (a published Sky Forum post for each edge-case use), but there is no deadline or cadence, and the core standard, 'due caution', is judgment language. The 'should consider' proposal is non-binding, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Edge-case multisig use must have a postmortem publicly published on the Sky Forum
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Council is both the actor and the reviewer of its own edge-case use, so enforcement is self-policing. Public posting only enables the generic Reports Of Misalignment and Adjudication catch-alls, which are weak on their own.

assessments.title: SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The SparkLend Security Access Multisig currently has a 3/5 signing requirement.
assessments.description: States the current signing threshold of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig as 3 of 5.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact, verifiable value (3-of-5 signers) for a named controlled system, so a third party could check it against the Safe configuration. It is descriptive rather than an obligation: it does not say the threshold must be maintained, changed only through a defined process, or checked on any cadence.
metrics: 3/5 signing requirement
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever threshold is actually configured, not the stated 3/5, so a mismatch is caught only by Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10), which has a named enforcer distinct from the actor. No quantified consequence attaches to this specific paragraph.

assessments.title: SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. The Core Facilitator should consider preparing an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.
assessments.description: Requires Governance Poll approval for SparkLend multisig signer changes, with two exceptions requiring a public Sky Forum post.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The approval route (Governance Poll, no Executive Vote) and the two enumerated exceptions are concrete and checkable. Timing is qualitative ("as soon as possible", "immediately"), and the expedited Executive Vote is only "should consider", so the escalation duty is not binding.
metrics: Signer modifications require approval through a Governance Poll
Exception 1: signer self-reports loss of private key access, communicated via public Sky Forum post
Exception 2: signer explicitly requests removal, communicated via public Sky Forum post
Replacement of affected signer "as soon as possible" (no deadline)
Unratified signer changes "should be questioned immediately" (no deadline)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check the multisig signer configuration against the approved Poll record and assess penalties, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can pre-authorize a freeze if an unauthorized signer change threatens security. Neither is quantified for this rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the signer approval requirement.

assessments.title: Emergency Spells Definition
assessments.quote: Emergency Spells are expedited ad hoc Spells that, while typically compliant with all customary quality-assurance processes, do not adhere to the normal Spell cadence. Emergency Spells solve the root issue of an emergency / urgent situation impacting the Protocol and are used when a rapid response time is needed. The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps are responsible for managing the use of Emergency Spells pursuant to [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b) and [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48).
assessments.description: Defines Emergency Spells as expedited ad hoc Spells outside the normal cadence, managed by Core Facilitator and Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actors and the referenced procedures, but gives no criteria for what qualifies as an emergency, no timing for rapid response, and no threshold for the 'typically compliant' QA standard. Compliance with 'when a rapid response time is needed' is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines the emergency tool and assigns its management to Core Facilitator and Core GovOps, which is self-management rather than an external enforcer. The Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) is the instrument itself, not a consequence for misusing this definition, and no penalty or escalation path is stated.

assessments.title: Standby Spells Definition
assessments.quote:
Sky Protocol uses circuit-breakers to mitigate undesired scenarios, which circuit-breakers are called MOM contracts. MOM contracts must first be triggered through a Spell, after which they bypass the GSM Pause Delay and can immediately act on the Protocol. See [A.1.10.3.2 - Exceptions](6781594b-5dff-45ec-89a4-1c9684c4eed8).

In emergency scenarios, time is a scarce resource. Therefore, Standby Spells are used in validated emergency scenarios to trigger a MOM contract. In an emergency situation, Spell teams can then focus on crafting an ad hoc Emergency Spell to solve the root cause of an issue, if appropriate. Due to Standby Spells, it is no longer necessary in an emergency for Spell teams to spend time crafting and reviewing a Spell whose sole purpose is to trigger a mitigation of the issue, i.e., the MOM contract.

Standby Spells open new attack vectors that must be mitigated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb).
assessments.description: Defines Standby Spells as validated-emergency triggers for MOM circuit-breaker contracts that bypass the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real mechanism (MOM contracts triggered by spell, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay) but gives no thresholds or deadlines. "Validated emergency scenarios" is never defined, so who validates and on what criteria is left to judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Spells framework (b8266c11) is the mechanism this paragraph defines, not a consequence for breaching it. Misuse of a Standby Spell has no quantified penalty, no enforcer distinct from the Spell teams, and no contract-level check on the validation step. The referenced ADs' Role doc (53cea69b) is a separate obligation, not an enforcement path.

assessments.title: Standby Spell Incorporation Into New MOM Contracts
assessments.quote: Each new MOM contract created must incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory, which can be used to create new Standby Spells that can trigger the MOM contract. With a Standby Spell per every MOM contract, the generation of technical debt can be avoided.
assessments.description: Requires every new MOM contract to incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory that can trigger it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete and checkable: each new MOM contract must include a Standby Spell or factory. It gives no criteria for what counts as incorporation or what a trigger must do, and no deadline or verification cadence.
metrics: Each new MOM contract must incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain control, penalty, or review path is tied to this design requirement. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) are the capability the standby spell feeds, not a consequence for omitting it, so only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Available Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The currently available Standby Spells are defined in the subdocuments herein. The following list of Standby Spells is not exhaustive: that is, the Core Facilitator, in collaboration with the Emergency Response Group and Spell teams, has the discretion to develop and use a Standby Spell that is not listed in the subdocuments below. When that occurs, however, the Core Facilitator must ensure that the new Standby Spell is subsequently added to the subdocuments below.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator create unlisted Standby Spells and requires them to be added to the subdocuments afterward.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actor (Core Facilitator) and the required action (add new spells to the subdocuments), but gives no deadline, cadence, or criteria for "subsequently" or for when discretion applies. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator is both the actor and the party responsible for the documentation duty, so enforcement is self-policed. Artifact review (d4bf73e7) covers Agents rather than the Core Facilitator, and the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) governs spell execution, not documentation of spells.

assessments.title: Single-Collateral Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The subdocuments herein define currently available single-collateral Standby Spells. For each instance of use, single-collateral Standby Spell contracts require a transaction to deploy the Standby Spell from a factory.
assessments.description: Requires each use of a single-collateral Standby Spell to be deployed by a transaction from a factory contract.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete, checkable operational step (one factory deployment transaction per instance of use), but it is introductory and gives no thresholds, cadence, or conditions for when a Standby Spell may be used. A defender could argue it is descriptive rather than binding.
metrics: One deployment transaction from a factory per instance of use of a single-collateral Standby Spell
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) govern pre-authorized executive use of these spells, so a use bypassing the factory deployment step would fall under that regime. The consequence for that bypass is not quantified for this paragraph, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: SingleOsmStopSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to freeze an OSM for a single collateral. If the oracle price provider fails for any reason, Governance can act before the OSM registers the next price; this allows for the problem to be fixed with no impact on the system.
assessments.description: Lets Governance freeze one collateral's OSM via a standby spell when its oracle price provider fails.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a specific action (freezing an OSM for a single collateral) and a trigger (oracle provider failure), but the trigger is 'for any reason' with no defined failure criteria, and there are no thresholds, timing windows, or approval requirements. Whether the spell may be used is arguable on any given facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The freeze is a pre-authorized Emergency Spell (A.1.10.5) that Governance can execute when an oracle failure threatens security, which plausibly reaches this trigger. However, no consequence is quantified and the freeze fires only if Governance chooses to cast it.

assessments.title: SingleDdmDisableSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to disable a D3M integration. If a D3M partner is experiencing a problem such as a hack, this emergency Spell can be used to prevent abuse. While it cannot recover Dai already injected into the compromised protocol, the Emergency Spell can prevent additional exposure.
assessments.description: Permits an emergency standby spell to disable a D3M integration when a partner faces a hack or similar problem.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete action (disable a D3M integration) and a trigger, but the trigger is qualitative ("experiencing a problem such as a hack") with no defined severity, threshold, or decision owner. A defender could argue the spell is merely available and does not bind any party to act.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention to freeze or pause a component when security is threatened, and this spell is one such intervention. However, invocation depends on someone volunteering to cast it, and no quantified consequence attaches to failing to disable a compromised D3M.

assessments.title: SingleLitePsmHaltFactory
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to halt a LitePSM completely.
assessments.description: Describes a standby emergency spell that can fully halt a LitePSM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete action (complete halt of a LitePSM) and a named controlled system, but the trigger ('an emergency') is undefined and no criteria, thresholds, or deadlines are given. Whether the spell may be used in a given situation is therefore arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Spells mechanism (pre-authorized executive intervention such as freezes or pauses) is the mechanism that would invoke this halt, but the escalation depends on someone invoking the spell and no quantified consequence attaches to the rule itself.

assessments.title: Grouped Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The subdocuments herein define currently available grouped Standby Spells. For each instance of use, grouped Standby Spell contracts require a transaction to deploy the Standby Spell from a factory. Unlike single-collateral Standby Spells, a grouped Standby Spell is configured at the time of deployment with a specific list of collaterals it can operate on. This setup enables a single grouped Standby Spell to operate on multiple related collaterals.
assessments.description: Describes that grouped Standby Spells are deployed per use via factory transaction, configured with a fixed collateral list.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete mechanics (factory deployment transaction, collateral list set at deployment) but states no thresholds, limits, or verifiable compliance criteria. It is largely descriptive, so a defender could argue it imposes no binding obligation.
metrics: One deployment transaction from a factory for each instance of use
Collateral list configured at deployment
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The text defines no violation mode, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Role Definitions, Penalty Mechanisms) reaches a deviation from the deployment or collateral-list setup. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) is the parent framework but does not itself enforce this descriptive configuration rule.

assessments.title: GroupedLineWipeSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell will perform a Line MOM Wipe (set debt ceiling to zero) for the specified collaterals. It can be used if the specified collaterals fail - for example, if a stablecoin depegs or the protocol that provides the token is hacked. Users will still be able to exit their positions, but no new debt will be allowed to be created for the collaterals.
assessments.description: Defines a standby spell that sets the debt ceiling to zero for specified collaterals when they fail, blocking new debt while allowing exits.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative action is concrete: debt ceiling set to zero for named collaterals, with exits still allowed. The trigger is qualitative ("if the specified collaterals fail", with depeg or hack given only as examples), and no failure threshold or measurement is defined.
metrics: Line (debt ceiling) set to zero for the specified collaterals
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The spell is a pre-authorized emergency intervention under Emergency Spells (b8266c11), executed through the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) when collateral security is threatened. Enforcement depends on governance invoking it, and the paragraph sets no quantified consequence.

assessments.title: GroupedClipBreakerSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to stop liquidations for the specified collaterals.
assessments.description: Permits an emergency standby spell to halt liquidations for specified collateral types.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real capability (halting liquidations) and a defined instrument (this Standby Spell), but the affected collaterals are unnamed ("the specified collaterals"), and it gives no trigger condition, duration, or scope limit. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a tool rather than constraining an actor, so no mechanism punishes or blocks misuse of the spell. The parent Emergency Spells system (b8266c11) governs spell execution, but it does not enforce a rule stated in this paragraph.

assessments.title: MultiLineWipeSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell will wipe all lines, setting the debt ceilings for all collaterals (lines) to zero. Users will still be able to exit their positions, but no new debt will be allowed to be created for any collateral.
assessments.description: Standby spell that sets all collateral debt ceilings (lines) to zero, halting new debt while leaving exits open.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative parameter is exact: every line's debt ceiling is set to zero, and the effect is verifiable on-chain after casting. It gives no trigger conditions or casting deadline, and the definition of 'lines' is external to the paragraph.
metrics: Debt ceiling for all collaterals (lines) set to 0
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) are the pre-authorized intervention for threatened security rules, and once cast the zeroed debt ceilings are enforced by the contracts. Casting still depends on governance volunteering the spell, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: MultiClipBreakerSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell will freeze liquidations for all collaterals.
assessments.description: Defines a standby emergency spell that freezes liquidations for all collateral types.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The action (freeze liquidations) and scope (all collaterals) are concrete and checkable against deployed code. The paragraph gives no trigger conditions, duration, or unfreeze criteria, so when the spell applies is left open.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes an emergency spell that is itself the enforcement instrument, not a rule whose breach is enforced. No mechanism reaches a violation of an obligation stated here, so none found.

assessments.title: MultiOsmStopSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell will freeze all OSMs. If the oracle price provider fails for any reason, Governance can act before the OSM registers the next price; this allows for the problem to be fixed with no impact on the system.
assessments.description: Describes a standby spell that freezes all OSMs so governance can act before the next price posts if the oracle provider fails.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete action (freezing all OSMs) and a timing window (before the next price registers), but the trigger is 'fails for any reason' with no defined failure criteria or detection threshold. No numeric parameters or cadence are stated for the OSM price update.
metrics: Trigger: oracle price provider fails 'for any reason'
Timing: governance acts before the OSM registers the next price
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The standby spell is an Emergency Spell (pre-authorized executive intervention) that is only cast when the oracle failure is threatened or occurs, so the Emergency Spells mechanism plausibly reaches the failure. Casting still depends on governance volunteering to act within the window, so it is not automatic.

assessments.title: SplitterStopSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to disable the Smart Burn Engine.
assessments.description: Permits a pre-defined Standby Spell to disable the Smart Burn Engine during an emergency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete action (disabling the Smart Burn Engine) and the instrument (a Standby Spell), but gives no definition of 'emergency', no trigger criteria, and no authorizing actor or approval path. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph confers a permissive capability rather than imposing an obligation, so there is no violation mode for a mechanism to reach. The Emergency Spells framework (b8266c11) is the instrument itself, not enforcement of this text.

assessments.title: SPBEAMHaltSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM). See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a). After this Standby Spell is invoked, the SP-BEAM will no longer be able to set rates in the system. Invoking the Standby Spell has no impact on rates, which remain at pre-invocation levels until adjusted by Sky Governance via an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Lets an emergency Standby Spell disable SP-BEAM from setting rates, with rates held until an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative effect is concrete: after invocation SP-BEAM can no longer set rates, and rates stay at pre-invocation levels until an Executive Vote. However, the trigger is only "an emergency", with no defined criteria, and no thresholds or deadlines are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is itself a pre-authorized Emergency Spell (A.1.10.5) that contains SP-BEAM rate-setting when a risk is threatened. Its use still depends on someone invoking it, and no automatic trigger or quantified consequence is stated for SP-BEAM misbehavior.

assessments.title: The Core Facilitator Role In Standby Spells
assessments.quote:
The role of the Core Facilitator in the Standby Spell process is as follows:

- Standby Spells can only be used in response to a properly validated and categorized emergency scenario, for which the Core Facilitator is responsible. See [A.1.9.1.5.1 - Incident Validation](97020aa2-9492-4fa4-8eee-d860d6f33618) and [A.1.9.1.5.2 - Incident Categorization](f3a647b2-8083-41f1-b67a-66bd322ccc16).

The decision to initiate the process to use a Standby Spell is reserved for the Core Facilitator; where possible, the Core Facilitator should consult with any relevant Scope Advisor(s). See [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b).

- The Core Facilitator must explicitly communicate the decision to use a Standby Spell in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf) or on a "war room" video call.

- After the decision to use a Standby Spell is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).

- After the Core Facilitator decides to use a Standby Spell, TechOps Services must promptly trigger an incident to the Emergency Response Group as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).

- The Core Facilitator is responsible for actioning the Standby Spell and liaising with the Ranked Delegates (and other Aligned Delegates as needed) to gather the necessary support for it.
assessments.description: Defines the Core Facilitator's duties in initiating, documenting, and actioning Standby Spells during emergencies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Core Facilitator, TechOps Services, Ranked Delegates) and named communication channels are concrete, and the steps are enumerated. However, 'promptly' and 'where possible' are unquantified, and no deadline or cadence is stated.
metrics: Decision communicated in the Emergency Response Signal Group or on a war room video call
Decision documented promptly in the Emergency Response Signal Group after a video call
TechOps Services triggers an incident promptly after the Core Facilitator's decision
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Failure to communicate, document, or trigger an incident promptly has no named enforcer distinct from the Core Facilitator and no defined consequence. The Emergency Spells and Emergency Response System docs describe the process itself, not a penalty for breaching these duties.

assessments.title: Core GovOps Role In Standby Spells
assessments.quote: Core GovOps must promptly acknowledge receipt of the Core Facilitator's decision to use a Standby Spell. This acknowledgment must take place in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to promptly acknowledge Core Facilitator Standby Spell decisions in the Emergency Response Signal Group channel.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, the triggering event, and the channel (via the cited Emergency Response Signal Group doc) are concrete. However, "promptly" has no numeric deadline or measurement, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps is an agent subject to scheduled Agent Artifact Review, which could surface a missed or late acknowledgment, and the Emergency Response System governs the signal channel this step uses. No specific penalty or remedy is stated for failing to acknowledge, so the consequence is unquantified.

assessments.title: Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Standby Spell
assessments.quote:
Two Authorized Representatives, as defined in the subdocument below, from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of the Standby Spell.

This validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf). Only the entities specified in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell](4cf98145-079f-44e0-9a2b-1d7b16037f4a) are authorized to provide the validation of authenticity.

Pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb), ADs are prohibited from voting for a Standby Spell without this validation of authenticity.
assessments.description: Requires two Core GovOps representatives to validate Standby Spell authenticity in writing before ADs may vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The count (two), the form (written communication), and the prohibition on ADs voting without validation are all stated. The secure channel and the list of authorized entities are delegated to referenced subdocuments, and no deadline or cadence is given.
metrics: Two Authorized Representatives from Core GovOps must validate authenticity
Validation must be a written communication in the secure channel specified in A.1.9.1.3.1
