Only entities listed in A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1.1 may validate
ADs prohibited from voting for a Standby Spell without validation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) cover pre-authorized intervention when security rules are violated, and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could check whether a Standby Spell was validated before AD votes. Neither defines a quantified consequence for this specific rule, and the AD voting prohibition has no direct penalty path.

assessments.title: Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell
assessments.quote:
This document defines the term "Authorized Representative" as used in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1 - Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Standby Spell](82393e1d-1021-4f48-ac4e-a98d2328f2e7).

The entities listed below are authorized to validate the authenticity of a Standby Spell on behalf of Core GovOps:

- Retro on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Adam Fraser on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Lex on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs

The Authorized Representatives listed are synonymous with the Sky Forum account holders with the following handles:

- retro
- adamfraser
- Lex
assessments.description: Names the three Core GovOps representatives (Retro, Adam Fraser, Lex) authorized to validate Standby Spell authenticity, and their Sky Forum handles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a closed, named list of authorized validators with the account handles that map to them, so membership is checkable from the text alone. It lacks any procedure, deadline, or validation standard, and the handle for Lex is inconsistently capitalized.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) could detect a Standby Spell validated by someone not on this list and assess penalties, with enforcer distinct from actor. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and escalation depends on the review being triggered.

assessments.title: Custom Spell Voting For Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may use the Custom Spell Voting Page when it is beneficial to coordinate voting without using the standard Spell process. The Core Facilitator must not use this method unless domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group have recommended this approach; such a recommendation must be explicitly documented in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Permits the Core Facilitator to use the Custom Spell Voting Page only with documented domain-expert recommendation in the Emergency Response Signal Group channel.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Core Facilitator), a gating condition (domain-expert Emergency Response Group recommendation), and a specific documentation channel (A.1.9.1.3.1), which makes compliance checkable. However, the permissive trigger 'when it is beneficial' is judgment language, and 'domain expert' is undefined, so the threshold for use remains qualitative.
metrics: Use requires a recommendation from domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group
Recommendation must be explicitly documented in the A.1.9.1.3.1 Emergency Response Signal Group communication channel
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limiter, role gating, artifact review) reaches a Core Facilitator bypassing the standard Spell process without the documented recommendation; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: ADs' Role In Standby Spells
assessments.quote:
ADs are strictly prohibited from voting to use a Standby Spell unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements:

- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's official notification of the emergency scenario in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).
- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's announcement of the decision to use a Standby Spell in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and
- Core GovOps has validated the authenticity of the Standby Spell. This validation must fulfill two requirements: (1) the validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and (2) the validation must be provided by the Authorized Representatives listed in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell](4cf98145-079f-44e0-9a2b-1d7b16037f4a).

After ADs have confirmed all requirements are met, they must either (1) promptly vote to approve the Standby Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution.
assessments.description: Requires ADs to confirm specified notifications, channel announcements, and GovOps authenticity validation before voting on a Standby Spell, then vote or escalate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (ADs, Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, Authorized Representatives), channels, and validation form are named and checkable. The timing is qualitative: 'promptly' and 'speedy resolution' carry no deadline or cadence.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Penalty Mechanisms, Conservatorship, and Artifact Review target Primes or Operational Agents rather than ADs voting conduct. Emergency Spells could freeze a spell but do not penalize a voter who skips the prerequisites.

assessments.title: AD Reliance On Core GovOps In Standby Spell Process Where Core GovOps Is Nonresponsive
assessments.quote: There is an exception to the requirement that two Authorized Representatives from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of a Standby Spell. In situations where the Authorized Representatives have failed to respond to the emergency situation, the Core Facilitator may temporarily grant an Operational Facilitator the sole authority to validate the authenticity of the Emergency Spell pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb). The Core Facilitator must communicate this in writing in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Allows the Core Facilitator to temporarily give one Operational Facilitator sole authority to validate Standby Spells when Core GovOps Authorized Representatives are nonresponsive, with written notice.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Core Facilitator, Operational Facilitator, Core GovOps Authorized Representatives) and the notice channel are named, and the written-communication step is verifiable. However, 'failed to respond' has no time threshold, and 'temporarily' has no duration or expiry, so the trigger and scope are not quantified.
metrics: Authorized Representative validation requires two Core GovOps representatives, with a single-validator exception on nonresponse
Core Facilitator must communicate the exception in writing in the Emergency Response Signal Group secure channel
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can audit whether the written exception notice was issued and whether the nonresponse trigger was met, with an enforcer distinct from the actor. Emergency Spells provide executive intervention if the exception is misused, but no quantified penalty or escalation is tied to this specific rule, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Misalignment To Vote For Unvalidated Standby Spell
assessments.quote: It is severe misalignment for an Aligned Delegate to vote for a Standby Spell whose authenticity has not been validated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb). Aligned Delegates in breach of this requirement must be immediately derecognized and their full AD Buffer should be confiscated.
assessments.description: Bars Aligned Delegates from voting for unvalidated Standby Spells, with derecognition and AD Buffer confiscation as breach remedies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, the prohibited act, and the remedies are concrete, and 'full AD Buffer' and 'immediately' are defined magnitudes. However, 'authenticity validated' is delegated to the referenced A.1.10.5.2.3.3 process, the remedy is worded as 'should be' confiscated, and no measurement or enforcement timing beyond 'immediately' is set.
metrics: Breach: an Aligned Delegate votes for a Standby Spell whose authenticity has not been validated
Remedy: immediate derecognition of the breaching Aligned Delegate
Remedy: confiscation of the full AD Buffer
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms provide quantified financial penalties that plausibly reach AD Buffer confiscation for this breach, and the paragraph states the consequence. The enforcer and escalation path are not named, so firing depends on someone invoking the penalty process, which keeps it at mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Accountability
assessments.quote: Breach of any requirement concerning Emergency Spells - including Standby Spells - constitutes misalignment and must be addressed pursuant to [A.1.9.1.6 - Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness](8df982ee-754c-4cd9-a5f9-ce1c30e06cf8).
assessments.description: Makes breaches of Emergency Spell requirements, including Standby Spells, misalignment to be addressed under the emergency-response accountability process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and identifiable, but it names no threshold, deadline, cadence, or outcome for a breach. "Must be addressed" is judgment language, and the operative procedure is delegated to an external paragraph (A.1.9.1.6) whose text is not provided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The only path stated is the misalignment route, which is the catch-all Reports of Misalignment mechanism and is weak alone. The cross-referenced A.1.9.1.6 (8df982ee) is not in the catalog and its consequences are not stated in this text, so no citable mechanism is confirmed.

assessments.title: Emergency Drop Spells
assessments.quote: The Protego contract can be used to deploy an Emergency Drop Spell. Once authorized by Sky Governance, the Emergency Drop Spell can cancel any planned governance action that is awaiting GSM Pause Delay expiration.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance authorize an Emergency Drop Spell via Protego to cancel governance actions awaiting GSM Pause Delay expiration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Sky Governance), the contract (Protego), and a verifiable trigger (action awaiting GSM Pause Delay expiration). It gives no numeric threshold, and the GSM Pause Delay value and any authorization threshold are left undefined here.
metrics: Action must be awaiting GSM Pause Delay expiration (delay value not stated in paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a remedial capability rather than setting a breachable obligation, so no consequence attaches to following or breaking it. The parent Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) is the tool itself, not an enforcer of a rule stated here.

assessments.title: Deployment Of Emergency Drop Spells
assessments.quote:
Any user can permissionlessly deploy an Emergency Drop Spell by invoking the `deploy` function on the Protego contract with parameters identifying the planned governance action to be canceled. The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
function deploy(address _usr, bytes32 _tag, bytes memory _fax, uint256 _eta) public returns (address _spell)
```

The parameters of the `deploy` function are defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).
assessments.description: Permits any user to permissionlessly deploy an Emergency Drop Spell via the Protego deploy function, with parameters defined elsewhere.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (any user) and the exact Solidity signature of the deploy function are fully specified, so compliance can be checked from the text. The parameter semantics are deferred to another section (A.1.10.5.3.1.3) and the paragraph states no thresholds, deadlines, or metrics.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a permission rather than imposing an obligation, so there is no violation mode for an enforcement mechanism to reach. The Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) is the spell this function produces, not an enforcer of this text.

assessments.title: Execution Of Emergency Drop Spells
assessments.quote: Once an Emergency Drop Spell has been deployed, it can be used to cancel the execution of the planned governance action by invoking its `drop` function. This function can only be invoked if the Emergency Drop Spell has been granted authority by Sky Governance by giving the Emergency Drop Spell the `hat` in the Chief contract.
assessments.description: Lets an Emergency Drop Spell cancel a planned governance action via its drop function, but only when it holds the Chief hat.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Emergency Drop Spell), the function (`drop`), the contract (Chief), and a verifiable access condition (holding the `hat`). It states no numeric thresholds, timing, or scope limits on what may be dropped.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The hat gate is an on-chain authority check, so calling drop without the hat fails. This is not in the catalog, so the rating rests on Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5), the pre-authorized intervention framework that governs when this spell may act. The consequence is not separately quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Allowing Permissionless Cancellation Of Planned Governance Actions
assessments.quote: The Protego contract can be granted authority by Sky Governance to allow any user to permissionlessly cancel any planned governance action. This is done by giving the Protego contract the `hat` in the Chief contract. Once the Protego contract has been granted authority, any user can cancel either a single planned governance action or a set of planned governance actions as specified herein.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance grant Protego the Chief hat so any user can cancel planned governance actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete parameters: the Protego contract, the `hat` in the Chief contract, and the scope of any planned governance action. The operative criteria for cancellation are delegated to "as specified herein", but nothing further is specified in this paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a capability rather than constraining an actor, and no catalog mechanism polices whether the hat grant or its use is compliant; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Permissionless Cancellation Of Single Planned Governance Action
assessments.quote:
If the Protego contract has authority from Sky Governance, any user can permissionlessly invoke the `drop` function to cancel a specified Spell. The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
/// @notice Permissionlessly drop anything that has been planned on the pause.
function drop(address _usr, bytes32 _tag, bytes memory _fax, uint256 _eta) public
```

The parameters of the `drop` function are defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).
assessments.description: Allows any user to permissionlessly cancel a planned governance spell via the Protego drop function, when Protego holds authority.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The function signature, the permissionless access condition, and the authority precondition are stated exactly, so a third party can verify the capability from the text. The drop parameters are deferred to A.1.10.5.3.1.3 without values being restated here, which leaves a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a permission rather than imposing an obligation on an actor, so no penalty, role check, or rate limit reverts or punishes a violation of it. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) is the parent framework and not an enforcer of this permission, and the catch-all mechanisms alone are weak.

assessments.title: Permissionless Cancellation Of Multiple Planned Governance Actions
assessments.quote:
If the Protego contract has authority from Sky Governance, any user can permissionlessly invoke the `drop` function to cancel a specified set of Spells. The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
/// @notice Drop multiple plans in a single call.
function drop(Plan[] calldata _plans) external
```

The parameter of the `drop` function is defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).
assessments.description: Lets any user cancel a specified set of planned Spells via the Protego contract's permissionless drop function, if Protego holds authority.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The function signature, the permissionless actor, and the authority precondition are stated exactly. The drop parameter type is delegated to A.1.10.5.3.1.3 with no value given here, and no metric, limit, or cadence is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Protego is part of the Emergency Spells framework (A.1.10.5), which is the pre-authorized intervention path for threatened security rules; drop is the cancellation step within it. Enforcement is not quantified for this rule, and the on-chain gating depends on Sky Governance granting authority, which the paragraph does not make contract-enforced.

assessments.title: Protego Usr Parameter Definition

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with no violation mode. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) govern Protego's use in general, but nothing in this text ties a consequence to supplying a wrong usr address.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines an input parameter with no stated violation mode. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) governs the Protego cancellation act rather than the definition of the tag, so it does not plausibly reach this text.

It states no operative threshold, format, matching criterion, or verification step, so it is definitional rather than a quantified obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines a parameter and imposes no violation mode. The parent Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) governs the Protego action as a whole, but nothing in this definition is a violable obligation that a mechanism would reach.

assessments.title: Protego Eta Parameter Definition
assessments.quote: The `eta` parameter is the expiration time of the scheduled Spell to be canceled.
assessments.description: Defines the eta parameter as the expiration time of a scheduled Spell that Protego cancels.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete parameter and its meaning, but states no value, unit, format, or verification criterion. It is a definition rather than an operative rule, so compliance cannot be checked from the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph imposes no obligation that an actor could breach; it only defines an input. The Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) governs Protego's cancellation actions, not this definition, so it does not reach this text.

assessments.description: Defines the Plan struct (usr, tag, fax, eta) used as the plans array of scheduled Spells that Protego cancels.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This paragraph defines a data schema rather than a violable obligation, and nothing in the text or the catalog penalizes a malformed Plan. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) is the vehicle carrying the parameter but does not police its format.

assessments.title: Determining Protego Parameters
assessments.quote: The parameters for the scheduled Spell to be canceled, as specified in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8), should always be determined by inspecting the logs emitted from the `plot` function of the Pause contract. The parameters should never be determined by calling functions on the Spell to be canceled, because these functions may not return the correct values in the case of a malicious Spell.
assessments.description: Requires Protego spell cancellations to take scheduled-spell parameters from Pause contract plot logs, never from calls to the target spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The method is concrete: parameters must come from the Pause contract's plot event logs and never from calling functions on the spell. No numeric threshold, deadline, or verification cadence is stated, so the obligation is procedural rather than quantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A Protego spell built from the wrong parameters would fail to cancel a malicious spell. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could plausibly catch a Protego whose parameters were not derived from plot logs, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule and escalation depends on the review being run.

assessments.title: The Core Facilitator Role In Protego Usage
assessments.quote:
The role of the Core Facilitator in the usage of Protego is as follows:

- Protego can only be used in response to a properly validated and categorized emergency scenario, for which the Core Facilitator is responsible. See [A.1.9.1.5.1 - Incident Validation](97020aa2-9492-4fa4-8eee-d860d6f33618) and [A.1.9.1.5.2 - Incident Categorization](f3a647b2-8083-41f1-b67a-66bd322ccc16).
- The decision to initiate the process to use Protego is reserved for the Core Facilitator; where possible, the Core Facilitator should consult with any relevant Scope Advisor(s). See [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b).
- The Core Facilitator must explicitly communicate the decision to use Protego in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf) or on a "war room" video call.
- If the decision to use Protego is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
- After the Core Facilitator decides to use Protego, TechOps Services must promptly trigger an incident to the Emergency Response Group as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).
- The Core Facilitator is responsible for actioning the usage of Protego and liaising with the Ranked Delegates (and other Aligned Delegates as needed) to gather the necessary support for it.
assessments.description: Defines the Core Facilitator's responsibilities and communication steps for initiating the use of Protego emergency spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors, channels, and referenced procedures are named, but the operative standards are judgment language: "properly validated," "where possible," "should consult," "promptly," and "as needed." No numeric threshold, time limit, or verifiable metric is stated, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: "promptly" to document the decision in the secure channel after a video-call decision (no time limit stated)
"promptly" for TechOps Services to trigger an incident after the Core Facilitator's decision (no time limit stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Protego is itself an Emergency Spell, and the Emergency Response System defines the escalation protocol these steps sit within, so misuse or a skipped step could be escalated through that machinery. The paragraph states no penalty for misusing Protego, and escalation depends on someone raising the issue, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Core GovOps Role In Protego Usage
assessments.quote: Core GovOps must promptly acknowledge receipt of the Core Facilitator's decision to use Protego. This acknowledgment must take place in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to promptly acknowledge the Core Facilitator's Protego usage decision in the specified emergency signal channel.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, action, and channel are named, with the channel defined by reference to A.1.9.1.3.1. However, 'promptly' has no time limit or measurable deadline, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System defines an escalation protocol outside the normal governance cycle that plausibly reaches a missed emergency acknowledgment. The consequence is unquantified for this rule and depends on someone escalating the omission.

assessments.title: Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.quote:
Two Authorized Representatives, as defined in the subdocument below, from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell, if applicable.

This validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf). Only the entities specified in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell](a15e7cd9-ea93-48ac-b53a-afc476ca2d05) are authorized to provide the validation of authenticity.

Pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52), ADs are prohibited from voting for an Emergency Drop Spell without this validation of authenticity.
assessments.description: Requires two Core GovOps Authorized Representatives to validate Emergency Drop Spell authenticity via a secure channel, and bars ADs from voting without it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule quantifies the validator count (two) and names the channel and authorized-entity list by cross-reference. It gives no deadline or cadence, and the 'if applicable' qualifier leaves the trigger undefined.
metrics: Two Authorized Representatives must validate authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell
Validation must be a written communication in the Emergency Response Signal Group secure channel
ADs prohibited from voting for an Emergency Drop Spell without validation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, contract gate, or named enforcer attaches to an AD voting without validation; the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) governs the spell itself, not this precondition, and the catch-all backstop alone is weak.

assessments.title: Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.quote:
This document defines the term "Authorized Representative" as used in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1 - Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Emergency Drop Spell](44b9503d-bc11-427e-8deb-47feed07eba2).

The entities listed below are authorized to validate the authenticity of an Emergency Drop Spell on behalf of Core GovOps:

- Retro on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Adam Fraser on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Lex on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs

The Authorized Representatives listed are synonymous with the Sky Forum account holders with the following handles:

- retro

assessments.description: Lists the named individuals authorized to validate Emergency Drop Spells on behalf of Core GovOps, and their Sky Forum handles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a fully enumerated set of named actors and their Sky Forum handles, so compliance can be checked against the list. It states no validation procedure, timing, or count of required validators; those are left to the linked section.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) are the pre-authorized intervention path for threatened security rules, which could reach an unauthorized or false validation of a drop spell. The consequence is not quantified for this list, and escalation depends on someone raising it.

assessments.title: Custom Spell Voting For Protego Usage
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may use the Custom Spell Voting Page when it is beneficial to coordinate voting without using the standard Spell process. The Core Facilitator must not use this method unless domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group have recommended this approach; such a recommendation must be explicitly documented in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Permits the Core Facilitator to use the Custom Spell Voting Page only after domain experts recommend it and the recommendation is documented in the emergency signal channel.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The gating condition is concrete and checkable: a recommendation from domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group, explicitly documented in a named channel (A.1.9.1.3.1). The initial permission rests on the undefined judgment term "when it is beneficial," with no criteria or threshold.
metrics: Use requires a recommendation from domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group
Recommendation must be explicitly documented in the A.1.9.1.3.1 Emergency Response Signal Group channel
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The documentation requirement is self-recorded by the Core Facilitator and the signal channel is a communication venue, not an enforcer. No on-chain control, penalty, or named reviewer reaches a use made without a documented recommendation.

assessments.title: ADs' Role In Protego Usage
assessments.quote:
ADs are strictly prohibited from voting to use an Emergency Drop Spell, or to give authority to the Protego contract, unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements:

- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's official notification of the emergency scenario in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5);
- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's announcement of the decision to use Protego or an Emergency Drop Spell in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and
- Core GovOps has validated the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell, if applicable. This validation must fulfill two requirements: (1) the validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and (2) the validation must be provided by the Authorized Representatives listed in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell](a15e7cd9-ea93-48ac-b53a-afc476ca2d05).

After ADs have confirmed all requirements are met, they must either (1) promptly vote to approve the usage of Protego or the Emergency Drop Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution.
assessments.description: Prohibits ADs from voting to use Protego or an Emergency Drop Spell until three confirmations are met, then requires a prompt vote or escalation of concerns.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The prohibition gate is objectively checkable: named notification channels, a named Authorized Representative list, and a written-communication requirement for validation. Gaps remain: "promptly" and "speedy resolution" have no deadline, and the post-confirmation path is an either/or left to judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention such as freezes or pauses when security rules are violated, which could reach an unauthorized Protego vote. No quantified penalty applies to an AD breach, and firing depends on someone raising the violation.

assessments.title: AD Reliance On Core GovOps In Emergency Drop Spell Process Where Core GovOps Is Nonresponsive
assessments.quote: There is an exception to the requirement that two Authorized Representatives from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of an Emergency Drop Spell. In situations where the Authorized Representatives have failed to respond to the emergency situation, the Core Facilitator may temporarily grant an Operational Facilitator the sole authority to validate the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52). The Core Facilitator must communicate this in writing in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Allows the Core Facilitator to temporarily give one Operational Facilitator sole authority to validate an Emergency Drop Spell when Core GovOps Authorized Representatives are nonresponsive, with written notice.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Core Facilitator, Operational Facilitator, Authorized Representatives) and a written-notice channel are named, so the procedure is concrete. The trigger "failed to respond" and the duration of "temporarily" have no time threshold or objective criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator grants and documents the exception itself, so enforcement is self-policed. No penalty, artifact review, or contract check reaches an improper or undocumented grant of validation authority.

assessments.title: Misalignment To Vote For Unvalidated Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.quote: It is severe misalignment for an Aligned Delegate to vote for an Emergency Drop Spell whose authenticity has not been validated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52). Aligned Delegates in breach of this requirement must be immediately derecognized and their full AD Buffer should be confiscated.
assessments.description: Makes voting for an unvalidated Emergency Drop Spell severe misalignment for Aligned Delegates, requiring immediate derecognition and AD Buffer confiscation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Aligned Delegates), the prohibited act, and the remedies (immediate derecognition, full AD Buffer confiscation) are concrete. However, the validation standard is delegated to a cross-referenced section, and confiscation uses 'should' rather than 'must'.
metrics: immediately derecognized
full AD Buffer confiscated
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph states concrete remedies with capital at risk (AD Buffer), but names no enforcer or escalation path. The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach the violation, though the consequence is not tied to a quantified penalty for ADs in this text.

assessments.title: Protego Usage Accountability
assessments.quote: Breach of any requirement concerning Emergency Spells - including usage of Protego - constitutes misalignment and must be addressed pursuant to [A.1.9.1.6 - Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness](8df982ee-754c-4cd9-a5f9-ce1c30e06cf8).
assessments.description: Classifies breaches of Emergency Spell requirements, including Protego usage, as misalignment to be addressed under A.1.9.1.6.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines a real obligation: breaches of Emergency Spell requirements, including Protego usage, are misalignment. It states no thresholds, cadence, or magnitudes, and 'addressed pursuant to' delegates the actual response to another document. A defender could plausibly argue the rule does not yet bind anything beyond the referral.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The only route is the referral to A.1.9.1.6 (8df982ee), which is cited verbatim in the text, but its content (penalties, escalation, enforcer) is not provided and cannot be verified. The paragraph itself reduces to the generic misalignment catch-all (Reports of Misalignment), which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Process For Misaligned Agent Artifacts
assessments.quote: In an emergency situation (see [A.1.9.1.1 - Definition Of Emergency Situations](5eafb29e-84a0-4a53-a798-3f958c880225)), Sky Core has the discretion to immediately suspend an Agent Artifact provision or function if it reasonably suspects that the Artifact is contributing towards a significant or system-level risk. Sky Core must act in good faith when exercising its discretion in emergency situations.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Core immediately suspend an Agent Artifact provision or function in an emergency when it reasonably suspects significant or system-level risk.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Sky Core) and action (immediate suspension) are defined, but the trigger relies on judgment terms: "reasonably suspects", "significant or system-level risk", and "good faith". The emergency definition is incorporated by reference to A.1.9.1.1 without a value here, and no metrics or thresholds are stated.
metrics: Suspension must be immediate upon Sky Core's reasonable suspicion of significant or system-level risk in an emergency situation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System provides a defined escalation path outside the standard governance cycle that can trigger suspension of an Artifact. Its firing still depends on Sky Core choosing to invoke it under its own discretion, and no quantified consequence attaches to the Artifact's conduct.

assessments.title: Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response
assessments.quote: All Agent Artifacts must contain a `Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response` document as a direct child of the `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document. This document and its subdocuments must specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol applicable in situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Requires every Agent Artifact to include a Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response document, directly under Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive, describing the Agent's protocol for ecosystem-wide emergencies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The structural requirement (a document placed as a direct child of a named parent) is verifiable, but the content obligation is judgment-based: 'specify the emergency response protocol' gives no criteria for what the protocol must contain or what counts as an 'entire Sky Ecosystem' impact. A defender could argue any protocol text complies.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps reviews agent artifacts on a schedule with staged findings and penalty assessment, and Core GovOps is distinct from the Agent, so it can catch a missing or non-conforming emergency response document. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Agent Emergency Response
assessments.quote: All Agent Artifacts must contain an `Agent-Specific Emergency Response` document as a direct child of the `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document. This document and its subdocuments must specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol applicable in situations solely impacting the Agent, versus the broader Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Requires every Agent Artifact to include an Agent-Specific Emergency Response document describing protocols for Agent-only situations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete document and its placement as a direct child of the Governance Information document, so presence is checkable. The required content, a protocol distinguishing Agent-only from ecosystem-wide situations, has no defined criteria, so compliance with the substance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps checks artifact contents against requirements, with an enforcer distinct from the Agent, so a missing or inadequate emergency response document would be flagged. Penalty assessment exists in that process but is not quantified for this rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Executor Agent Facilitators
assessments.quote: Executor Agent Facilitators are Facilitators that carry out specific activities on behalf of Executor Agents. Whenever an Executor Agent must interpret an Artifact, that interpretation must be done by the Facilitator. Whenever an Executor Agent has privileged access to smart contracts of Sky or an Agent, that access must be held by the Facilitator. Facilitators use this access to carry out the Executor Agent’s operational responsibilities as directed by GovOps, unless the Facilitator believes that GovOps is misaligned.
assessments.description: Requires Executor Agent Facilitators to hold Executor Agent privileged contract access and interpret Artifacts, acting on GovOps direction unless they judge GovOps misaligned.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph fixes concrete allocations: the Facilitator must hold privileged access and must do Artifact interpretation, which a third party could check. assessments.title: Rate Limits
assessments.quote:
Rate limits set the maximum allowable amount of tokens that can be processed for specific operations within a given time period. Each rate limit contains the rate limit data: `maxAmount`, `slope`, `lastAmount` and `lastUpdated`. The current rate limit is calculated using the formula:

`currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount)`.

The rate limit data `maxAmount` and `slope` are configurable parameters that are set and modified by Governance. The rate limit data `lastAmount` and `lastUpdated` are internal state data dynamically tracked by the Rate Limiter to perform its calculations.

Rate limits set caps on the rate of allocation to a given Instance, they do not act as a limit on the total amount that may be allocated to that Instance.
assessments.description: Defines rate limits as capped allocation rates per operation, computed by a linear-recovery formula from governance-set maxAmount and slope.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount) and the four data fields are exact and checkable against contract state. The governance-set maxAmount and slope have no stated values or update cadence in the text, so the operative magnitudes are delegated.
metrics: currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount)
maxAmount: governance-configurable cap (no value stated)
slope: governance-configurable rate of recovery (no value stated)
Rate limits cap the rate of allocation per Instance, not total allocation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter (a578830d) is the RateLimits contract that reverts any controller operation above its current rate limit, so the cap defined here is contract-enforced and self-executing.

assessments.title: MaxAmount
assessments.quote: `maxAmount` sets a hard cap on the level of allocation to an Instance at any given time. It sets the absolute rate limit regardless of how much time has passed since the last allocation. For example, if `maxAmount` is set to 1,000,000 tokens, the rate limit will increase over time at the rate determined by the `slope` until it reaches 1,000,000 tokens. At this point the rate limit will stop increasing, but it will resume increasing once an allocation to the Instance has been made.
assessments.description: Defines maxAmount as an absolute cap on allocation to an Instance, with the rate limit recovering at slope until reaching it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete mechanism: a hard cap on allocation, a slope-driven increase, and a reset on each allocation. The only numeric value is an illustrative 1,000,000-token example, and the actual maxAmount and slope values are defined elsewhere.
metrics: maxAmount: hard cap on allocation level to an Instance at any time
Rate limit increases at the slope rate until it reaches maxAmount
Example: maxAmount = 1,000,000 tokens
Rate limit resumes increasing after each allocation to the Instance
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter (a578830d) is contract-enforced: the RateLimits contracts revert any controller operation that exceeds the current rate limit. This paragraph defines the maxAmount and slope parameters that drive that limit, so the Rate Limiter reaches it directly.

assessments.title: LastAmount
assessments.quote: `lastAmount` is the remaining allowance available at the last update, used to compute the current rate limit by adding accrued capacity.
assessments.description: Defines lastAmount as the remaining rate-limit allowance at last update, used with accrued capacity to compute the current limit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a formula shape (current limit equals lastAmount plus accrued capacity) but states no value, accrual rate, or update cadence. It is a state-variable definition rather than an obligation, and the accrual term is defined nowhere here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The RateLimits contracts compute the current limit from lastAmount plus accrued capacity and revert any controller operation above it, so the on-chain Rate Limiter enforces the quantity this paragraph defines.

assessments.title: Outflow Rate Limits
assessments.quote:
Outflow Rate Limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced from a scope. "Outflow" means movements that lower exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as withdrawals, redemptions, or unwind operations.

Outflow limits are often configured more permissively to prioritize safety and fast exits. When outflow limits are "unlimited," the rate limits contract simply does not apply a cap in that direction.
assessments.description: Defines outflow rate limits as caps on how fast allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced, and states that unlimited means no cap applies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines outflow and describes the limit concept, but states no threshold, formula, or cadence. Its only operative statements are qualitative ('often configured more permissively') and a semantic rule that 'unlimited' means no cap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter contracts revert any controller operation exceeding its configured rate limit, which reaches the outflow direction when a cap is set. The paragraph itself does not state a value, so enforcement applies only to limits configured on the controller.

assessments.title: MaxSlippage
assessments.quote: `maxSlippage` is a configurable parameter that sets the maximum allowed price impact or deviation from expected output when executing trades or liquidity operations in a pool. `maxslippage` is expressed as a decimal and must be a non-zero value. This protects against excessive price impact during volatile market conditions.
assessments.description: Defines maxSlippage as a non-zero decimal parameter capping price impact or deviation from expected output in pool operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a parameter and its type (non-zero decimal), giving a checkable constraint. It states no numeric threshold, default, per-pool value, or measurement method, so a defender could argue it is definitional rather than binding.
metrics: maxSlippage must be a non-zero decimal value
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Rate Limiter reaches rate limits, slopes, and maxAmount caps, not slippage tolerances, and nothing in the text ties a slippage breach to a penalty, role check, or emergency path.

assessments.title: Maximum Exposure Tolerance
assessments.quote: Where the Atlas specifies a maximum exposure, actual exposure may exceed that maximum by up to 5%, provided the excess is solely attributable to accrued interest and not to new principal. A Prime Agent is responsible for claiming and returning accrued interest as necessary to keep exposure within the specified maximum.
assessments.description: Permits exposure to exceed maximums by 5% if caused by accrued interest; Prime Agents manage interest.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 5% tolerance and the 'solely accrued interest, not new principal' condition are concrete and checkable. The 5% base (of the maximum or of exposure) is unstated, and the Prime Agent's duty to claim or return interest 'as necessary' has no cadence or deadline.
metrics: Exposure may exceed a specified maximum by up to 5%
Excess must be solely attributable to accrued interest, not new principal
Prime Agent claims and returns accrued interest as necessary to keep exposure within the maximum
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can plausibly reach a Prime that lets exposure drift beyond its maximum, and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could catch a breach, but no penalty is quantified for this rule. Rate Limiter (a578830d) does not reach accrued interest because interest accrual is not a controller operation that reverts.

assessments.title: Revoker
assessments.quote: A Revoker is an address registered on the AdministeredAgent that is authorized to remove an Actor as a rapid-response measure, without affecting the Allocator Role held by the AdministeredAgent. The Freezer Multisig of a Prime Agent is registered as a Revoker, providing the emergency capability to remove a compromised or malicious Actor outside the standard governance process.
assessments.description: Defines the Revoker role on AdministeredAgent and assigns it to the Prime Agent's Freezer Multisig for emergency actor removal.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete actor (the Prime's Freezer Multisig), a registry (AdministeredAgent), and a function (removing an Actor without affecting the Allocator Role). The trigger, 'compromised or malicious', is qualitative, and no thresholds, timing, or verification method are given.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Liquidity Layer Role Definitions gate the removal function to registered Revoker addresses, so a call from any other address reverts. Nothing on-chain constrains the Revoker to the compromised-or-malicious trigger, so misuse depends on governance response rather than contract enforcement.

assessments.title: Hop Definition
assessments.quote:
The `hop` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive increases any cBEAM makes to the same rate limit's `maxAmount` or `slope`. Its value is set per `RateLimits` contract, but the interval is tracked independently for each rate limit within it, so increasing one rate limit does not affect when another can next be increased. A decrease is not subject to `hop`.

Changes to the `hop` parameter are proposed by the Core Council Multisig, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), or made directly via an Executive Vote at any time, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4 - PAS](989171ed-5424-42ee-83f4-199e1149699c).
assessments.description: Sets a per-rate-limit minimum interval, in seconds, between cBEAM increases to maxAmount or slope, with decreases exempt and hop changes governed by the Core Council Multisig or Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete parameter, the `hop` interval in seconds, and its scope (per rate limit, per RateLimits contract, increases only). However, the operative magnitude is never stated and is delegated to each contract's setting, so the rule does not say how long the interval is. Changes are also allowed by Executive Vote 'at any time' with no stated timing constraint beyond that.
metrics: hop: minimum interval in seconds between consecutive increases to the same rate limit's maxAmount or slope (value set per RateLimits contract; no numeric value stated)
Interval tracked independently for each rate limit within a RateLimits contract
Decreases to maxAmount or slope are not subject to hop
Changes to hop proposed by Core Council Multisig or made via Executive Vote at any time without a prior Governance Poll
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The hop interval is a parameter of the RateLimits contracts that gate cBEAM's maxAmount and slope changes, so the contract enforces the timing constraint on-chain and reverts non-compliant increases, which the Rate Limiter (a578830d) covers for any paragraph stating a maxAmount or slope.

assessments.title: Hop Default Value
assessments.quote: All `RateLimits` contracts on Ethereum Mainnet use a single, shared `hop` value unless the Core Council Multisig or an Executive Vote sets one specifically for a given contract. That shared value is 57,600 seconds (16 hours).
assessments.description: Sets a shared default 57,600-second (16-hour) hop for Ethereum Mainnet RateLimits contracts, overridable per contract by the Core Council Multisig or an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The default value (57,600 seconds) and the scope (all Ethereum Mainnet RateLimits contracts) are stated exactly, and the override actors are named. Gaps: the paragraph does not define how hop operates in the rate-limit formula, and it gives no cadence for reviewing overrides.
metrics: Default hop value: 57,600 seconds (16 hours)
Applies to all RateLimits contracts on Ethereum Mainnet unless overridden
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The hop is a parameter of the RateLimits contracts, which revert any controller operation above its current rate limit, so the configured hop is contract-enforced. The override path depends on Core Council Multisig or Executive Vote action, which is an actor-level control rather than an on-chain constraint on the default text itself.

assessments.title: Max Change Definition
assessments.quote:
The `maxChange` parameter, defined per `RateLimits` contract, bounds how far a cBEAM may raise a rate limit's `maxAmount` or `slope` in a single adjustment: the new value cannot exceed the higher of the current value multiplied by `maxChange`, or that rate limit's own registered default.

`maxChange` itself can only be set to zero or to `WAD` (`10**18`, a multiplier of one (1)) or more; it cannot be set to a fractional multiplier below one (1).

Changes to the `maxChange` parameter are proposed by the Core Council Multisig, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), or made directly via an Executive Vote at any time, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4 - PAS](989171ed-5424-42ee-83f4-199e1149699c).
assessments.description: Caps how far a cBEAM may raise a rate limit's maxAmount or slope per adjustment, and restricts who may change maxChange.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The adjustment bound is an explicit formula (new value ≤ max(current × maxChange, default)) and maxChange has a numeric floor of zero or WAD (10**18). The registered default is referenced but its value is defined elsewhere, and the rule sets no cadence for adjustments.
metrics: maxChange must be 0 or at least WAD (10**18, a multiplier of 1)
new maxAmount/slope ≤ max(current value × maxChange, registered default)
adjustment bound applies per single adjustment
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter (a578830d) governs the RateLimits contracts that hold maxAmount and slope, so out-of-bound adjustments are reverted on-chain. Liquidity Layer Role Definitions (2ae4b91a) restrict who can call the setter, reaching the proposer and executive-vote restriction.

assessments.title: Locked Unlimited Rate Limit Definition
assessments.quote:
A rate limit is locked as unlimited, and a cBEAM must keep it at a `maxAmount` equal to the maximum uint256 value with a zero slope, in either of two (2) cases:

- It has a default of that same value.
- It already holds that value on the `RateLimits` contract and has no default at all. A rate limit that is already unlimited is locked the same way whether or not it was ever registered.

Registering a default other than the unlimited value removes that lock.
assessments.description: Locks a rate limit at unlimited (max uint256 maxAmount, zero slope) when its default is that value or it already holds that value with no default.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives exact values (maxAmount equal to the maximum uint256, slope zero) and two explicit trigger cases, so compliance is checkable. It falls short of a 5 because the actor 'cBEAM' is not defined in the text and no check cadence or verification step is stated.

applies when RateLimits contract already holds unlimited value and no default is registered

Role-gated access (Liquidity Layer roles) restricts who can change limits, but the rule does not prevent a permitted cBEAM from lowering the value, so the consequence depends on artifact review, which is unquantified here.

assessments.title: Core Council Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Core Council Multisig (`coreCouncil`) can call any of BeamState's immediate functions directly, without a Spell, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.4 - Immediate Function Calls](2c82cfd0-7a9a-464f-844d-ebc43b31c2a6), including halting Configurator operations as an emergency action. Sky Governance can independently halt Configurator operations or pause the Timelock through the PASMom contract, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71) and [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.6 - PASMom](88e11076-5fe1-42a5-b2ba-bdb1bc929ec8).

The Core Council Multisig proposes and can cancel changes to BeamState's delayed registries and bounds on the Timelock, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3 - Delayed Function Calls](4a388764-7469-4efb-84f0-6b91278428fb). The Core Council Multisig also proposes restarting Configurator operations, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.5 - Restart After Halt](e049feea-5af3-4a8d-8766-36e348fd5d7b). Once the minimum delay has passed, any address may execute the proposed change, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.2 - Timelock](a824d088-be58-4163-b382-54a95a728103); proposing, canceling, and executing are all blocked while the Timelock is paused.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actors (coreCouncil, Sky Governance, PASMom, Timelock) and enumerates specific powers such as immediate calls, proposing and canceling delayed changes, and restarting Configurator operations. The key magnitude, the minimum delay before execution, is delegated to the Timelock doc and no numeric value is given.

Immediate calls by coreCouncil are not delayed, and the PASMom pause path is a governance power rather than a penalty, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Timelock
assessments.quote:
The Timelock gates delayed changes to BeamState's registries and bounds: the Core Council Multisig proposes and can cancel a change, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), and once the minimum delay has passed, any address may execute it, since the Timelock's `EXECUTOR_ROLE` is granted to `address(0)`, making execution permissionless. Proposing, canceling, and executing are all blocked while the Timelock is paused; only unpausing restores them. The minimum delay is fourteen (14) days.

The Timelock's `PROPOSER_ROLE` and `CANCELLER_ROLE` are held by the Core Council Multisig. Its `PAUSER_ROLE`, which can pause the Timelock, is held by PASMom, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.6 - PASMom](88e11076-5fe1-42a5-b2ba-bdb1bc929ec8). The Timelock's `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which can grant and revoke its other roles and change its minimum delay, is held by the Sky Pause Proxy. Its address is specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.3.1.8 - Timelock](f6791cf7-f3aa-49da-9691-73e480bf3328).
assessments.description: Governs the Timelock's delay, proposer, canceller, executor, pauser and admin roles over BeamState registry and bounds changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a 14-day minimum delay, with named role holders and specified addresses for each role. The gap is that the delay is a minimum the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can change, and the pause and unpause conditions are described without measurable criteria.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Timelock contract itself (cited in the text as f6791cf7) enforces the 14-day delay on-chain, so changes cannot execute early, and role-gated calls revert for addresses lacking PROPOSER, CANCELLER, PAUSER or EXECUTOR roles, as in the Liquidity Layer role model (2ae4b91a). This is contract-enforced with no human in the loop.

assessments.title: Restart After Halt
assessments.quote:
Restarting Configurator operations after a halt is done via BeamState's `start()` function, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.8 - Start Function Call](032164e4-cf66-4e79-bb8c-18f095a1cdef). `start()` is proposed by the Core Council Multisig, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), and takes effect only after a minimum delay has passed since being proposed. While the Timelock is paused, `start()` cannot take effect this way; restarting instead requires an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.5 - Transitional Measures](d5240aa5-72c1-4f92-b22c-7a80a35d733c).

Unpausing the Timelock does not route through this minimum delay, since it is gated by the Timelock's own access control rather than BeamState's role system. This holds regardless of how the Timelock came to be paused, and requires an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll — the same process specified for reversing PASMom's `pause()` in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71).
assessments.description: Governs how Configurator operations restart after a halt, via BeamState start() with a minimum delay, or an Executive Vote when the Timelock is paused.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors (Core Council Multisig, Executive Vote) and steps are concrete, but the minimum delay is referenced without any value. The Timelock unpause path and the PASMom reversal are defined by process reference rather than stated magnitudes.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Liquidity Layer Role Definitions access control reverts calls from addresses lacking the required role, so only the designated proposer can invoke start() and the Timelock's own access control gates unpausing. The minimum delay is also a contract-enforced timelock, but its magnitude is unstated.

assessments.title: Operator Execution
assessments.quote:
An Operator exercises a rate limit adjustment by calling the Configurator directly. A rate limit locked as unlimited, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.1.3 - Locked Unlimited Rate Limit Definition](92a74fe1-3115-4cd7-bbf8-4e16fb4b0aa8), cannot be raised or lowered. Otherwise, an Operator may lower a rate limit's `maxAmount` or `slope` to any value, including to zero, at any time. It may raise either value up to the bound set by [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.1.2.1 - Max Change Definition](942d6607-b92c-4779-8012-ea3b259ebf2b), and only after the interval set by [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.1.1.1 - Hop Definition](dc0e3a84-b542-4985-a41b-7ae2a3921cf3) has passed since its last raise to that rate limit.

An Operator exercises a controller action by calling the Configurator to execute an enabled action on its paired Controller.

Both are unaffected by whether the Timelock is paused, but are blocked while Configurator operations are halted, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.4.10 - Stop Function Call](52895c20-8322-4cbf-800f-8ea107f00f85).

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The lowering rule is fully stated (any value, including zero, at any time) and the raise rule is a clear formula gated by two cross-referenced definitions. However, the Max Change bound and Hop interval values are defined elsewhere and not stated in this paragraph, and no measurement cadence is given.

assessments.title: Transitional Measures
assessments.quote:
The PAS launches with the Timelock paused, as a transitional measure, via the August 27, 2026 Executive Vote. This means that, while the Timelock is paused, the functions described below, which the Core Council Multisig otherwise proposes through the Timelock, cannot take effect. Any updates instead require an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll:

- `setHop()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.1 - Set Hop Function Call](8ead8771-c769-48d0-af2a-802099c61d42).
- `setMaxChange()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.2 - Set Max Change Function Call](da93e0a7-5fa1-4d93-af72-24557fbd9f24).
- `addRateLimits()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.3 - Add Rate Limits Function Call](87da775d-430e-4db9-b58e-bbcf323e375a).
- `addController()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.4 - Add Controller Function Call](2ef770b2-3636-4545-9aad-0f7cf94c0619).
- `addInitRateLimits()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.5 - Add Init Rate Limits Function Call](bbdf1e6a-821b-43ec-aabf-e43a3bd6e113).
- `addInitControllerActions()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.6 - Add Init Controller Actions Function Call](010a904e-e0e0-4c1d-8460-b8e3118b680f).
- `addCBeam()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.7 - Add cBEAM Function Call](33d6773e-d3d8-4141-943b-bfac186574b1).
- `start()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.3.8 - Start Function Call](032164e4-cf66-4e79-bb8c-18f095a1cdef).

The Core Council Multisig also cannot cancel an already-proposed delayed change while the Timelock is paused; only unpausing it, via an Executive Vote, restores that ability.

The Core Council Multisig's immediate functions, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.4 - Immediate Function Calls](2c82cfd0-7a9a-464f-844d-ebc43b31c2a6), are unaffected by the Timelock being paused, since they do not route through it.

assessments.title: Timelock
assessments.quote:
The Timelock's mechanism is as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.2 - Timelock](a824d088-be58-4163-b382-54a95a728103). The minimum delay is fourteen (14) days. Its address is specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.3.2.7 - Timelock](c0642bfe-493c-489d-9f9f-9171dbb99d99).

The Timelock's `PROPOSER_ROLE` and `CANCELLER_ROLE` are held by the Core Council Multisig. Arbitrum has no PASMom equivalent, so no address holds the Timelock's `PAUSER_ROLE`; Sky Governance's emergency halt instead relies on the Core Council Multisig calling BeamState's `stop()` directly, as an immediate action, or, if the Core Council Multisig is itself unavailable, a Sky Core Spell relayed to Arbitrum. The Timelock's `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which can grant and revoke its other roles and change its minimum delay, is held by Sky Governance through the Governance Relay (`0x10E6593CDda8c58a1d0f14C5164B376352a55f2F`). If the Core Council Multisig itself is compromised or acting maliciously, Sky Governance can use this `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` to grant itself the Timelock's `PAUSER_ROLE` and pause it directly, via a Sky Core Spell relayed to Arbitrum.

assessments.title: Timelock
assessments.quote:
The Timelock's mechanism is as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3.2 - Timelock](a824d088-be58-4163-b382-54a95a728103). The minimum delay is fourteen (14) days. The Timelock launches paused, as a transitional measure, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.5 - Transitional Measures](9f398df8-0484-4c16-8cb9-8d7b04a8b531). Its address is specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.3.3.7 - Timelock](72b0384e-0151-44f8-bd0f-c5d90d0fb037).

The Timelock's `PROPOSER_ROLE` and `CANCELLER_ROLE` are held by the Core Council Multisig. Base has no PASMom equivalent, so no address holds the Timelock's `PAUSER_ROLE`; Sky Governance's emergency halt instead relies on the Core Council Multisig calling BeamState's `stop()` directly, as an immediate action, or, if the Core Council Multisig is itself unavailable, a Sky Core Spell relayed to Base. The Timelock's `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which can grant and revoke its other roles and change its minimum delay, is held by Sky Governance through the Governance Relay (`0xdD0BCc201C9E47c6F6eE68E4dB05b652Bb6aC255`). If the Core Council Multisig itself is compromised or acting maliciously, Sky Governance can use this `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` to grant itself the Timelock's `PAUSER_ROLE` and pause it directly, via a Sky Core Spell relayed to Base.

To open a new position, it calls the Uniswap v3 position manager's `mint` function. To add to an existing position, it calls the position manager's `increaseLiquidity` function instead — but only after confirming the ALM Proxy is the current owner of that position. Depositing into a tick range does not necessarily use the full target amount of both tokens; the Uniswap v3 Facet measures the amounts actually deposited by comparing the ALM Proxy's token balances before and after the call, rather than relying on the target amounts or the position manager's own return values. Before depositing, the Uniswap v3 Facet checks the specified minimums against expected amounts derived from the pool's time-weighted average price, not its current spot price. assessments.title: Swap Tokens Through Uniswap v3 Pool
assessments.quote: The Uniswap v3 Facet's `swap` function attempts to sell the specified amount of the given token through the Uniswap v3 router for the pool's other token. The execution price is bounded against the pool's time-weighted average price by the specified maximum tick deviation. If the swap reaches this price limit before selling the full specified amount, execution stops without reverting, and part of the specified amount goes unsold. The Uniswap v3 Facet measures the amount actually sold by comparing the ALM Proxy's balance of the given token before and after the swap, and applies the Rate Limit against that measured amount rather than the specified amount. The swap does not complete unless the specified tick deviation falls within the configured maximum for the pool and the amount received is at least the specified minimum, which must be a non-zero value. The maximum tick deviation is the only governance-configured control on the swap's execution quality; the minimum amount received has no equivalent governance floor beyond being non-zero.
assessments.description: Describes Uniswap v3 Facet swaps: tick-deviation bounds, a non-zero minimum received, and Rate Limit application on the measured sold amount.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete controls (maximum tick deviation, non-zero minimum received, balance-diff measurement against the Rate Limit), but the tick-deviation maximum is only 'the configured maximum for the pool' with no value given. The minimum has no stated magnitude beyond being non-zero.
metrics: Specified tick deviation must fall within the configured maximum for the pool
Amount received must be at least the specified minimum, which must be non-zero

The tick-deviation and minimum-received checks have no cited contract-enforced mechanism in the text, so they are not counted here.

The Controller dispatches the call to the ERC-4626 Facet, which performs the deposit on behalf of the ALM Proxy.

A vault for which no rate limit is configured cannot be deposited into, so the rate limit configuration also determines which vaults are available to the Diamond PAU.

assessments.title: Record Maximum Exchange Rate For ERC-4626 Vault
assessments.quote: The ERC-4626 Facet's `setMaxExchangeRate` function records the maximum exchange rate for the specified vault. The rate is computed as `1e36 * assets / shares`, where `assets` is the maximum amount of the underlying asset those shares may represent and `shares` is the given number of vault shares, and is recorded at `1e36` precision. A deposit into that vault does not complete unless the vault's exchange rate is within this maximum, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.6.1.3 - Deposit Asset Into ERC-4626 Vault](24b65a81-c816-480d-ad05-6161d9f01613). Withdrawals and redemptions are not bounded by this maximum.
assessments.description: Defines how the ERC-4626 vault maximum exchange rate is computed and recorded, and gates deposits against it while leaving withdrawals unbounded.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives an exact formula (1e36 * assets / shares), a fixed recording precision of 1e36, and a binary deposit gate that a third party could check from the text. Withdrawals and redemptions are explicitly excluded from the bound.

assessments.title: Remove Compromised Actor As Freezer
assessments.quote: In the event of a compromised or malicious Actor, the Freezer Multisig — registered as a Revoker on the AdministeredAgent, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.2.5 - Revoker](cc7cb4b7-981e-44f5-a0d5-62e5b47d112e) — removes that Actor by calling `removeActor` on the AdministeredAgent contract. Removing the Actor prevents it from submitting further operations, while the Allocator Role itself remains with the AdministeredAgent. This action should only be taken if a Relayer Multisig's keys have been leaked or compromised and the Actor is in the control of an external bad actor.

assessments.title: Withdraw All Positions From Aave v3 Facet
assessments.quote: In the event that liquidity must be recovered from an Aave v3 market and centralized in the associated ALM Proxy, a Relayer Multisig, acting as an Actor, withdraws the Liquidity Layer's full position in that market through the Aave v3 Facet, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.2 - Withdraw From Aave v3 Market](038eaa5c-d4c0-4a56-8d30-bc3a04508f0e). If the recovered asset is USDC rather than USDS, it is swapped to USDS through the PSM Facet, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.4.2 - Swap USDC To USDS](3fd327ea-7043-434a-996a-3419e7692959). The recovered USDS is then repaid and burned through the USDS Facet, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.1.2 - Burn USDS](f01e63b7-dde7-422a-89a1-6931839d49f5).
assessments.description: Specifies the Relayer Multisig steps to withdraw all Aave v3 liquidity, swap recovered USDC to USDS, and burn the USDS.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Relayer Multisig's calls through the Aave v3 Facet are gated by Diamond PAU role-based access control, which reverts calls from addresses lacking the required role. The paragraph does not state an explicit role-exclusivity clause, so this is mid rather than strong, and nothing quantifies a penalty for a misexecuted withdrawal.
