assessments.description: Requires a Relayer Multisig to withdraw all Basin positions to the ALM Proxy, then swap or burn the recovered USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Relayer Multisig) and gives an ordered sequence of facet calls with conditional branching for USDC versus USDS. The trigger, 'must be recovered', is qualitative and has no threshold, deadline, or cadence, and 'full position' is not numerically stated.
metrics: Withdraw the Liquidity Layer's full position from the Basin
Swap recovered USDC to USDS via PSM Facet if the recovered asset is USDC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Relayer Multisig is the designated caller of the Basin Facet withdrawal, and the Liquidity Layer Role Definitions revert calls from addresses lacking the required role, so the actor assignment is contract-gated. The paragraph does not state an explicit 'only' role requirement or a withdrawal maximum, so the Rate Limiter does not clearly reach it, and enforcement stays at mid.

assessments.title: Withdraw All Positions From Uniswap v3 Facet
assessments.quote: In the event that liquidity must be recovered from a Uniswap v3 pool and centralized in the associated ALM Proxy, a Relayer Multisig, acting as an Actor, removes the Liquidity Layer's full liquidity from each open position in that pool through the Uniswap v3 Facet, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.2.3 - Remove Liquidity From Uniswap v3 Position](315b3614-18bb-4ca0-b1c7-3459fd449ad8). If a recovered asset is USDC, it is swapped to USDS through the PSM Facet, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.4.2 - Swap USDC To USDS](3fd327ea-7043-434a-996a-3419e7692959), and then repaid and burned through the USDS Facet, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.1.2 - Burn USDS](f01e63b7-dde7-422a-89a1-6931839d49f5). Consolidating a recovered asset that is neither USDC nor USDS will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Requires a Relayer Multisig to remove all Uniswap v3 liquidity, then swap USDC to USDS and burn it; other assets are deferred.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Relayer Multisig) and enumerates concrete steps through specific facets, with a "full liquidity" magnitude. It gives no deadline or cadence, the recovery trigger ("must be recovered") is qualitative, and handling of non-USDC/USDS assets is explicitly deferred.
metrics: Removes the Liquidity Layer's full liquidity from each open position in the pool
Recovered USDC is swapped to USDS through the PSM Facet, then burned through the USDS Facet
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Liquidity Layer Role Definitions gate the Diamond PAU's functions, so a removal call from an address lacking the relayer role reverts on-chain. The paragraph does not explicitly state an exclusive role requirement, and no rate limit or penalty is stated for this specific removal, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Role Configuration
assessments.quote:
Morpho vaults must use the following role configuration:

- The Owner role must be held by the relevant Prime Agent's SubProxy or, on another blockchain, by its governance Executor acting on instructions relayed from that SubProxy.
- The Curator role must be held by a Multisig jointly controlled by the Operational Executor Agent and either the relevant Prime Agent or an external curator. The Multisig must require a 2 of 2 signer approval threshold.
- The Allocator role may be held by an externally owned account or Multisig controlled by the relevant Prime Agent or an external curator, or by the Morpho Public Allocator contract. Where the Morpho Public Allocator contract holds the Allocator role, any emergency action that withdraws vault assets from a market must also set the Public Allocator's caps for that market to zero, so that the Public Allocator cannot reallocate assets back into that market.
- The Sentinel role must be held by at least one (1) address controlled by the Operational Executor Agent, using a signer set separate from the signer set controlling the Curator role. Additional Sentinel addresses may be designated. These additional Sentinel addresses are recommended but not required, and no restriction applies to who may control them. Any automated monitoring solution serving as a Sentinel must be capable of automatically revoking pending actions when it detects a threat.
assessments.description: Specifies required role holders and signer thresholds for Morpho vaults, including Owner, Curator, Allocator and Sentinel roles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Curator 2-of-2 threshold and the requirement of at least one Sentinel address are concrete and checkable, and the Allocator cap-zeroing action is specific. Gaps remain: "capable of automatically revoking pending actions" and "detects a threat" have no defined criteria, and the separate-signer-set requirement has no verifiable test.
metrics: Curator Multisig signer approval threshold: 2 of 2
Sentinel role held by at least one (1) address controlled by the Operational Executor Agent
Public Allocator caps for the market set to zero after an emergency withdrawal from that market
Sentinel signer set separate from Curator signer set
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Role holders and signer thresholds are set off-chain in the Safe and vault configuration, so a mismatch with the stated 2-of-2 or separate-signer requirement is caught only by Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7). Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could reach the emergency-withdrawal cap-zeroing duty, but no consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Permissioned Role Records
assessments.quote:
For each Morpho vault used by a Prime Agent, the relevant Instance Configuration Document must specify each permissioned role, the entity or entities holding that role, and each corresponding on-chain address. Where a role has multiple holders, each holder must be recorded separately. Where a role is held by a permissionless contract without a controlling entity, the record must identify that contract and its address.

Where the Curator role is held by a Multisig jointly controlled by multiple entities, the record must distinguish the address of the Curator Multisig from the co-curator address controlled by each participating entity. The co-curator address may be an externally owned account or a Multisig. Individual signers of an entity's Multisig are not required to be listed.

An approved change to a role holder or address that has not yet been implemented must be distinguished from the current configuration, with its condition for taking effect specified.
assessments.description: Requires Instance Configuration Documents for Morpho vaults used by Primes to list permissioned roles, holders, and addresses.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states concrete record-content requirements: each role, each holder recorded separately, the Curator Multisig distinguished from each co-curator address, and pending changes flagged with their activation condition. It lacks a update cadence, a deadline, and a definition of 'approved change', so the core obligation is verifiable but not fully bounded.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check the Instance Configuration Document against on-chain role holders, issue staged findings, and assess penalties, with enforcer distinct from the Prime. The penalty is unquantified for this documentation rule, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Eligible Loan Assets
assessments.quote:
USDC, USDT, and pyUSD, as defined in [A.3.3.2.1.3 - Cash Stablecoins](066a4d9f-13ed-4ac3-a55a-df7bf3429649), are eligible loan assets. RLUSD and USDG are also eligible loan assets.

Any other loan asset must undergo a risk review before it may be used.
assessments.description: Lists USDC, USDT, pyUSD, RLUSD and USDG as eligible loan assets and requires risk review before any other loan asset is used.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The eligible asset list is concrete and cross-referenced to a defined category, but the gate for any other asset is only 'undergo a risk review', with no reviewer, criteria, threshold, or deadline. Compliance for non-listed assets cannot be verified from the text alone.
metrics: Eligible loan assets: USDC, USDT, pyUSD (per A.3.3.2.1.3 Cash Stablecoins), RLUSD, USDG
Any other loan asset must undergo a risk review before use
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could check that deployed loan-asset configuration matches the approved list, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could apply to Primes or Operational Agents who allocate into unapproved assets. Neither is quantified for this rule and no on-chain gate is stated in the text, so the rating is mid, not strong.

assessments.title: Eligible Collateral And Liquidation Loan-To-Value Limits
assessments.quote:
The eligible collateral assets and maximum liquidation loan-to-value limits are:

| Collateral Asset | Maximum Liquidation Loan-To-Value |
| --- | --- |
| ETH | 86% |
| cbBTC | 86% |
| stETH | 86% |
| WBTC | 86% |
| sUSDS | 96.5% |

Lower liquidation loan-to-value tiers are permitted and may result in a lower Instance Financial CRR. The Instance Financial CRR for cbBTC, WBTC, and stETH markets using an 86% liquidation loan-to-value limit must account for any difference between that limit and the limit produced by the applicable risk model. Any collateral asset not listed herein requires due diligence and approval by the [A.0.1.1.46 - Core Council](5a03a0c4-a47a-409c-9b23-52ac93e63d45) before adoption.
assessments.description: Sets maximum liquidation loan-to-value limits for five listed collateral assets and requires Core Council approval for any other collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a table gives an exact maximum liquidation LTV for ETH, cbBTC, stETH, WBTC (86%) and sUSDS (96.5%). Gaps remain: lower LTV tiers are permitted with no stated values, and the method for accounting for the difference from the risk-model limit is undefined.
metrics: ETH maximum liquidation LTV 86%
cbBTC maximum liquidation LTV 86%
stETH maximum liquidation LTV 86%
WBTC maximum liquidation LTV 86%
sUSDS maximum liquidation LTV 96.5%
Lower liquidation LTV tiers permitted (no value stated)
Unlisted collateral requires due diligence and Core Council approval before adoption
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Instance Financial CRR accounting requirement is a risk-capital rule, so the Penalty Mechanisms plausibly reach a Prime that breaches it. No consequence is quantified for this paragraph, and the Liquidation Penalty does not clearly reach these allocation markets, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Multi-Source Oracle Methodology
assessments.quote: Oracle-based market pricing must use Chainlink, RedStone, and Chronicle oracle feeds as its sources. When all three (3) sources are available and valid, the median of those sources must be used. If only two (2) valid sources are available, the average of those sources must be used. If only one (1) valid source is available, a credible fallback source must be used.
assessments.description: Requires oracle-based market pricing to use Chainlink, RedStone, and Chronicle feeds, aggregated by median or average depending on how many are valid.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The source set is named and the three-, two-, and one-source aggregation rules are concrete. However, "valid" is undefined (no staleness, deviation, or heartbeat threshold), and the one-source case delegates to an unspecified "credible fallback source", and zero sources is not addressed.
metrics: Three oracle sources: Chainlink, RedStone, Chronicle
Median used when 3 sources are available and valid
Average used when exactly 2 sources are available and valid
Fallback source used when only 1 source is valid
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No on-chain mechanism enforces oracle source selection for allocation pricing, and the Rate Limiter and Liquidation Penalty do not reach this rule. Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps could catch a deviation in the aggregation logic or source configuration, with staged findings and penalty assessment, but no consequence is quantified for this rule and firing depends on review.

assessments.title: Temporary Single-Source Oracle Exception
assessments.quote: Single-source Chainlink oracle feeds may be used temporarily for a major collateral asset. Such a configuration should migrate toward the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.1 - Multi-Source Oracle Methodology](191fbabc-d4e1-4ec4-9ea8-35b80eb809b0), following the structure used by SparkLend and on a schedule coordinated with the affected Prime Agent to avoid unnecessary operational disruption.
assessments.description: Permits temporary single-source Chainlink oracle feeds for major collateral and directs migration to multi-source oracles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph permits a single-source oracle for a 'major collateral asset' and says it 'should migrate' to multi-source on a schedule 'coordinated with the affected Prime Agent.' No duration, deadline, asset criteria, or migration cadence is stated, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph sets no threshold that a contract or named enforcer checks, and the migration duty is a soft 'should.' Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Eligible Collateral Oracle Methodologies
assessments.quote:
The following pricing methods apply to eligible collateral assets and must comply with the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.1 - Multi-Source Oracle Methodology](191fbabc-d4e1-4ec4-9ea8-35b80eb809b0) for any price taken from oracle feeds:

- ETH: the ETH price from oracle feeds.
- cbBTC: the BTC price from oracle feeds.
- stETH: the wstETH-to-ETH contract exchange rate multiplied by the ETH price from oracle feeds.
- WBTC: the WBTC price from oracle feeds.
- sUSDS: the sUSDS-to-USDS contract exchange rate multiplied by the USDS price from oracle feeds.

Where a method combines a contract exchange rate with a price from oracle feeds, as for stETH and sUSDS, the combination is computed within the Morpho oracle contract, which must meet [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.4 - Morpho Oracle Contract Requirements](8394d47c-af13-4d20-af8e-6441b944c895).
assessments.description: Specifies pricing formulas for eligible collateral assets (ETH, cbBTC, stETH, WBTC, sUSDS) and requires Morpho oracle combination logic to meet referenced requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each eligible asset has an explicit pricing formula, including the stETH and sUSDS contract-rate-times-oracle-price combinations. Gaps remain: the oracle feeds are not identified, no staleness or deviation thresholds or update cadence are stated, and the multi-source and Morpho contract requirements are defined elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could review the Morpho oracle artifacts that implement these pricing methods, with penalty assessment. Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach Allocation Risk violations. Neither is quantified for this specific pricing rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the formulas, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: New Collateral Oracle Approval
assessments.quote: The oracle methodology for any new collateral asset requires due diligence and approval by the [A.0.1.1.46 - Core Council](5a03a0c4-a47a-409c-9b23-52ac93e63d45) before adoption.
assessments.description: Requires Core Council due diligence and approval before a new collateral asset's oracle methodology is adopted.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named approver (Core Council) and a gating sequence (approval before adoption) are stated, but 'due diligence' has no criteria, scope, or timeline. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Core Council approval must precede adoption of a new collateral asset's oracle methodology
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a missing Core Council approval for oracle adoption. Artifact review and role-gated access do not cover this gate, so only the misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Morpho Oracle Contract Requirements
assessments.quote: A Morpho oracle contract is the contract attached to a Morpho market that reads one or more oracle feeds and provides the resulting price to the market. It is distinct from the oracle feeds it reads. A Morpho oracle contract may implement custom logic, provided that it has been audited.
assessments.description: Defines a Morpho oracle contract and permits custom oracle logic only if the contract has been audited.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The only operative requirement is that custom logic must be 'audited', with no auditor standard, scope, depth, timing, or verification method stated. The rest is definitional, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps could plausibly check whether deployed Morpho oracle contracts with custom logic have an audit, with staged findings and penalty assessment. No consequence is quantified for this specific audit condition, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Interest Rate Requirements
assessments.quote: Morpho Blue variable-rate markets must use the Morpho Adaptive Curve Interest Rate Model (https://docs.morpho.org/developers/contracts/irm/#adaptivecurveirm). Morpho Midnight fixed-rate markets use market-set rates rather than an interest rate model. A maker posts an offer at a price in a fixed-maturity market, and the implied fixed rate for the remaining term is locked when a taker executes the offer.
assessments.description: Requires Morpho Blue variable-rate markets to use the Adaptive Curve IRM; describes Morpho Midnight fixed-rate market pricing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Morpho Blue requirement names a specific, verifiable interest rate model (Adaptive Curve IRM) and can be checked against a market's IRM setting. The Midnight sentence is descriptive, not a constraint, and no rate bounds or parameter values are stated for either market type.
metrics: Variable-rate Morpho Blue markets must use the Morpho Adaptive Curve Interest Rate Model
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can check which IRM each market uses and assess penalties, and the Penalty Mechanisms can apply to Primes and Operational Agents for breaches. Neither consequence is quantified for this rule, and no on-chain mechanism reaches the IRM choice; the Liquidation Penalty does not apply to off-chain Morpho markets.

assessments.title: Vault Timelock Requirements
assessments.quote:
Morpho vaults must use at least the following timelock delays for protected functions:

| Action | Minimum Timelock Delay |
| --- | --- |
| Abdicate | seven (7) days |
| Add adapter | seven (7) days |
| Increase absolute cap | seven (7) days |
| Increase relative cap | seven (7) days |
| Increase timelock duration | seven (7) days |
| Remove adapter | seven (7) days |
| Set adapter registry | seven (7) days |
| Set management fee | three (3) days |
| Set management fee recipient | three (3) days |
| Set performance fee | three (3) days |
| Set performance fee recipient | three (3) days |
| Set receive assets gate | seven (7) days |
| Set receive shares gate | seven (7) days |
| Set send assets gate | seven (7) days |
| Set send shares gate | seven (7) days |

The following functions must not be subject to a timelock delay:

- Adding or removing an allocator, so that a compromised allocator can be removed immediately.
- Setting the force deallocate penalty, so that a penalty can be introduced immediately in response to a griefing attack.

Decreases to absolute or relative caps may be executed without delay. A decrease to a function's timelock duration is subject to that function's then-current timelock delay. For the Set adapter registry, Set receive assets gate, Set receive shares gate, and Set send shares gate functions, permanently abdicating the function is accepted in place of the timelock delay.
assessments.description: Sets minimum timelock delays (3 or 7 days) for protected Morpho vault functions and lists functions exempt from timelocks.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each protected action has an explicit numeric minimum delay in a table, and the exemptions and abdication alternative are stated as concrete conditions. A third party could check compliance directly against the vault's configured timelocks.
metrics: Abdicate: minimum 7 days
Add adapter: minimum 7 days
Increase absolute cap: minimum 7 days
Increase relative cap: minimum 7 days
Increase timelock duration: minimum 7 days
Remove adapter: minimum 7 days
Set adapter registry: minimum 7 days
Set management fee: minimum 3 days
Set management fee recipient: minimum 3 days
Set performance fee: minimum 3 days
Set performance fee recipient: minimum 3 days
Set receive assets gate: minimum 7 days
Set receive shares gate: minimum 7 days
Set send assets gate: minimum 7 days
Set send shares gate: minimum 7 days
Adding or removing an allocator: no timelock
Setting force deallocate penalty: no timelock
Decreases to absolute or relative caps: no delay
Timelock duration decrease: subject to the function's then-current delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The timelock is a property of the Morpho vault contract, but no catalog mechanism covers it and its UUID does not appear in the text, so it cannot be cited. Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) can pre-authorize freezes or pauses when a vault's security configuration is violated, which plausibly reaches a vault configured with shorter delays, but no quantified consequence is attached to this rule.

assessments.title: Adapter Timelock Requirements
assessments.quote:
Adapters used by Morpho vaults must use at least the following timelock delays for protected adapter functions:

| Action | Minimum Timelock Delay |
| --- | --- |
| Abdicate | seven (7) days |
| Burn shares | three (3) days |
| Increase timelock | seven (7) days |
| Skim recipient | three (3) days |
assessments.description: Requires Morpho vault adapters to use minimum timelock delays of 3 to 7 days for abdicate, burn shares, increase timelock, and skim recipient.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each protected adapter function has an explicit minimum delay in days (7, 3, 7, 3), and the actor is named as adapters used by Morpho vaults. A third party can check the configured timelocks against the table directly.
metrics: Abdicate: minimum timelock delay of seven (7) days
Burn shares: minimum timelock delay of three (3) days
Increase timelock: minimum timelock delay of seven (7) days
Skim recipient: minimum timelock delay of three (3) days
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can catch adapters configured with timelocks below the table minimums, with staged findings and penalty assessment. The penalty magnitude is not quantified for this rule, and no on-chain mechanism in the atlas enforces these delays, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Eligible Chains
assessments.quote: Morpho vaults may initially be deployed on Ethereum Mainnet, Base, and Robinhood Chain. Deployment on any other chain requires a risk review.
assessments.description: Limits initial Morpho vault deployment to three named chains and requires a risk review for any other chain.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The three permitted chains are enumerated, a concrete parameter. The 'risk review' gate has no defined reviewer, criteria, scope, or deadline, and 'may initially' leaves the permitted set open-ended.
metrics: Permitted initial chains: Ethereum Mainnet, Base, Robinhood Chain
Deployment on any other chain requires a risk review
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Chain deployment is an off-chain allocation decision that the Rate Limiter and role-based access controls do not gate, and no named enforcer is tied to the required risk review.

assessments.title: Transition And Compliance
assessments.quote:
Notwithstanding the other requirements of the Morpho Vault Curation Framework, Morpho vault exposure existing as of August 17, 2026, must be migrated to new vaults or upgraded to comply with the framework no later than the execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote. Migration may be staged to account for underlying market utilization and existing vault configurations, but must be completed by that time.

Following that deadline, noncompliant Morpho vault allocations are subject to the Instance Financial CRR specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.3.8.2 - Noncompliant Morpho Vault Allocations](20aa9663-214b-46f5-8b37-53be387b996b).
assessments.description: Requires existing Morpho vault exposure to be migrated or upgraded to framework compliance by the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote, then subjects noncompliant allocations to a Financial CRR.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The deadlines (August 17, 2026 exposure cutoff; October 8, 2026 Executive Vote) are concrete, but the substantive compliance standard is delegated to the Morpho Vault Curation Framework and the consequence to the referenced CRR. Staging is permitted with no cadence or milestones.
metrics: Morpho vault exposure existing as of August 17, 2026 must be migrated or upgraded no later than execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote
Migration may be staged for underlying market utilization and existing vault configurations, but must be completed by the October 8, 2026 deadline
assessments.enforcementReasoning: After the deadline, noncompliant allocations fall under the referenced Instance Financial CRR (20aa9663), which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) would reach as a Risk Capital rule. Before the deadline, no specific consequence attaches to the migration duty, and the CRR's terms are not stated here, so it stops at mid.

assessments.title: Grove Exception
assessments.quote: For Grove's Morpho vault exposure, the deadline specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.5 - Transition And Compliance](41824fb1-a4e0-4f58-9095-0b3e646fb42c) is extended by three (3) days beyond the execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote, to account for daily rate limits on migrating that exposure to compliant vaults.
assessments.description: Extends the Transition And Compliance deadline for Grove's Morpho vault exposure by three days after the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The three-day extension and its anchor event (execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote) are concrete. However, the base deadline is defined only by cross-reference to another paragraph, and "compliant vaults" is undefined here, so the compliance target cannot be verified from this text alone.
metrics: Extension of three (3) days beyond execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter reverts migration operations above their daily limits, physically bounding the pace the extension is premised on. Artifact Review By Core GovOps can check whether migration met the extended deadline, but no consequence is quantified for this exception and escalation depends on someone initiating review.

assessments.title: Spark Exception
assessments.quote: For Spark's Morpho vault exposure, and only for compliance with [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3 - Timelock Requirements](1078548f-1086-49d2-bc01-f5727f088e41), the deadline specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.5 - Transition And Compliance](41824fb1-a4e0-4f58-9095-0b3e646fb42c) is extended by three (3) weeks beyond the execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote, to account for the timelock changes required on Spark's Morpho vaults. Until that extended deadline, an allocation to a Spark Morpho vault whose only noncompliance is with the Timelock Requirements is not subject to the Instance Financial CRR specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.3.8.2 - Noncompliant Morpho Vault Allocations](20aa9663-214b-46f5-8b37-53be387b996b).
assessments.description: Extends Spark's Morpho vault timelock compliance deadline by three weeks and exempts timelock-only noncompliant allocations from the Instance Financial CRR until then.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The three-week extension and the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote anchor are concrete, and the exemption scope is limited to timelock-only noncompliance. The base deadline lives in A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.5, and the vote's execution date is not fixed, so the exact extended deadline is not computable from this text alone.
metrics: Extension of three (3) weeks beyond execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote
Exemption applies until the extended deadline
Applies only where the sole noncompliance is with the Timelock Requirements
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Once the extended deadline passes, the Instance Financial CRR applies to these Spark Morpho allocations, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) would plausibly reach the resulting Risk Capital breach. No quantified penalty or escalation is stated for this specific extension, and nothing enforces the timelock change itself within the window, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Pull Request Approval Requirements
assessments.quote: All Prime Agent Liquidity Layer GitHub repositories require a minimum of two (2) approvals from accounts held by distinct individuals or entities before merging any Pull Request.
assessments.description: Requires two approvals from distinct individuals or entities before merging any pull request in Prime Agent Liquidity Layer repositories.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an exact approval count (two) and a distinctness condition on approvers, applied to a defined repository set and a defined event (merge). A third party could check GitHub merge records against it. The only soft spot is that 'distinct individuals or entities' is not operationalized, such as how shared accounts or affiliated entities are treated.
metrics: minimum of two (2) approvals
approvals from accounts held by distinct individuals or entities
applies before merging any Pull Request in Prime Agent Liquidity Layer GitHub repositories
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Liquidity Layer Role Definitions (2ae4b91a) and Rate Limiter (a578830d) are on-chain controls and do not reach GitHub merge approvals, and the penalty, conservatorship, and insurance-pricing mechanisms are tied to Risk Capital and Prime security rather than repository review practice. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls remain, which are weak on their own.

assessments.title: Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote: Each Liquidity Layer must include at least one (1) Freezer Multisig, holding the emergency authority to remove a compromised or malicious address authorized to submit allocation operations. Each Freezer Multisig must use the default configuration specified in the documents herein unless a deviation has been approved as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3 - Default Configuration Deviations](3b9336c2-53c8-4967-ab45-a2f8c5a36556).
assessments.description: Requires each Liquidity Layer to have a Freezer Multisig using default configuration unless deviation approved.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: at least one Freezer Multisig per Liquidity Layer, which a third party could verify by counting. The default configuration is deferred to other documents and the deviation approval process has no stated criteria, so the rule is not fully self-contained.
metrics: At least one (1) Freezer Multisig per Liquidity Layer
Default configuration unless a deviation is approved under A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can pre-authorize freezes when security rules are violated or threatened, which reaches the emergency-authority function. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) can catch a missing multisig or a configuration that deviates from the default, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule and escalation depends on the review being run.

assessments.title: Required Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The Freezer Multisig has a default 2/5 signing requirement. This default is below the baseline threshold specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98) and applies under the standing exemption for emergency-response Multisigs specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.2.1 - Emergency-Response Multisig Threshold Exception](55f1c795-0653-4dda-9f05-b3068d2608e3).
assessments.description: Sets the Freezer Multisig's default 2-of-5 signing requirement, stated as below a baseline threshold under an emergency-response exemption.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The default 2/5 signing threshold is a concrete, verifiable value. However, the baseline threshold and the exemption that makes 2/5 compliant are delegated to other documents whose values are not stated here, so the operative compliance criterion is not fully determinable from this text.
metrics: Freezer Multisig default signing requirement: 2 of 5 signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever signing threshold is actually configured, not the stated 2/5, so a mismatch is caught only through Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps, which has staged findings and penalty assessment. Nothing quantifies a specific consequence for this rule, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Required Signers
assessments.quote: The default signer composition is five (5) signers: four (4) controlled by the Operational Executor Agent, including at least one (1) controlled by Operational GovOps and at least one (1) controlled by the Operational Facilitator, and one (1) controlled by the Prime Agent.
assessments.description: Sets the default five-signer composition for allocation multisigs, split between Operational Executor, Operational GovOps, Operational Facilitator and Prime Agent.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The signer count (5) and the split (4 Executor-controlled, 1 Prime-controlled) are explicit, and minimums of one each are stated for GovOps and Facilitator. The term "default" leaves open when and how the composition may differ, and the two minimums do not fix the remaining signers' assignment.
metrics: Total signers: five (5)
Operational Executor Agent-controlled signers: four (4)
Operational GovOps-controlled signers: at least one (1)
Operational Facilitator-controlled signers: at least one (1)
Prime Agent-controlled signers: one (1)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever threshold and owner set is configured, not this stated composition, so a mismatch is caught only by Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps, a named enforcer with staged findings and penalty assessment. No on-chain mechanism or quantified penalty specific to signer composition is cited.

assessments.title: Default Configuration Deviations
assessments.quote: Deviations from the defaults specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.1 - Required Number Of Signers](040b5603-9c1c-4730-9e65-8be855db5f55) and [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.2 - Required Signers](4723757a-405c-4eca-9044-f8a1ed5f4120) require approval from the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps. Approved deviations are recorded as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3.1 - List Of Approved Deviations](5e7f23f6-4ff0-4a81-81f0-0b102b33dfbf).
assessments.description: Requires Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps approval for any deviation from default signer settings, with approved deviations recorded in a list.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the approving actors, the triggering condition (deviation from the linked default signer count and signer list), and a recording artifact. It gives no approval criteria, timeline, or measurable limit on how far a deviation may go, and the defaults themselves are only linked, not stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever signer configuration is actually set, so a deviation not matching the approved list is caught only through Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps, which has staged findings and penalty assessment. No automatic consequence or quantified penalty is attached to this specific rule.

assessments.title: List Of Approved Deviations
assessments.quote:
The list of approved deviations is defined as Active Data in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3.1.0.6.1 - Approved Deviations](c304cb9f-ab10-4d5b-8f94-588170b36a9e).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is Core GovOps.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for 'Direct Edit'.
- An entry may be added only for a deviation approved as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3 - Default Configuration Deviations](3b9336c2-53c8-4967-ab45-a2f8c5a36556).
assessments.description: Makes the approved-deviations list Active Data, updated only by Core GovOps via Direct Edit, with additions limited to approved default-configuration deviations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The responsible actor (Core GovOps) and update protocol (Direct Edit) are named, but the approval criteria for entries are delegated to another document with no stated thresholds, cadence, or deadlines. Compliance can be checked against the named actor and process, but not against a quantified standard.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The list is Active Data, not a contract-controlled rate limit or role-gated call, so no on-chain mechanism is cited. Core GovOps is both the responsible party and the only editor, so enforcement is self-policing; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Approved Deviations
assessments.quote:
The approved deviations are:

| **Liquidity Layer** | **Multisig Address** | **Approved Deviation** |
|---|---|---|
| Spark Liquidity Layer | `0x90D8c80C028B4C09C0d8dcAab9bbB057F0513431` | Two (2) of four (4) signing requirement, with signers controlled by Phoenix Labs and VoteWizard |
assessments.description: Approves a 2-of-4 signing requirement for the Spark Liquidity Layer multisig, with signers controlled by Phoenix Labs and VoteWizard.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact threshold (2 of 4), a specific multisig address, and named signer-controlling entities, which a third party could check against the Safe. It leaves the signer addresses unlisted and does not restate the baseline requirement being deviated from, so it falls short of a fully self-contained rule.
metrics: Two (2) of four (4) signing requirement
Multisig address 0x90D8c80C028B4C09C0d8dcAab9bbB057F0513431
Signers controlled by Phoenix Labs and VoteWizard
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe contract enforces whatever threshold is configured rather than this approved value, so a mismatch is caught only through Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which is a scheduled review with penalty assessment but is not a quantified consequence for this specific deviation.

assessments.title: Initial Concept And Feasibility Discussions
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent identifies a yield opportunity on a target chain that can exceed the Base Rate. The Prime Agent estimates Required Risk Capital (RRC) and Asset Liability Management requirements associated with the opportunity and evaluates options for fulfilling them. The Prime Agent also considers exchange and bridging costs, if applicable. Based on this, the Prime Agent develops a net yield target for the opportunity factoring in all of these costs. The output of this step is an internal meeting note summarizing the idea as well as estimates of Required Risk Capital, Asset Liability Management, and exchange / bridging costs.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to identify a yield opportunity above the Base Rate and document RRC, ALM, and cost estimates in a meeting note.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor, enumerated process steps, and a defined output (an internal meeting note), but sets no numeric thresholds or deadlines. Verbs such as 'identifies', 'estimates', 'evaluates', and 'considers' leave compliance arguable, and the 'net yield target' has no defined formula.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The step is a self-executed internal analysis with no contract or governance mechanism checking the estimates. Risk Capital enforcement attaches to later allocation decisions, not to this preliminary note.

assessments.title: Preliminary Required Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management Arrangement
assessments.quote: If necessary, the Prime Agent reaches out to other Prime Agents that could provide Junior Risk Capital (JRC) / Senior Risk Capital (SRC) or assume Asset Liability Management obligations. The Prime Agent negotiates with these other Prime Agents and documents these potential deals. The output of this step is an informal confirmation of JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management transfer details.
assessments.description: Directs a Prime Agent, when needed, to seek other Primes to provide risk capital or assume asset-liability obligations and document informal deal terms.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real process obligation exists (reach out, negotiate, document, produce informal confirmation), but it has no thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria; 'if necessary' and 'informal confirmation' leave compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The step is a process description with no quantified consequence; any violation would only surface through the generic misalignment or adjudication backstops, and the informal output is not itself enforced by any mechanism.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Preparation Of Capital And Operational Plan
assessments.quote:
The Capital and Operational Plan ("C&O Plan") articulates the Prime Agent’s strategy for a proposed new Allocation Instance or a modification to an existing Instance. In addition to articulating the Instance’s strategic objectives and operational parameters, the C&O Plan includes a pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate and a strategy for ensuring sufficient Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage.

The C&O Plan is the major input into the Artifact Edit Proposal that codifies the new or modified Instance. Following the approval of such a proposal by Prime governance, the details and commitments outlined in the C&O Plan are formally integrated into the respective Instance Configuration Document of the Prime Agent’s Artifact.
assessments.description: Requires Prime C&O Plans for new or changed Instances to include a pro-forma RRC estimate and a TRC coverage strategy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The plan must contain a pro-forma RRC estimate and a TRC coverage strategy, so the required components are named. No numeric coverage threshold, cadence, or deadline is stated, and 'sufficient' TRC coverage is undefined, so a defender could argue the plan is complete once any estimate is included.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Once the plan's commitments are integrated into the Instance Configuration Document, Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) can check them and assess penalties. The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a failure to maintain the TRC coverage the plan describes, but no consequence is quantified for this paragraph itself.

assessments.title: Pro-Forma Instance RRC Estimate
assessments.quote: As a critical component of the Capital & Operational Plan, the Prime Agent must prepare an initial pro-forma Instance Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate. This estimate serves as the basis for the Prime’s capital planning prior to the availability of official RRC figures from Sky Core. The estimate must strictly adhere to the implementation of RRC-models defined in [A.3.2 - Risk Capital](55999acf-75fe-4adf-8584-9746ef50d3e4).
assessments.description: Requires Primes to prepare an initial pro-forma Instance RRC estimate that follows the RRC models in A.3.2.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to prepare an estimate is concrete, but the paragraph gives no threshold, deadline, cadence, or content requirement. 'Strictly adhere' delegates the operative method to A.3.2, so a Prime could argue it complied by producing any estimate.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The RRC models are Risk Capital rules, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) quantify financial penalties that incentivize Primes to follow them. The paragraph itself sets no consequence, and the penalty amount is not specified for this estimate.

assessments.title: Notional Total Risk Capital (TRC) Coverage Strategy
assessments.quote:
As a critical component of the Capital & Operational Plan, the Prime Agent must articulate its strategy for ensuring its Total Risk Capital (TRC) adequately covers the pro-forma Instance RRC of a new or modified Instance and the resulting impact on its Aggregate RRC.

The Prime’s notional TRC coverage strategy must outline how this new Instance’s RRC will be notionally accounted for or supported by the Prime’s overall TRC pool. If the Prime’s current TRC is not sufficient to cover its estimated increased Aggregate RRC, the strategy should outline the Prime Agent’s intended steps for acquiring additional JRC/SRC.

For instance, this risk-capital acquisition strategy could involve:

1. Renting Junior Risk Capital (JRC)
    - Sourcing Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) by renting it from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords.
    - Sourcing Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) from external capital providers.
2. Sourcing Senior Risk Capital (SRC):
    - Originating SRC through the Sky monthly auction.
    - Renting OSRC from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords.
3. Increasing Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC): A Prime might have plans to bolster its own IJRC through retained earnings or other internal means.
4. Decreasing exposure in an existing Instance(s) to lower Aggregate RRC.

The Prime’s capital-acquisition strategy should indicate how the Prime will remain in compliance with all relevant Atlas rules, such as sourcing ratios that constrain how much Senior Risk Capital can be "enabled" or counted toward a Prime’s Aggregate RRC. See [A.3.2.1.2.3 - Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios](9e99b084-f15a-4f60-b831-d6c0bd9aec04).
assessments.description: Requires Primes to articulate a strategy for covering new or modified Instance RRC with Total Risk Capital, including acquiring JRC/SRC if needed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph imposes a real obligation to articulate a TRC coverage strategy, but it is framed in judgment language ("should outline", "could involve", "might have plans"). It states no coverage ratio, threshold, deadline, or measurement cadence, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Capital & Operational Plan is a reviewable artifact, so Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can assess the strategy, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) apply to Risk Capital rule breaches. No consequence is quantified for this planning obligation, and enforcement depends on review being triggered.

assessments.title: Additional Elements Of Capital And Operational Plan
assessments.quote:
The Capital & Operational Plan includes the following additional elements:

- Operational Parameters: defines the Instance’s target chain(s), protocols, initial capital, maximum deposit sizes, and any other parameters that underpin the pro-forma RRC calculation.
- Data Submission Protocol: defines how yields, Required Risk Capital usage, ALM costs, exchange data, etc. will be reported and audited.
- Emergency Procedures: defines mechanisms to be triggered if security or risk capital thresholds are breached, such as a kill switch or partial freeze.
- Asset Liability Management (ALM) Strategy: details if the Prime will meet its ALM requirements through its own direct asset management or by transferring its obligations to another Prime Agent via the ASC Rental Primitive. If the latter, the C&O Plan must reference the governing Ecosystem Accord and its key terms.
- Performance-based Adjustments: define the conditions or KPIs that allow adjustments to Instance deposit caps or yield expansions without requiring a formal Artifact edit.
assessments.description: Lists required contents of a Prime's Capital & Operational Plan: operational parameters, data reporting, emergency procedures, ALM strategy, and performance adjustments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each element is a required section, but the text only says what each must 'define' without thresholds, formulas, cadences, or deadlines. Terms such as 'any other parameters', 'etc.', and 'such as' leave the required content open, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review by a party distinct from the Prime that can assess whether the C&O Plan contains these elements, with penalty assessment. Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach Risk Capital-related omissions, but no consequence is quantified for this paragraph.

assessments.title: Preliminary Informal Check With Operational GovOps
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent presents the Capital and Operational Plan for the Allocation Instance to Operational GovOps, including any associated JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management arrangements. Operational GovOps reviews and either provides an informal greenlight or requests modifications to the Plan. The output of this step is Operational GovOps approval to proceed with a request to revise the C&O Plan, as applicable.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to present its Capital and Operational Plan to Operational GovOps for an informal greenlight or requested modifications.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Defines the actors (Prime Agent, Operational GovOps) and a process step with two outcomes, but sets no thresholds, criteria, or deadlines for the review. Whether a plan passes the informal check rests on GovOps' judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes an informal procedural gate with no consequence for skipping or failing it. Artifact review and penalty machinery do not clearly reach a pre-submission informal check, and the catch-all backstops alone are weak.

assessments.title: Agent Inputs
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent drafts an update to the Prime Agent Artifact adding the Allocation Instance to the list of active Allocation Instances and including the information specified in [A.2.2.10.1.2.6 - List Of Allocation Instances](e4975062-6d19-438b-a5d5-cfc1a7fd8cb9). The Prime Agent submits the draft to the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is a draft Prime Agent Artifact update in the Powerhouse system.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to draft and submit an Artifact update adding an Allocation Instance to Powerhouse.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor, a system (Powerhouse), and concrete ordered steps with a verifiable output (a draft artifact update). However, it gives no timing or completeness criteria, and the required content is delegated to the List Of Allocation Instances section.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps reviews Prime Agent Artifact contents and can assess penalties, so an omitted or incorrect allocation instance entry in the draft could be caught there. The consequence is not quantified for this step, and escalation depends on the review actually being run.

assessments.title: Validation And Off-Chain Vote
assessments.quote: The Operational Executor Facilitator reviews the proposal to ensure that it is complete and aligned with the Atlas. The Operational Executor Facilitator then initiates an off-chain snapshot vote, following the quorum and majority rules in the Prime Agent Artifact. When complete, the result of the vote is recorded in the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is the snapshot vote result recorded in the Powerhouse system.
assessments.description: Operational Executor Facilitator reviews allocation proposals, runs an off-chain snapshot vote, and records the result in Powerhouse.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the responsible actor and enumerates the process steps (review, initiate vote, record result). Completeness and Atlas alignment are judgment calls, and the quorum and majority thresholds are delegated to the Prime Agent Artifact with no values stated here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can check whether the vote followed the Prime Agent Artifact's quorum and majority rules, with staged findings and penalty assessment by an enforcer distinct from the facilitator. No quantified consequence attaches to this specific step, and firing depends on the review being scheduled and run.

assessments.title: Official Update of Artifact
assessments.quote:
If the Allocation Instance is successfully approved, the Operational Executor Facilitator finalizes and publishes the update to the Prime Agent Artifact, making it effective in the Atlas. The output of this step is an updated Prime Agent Artifact with the new Allocation Instance.

Once a new Instance is deployed, its data is integrated into risk-capital monitoring systems and its RRC will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard](4eac2c9e-2718-4881-a3f1-ed10fb3f4d13). This official RRC figure supersedes the Prime-prepared pro-forma RRC.
assessments.description: Requires publishing approved Allocation Instances to the Prime Agent Artifact and treating the dashboard RRC figure as superseding pro-forma RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Operational Executor Facilitator) and an output (updated Prime Agent Artifact), but has no thresholds, deadlines, or metrics. 'Integrated', 'officially determined', and 'tracked' are undefined, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can check whether the instance was approved and published and assess penalties for non-compliance. Penalty Mechanisms plausibly reach failure to track RRC as a risk-capital rule. Neither is quantified for this specific step, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Instance Setup Deployments
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define how the deployment of an Allocation Instance is executed on-chain. In the short-term, an Allocation Instance may also be deployed using the process for Interim Deployments specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.2 - Interim Deployments](9b3edbbf-89d1-42da-a9c3-18f858f8471f).

The Prime Agent must subsequently prepare a pro-forma Required Risk Capital estimate, which must be approved by the Core Council Risk Advisor, before the parameters of the Instance can be updated for normal operation.
assessments.description: Requires a Prime Agent to prepare a pro-forma Required Risk Capital estimate, approved by the Core Council Risk Advisor, before normal-operation parameter updates.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actors (Prime Agent, Core Council Risk Advisor) and a sequencing gate (approval before parameter update), but gives no threshold, deadline, or criteria for what the pro-forma estimate must contain. Deployment mechanics are delegated to other documents.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check whether the pro-forma estimate was prepared and approved before parameters changed, with a separate enforcer. The Penalty Mechanisms reach Prime Risk Capital rule violations, but no consequence is quantified for this specific sequencing requirement, so it is rated mid.

assessments.title: Conduit Development And Testing
assessments.quote: Once formally validated, the Prime Agent implements the new Allocation Instance based on the specifications in the Prime Agent Artifact. Operational GovOps must test the Allocation Instance with minimal funds from the Prime Agent’s Central Allocation Buffer, verifying deposit / withdrawal logic, slippage constraints, and oracle checks. If this testing is successful Operational GovOps confirms that the Allocation Instance satisfies all risk constraints specified in the Prime Agent Artifact. The output of this step is validated contracts for the Allocation Instance and a green light to proceed with a scaled deployment.
assessments.description: Requires Operational GovOps to test a new Allocation Instance with minimal funds and confirm it meets Prime Agent Artifact risk constraints before scaled deployment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates test areas (deposit/withdrawal logic, slippage, oracle checks) and names the actor, but gives no thresholds, slippage limits, oracle tolerances, or sample size. 'Minimal funds' and 'all risk constraints specified in the Prime Agent Artifact' are undefined here, so a defender could argue either compliance or non-binding.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a named enforcer distinct from the Prime Agent and can check whether the Allocation Instance matches the Artifact and passed testing. The consequence is unquantified for this rule, and no contract gate ties the green light to the testing result.

assessments.title: Initial Deployment and Required Risk Capital / Asset Liability Management Execution
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent finalizes JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management Arrangements. Operational GovOps records these arrangements in the Powerhouse interface. If Operational GovOps is charged with operationalizing an Instance, it deploys funds from the Prime Agent’s Operational Buffer into the Allocation Instance, performing any necessary DEX exchanges. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.1 - Operationalization Of Allocation Instances](989512c2-4fa1-46b8-947c-00e3c0b56024). In doing so, Operational GovOps follows instructions in the Agent Artifact regarding the amount of capital to deploy and slippage tolerances. The output of this step is a fully deployed Allocation Instance conforming to Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements.
assessments.description: Sequences Prime ALM arrangement finalization, recording, and deployment of Operational Buffer funds into Allocation Instances per Agent Artifact instructions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete parameters (deployment amount, slippage tolerance) and steps, but states no numeric values and delegates both to the Agent Artifact. It also requires conformance to undefined 'Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements', so a defender could argue either compliance or no binding obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Deployments into an Allocation Instance are controller operations, so the Rate Limiter reverts any deployment above the artifact's configured limit, partially reaching the amount. Liquidity Layer role definitions revert calls from addresses lacking the operator role. Slippage tolerance is not reached by any contract mechanism, and the rule relies on artifact review to catch mismatches.

assessments.title: Operationalization Of Allocation Instances
assessments.quote:
Prime Agent teams may choose to directly operationalize their Allocation System Primitive Instances ("Instances") using internal, proprietary strategies that are not defined in their Artifacts. Alternatively, Prime Agents may elect to have the Instances operationalized by their Operational Executor Agent. This constitutes an exception to the general rule that Operational Executor Agents operationalize all Sky Primitives on behalf of Prime Agents. See [A.1.14.3.4 - Agent Role Delineation](fdf32ca5-5e2e-481e-9047-4d1599547216).

For Prime Agent teams that operationalize their Instances, they will be required to formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies; should an Instance under-perform these KPIs, Operational GovOps is authorized to step in and operationalize the Instance(s) via a back-up strategy that is defined in the Agent Artifact. Additional logic on this point will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Lets Primes self-operationalize allocation Instances if they formulate KPIs; under-performance lets Operational GovOps step in with a back-up strategy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to formulate KPIs and the step-in authority are identifiable, but no KPI values, under-performance threshold, or measurement cadence is stated. The paragraph defers the operative escalation logic to a future iteration, so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Prime Agent teams that self-operationalize must formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies
Under-performance of an Instance against those KPIs triggers Operational GovOps step-in (no threshold stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps plausibly reaches a Prime that fails to formulate KPIs or defines no back-up strategy in its Artifact. Consequences are unquantified and firing depends on review, and the step-in escalation itself is undefined.

assessments.title: Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard
assessments.quote:
The Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard serves as the official system for determining and disseminating RRC figures for Prime Agents and their Allocation System Primitive Instances.

Prior to the full operational deployment of the Powerhouse system, Prime Agents must utilize the Sky Core RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for their official Instance Total RRCs and Aggregate RRC. Data from this source is to be used for all internal TRC management, required reporting and compliance assessments.

The Sky Core RRC Dashboard is located at [https://info.skyeco.com/required-risk-capital](https://info.skyeco.com/required-risk-capital).
assessments.description: Designates the Sky Core RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for Prime RRC figures, required until Powerhouse deployment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete: Prime Agents must use a named dashboard URL as the authoritative source for Instance Total RRCs and Aggregate RRC. No RRC magnitudes are stated, and the 'full operational deployment of the Powerhouse system' trigger has no date or defined condition, so the end of the obligation is open.
metrics: Prime Agents must use the Sky Core RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for Instance Total RRCs and Aggregate RRC
Applies prior to full operational deployment of the Powerhouse system (undated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Using a non-authoritative RRC source would misstate capital requirements, which falls under the Risk Capital rules that the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) enforce with quantified penalties. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could check which source a Prime uses, but no consequence is quantified for this specific source-of-truth rule.

assessments.title: Interim Notice Regarding RRC Dashboard Coverage
assessments.quote: Some Allocation System Instances displayed on the RRC Dashboard concern asset types whose risk models have not yet been fully developed. See [A.3.2.1.1.4.3 - Financial Risk Models](2af9fa64-ab25-4017-920c-f1c07dff4c06). An active Instance’s respective Instance Configuration Document will specify its `RRC Framework Full Implementation` status as either `Covered` or `Pending`.
assessments.description: Discloses that some dashboard instances lack full risk models and sets each instance's RRC implementation status to Covered or Pending.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a status field with two enumerated values, but gives no criteria for choosing Covered versus Pending and no deadline for reaching Covered. Those criteria are delegated to each Instance Configuration Document, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: RRC Framework Full Implementation status set to Covered or Pending in each active Instance's Configuration Document
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is an interim disclosure notice with no penalty, reverting control, or escalation path reaching the status labelling; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management
assessments.quote:
Prime Agent teams are responsible for managing their Total Risk Capital (TRC) to continuously meet their Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC). The accounting of TRC considers all on-chain holdings and any off-chain agreements, encumbrances, or conditions that may affect the immediate availability or eligibility of capital for RRC coverage. For a definition of Total Risk Capital, see [A.3.2.1.2.1 - Total Risk Capital Definition](6f6b25d6-f73c-4733-ba37-12a0a411433c).

The documents herein define requirements and standards for a Prime Agent’s internal TRC management systems.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agent teams to manage Total Risk Capital so it continuously meets Aggregate Required Risk Capital, accounting for off-chain encumbrances.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to continuously meet RRC is stated, but no numeric threshold, formula, or measurement cadence appears in the text; TRC and RRC are defined elsewhere, and the accounting scope relies on judgment terms like 'may affect' and 'eligibility'.

assessments.title: Objective of Prime TRC Management
assessments.quote:
To comply with Atlas risk capital requirements, Prime Agent teams must establish, maintain, and operate an internal system for TRC management. A Prime Agent’s internal TRC management system should enable proactive operational risk management. This entails ongoing capital adequacy assessment and strategic capital allocation planning for current and future Allocation System Primitive Instances, including the ability to perform scenario analyses for potential deployments or market stresses.

Prime Agents’ internal TRC management systems should enable them to maintain continuous sufficiency of the Prime Agent’s held TRC against its official Aggregate RRC. This requires real-time or near real-time comparison and internal alerting mechanisms to prevent and address potential shortfalls.
Primes must ensure that their internal TRC management systems maintain comprehensive, verifiable internal records of all TRC components, related transactions, and compliance activities to support internal governance and external verification processes, such as the submission of TRC Reports to Core GovOps. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc).
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to run an internal TRC management system covering capital planning, near-real-time sufficiency checks against Aggregate RRC, and verifiable records.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names real obligations (internal TRC system, sufficiency against Aggregate RRC, verifiable records, TRC Reports) but quantifies none of them. 'Continuous sufficiency', 'real-time or near real-time', and 'comprehensive, verifiable' are judgment language, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Continuous sufficiency of held TRC against official Aggregate RRC
Real-time or near real-time comparison and internal alerting
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A shortfall in held TRC versus Aggregate RRC is a Risk Capital breach that Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements plausibly reach, with Core GovOps as a distinct enforcer. However, no penalty is quantified for this process or record-keeping duty, and escalation depends on a breach being detected and surfaced.

assessments.title: Minimum Capabilities of Prime TRC Management Systems
assessments.quote:
A Prime Agent’s internal TRC management system should possess the following capabilities to meet the objectives outlined in [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Objective of Prime TRC Management](9a8120c4-0a5b-426f-97a5-283c708413f5).

1. Prime Agents’ internal TRC management systems should enable compliant sourcing and tracking of all TRC components, including Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC), Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC), and Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). Compliance in this context includes strict adherence to eligibility criteria and capital-sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal, Senior Per Junior) as defined in the Atlas. See [A.3.2.1.2.3 - Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios](9e99b084-f15a-4f60-b831-d6c0bd9aec04).
The system must provide real-time or near real-time tracking of all held Total Risk Capital (TRC) components. This includes, for each TRC component:
    - Accurate valuation of the assets comprising each component.
    - Clear identification of the source of each component (e.g., Prime’s own SubProxy for IJRC, specific Ecosystem Accord references for rented PEJRC or OSRC, TEJRC encumbrance details, OSRC origination details).
    - Verification of each TRC component’s eligibility status according to Atlas rules. This includes tracking whether capital is “enabled” or “active” for RRC coverage purposes (e.g., based on Ecosystem Accord status, compliance with sourcing ratios, etc.).
    - Distinction between capital directly held by the Prime Agent and capital that is encumbered (e.g., PEJRC where the lending Prime retains custody but the capital is contractually committed).
2. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should enable dynamic-state accounting. The system must account for TRC components that are in dynamic, pending, or off-chain states, as these can impact the true risk capital available to a Prime Agent. This includes:
    - Pending transactions such as PEJRC or OSRC rental Ecosystem Accords that have been committed to by the parties, but not yet codified in the Atlas.
    - Capital in transit, e.g., assets that are committed to be IJRC, but currently moving between chains via bridges or locked in Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) messages awaiting finality.
    - Operational expenditures funded by TRC components (typically IJRC), such as blockchain transaction fees, oracle service fees, audit costs, and other operational overhead that reduces available risk capital. The system should track these expenditures in real-time or near real-time.
    - Any off-chain factors that could impair the immediate deployability or availability of TRC components.
3. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should enable continuous capital adequacy monitoring. The system must enable the near real-time comparison of the Prime Agent's internally tracked and calculated TRC against its official Aggregate RRC, as obtained from the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard](4eac2c9e-2718-4881-a3f1-ed10fb3f4d13). This core functionality is essential for the Prime Agent to proactively monitor its capital adequacy, identify potential or actual TRC shortfalls, and make timely operational and capital management decisions to maintain compliance.
4. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should define a RRC-incident (e.g., TRC shortfall) response protocol. The system should enable internal alerting mechanisms that detect when a Prime Agent’s TRC approaches predefined internal buffer thresholds relative to its Aggregate RRC. See [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9). The system should also detect an actual shortfall where the Prime Agent’s held TRC falls below its Aggregate RRC. Furthermore, Prime Agent teams should establish and document internal processes for responding to such alerts. Such internal processes should include: 1) internal escalation and assessment of the shortfall’s cause and magnitude; 2) formulation of potential responses or corrective actions, which may include sourcing additional TRC, reducing risk-weighted exposures, or other measures; 3) internal decision-making framework for the evaluation of potential responses and selection of the most appropriate one; and 4) notifying any pertinent parties (Operational GovOps) as needed for the purpose of planning or implementing follow-up action.

Prime Agent teams' internal decision-making framework may consider the economic trade-offs of various actions, including the strategic acceptance of penalties for a TRC shortfall where such an approach is determined to be economically advantageous compared to immediate rebalancing (e.g., avoiding excessive transaction costs or market impact).
assessments.description: Lists capabilities a Prime's internal TRC management system should have for tracking, dynamic accounting, adequacy monitoring, and shortfall response.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph uses 'should' throughout and describes required capabilities in judgment terms, such as 'near real-time' tracking and 'internal processes'. It states no numeric thresholds; the buffer thresholds are 'predefined' but never given, and the sourcing ratios are delegated to the Atlas.

The rule is also soft ('should'), so enforcement is not automatic.

assessments.title: Primes’ TRC Report
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are required to submit periodic Total Risk Capital (TRC) Reports to provide an accurate and verifiable attestation of their TRC composition and adherence to capital requirements.

But no cadence defines "periodic", no content metric or threshold is stated, and "accurate and verifiable" is judgment language. A Prime could plausibly argue it complied by submitting any report, so the score is capped at 2.

Neither is quantified for this reporting duty, and firing depends on review being triggered.

assessments.title: Mandate and Rationale
assessments.quote:
Prime Agents are required to periodically submit TRC Reports to Core GovOps. This report serves a dual purpose. It provides a verifiable snapshot of the Prime Agent's TRC composition and key capital ratios as of the end of the reporting period; and second, it provides a formal attestation regarding the Prime Agent's maintenance of TRC at or above its dynamically changing Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC) throughout the entire reporting period. See [A.3.2.1.1.2 - Aggregate RRC](6aed5cc1-9671-4b73-88a9-fdd86ac93ece).

This comprehensive reporting, encompassing both an end-of-period statement and disclosures of any intra-period events affecting TRC, is essential. On-chain data alone (such as that captured by the planned OVRC system) cannot definitively prove the full eligibility and unimpaired availability of a Prime Agent's capital position for continuous RRC coverage, nor can it capture all off-chain factors. These factors include, but are not limited to, whether assets are subject to Prime-initiated off-chain contractual pledges, if the economic value or redeemability of its bridged assets is compromised by issues with their originating bridge, or if its assets are encumbered by derivative structures or other off-chain commitments that would impair their immediate use at any point during the period.

The TRC Report serves as an important basis for Core GovOps’ verification procedures. This entails: 1) reconciling reported end-of-period TRC components against the Sky Atlas, on-chain data, and other relevant sources to validate the period-end capital position and adherence to Atlas-defined capital requirements; and 2) reviewing Prime Agents’ attestations and disclosures regarding its TRC management and any material events throughout the reporting period to assess continuous compliance with its dynamically changing Aggregate RRC. The outcome of this validation is a critical input for the monthly settlement cycles, which latter includes the determination and retroactive application of penalties for any identified discrepancies or violations of capital requirements during the period.

The long-term vision is for the Powerhouse system to enable the automation of TRC data aggregation and verification. The Powerhouse system will have capabilities such as directly querying Prime Agent SubProxy accounts for IJRC assets, programmatically accessing and interpreting Ecosystem Accords recorded in the Atlas, interfacing with TEJRC and OSRC smart contract systems, and automatically applying Atlas-defined eligibility rules. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.3.1 - Continuous Monitoring Of On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital (OVRC)](8048bdf0-84b7-4546-8f1a-98b62d073c84). Even in this advanced state, the TRC Report, or a similar form of periodic attestation, may remain necessary to cover elements of TRC verification that are not fully able to be automated or require explicit Prime Agent declaration.

However, the reporting cadence is only "periodically", the reporting period is undefined, the RRC value is delegated to another paragraph, and the verification review is judgment-based.
