Breaches of capital requirements also escalate to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), with Core GovOps as an enforcer distinct from the Prime.

assessments.title: TRC Report Contents
assessments.quote:
The Total Risk Capital (TRC) Report submitted by a Prime Agent must provide an accurate and verifiable breakdown of all TRC components held by the Prime Agent as of the end of the specified reporting period. The TRC Report should include the following essential information:

- Aggregate TRC Value As of End of Period: The total declared value in USD of all eligible TRC components held by the Prime Agent as of the end of the reporting period.
- Detailed Breakdown of TRC Components As of End of Period: For each category of TRC held, the report must detail the following values as of the end of the reporting period:
    - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC): The total amount of IJRC, a breakdown of its constituent asset types, and their respective values in USD.
    - Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC): The total amount of PEJRC. For each portion of PEJRC sourced from another Prime Agent, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the counterparty Prime Agent, the expiry date of the arrangement, and a direct reference to the Ecosystem Accord that governs the PEJRC arrangement.
    - Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC): The total amount of TEJRC. For each TEJRC source, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the TEJRC smart contract or facility and any relevant encumbrance identifier.
    - Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC): The total amount of OSRC. The report must specify the amount originated directly by the Prime Agent from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool and any amount of OSRC rented from other Prime Agents. For any rented OSRC, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the counterparty Prime Agent, the expiry date, and a direct reference to the pertinent Ecosystem Accord.
    - Key Ratio Inputs and Computed Totals (Prime Internal Calculation) As Of End Of Period: Based on the component values reported above (as of the end of the reporting period), the report must include key figures used in and resulting from the Prime Agent's internal capital adequacy calculations. These figures reflect the capital structure and ratios as of the end of the reporting period and include:
        - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)
        - External Junior Risk Capital (EJRC) generated via External Per Internal Ratio (Prime External Junior Risk Capital + Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital sourced via the EPI ratio still carries Senior Per Junior or SPJ capacity)
        - EJRC-via-SPJ (sourced by spending SPJ capacity; zero-SPJ-capacity thereafter)
        - Enabled Senior Risk Capital (SRC)
        - Total Senior Per Junior capacity
            - Allocation of SPJ capacity to 1) enable SRC; or to 2) source EJRC
        - Prime-computed eligible Total Risk Capital (IJRC + EJRC-via-EPI + EJRC-via-SPJ + enabled SRC)
        - Official Aggregate RRC
        - Capital buffer = TRC – Aggregate RRC
        - Effective ratios
            - EPI = EJRC-via-EPI ÷ IJRC
            - SPJ utilization:
                - enabled SRC ÷ total SPJ capacity
                - EJRC-via-SPJ ÷ total SPJ capacity
- Dynamic Period Attestation and Disclosures: In addition to the end-of-period snapshot figures, the TRC Report must include an Attestation from the Prime Agent confirming it maintained TRC at or above its Aggregate RRC at all times throughout the entire reporting period. In addition, the TRC Report must include disclosure of any events, Prime-initiated off-chain contractual obligations, impairments to the value or redeemability of held assets (such as RWA backing or bridged asset viability), encumbrances, or other conditions that occurred at any point during the reporting period which materially affected its TRC, even if such conditions were temporary or not continuously visible to on-chain monitoring systems. This disclosure must include the nature of the event/condition, its precise timing and duration, and its quantified impact on the Prime Agent's TRC.
assessments.description: Requires Primes to submit a TRC Report itemizing end-of-period capital components, ratios, and an attestation of continuous RRC coverage with material event disclosures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines explicit formulas (capital buffer = TRC – Aggregate RRC; EPI = EJRC-via-EPI ÷ IJRC; SPJ utilization ratios) and required fields such as USD amounts, counterparty identifiers, and expiry dates. Gaps remain: no submission deadline or cadence, "relevant encumbrance identifier" and "materially affected" are undefined, and the report's figures are not tied to a numeric minimum beyond the attestation.

The consequence for misreporting is not quantified for this paragraph and firing depends on review, so mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Continuous Monitoring Of On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital (OVRC)
assessments.quote:
An autonomous monitoring system must be designed and implemented to enable continuous tracking of Prime Agents’ on-chain verifiable risk-capital components in near real-time. The on-chain, verifiable risk-capital components that can be tracked by such a monitoring system in real time are termed "On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital" (OVRC).

OVRC is not necessarily equivalent to Total Risk Capital (TRC). A Prime Agent’s actual TRC cannot be determined definitively without accounting for off-chain agreements, encumbrances or other relevant conditions affecting capital eligibility or availability, which conditions must be disclosed in the TRC Reports submitted by Prime Agents. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc).

Where the OVRC of a Prime Agent is less than its Aggregate RRC, the shortfall will be logged and penalty accrual will commence on a pro-rata, per-second basis for the duration and magnitude of the observed shortfall, according to the penalty schedule defined in the Atlas. Thus, this on-chain monitoring system serves as an interim penalty ledger.
assessments.description: Requires an autonomous system to track Primes' on-chain verifiable risk capital and accrue per-second penalties on shortfalls below Aggregate RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The shortfall trigger (OVRC below Aggregate RRC) and per-second, pro-rata accrual are concrete, but 'near real-time' is unquantified and the penalty magnitude is delegated to a schedule 'defined in the Atlas' without a stated value.

assessments.title: Validation of TRC Report In General
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are required to submit periodic Total Risk Capital (TRC) Reports to Core GovOps. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc). The protocol for validation of Primes’ TRC reports is defined in the documents herein.

The validation protocol is only referenced ('defined in the documents herein') and not stated, so compliance cannot be verified from this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: TRC reporting is part of the Risk Capital framework, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a missed or deficient report. Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, distinct enforcer that could assess such findings. Neither is quantified for this specific reporting duty, and no escalation path for late or missing reports is stated.

assessments.title: Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process
assessments.quote:
Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Primes on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process.

Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas.

Core GovOps validates the Prime Agent's reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Prime Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of "eligible assets" for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.1.1 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)](8728abee-0dc5-449b-b4c2-78698da16f10).

For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Prime, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components.

Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Prime Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Prime Agent's TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Prime Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations.

Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Prime Agent's compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)).

Operative magnitudes are delegated to the Atlas.

assessments.title: Finalized Determination Of TRC Position And Penalties
assessments.quote:
After reaching a definitive accounting of Prime Agents’ capital position and TRC adequacy, penalties are finalized by Core GovOps. This involves reconciling the interim penalty ledger (derived from the OVRC system) with the definitive TRC history, which incorporates all validated information from the TRC Report including any intra-period shortfalls.

1. If the validated TRC Report indicates that the Prime Agent's TRC was below its Aggregate RRC during the reporting period, and this actual shortfall was more severe than, or not detected by, the OVRC monitoring system, then penalties will be finalized as follows: if the OVRC system had already accrued penalties, these will be adjusted upwards to match the actual shortfall; if the OVRC system had not detected a shortfall, penalties will be assessed and applied retroactively based on the full duration and magnitude of the actual shortfall.
2. If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC shortfalls were identical in duration and magnitude to those logged by the OVRC monitoring system throughout the reporting period: the penalties accrued in the interim penalty ledger will be confirmed and finalized.
3. If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC was higher than a misleading OVRC reading during a specific portion of the reporting period which led to an erroneously logged penalty: Core GovOps will adjust or void the penalty accordingly.
assessments.description: Specifies how Core GovOps finalizes Prime Agent penalties by reconciling OVRC interim penalties with validated TRC shortfall data.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives three conditional branches with named metrics (TRC, Aggregate RRC, OVRC accruals) and a named actor (Core GovOps). However, penalty magnitudes are delegated to phrases like "adjusted upwards to match the actual shortfall" and "adjust or void the penalty accordingly," with no numeric rate or deadline.

shortfall duration and magnitude matching OVRC-logged shortfalls
penalties adjusted upwards to match actual shortfall

The Risk-Capital Incident Response (12b7d480) provides the escalation path up to conservatorship for TRC breaches that these penalties reach.

assessments.title: Risk-Capital Incident Response
assessments.quote:
Where a Prime Agent’s Allocation System Instances are operationalized by its Operational Executor Agent, the management of and response to Required Risk Capital (RRC)-related incidents requires a defined framework within each Prime Agent's Artifact (the Multi-Instance Coordinator Document for the Allocation System Primitive) and its associated Executor Accord.

While the Prime Agent's strategic team ("Prime Team") determines the specific rectification strategy for an RRC incident—considering its holistic portfolio, prevailing market conditions, and the potential for strategic acceptance of penalties—this discretion is exercised subject to the authority of Sky Core to impose penalties and take corrective measures, up to and including the conservatorship of a Prime Agent, to protect the ecosystem and make any losses whole.

This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Requires a defined framework for Required Risk Capital incidents and gives Sky Core authority to penalize or conservator Primes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Prime Team, Sky Core) and remedies (penalties, conservatorship), but states no threshold, metric, or deadline. The operative framework is deferred to the Artifact and Executor Accord, and the closing sentence is a stub.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Sky Core, a distinct enforcer, may impose penalties up to conservatorship via the Risk-Capital Incident Response and Penalty Mechanisms, which reach RRC incident mismanagement. The penalty amounts are unquantified and the escalation path is not defined in this text, so it rates mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Instance Operational Conformance
assessments.quote: Operational deviation from Artifact specifications can render an Instance’s RRC, and thus the Prime’s Aggregate RRC, invalid. Prime Agents must therefore ensure that each Allocation System Instance adheres to its respective Instance Configuration Document. Whether a Prime self-operationalizes its Allocation System or contracts with an Operational Executor Agent, its Agent Artifact must define processes for monitoring for, and addressing deviations of, Instance operational conformance. This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to keep each Allocation System Instance conformant with its Instance Configuration Document and to define deviation-monitoring processes, with details deferred.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real obligation (adherence to the Instance Configuration Document, and Agent Artifacts must define monitoring and deviation-handling processes), but gives no thresholds, metrics, cadence, or deadlines. The closing sentence defers the substance to a future iteration, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Rate Limiter reaches only stated controller rate limits and Liquidity Layer roles reach only role-gated calls, neither of which covers general instance deviation. Penalty Mechanisms and Artifact Review could in principle reach this, but the monitoring processes they would review are not yet defined, and no consequence is stated for deviation.

assessments.title: Allocation Instance Adjustments, Scaling, And Settlement
assessments.quote: On an ongoing basis, the Prime Agent team or Operational GovOps operates the Allocation Instance, scaling exposure up and down. Any change to the Allocation Instance outside of the limits specified in the Prime Agent Artifact or requiring judgment on the part of Operational GovOps (where the Allocation System Instance is operationalized by the Operational Executor Agent) requires a new vote of Prime Agent token holders. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.3.1 - Modification Of Existing Instances](c1b5708c-e88f-45e0-92e1-b76e68b34f13). As part of monthly and quarterly settlement cycles, Core GovOps reviews yields and obligations, applying penalties retroactively for any previously undisclosed violations. In the event of any such violations, Operational GovOps may be required to take escalatory steps based on the fallback strategy in the Prime Agent Artifact.

assessments.title: Modification Of Existing Instances
assessments.quote: When a Prime Agent wishes to modify an existing Allocation System Primitive Instance in a manner that cannot be accommodated by the existing operational parameters defined in its Agent Artifact, the Prime Agent must initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal process as detailed herein.
assessments.description: Requires a Prime Agent to initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal when modifying an Allocation System instance beyond its Agent Artifact parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger is a named process and a named actor, but whether a change "cannot be accommodated" by existing parameters is a judgment call. No threshold, deadline, or cadence is stated, and the process itself is deferred to "as detailed herein" elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps is a scheduled review by an enforcer distinct from the Prime, with staged findings and penalty assessment, which could catch an unannounced out-of-parameter modification. Consequences are not quantified for this rule, and detection depends on the review occurring.

assessments.title: Conditions Requiring Artifact Edit Proposal
assessments.quote:
An Artifact Edit Proposal is mandatory for an Instance modification under the following conditions:

1. a desired modification to the Instance's operational parameters falls outside the pre-defined operational ranges codified in the respective Instance Configuration Document or other applicable Artifact Documents; or
2. a desired modification, even if notionally within defined ranges in the Artifact, is determined by Operational GovOps to materially alter the Instance's risk profile in a way that could invalidate the underlying Capital and Operational Plan and, consequently, the premises driving the current Required Risk Capital (RRC) for that Instance. Operational GovOps retains the discretion to require an Artifact Edit Proposal if a proposed change, regardless of its fit within existing operational ranges, is determined to pose a material change to the assessed risk.
assessments.description: Requires an Artifact Edit Proposal for Instance changes outside configured ranges or deemed materially risk-altering by Operational GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Condition 1 is objectively checkable, but the operational ranges are defined only by reference to the Instance Configuration Document, with no values stated here. Condition 2 turns on Operational GovOps' judgment that a change 'materially' alters risk, which is qualitative and discretionary.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review by an enforcer distinct from the actor, with staged findings and penalty assessment, and could catch an unproposed out-of-range change. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and condition 2's discretionary trigger depends on Operational GovOps itself choosing to require a proposal. The Rate Limiter does not reach this rule because it blocks operations above a limit, not changes to the limit itself.

assessments.title: Revision of Capital and Operational Plan for Instance Modification
assessments.quote:
Prior to submitting an Artifact Edit Proposal for an Instance modification, the Prime Agent must revise the Capital and Operational Plan (C&O Plan) associated with that Instance to reflect the desired new state.

The revised Capital and Operational Plan for an Instance modification must include the following information:

1. Updates to the Instance's strategy and operational parameters;
2. A new pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate specifically calculated to reflect the Instance's proposed modified state; and
3. A revised notional Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage strategy, detailing how the Prime Agent will manage any changes to the Instance RRC and the consequential impact on its Aggregate RRC, including plans for acquiring additional JRC or SRC if necessary.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to revise the Capital and Operational Plan, with three specified contents, before submitting an Instance modification proposal.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule sets a sequencing condition (revision before submitting an Artifact Edit Proposal) and enumerates three required contents, with a defined actor. It gives no numeric thresholds, no method for the pro-forma RRC estimate, and no criteria for adequacy of the TRC coverage plan, so compliance is arguable.

No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Post-Approval Integration and RRC Update
assessments.quote:
If the Artifact Edit Proposal for the Instance modification is approved through the Prime Agent’s governance process, the relevant content from the revised Capital and Operational Plan is formally integrated into the respective Instance Configuration Document within the Prime Agent's Artifact.

Once the modified Instance is operational under its new, approved parameters and its data is integrated into the ecosystem’s monitoring systems, its adjusted Required Risk Capital (RRC) will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. This official RRC figure then supersedes the Prime-prepared pro-forma RRC that was part of the modification proposal.
assessments.description: Requires that approved Instance modifications be integrated into the Instance Configuration Document, and that the official post-deployment RRC on the Sky Core dashboard supersede the pro-forma RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete steps (ICD integration, official RRC tracking on the Sky Core RRC Dashboard, supersession of the pro-forma figure), but gives no formula, threshold, or deadline. "Once... operational" and "integrated into the ecosystem's monitoring systems" have no verifiable trigger, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check whether the ICD was updated and the official RRC used. The RRC feeds Risk Capital requirements, so a misstated RRC could trigger the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). The penalty path is not quantified for this paragraph's specific steps, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Required Allocation Instance Fallback Strategy
assessments.quote: The fallback strategy for each Allocation Instance must specify how Operational GovOps should determine when an emergency situation is occurring regarding the Allocation Instance and what actions it should take to protect the Prime Agent from losses associated with the Allocation Instance. The fallback strategy must include emergency measures for Operational GovOps to reduce exposure to, drain, and ultimately shut down the Allocation Instance if Required Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management obligations are breached.

Whether a given fallback strategy complies is arguable on the same facts.

assessments.title: Step 0: Net Revenue
assessments.quote:
The sole function of Step 0 is to establish the Net Revenue of the Sky Protocol. It performs no allocations to downstream functions or buffers, unlike subsequent steps for which this Net Revenue serves as the input.

Net Revenue is calculated for a single calendar month. Income from and Expenses owed to Prime Agents that settle through the Monthly Settlement Cycle are recognized in the month covered by that cycle. Where an amount recognized in an earlier month is subsequently adjusted, the adjustment is likewise recognized in the month covered by the cycle that settles it, and the earlier month's Net Revenue is not changed, as specified in [A.2.4.1.2.1.4 - True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle](de1592f5-dbce-46de-913f-6ec9589d36e8). Stability Fees on crypto vaults, legacy Real World Assets, and the SKY-Backed Borrowing vaults are recognized as they accrue, as are the interest expenses of the Sky Savings Rate, the Dai Savings Rate, and stUSDS. All other items of Income and Expense are recognized when USDS or DAI enter or leave the Sky Surplus Buffer. Transfers out of accounts other than the Sky Surplus Buffer are not recognized as Expenses, except as provided in [A.2.3.1.2.2.2.1.6.4 - Expense Recognition For Legacy Account Consolidation](1760b35f-da5a-4504-a014-dd7a611b4c0e).
assessments.description: Defines when Income and Expenses are recognized in Net Revenue for a calendar month, by item type and cycle timing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Recognition timing is defined per item class (accrual for certain Stability Fees and savings-rate interest, Sky Surplus Buffer flow for all others) with a single-month scope and a true-up rule. The paragraph gives no Net Revenue formula and does not enumerate the 'other items' it covers.

assessments.title: Internal Senior Risk Capital Income
assessments.quote: Internal Senior Risk Capital income is the revenue attributed to Sky from the total payments made by Primes for Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). ISRC itself is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital, as specified in [A.2.3.1.3 - Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital](ac7a6636-acbc-40c9-abc1-4543c0beb300). While Primes pay a single clearing price for their OSRC based on the monthly Origination Process, the total revenue received by Sky is subsequently allocated proportionally, with the portion corresponding to ISRC's share of the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool designated as ISRC Income.
assessments.description: Defines ISRC Income as Sky's proportional share of Primes' OSRC payments, based on ISRC's share of TSRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete allocation basis (ISRC's share of the TSRC pool, applied proportionally to total payments) and a monthly cadence via the Origination Process. However, the single clearing price is not stated or given a formula, so the operative amount is left to the external Origination Process.

assessments.title: External Senior Risk Capital Fees
assessments.quote: External Senior Risk Capital Fees are levied by Sky and calculated as 5% of the net interest earnings generated by the External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) pool each Monthly Settlement Cycle. These earnings represent the portion of the total revenue from Primes' Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) payments that is attributed proportionally to ESRC, based on its contribution to the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool for that cycle. This 5% fee is deducted before the remaining ESRC earnings contribute to the srUSDS conversion rate. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.3.3.2 - ESRC Earnings Fee](559f6fb6-daf6-41b2-9882-53a91aaf132f).

"Net interest earnings" and the proportional attribution to TSRC are described in prose rather than given as a formula, and the cross-referenced ESRC Earnings Fee doc holds the operative detail.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain or named mechanism reaches this accounting treatment; it only changes how a consolidation is classified in the Net Revenue calculation, and the catch-all backstops alone are weak.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig Required Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig has a 3/4 signing requirement.
assessments.description: Sets the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig signing threshold at 3 of 4 signers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The named multisig and the numeric 3-of-4 threshold are concrete and checkable against the Safe configuration. The paragraph is a descriptive statement of current configuration rather than a binding duty, and the signer set is not enumerated.
metrics: 3/4 signing requirement
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever threshold is actually configured, not the stated 3/4, so a mismatch is caught only through Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps. That review has staged findings and penalty assessment, but no consequence is quantified for this specific threshold.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps must use the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig to disburse funds to Aligned Delegates.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps to disburse Aligned Delegates funds only through the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names specific actors, a specific controlled system, and a concrete procedural requirement, so compliance is checkable against disbursement records. It states no amount, cadence, or threshold, and it does not define what counts as a disbursement or how the multisig's signing configuration is set.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review by a named enforcer distinct from the actor, with staged findings and penalty assessment, and it could catch disbursements routed outside the multisig. No on-chain mechanism forces disbursements through the Buffer Multisig, and the consequence is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig Modification
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps can change the signers of the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig so long as:

- there are at least four (4) signers;
- a majority of signers are required to execute transactions; and
- an equal number of signers are controlled by the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps.
assessments.description: Permits Core Facilitator and Core GovOps to change Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig signers if count, threshold, and equal-control conditions hold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a numeric minimum of four signers, a majority execution threshold, and an equal split of signers between the two named actors, all verifiable from the text. It gives no measurement cadence and leaves "majority" and the handling of odd signer counts without explicit definition.
metrics: at least four (4) signers
a majority of signers are required to execute transactions
an equal number of signers are controlled by the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever signer set and threshold are configured, not these composition constraints, so a mismatch is caught only by scheduled Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps, which has staged findings and penalty assessment. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.quote:
Step 1 Capital that remains after the Step 1 allocation becomes Step 2 Capital.

The allocation of Step 2 Capital depends on the level of Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) relative to the Turbo-Fill Floor (see [A.3.5.3.2.2 - Turbo-Fill Floor](db2aaf07-4ebb-4e5d-ae5e-575717d8fbcd)) and the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.2.1 - Target Aggregate Backstop Capital](f73dda95-0b1c-4bdc-b957-469253d27281)).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is below the Turbo-Fill Floor, fifty percent (50%) of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital. The remainder of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above the Turbo-Fill Floor and below the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, the portion of Step 2 Capital retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital is calculated as fifty percent (50%) multiplied by the fill factor, where the fill factor is one (1) minus the ratio of current Aggregate Backstop Capital to the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital. The remainder of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above the Turbo-Fill Floor and at or above the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, none of Step 2 Capital is retained; all of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).
assessments.description: Splits Step 2 Capital between growing Aggregate Backstop Capital and passing funds to Step 3, based on the backstop's level versus floor and target.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 50% retention and the fill-factor formula (1 minus current ABC over Target ABC) are fully specified and checkable. The Turbo-Fill Floor and Target ABC are defined elsewhere in the atlas and no values appear in this paragraph, and no measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: Retention below Turbo-Fill Floor: 50% of Step 2 Capital
Retention between floor and target: 50% × fill factor, where fill factor = 1 − (current ABC / Target ABC)
Retention at or above target: 0% of Step 2 Capital
Turbo-Fill Floor and Target ABC referenced from A.3.5.3.2.2 and A.3.5.3.2.1 (values not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is an internal allocation formula with no contract revert, penalty, or escalation attached to misapplying it. The Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) is the asset being funded, not an enforcer of this split, so it does not reach the rule.

assessments.title: Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital
assessments.quote: Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) consists of a portion of the excess capital of the Sky Protocol that is reinvested in providing Senior Risk Capital to Prime Agents. ISRC is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) in two components: one hundred percent (100%) of any Aggregate Backstop Capital in excess of the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.2.1 - Target Aggregate Backstop Capital](f73dda95-0b1c-4bdc-b957-469253d27281)), plus one third (1/3) of Aggregate Backstop Capital up to the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital.
assessments.description: Defines how Internal Senior Risk Capital is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital: 100% of excess over target plus one-third up to target.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The sourcing formula is fully quantified (100% of excess, 1/3 up to target), but its key input, Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, is defined in another section without a value here. No cadence for measuring ABC against target is stated.
metrics: 100% of Aggregate Backstop Capital in excess of Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
1/3 of Aggregate Backstop Capital up to Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is an internal treasury sourcing formula with no named enforcer, rate limit, or contract check. The Surplus Buffer and SKY Backstop are protocol-level loss absorbers that do not reach misallocation of this sourcing split.

assessments.title: Allocation Modification
assessments.quote:
In the short term, the Core Council may reduce the allocations of Step 1 Capital (see [A.2.3.1.2.2 - Step 1: Security And Maintenance](324e9d22-70fe-4e44-82ab-118815f5c42e)) and Step 2 Capital (see [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88)) below their specified levels and restore them up to those levels, and modify the allocation of Step 3 Capital among its specified uses (see [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121)). A reduction to the Step 1 allocation may be apportioned among its components as the Core Council determines. For Step 2 Capital, the specified level is the retention its allocation formula specifies for the current state. The Core Council exercises this authority through a public post by the Core Facilitator on the Sky Forum, confirmed by Core GovOps and the Core Council Risk Advisor.

The implementation of such modifications is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without requiring a prior Governance Poll.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Council reduce and restore Step 1 and Step 2 capital allocations and modify Step 3 uses via a confirmed Sky Forum post.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors (Core Council, Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, Risk Advisor) and a concrete procedure (public Sky Forum post, confirmation, direct Executive Vote). The operative magnitudes are discretionary and undefined: reduction amounts, the duration of 'short term', and the Step 1 apportionment are left to the Core Council's determination.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core GovOps and Risk Advisor confirmation is an in-process check among Core bodies, not a defined consequence for misuse. The penalty, conservatorship, and artifact review mechanisms target Primes and Operational Agents rather than the Core Council, so no citable mechanism reaches this rule's violation modes.

assessments.title: Operational Processes
assessments.quote:
The Monthly Settlement Cycle (MSC) synchronizes several key operational processes across the ecosystem, including:

1. Sky Protocol’s net revenue for the month covered by the cycle is calculated and allocated through the steps of the Treasury Management Function. See [A.2.3 - Treasury Management](6c0af059-5d33-4e2b-90f1-1606957b8f85).
2. The monthly Senior Risk Capital (SRC) origination process is settled: the clearing price is established, costs are deducted from winning Prime Agents’ accounts, and their accounts are credited with Originated SRC (OSRC) for the upcoming month. See [A.3.2.2.4.3.5 - Settlement Of Origination](fff0112a-58dd-4041-97f9-7baf113b4e70).
3. Queued conversions between USDS and srUSDS within the SRC system are processed. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.2 - Deposit And Redemption Queues](38a99586-4a13-4ce3-8b2f-cee025e0c390).
4. Pioneer Incentive Pools are funded with an amount equivalent to the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS. See [A.2.2.9.3 - Pioneer Chain Primitive](4c7be4c6-44b5-407a-94ae-3d7ca7e8039c).
5. Smart Burn Engine parameters are updated at each Monthly Settlement Cycle based on the prior month's state, and between Monthly Settlement Cycles as necessary as specified in [A.2.3.1.4.1 - Staking Rewards Rate Adjustment](de233df4-34cc-4e88-a065-9a9dde9add3c). See [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121) and [A.3.5.2 - Smart Burn Engine Parameters](ddb90fee-2851-4bf0-b924-f1d73e30ce7a).
6. Critical Core GovOps functions related to the operationalization of Sky Primitives are executed, including payment/reimbursement processing, compliance monitoring, and the calculation and application of retroactive penalties.
assessments.description: Lists processes the Monthly Settlement Cycle synchronizes, including revenue allocation, SRC origination settlement, queue processing, and Pioneer pool funding.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Item 4 states a concrete formula (Sky Savings Rate times Unrewarded USDS balance) and the cycle sets monthly cadence. Most other items are cross-references to linked docs, and item 6 lists functions without criteria, so the operative magnitudes are largely delegated.
metrics: Pioneer Incentive Pool funding equals the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS
Smart Burn Engine parameters updated at each Monthly Settlement Cycle and between cycles as necessary
Settlement performed monthly for the prior month's net revenue and OSRC crediting for the upcoming month
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Item 6 places compliance monitoring and the calculation and application of retroactive penalties within Core GovOps' cycle functions, which draws on the Penalty Mechanisms for Prime and Operational Agent breaches. The consequence is not quantified for the settlement processes themselves, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Payment Of Amounts Due To Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Amounts due to Prime Agents, excluding reimbursements made to Operational Executor Agents (see [A.2.4.1.2.1.3.3 - Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents](07c5cfd2-d68a-40d6-873d-b82cea9a92be)), are transferred from the Sky Surplus Buffer to the Prime SubProxy Account through an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires amounts due to Prime Agents, excluding Operational Executor reimbursements, to be transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Prime SubProxy via Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The source account (Sky Surplus Buffer), destination (Prime SubProxy Account), and approval path (Executive Vote) are named, and the reimbursement exclusion is cross-referenced. The amounts themselves are not quantified and are defined only by reference to the settlement cycle, with no cadence or formula stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Executive Vote is the authorizing step for the transfer, not a consequence attached to a violation. No penalty, conservatorship, or contract-enforced limit reaches misstated or unauthorized payments under this paragraph.

assessments.title: Collection Of Amounts Due From Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Amounts due from Prime Agents, excluding reimbursements made to Operational Executor Agents (see [A.2.4.1.2.1.3.3 - Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents](07c5cfd2-d68a-40d6-873d-b82cea9a92be)) are settled in a way that is equivalent to a transfer from the Prime to the Sky Surplus Buffer through actions included in an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires amounts due from Prime Agents to be settled as transfers to the Sky Surplus Buffer via Executive Vote actions, excluding Operational Executor reimbursements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete actors (Prime Agents, Sky Surplus Buffer) and a mechanism (Executive Vote), but gives no amount, rate, cadence, or deadline. "Equivalent to a transfer" leaves the settlement form and timing open to interpretation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog mechanism reaches non-payment of settlement amounts. Penalty Mechanisms cover Risk Capital rules, and the Surplus Buffer is the recipient of the transfer rather than an enforcer, so only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Revenue Share
assessments.quote: Grove and Spark agree to a bilateral revenue share, up to 40% maximum with JRC rental, see [A.2.2.10.2 - Risk Capital Rental Primitive](d8086dc0-7e77-4c6b-98c7-5fc41337a1ce).
assessments.description: Caps the bilateral revenue share between Grove and Spark agents at 40% in connection with JRC rental.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 40% maximum is a concrete numeric cap, but the revenue base, the calculation, the payment cadence, and the link to JRC rental are not defined in the paragraph. The cross-referenced primitive is a definitional source, not a stated parameter.
metrics: Revenue share up to 40% maximum
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism (rate limiter, role gating, penalty, or liquidation) reaches a negotiated revenue-share cap. The cited rental primitive (d8086dc0) is a cross-reference to a definition, not an enforcement mechanism, and no on-chain control enforces the share.

assessments.title: ASC Provision
assessments.quote: Grove retains the right to deploy into repo lending protocols to meet ASC requirements. Deposits must be capped at the lower of either 10% of protocol USDC deposits or the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral, as defined in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8). The Spark Agent retains the right to use the PSM for ASC, provided it covers the cost to Grove.
assessments.description: Caps Grove's repo lending deposits at the lower of 10% of USDC deposits or minimum ASC; permits Spark PSM use if cost-covered.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 10% deposit cap and the lower-of comparison are numeric and checkable, but the Minimum ASC input is defined only by reference to another paragraph. The PSM condition 'covers the cost to Grove' has no metric, and no measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: Repo lending deposits capped at the lower of 10% of protocol USDC deposits or Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (per 475fe222)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Grove is a Prime-level actor bound by the Risk Capital/ASC framework, so Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a breach of the cap. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific cap, and repo lending is off-chain, so the Liquidation Penalty and Rate Limiter do not clearly apply.

assessments.title: Risk Capital Share
assessments.quote: Grove agrees to rent to Spark 50% of the Required Risk Capital associated with Spark’s investments in USDe and sUSDe as a Junior Risk Capital Rental. See [A.2.2.10.2 - Risk Capital Rental Primitive](d8086dc0-7e77-4c6b-98c7-5fc41337a1ce).
assessments.description: Grover agrees to rent Spark 50% of the Required Risk Capital tied to its USDe and sUSDe investments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified at 50% of Required Risk Capital, with named parties and a cross-reference to the rental primitive. Missing elements are the value or formula for Required Risk Capital (defined elsewhere) and any measurement cadence or deadline for delivering the rental.
metrics: 50% of the Required Risk Capital associated with Spark's investments in USDe and sUSDe
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Spark is a Prime, so a shortfall in rented Risk Capital plausibly falls under the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and, for serious breaches of capital requirements, conservatorship (5c3dd35a). Neither is quantified for this accord term, so the rating stays at mid. The cited rental primitive (d8086dc0) defines the mechanism rather than enforcing it.

assessments.title: Implementation
assessments.quote:
Spark and Grove expressly intend that Grove shares in 50% of the risks of Spark’s investment in USDe and sUSDe and not in the risk of any other investments by Spark.

To the extent that USDe or sUSDe investments experience losses and Spark is allocated a greater than 50% share of those losses relative to Grove under the TIP JRC mechanism (see [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.2.1 - Initial Loss Absorption By "Tip JRC"](6c33bcf5-c29d-48ca-9ee5-e37dcdeb0630)), Grove will transfer funds to Spark so that Grove and Spark each bear 50% of the losses that occur.

To the extent that Spark experiences losses on investments other than USDe or sUSDe and a portion of those losses is allocated to the Junior Risk Capital rented from Grove, Spark shall reimburse Grove for those losses.
assessments.description: Splits USDe/sUSDe investment losses 50/50 between Spark and Grove and requires Spark to reimburse Grove for rented JRC losses on other assets.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 50% loss-sharing split is a hard numeric threshold with named actors (Spark, Grove). It lacks a measurement cadence and a formula for computing the transfer amount, and the reimbursement obligation for non-USDe losses is stated without a quantity or deadline.
metrics: Grove shares 50% of the risks of Spark's USDe and sUSDe investments
Grove transfers funds to Spark when Spark bears more than 50% of USDe/sUSDe losses relative to Grove under TIP JRC
Spark reimburses Grove for losses on non-USDe/sUSDe investments allocated to rented Junior Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach breaches of the Risk Capital allocation terms, and the TIP JRC loss-absorption mechanism (6c33bcf5, cited in the text) sets the loss allocation that triggers the transfer. However, no consequence is quantified for this specific sharing or reimbursement obligation, and no named enforcer is defined for the transfer.

assessments.title: Recourse
assessments.quote: Sky’s recourse for bad debt consists of (1) minting Prime Agent tokens; (2) terminating a Prime’s right to further borrowing; and (3) activation of the Resolution Mechanism which includes, without limitation, the authority to suspend all protocol operations, seize or reallocate all of the Prime assets, override or disable smart contract functions, initiate managed restructuring, or execute full and permanent liquidation of the affected sub-protocol and all of its assets, in order to contain risk and preserve the stability and solvency of the broader ecosystem.
assessments.description: Defines Sky's recourse for Prime bad debt: Prime Agent token minting, borrowing termination, and a broad Resolution Mechanism.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates three remedy categories and a non-exhaustive list of Resolution Mechanism powers, but gives no trigger threshold for 'bad debt', no quantities, and no deadlines. 'Without limitation' and 'in order to contain risk' leave the operative conditions to judgment, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Risk-Capital Incident Response framework (12b7d480) defines an incident path through which Sky Core can impose penalties up to conservatorship to recover losses, which plausibly reaches bad-debt events. Conservatorship (5c3dd35a) overlaps with the Prime takeover powers. The remedies are unquantified for this paragraph and firing depends on incident escalation, so mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.quote: Each genesis capital allocation is subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)).
assessments.description: Subjects each genesis capital allocation to the Genesis Capital Backstop, by cross-reference to A.3.7.1.6.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states no threshold, formula, deadline, or actor-specific metric. Its only operative content is a cross-reference to A.3.7.1.6, so there is nothing to measure compliance against in this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph cites the Genesis Capital Backstop (a9965d58), but its content is not in this text and it does not match any catalog mechanism, so I cannot verify that it reaches a violation of this rule. No catalog mechanism applies.

assessments.title: Current Control (Until 2026)
assessments.quote: The Peg Stability Module (PSM) remains directly managed and controlled by Sky until the full deployment and operationalization of the Actively Stabilizing Collateral (ASC) system. Sky retains responsibility for setting debt ceilings, determining liquidity levels, and overseeing asset management activities within the PSM during this period.
assessments.description: Keeps Sky directly controlling the PSM, including debt ceilings, liquidity levels and asset management, until ASC is fully deployed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actor (Sky) and the controlled parameters (debt ceilings, liquidity levels, asset management), but gives no magnitudes or measurement criteria. The end point, 'full deployment and operationalization' of ASC, is not objectively verifiable.
metrics: Control applies until full deployment and operationalization of the ASC system
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No cited mechanism reaches Sky's responsibility for setting ceilings and liquidity. The PSM's on-chain fixed-rate swap (0082c12d) arbitrages peg deviation but does not enforce who sets these parameters or how well, and the paragraph names no escalation path.

assessments.title: Transition to Grove (2025)
assessments.quote: Beginning in 2025, Grove shall assume operational and accounting ownership of the PSM, incorporating the PSM’s assets into its total value locked (TVL). Sky maintains active oversight and retains final control over strategic and operational decision-making within the PSM until full ASC implementation occurs.
assessments.description: Transfers operational and accounting ownership of the PSM to Grove from 2025, while Sky retains oversight and final control until full ASC implementation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation names actors (Grove, Sky), an action (assuming ownership and incorporating PSM assets into TVL), and a start year. However, the deadline is only a year with no month, 'active oversight' is judgment language, and the end of Sky's control depends on 'full ASC implementation', which is not defined here.
metrics: Beginning in 2025 (start of Grove ownership)
Sky retains final control until full ASC implementation occurs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can review Grove's compliance with its PSM ownership and control terms and assess penalties, with the enforcer distinct from the actor. Consequences are not quantified for this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the ownership transfer.

assessments.title: Base Rate Obligation
assessments.quote: Grove will be required to pay the Base Rate on all assets within the PSM. The Base Rate is dynamic and will align with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate), expected to fluctuate between the Aave and Ethena rates. See [A.2.8.2.2.2.2.3 - Base Rate](fd39df25-6093-49ae-be12-36df34754612).
assessments.description: Requires Grove to pay a dynamic Base Rate, aligned with the SSR, on all assets within the PSM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is identifiable (Grove pays a Base Rate on PSM assets), but no rate value, formula, or payment cadence is stated. The rate is only 'expected to fluctuate' between Aave and Ethena rates, with the operative definition delegated to a cross-referenced doc.
metrics: Base Rate aligned with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate)
Expected to fluctuate between the Aave and Ethena rates (no bounds or values stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain check, or named enforcer is tied to non-payment of the Base Rate. The cross-referenced UUID fd39df25 is a definitional doc, not an enforcement mechanism, and only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Yield on USDC
assessments.quote: Grove shall earn yield through Coinbase Custody on USDC holdings within the PSM, enabling potential positive carry depending upon the spread between custody yield and the Base Rate.
assessments.description: Requires Grove to earn yield via Coinbase Custody on PSM-held USDC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Grove), a venue (Coinbase Custody), and an asset (USDC in the PSM), but states no yield target, rate, amount, or cadence. The 'potential' carry language lets a defender argue the clause is permissive rather than binding, which caps the score at 2.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The PSM (0082c12d) enforces the USDC peg through fixed-rate swaps, not Grove's yield-earning obligation, and no penalty, rate limiter, or role gate applies to yield generation. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Economic Rationale
assessments.quote: Grove will pay the Base Rate on the PSM for the purpose of meeting ASC requirements, if there are no better alternatives available. Unlike other alternatives, USDC in the PSM will have no capital requirement. If other, better options for ASC are available, Grove should empty the PSM and allocate the assets to those options. It is anticipated that other protocols will also be willing to rent ASC "points", potentially allowing for the management of ASC needs across several Prime Agents for a profit.
assessments.description: Describes Grove paying the Base Rate on PSM USDC to meet ASC needs, emptying the PSM when better ASC options exist.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real (pay Base Rate on PSM USDC, empty the PSM if better ASC options exist), but 'better alternatives' and 'should' are judgment terms with no criteria. The Base Rate is named without a value, and the PSM's zero capital requirement is stated without a figure.
metrics: Base Rate on the PSM (named, no value stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is economic rationale rather than an enforceable limit. No rate limiter, role gate, or penalty reaches the 'should empty the PSM' or 'better alternatives' language, so only the misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Short Term (2025-2026)
assessments.quote: The PSM will remain a central liquidity hub for stablecoin deployment. Grove will manage the PSM, paying the Base Rate while earning USDC yield, under Sky oversight until full ASC implementation. PSM assets will count toward Grove's TVL, enhancing its economic standing and collateral efficiency.
assessments.description: Short-term plan for Grove to manage the PSM, paying Base Rate and counting PSM assets toward its TVL until full ASC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names a real obligation (Grove manages the PSM and pays Base Rate) but gives no Base Rate value, no cadence, and no definition of 'Sky oversight'. Much of the text is posture ('central liquidity hub', 'enhancing economic standing'), so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Base Rate payment to Sky (named, no value stated)
Duration: until full ASC implementation (no date or trigger defined)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The PSM's fixed-rate swap (0082c12d) enforces peg arbitrage, not Grove's Base Rate payment or oversight duties. Penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12) target Risk Capital rule breaches, and artifact review (d4bf73e7) is not tied to this Accord term, so no citable mechanism reaches it.

assessments.title: Long Term (Post-2026)
assessments.quote: The PSM's role will diminish as the ASC system becomes the primary liquidity management tool. Grove can wind down the PSM entirely if ASC requirements are fulfilled through other mechanisms (e.g., Uniswap positions, Curve pools). If ASC obligations rise significantly, PSM usage will increase, but as the system matures, its relevance will gradually decline.
assessments.description: Describes the expected long-term decline of PSM usage as ASC becomes the main liquidity tool, and Grove's option to wind down the PSM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a posture statement with no numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines. Terms such as 'fulfilled', 'rise significantly', and 'gradually decline' have no measurable criteria, so there is nothing a third party could verify.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is permissive and predictive rather than a binding limit, and no mechanism reaches its conditions. The PSM mechanism (0082c12d) enforces the peg, not this outlook, and the Rate Limiter does not apply because no limit is stated.

assessments.title: Risk Management
assessments.quote: The PSM serves as a capital buffer, enabling Grove to scale liquidity massively without additional credit enhancement. As ASC obligations fluctuate, the PSM will act as a dynamic backstop, ensuring resilience during periods of high demand.
assessments.description: Describes the PSM as a capital buffer that backstops Grove's ASC obligations during demand swings.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is posture language with no thresholds, formulas, metrics, or deadlines. Phrases such as 'dynamic backstop' and 'scale liquidity massively' define no operative magnitude or verifiable condition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The PSM's on-chain fixed-rate swap (0082c12d) enforces peg deviation, not this descriptive statement about backstopping ASC obligations, and no mechanism reaches a violation of this text.

assessments.title: Transfer Of Capital Funds
assessments.quote: The transfer of the Genesis Capital Allocation to each Prime SubProxy (i.e. the Spark SubProxy and Grove SubProxy) shall occur once funding from the Surplus Buffer is approved. This condition ensures that capital deployment is aligned with the successful launch of the Prime's token and the commencement of its independent operations.
assessments.description: Conditions the transfer of Genesis Capital Allocation to the Spark and Grove SubProxies on Surplus Buffer funding approval.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actors (Spark and Grove SubProxies) and a trigger (Surplus Buffer funding approval), but gives no transfer amount, deadline, or identified approver. Whether the condition is met is arguable, since 'approved' has no defined authority or process.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) is a funding source and loss-absorption backstop, not an enforcer of this transfer condition, and no mechanism reaches a premature or unapproved transfer. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Skybase Foundation Grant Authorization: November 2026
assessments.quote:
The founding team of Skybase has proposed a cash grant of 900,000 USDS to the Skybase Foundation from Skybase's SubProxy to fund operational costs and partner payouts through the end of 2026, for inclusion in the November 2026 Executive Vote.

Sky Governance hereby consents to this grant. The transfer must be made to the Skybase Foundation Operational Multisig at `0x58B945c8Ce34BD8cEA3Fc0437626F9F87d58A621` in the Sky Core Spell unless otherwise agreed by Sky and Skybase.
assessments.description: Authorizes a 900,000 USDS grant from Skybase's SubProxy to the Skybase Foundation multisig via the Sky Core Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The grant amount, source, exact recipient address, and execution vehicle are all stated. Gaps are the lack of a transfer deadline ("through the end of 2026" governs use of funds, not timing of transfer) and the open "unless otherwise agreed by Sky and Skybase" carve-out.
metrics: Grant amount: 900,000 USDS
Source: Skybase SubProxy
Recipient: Skybase Foundation Operational Multisig 0x58B945c8Ce34BD8cEA3Fc0437626F9F87d58A621
Transfer executed in the Sky Core Spell
Funds to cover operational costs and partner payouts through end of 2026
Inclusion in November 2026 Executive Vote
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a one-time authorization whose execution is controlled by the Executive Vote and spell, but no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limiter, role gating) reaches post-approval use or deviation from the stated recipient or amount; the "unless otherwise agreed" clause also sits outside any enforcer.

assessments.title: Prime Revenue Credit
assessments.quote: Grove is owed 2,528,000 USDS based on the true-up of prior Monthly Settlement Cycles. Until this amount is paid to Grove through the next Monthly Settlement Cycle, this credit counts toward Grove's Total Risk Capital (TRC), as defined in [A.3.2.1.2.1 - Total Risk Capital Definition](6f6b25d6-f73c-4733-ba37-12a0a411433c).
assessments.description: Records 2,528,000 USDS owed to Grove, counted toward its Total Risk Capital until paid through the next Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The amount (2,528,000 USDS) and the payment deadline (next Monthly Settlement Cycle) are concrete, and the TRC inclusion is clear by reference. Gaps: the cycle's timing is not specified, and the TRC calculation is delegated to another section.
metrics: Amount owed to Grove: 2,528,000 USDS
Credit counts toward Grove's Total Risk Capital until paid through the next Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The credit's effect on Grove's Total Risk Capital is a Risk Capital rule, which the Penalty Mechanisms reach for Primes. The consequence is not quantified for this specific payment or counting obligation, and no on-chain control enforces it.

assessments.title: Resilience Fund Aggregate Cap
assessments.quote: Claims will be subject to an aggregate cap for all claims in relation to a Claim Event determined by the risk models elaborated by the Resilience Technical Committee.
assessments.description: Caps aggregate claims for a single Claim Event at a level set by Resilience Technical Committee risk models.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (Resilience Technical Committee) and a concept (aggregate cap per Claim Event), but gives no numeric cap, formula, or verifiable input. The magnitude is delegated to unpublished risk models, so compliance cannot be checked from the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalogued mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Penalty Mechanisms, Risk-Capital Incident Response) reaches a claims-payout cap, and the paragraph names no enforcer or consequence for exceeding it.

assessments.title: Bug Bounty Program For Critical Infrastructure
assessments.quote: As one of the most important DeFi protocols with a high TVL, the Sky Protocol is a honeypot for hackers and other nefarious actors. The Sky Protocol must always be protected by an active Bug Bounty Program. This document regulates the budget and processes of the Bug Bounty Program, which serves to protect the Sky Protocol and its users from hacks and exploits. The Bug Bounty Program is conducted on the Immunefi platform.
assessments.description: Requires the Sky Protocol to always have an active Bug Bounty Program conducted on Immunefi, deferring budget and process details to another document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to always maintain an active program is real and binary, but 'active' is undefined and no threshold, budget amount, or cadence is stated. The budget and process rules are explicitly deferred to a document not present here.
metrics: Bug Bounty Program must always be active
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no enforcer, penalty, or automatic control tied to maintaining the program, and no catalog mechanism reaches a failure to keep it active; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Introduction
assessments.quote:
The Bug Bounty Program aims to create incentives for hackers to contribute to the resilience of the Sky Protocol as opposed to exploiting vulnerabilities for personal gain. Immunefi is the party responsible for conducting the Bug Bounty Program; its setup and operations are based on standards set by Immunefi.

The Sky Ecosystem must continue to maintain a Bug Bounty Program for SparkLend until the launch of the Spark Agent.
assessments.description: Describes the Bug Bounty Program's purpose and Immunefi's role, and requires the Sky Ecosystem to keep a SparkLend bounty until the Spark Agent launches.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative obligation is a continuing duty to maintain a SparkLend bug bounty, bounded only by the undefined event 'launch of the Spark Agent'. 'Maintain' and the Immunefi standards are not quantified or specified, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Bug bounty for SparkLend maintained until the launch of the Spark Agent (event-based end condition, launch date not defined)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism in the catalog reaches a duty to maintain a bounty program; the only plausible backstop is the misalignment/adjudication catch-all, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Assets In Scope
assessments.quote:
The Assets In Scope of the Sky Core Bug Bounty Program will be those identified as critical infrastructure for the Sky Ecosystem.

For Sky Core, the Assets In Scope accepted for this Bug Bounty Program are specified on Sky’s listing on the Immunefi platform, which can be found at ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/)). Assets in Scope include smart contracts, frontend applications, data infrastructure and oracles.

For SparkLend, the Assets In Scope for the Bug Bounty Program is specified on SparkLend’s listing on the Immunefi platform, which can be found at ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/)). For SparkLend, the Assets In Scope only include smart contracts.

The Protocol Security Workstream Lead is responsible for maintaining these lists of Assets In Scope, in consultation with the relevant stakeholders.
assessments.description: Defines the Bug Bounty Program's in-scope assets as critical infrastructure, listed externally on Immunefi for Sky Core and SparkLend.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to maintain scope lists is real and names an actor (Protocol Security Workstream Lead), but "critical infrastructure" is undefined and the operative scope is delegated to external Immunefi pages. Categories like smart contracts, frontend applications, and data infrastructure have no criteria or cadence, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism reaches a failure to maintain or correctly publish the scope lists; the only available backstop is the generic misalignment and adjudication process.

assessments.title: Severity Classification
assessments.quote: The Immunefi Vulnerability Severity Classification System ([https://immunefi.com/severity-updated/](https://immunefi.com/severity-updated/)) is applicable to both Sky Core and SparkLend. The Protocol Security Workstream Lead is authorized to adopt a new severity system for the Bug Bounty Programs in consultation with relevant technical stakeholders.
assessments.description: Applies Immunefi severity classification to Sky Core and SparkLend bounties; Workstream Lead may replace it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete external severity standard and defined systems, but gives no thresholds or metrics. The Workstream Lead's power to adopt a replacement system depends on undefined 'consultation with relevant technical stakeholders', so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism in the catalog or the text checks whether bounty severity is classified under the Immunefi system or a substitute; the bounty payout incentive does not enforce the classification rule itself.

assessments.title: Out Of Scope Vulnerabilities And Other Limitations
assessments.quote:
A selection of vulnerabilities is deemed out of scope for the Bug Bounty Program. An overview of these out of scope vulnerabilities can be found on Sky’s listing on the Immunefi platform ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/)). Feasibility limitations also apply, which can be found in the aforementioned listing on the Immunefi website.

Specific rules applying to the Bug Bounty Program can be found at the website above, listed under the following categories:

- Repeatable attack limitations
- Restrictions on security researcher eligibility
- Public disclosure of known issues
- Proof of Concept (PoC) requirements
- Other terms and information
- Prohibited activities

For SparkLend, the rules, terms, and exceptions can be found on SparkLend’s listing on the Immunefi platform ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/)).
assessments.description: Defers which vulnerabilities are out of scope for the bug bounty program to external Immunefi listings.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states no thresholds, criteria, or metrics. It names categories of rules but points to external Immunefi pages for their content, so there is nothing operative to comply with in the text itself.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines bug bounty scope rather than imposing a duty on a regulated actor, and no penalty, contract-enforced control, or named enforcer reaches it.

assessments.title: Rewards Payout Process
assessments.quote:
Sky Core bug bounty payouts are paid from the [A.2.3.1.2.2.2.1 - Core Council Buffer](8b6781d7-f35c-4ffe-b8ed-299fa98e3da7). Upon confirmation, the payout is sent in USDS directly from the Core Council Buffer to the whitehat hacker. If the payout exceeds 500,000 USDS or 50% of the USDS balance of the Core Council Buffer, the Core Facilitator may instead choose to include a payout in the next possible Executive Vote, sending USDS directly from the Surplus Buffer to the whitehat hacker.

The [A.1.8.1.2 - Protocol Security Workstream Lead](93651fb8-13c5-46dd-93cb-33fa89671b4f) publicly requests each payout in a post on the Sky Forum, including a specification of the respective vulnerability report, the requested amount, and the Ethereum mainnet addresses of the beneficiaries. The request should also include the payment details of the Immunefi fee, if it applies. Any applicable Immunefi fee is paid in USDS from the same source as the payout. The Protocol Security Workstream Lead and the [A.2.3.1.2.2.2.1.3 - Core Council Buffer Multisig Signers](5aeba17d-3869-447d-adcd-8c55f41afc01), or the Core Facilitator for a payout included in an Executive Vote, should make sure the payout is made within one full calendar month after the report was approved.

For Bug Bounty rewards over USD 1,000,000: after the first million is paid out, the remaining amount is paid out over time with up to USD 1,000,000 per consecutive month until the determined amount for payout is reached.
assessments.description: Governs bug bounty payout sourcing, approval posting, a one-month payment target, and staged payment of rewards above USD 1,000,000.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Concrete thresholds are stated: 500,000 USDS or 50% of the Core Council Buffer balance, a one-full-calendar-month deadline, and USD 1,000,000 per month. The deadline is softened by 'should make sure', 'Upon confirmation' is undefined, and the Immunefi fee amount is not specified.
metrics: Payout over 500,000 USDS or 50% of Core Council Buffer USDS balance may instead go through an Executive Vote from the Surplus Buffer
Payout made within one full calendar month after report approval (should)
Rewards over USD 1,000,000: first million paid, then up to USD 1,000,000 per consecutive month
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The one-month payment target and the payout thresholds have no on-chain or penalty mechanism reaching them; only the generic misalignment reporting and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Rewards Budget
assessments.quote:
The Bug Bounty Programs incur fixed and variable costs.

- Variable costs: Bug bounty payouts including related fees to Immunefi are considered variable costs and are covered by the process described in [A.2.11.1.1.3.3 - Rewards Payment Terms](cf4e6968-18a3-48d8-b38e-15ae8009d03d). When paid from the Core Council Buffer, they are funded from the [A.2.3.1.2.2.2 - Core Council Allocation](91b281c2-0687-45a3-939d-0480c7c33f9f). When paid through an Executive Vote from the Surplus Buffer, the payout and any Immunefi fee do not reduce [A.2.3.1.2.1.1 - Net Revenue](bddce7bf-c568-444b-b196-e15a99016696) for the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Instead, Core GovOps deducts the amount from the [A.2.3.1.2.2.2 - Core Council Allocation](91b281c2-0687-45a3-939d-0480c7c33f9f) in subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycles to repay the Surplus Buffer, and may spread the deduction across multiple Monthly Settlement Cycles.
- Fixed costs: Fixed costs comprise service fees for the Immunefi Premium Triaging Service, and compensation of a part-time Bug Bounty program steward. These costs will be funded by Sky.
assessments.description: Specifies how Bug Bounty payouts and fixed program costs are funded, including Core GovOps repayment of the Surplus Buffer via later deductions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names funding sources (Core Council Buffer, Surplus Buffer, Core Council Allocation) and a repayment process, but gives no amounts, repayment deadlines, or cadence. The repayment may be spread across cycles at Core GovOps' discretion, and fixed costs are simply 'funded by Sky.'
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or contract-enforced path reaches misallocation of bounty funds or failure to repay the Surplus Buffer; the Surplus Buffer is only a protocol-level backstop and the rule has no named enforcer.

assessments.title: Safe Harbor
assessments.quote: Sky Ecosystem is adopting the Security Alliance Safe Harbor Agreement ("Safe Harbor") by executing the procedures specified in [A.2.11.1.2.2 - Execution](25015208-5234-4818-8479-c46f927c272c). Safe Harbor is a public agreement that protocols may adopt to waive the right to pursue legal claims against a whitehat hacker, provided that the hacker acts competently, lawfully, and in good faith. Under Safe Harbor, any whitehat hacker who identifies a time-critical active exploit that could result in the loss of funds is authorized to act immediately to rescue those funds. Immediate intervention prevents delays that might otherwise cause irrevocable financial harm. Once the funds have been secured, the whitehat hacker returns them within 72 hours to an Asset Recovery Address (see [A.2.11.1.2.2.3.3.2 - Asset Recovery Addresses](3f125522-dff7-48a3-948f-e99c71fc3929)) designated by the protocol that has adopted the Safe Harbor Agreement.
assessments.description: Adopts the Security Alliance Safe Harbor, letting whitehats rescue funds from active exploits and return them within 72 hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 72-hour return deadline and the Asset Recovery Address destination are concrete and checkable. The trigger (a 'time-critical active exploit') and the conduct standard ('competently, lawfully, and in good faith') are qualitative, so compliance on the rescue step is arguable.
metrics: Return rescued funds within 72 hours
Return to the Asset Recovery Address designated by the adopting protocol
Rescue limited to time-critical active exploits that could result in loss of funds
Whitehat must act competently, lawfully, and in good faith
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph's only consequence is the protocol's waiver of legal claims, which is not an enforcement mechanism in the catalog. No on-chain, penalty, or escalation path reaches the 72-hour return or the good-faith conduct requirement.

assessments.title: Accounts
assessments.quote:
The `accounts` parameter for each chain is a list of contracts to be included in Safe Harbor. Each contract listed must include the sub-elements of (1) the `accountAddress` of the contract and (2) the `childContractScope`, which specifies whether child contracts of the specified contract are covered. The possible values for the `childContractScope` parameter are: (1) `None` (no child contracts are in scope), (2) `ExistingOnly` (only child contracts created prior to calling `adoptSafeHarbor` are in scope), or (3) `All` (all child contracts are in scope).

The value of the `scope` parameter is all contracts specified in the Bug Bounty Program.

The `childContractScope` parameter for each contract is specified in the Bug Bounty Program.
assessments.description: Defines required fields and allowed values for contracts listed under the Safe Harbor accounts parameter, with scope delegated to the Bug Bounty Program.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates required sub-elements (accountAddress, childContractScope) and three fixed values for childContractScope, which a checker could verify.
