However, the actual contract list and each contract's childContractScope are delegated to the Bug Bounty Program, so the operative content is not stated in this text.
metrics: childContractScope must be one of: None, ExistingOnly, All
Each listed contract must include accountAddress and childContractScope
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a misconfigured Safe Harbor accounts entry; the Safe Harbor list is not controller-enforced, and artifact review or misalignment reporting would only catch it indirectly, which is weak.

assessments.title: Maintenance
assessments.quote: The list of contracts covered by the Safe Harbor agreement for Sky must be updated when new contracts are added. Whenever a contract is added to the Bug Bounty Program, it should also be added to Safe Harbor. The Spell Teams are primarily responsible for updating the Safe Harbor registry each time a contract is added to the Bug Bounty Program. The Core Facilitator is responsible for reviewing the work of the Spell Teams to ensure that this requirement is met.
assessments.description: Requires Spell Teams to add newly bug-bounty-covered contracts to the Safe Harbor registry, with Core Facilitator review.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger (contract added to the Bug Bounty Program) and the responsible actors (Spell Teams, Core Facilitator) are concrete and checkable. However, there is no deadline or cadence, and the operative sentence uses "should" while the opening uses "must", so a defender could argue the duty is not binding.
metrics: Each time a contract is added to the Bug Bounty Program, the contract is added to the Safe Harbor registry (event-triggered, no deadline)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Core Facilitator review is a named check, but it defines no escalation, penalty, or remedy for a missed registry update. No catalog mechanism (penalty, artifact review, rate limit, role gating) clearly reaches Spell Team registry updates, so none found.

assessments.title: Multisig Administrator
assessments.quote: A Multisig Administrator is the entity or individual responsible for the setup, configuration, ongoing management, and compliance of a Multisig. Each Multisig must have a designated Multisig Administrator, communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps prior to the Multisig's activation or operational use.
assessments.description: Requires each Multisig to have a designated Multisig Administrator, communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps before activation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The designation and communication obligation is concrete, with named recipients and a timing deadline (before activation or operational use). However, the administrator's responsibilities ('ongoing management, and compliance') are undefined and not measurable.
metrics: Each Multisig must have a designated Multisig Administrator
Designation communicated to Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps
Communication occurs prior to the Multisig's activation or operational use
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check multisig setup and designation documentation against this rule and assess penalties, but no consequence is quantified for a missing or late designation.

assessments.title: Impact Assessment
assessments.quote:
Impact Assessment defines the assessment process in which the potential impact of a Multisig compromise or failure is evaluated. The result of this evaluation is the assignment of an Impact Classification level as defined below. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for determining this classification and must provide it to Core GovOps as part of the Multisig registration process in accordance with [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.8 - Multisig Registration](110614e9-6375-464a-90b3-3b350d3cf79c).

| **Impact Classification Level** | **Financial Exposure** | **Decision Context** | **Reputational Impact** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low | <$100k direct exposure | Minimal disruption, alternative paths exist | Limited scope impact |
| Medium | $100k – $1M exposure | Significant operational delays, workarounds available | Moderate reputational concern |
| High | $1M – $10M exposure | Major protocol disruption, difficult recovery | Serious reputational damage |
| Critical | >$10M exposure | Protocol-wide failure, catastrophic impact | Severe reputational damage |

When a Multisig falls between two classification levels, the higher security classification must be selected.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to assign an impact level from exposure-based tiers and submit it to Core GovOps during registration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Financial exposure has numeric dollar bands ($100k, $1M, $10M) and a tie-break rule, but the Decision Context and Reputational Impact columns are qualitative, and 'direct exposure' is undefined. A defender could argue the classification may follow any column, so the operative criteria are partly delegated.
metrics: Low: <$100k direct exposure
Medium: $100k – $1M exposure
High: $1M – $10M exposure
Critical: >$10M exposure
When a Multisig falls between two classification levels, the higher security classification must be selected
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can examine the classification submitted with Multisig registration and assess penalties for misreporting, which plausibly reaches a misclassification. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the paragraph attaches no direct consequence to the classification itself.

assessments.title: Operational Assessment
assessments.quote:
Operational Assessment defines the assessment process in which the operational response requirements of a Multisig are evaluated. The result of this evaluation is the assignment of an Operational Classification type as defined below. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for determining this classification and must provide it to Core GovOps as part of the Multisig registration process in accordance with [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.8 - Multisig Registration](110614e9-6375-464a-90b3-3b350d3cf79c).

| **Operational Classification Type** | **Response Time** | **Decision Context** | **Verification Process** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routine | 24 - 48 hours | Standard procedures, predictable operations | Full verification protocols |
| Time-Sensitive | 2 - 12 hours | Market conditions, protocol needs | Streamlined but thorough |
| Emergency | <2 hours | Crisis response, preventing immediate damage | Minimal delays, risk-appropriate |

When a Multisig falls between two classification levels, the higher security classification must be selected.
assessments.description: Defines Multisig operational classifications with response times and verification levels, and requires the higher level when a Multisig falls between two.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Response-time bands (24-48h, 2-12h, <2h) are numeric, but the criteria for assigning a classification are qualitative ("standard procedures", "market conditions", "crisis response"). Verification depth ("streamlined but thorough", "risk-appropriate") is unquantified, and the paragraph gives no cadence for the Administrator's submission beyond registration.
metrics: Routine response time: 24 - 48 hours
Time-Sensitive response time: 2 - 12 hours
Emergency response time: <2 hours
When between two levels, the higher security classification must be selected
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The classification is submitted to Core GovOps at registration, so scheduled Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could catch a misclassified Multisig against the stated response times. No quantified penalty applies to this rule, and no mechanism enforces the response times at runtime.

assessments.title: Threshold Requirements
assessments.quote:
The baseline minimum threshold standards applicable to all Multisigs are:

- Multisigs must have a minimum of three (3) signers.
- Multisigs must maintain a signing threshold of at least fifty percent (50%) of total signers.

These requirements apply unless explicitly exempted in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.2 - Threshold Exceptions](130a44af-0715-4aa6-b248-f4a267ebe1a4).

Additional threshold requirements or considerations may apply depending on the specific operational use case of the Multisig. Such requirements are defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.3 - Additional Use-Case Specific Threshold Requirements And Considerations](5af1115e-5155-449a-829d-6e641af49b0f).
assessments.description: Sets baseline multisig rules: at least three signers and a signing threshold of at least 50% of total signers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Both core obligations carry explicit numeric thresholds (three signers; 50% of total signers) that a third party could check from the text. Exemptions and use-case requirements are deferred to linked sections, and no measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: Minimum of three (3) signers per Multisig
Signing threshold of at least fifty percent (50%) of total signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever signer count and threshold are configured, not the stated minimums, so a mismatch is caught only by scheduled Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7). Poor multisig practice can also raise a Prime's insurance fees via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c), but no quantified penalty attaches to this rule specifically, so mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Threshold Exceptions
assessments.quote:
Threshold Exceptions define the limited circumstances under which Multisigs may operate below the baseline threshold requirements defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98).

Exceptions may be permitted by Core GovOps, in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. Examples include rate-setting or parameter adjustment operations where parameters are tightly bounded and set by governance, and where a defined recovery or replacement mechanism exists in the event of Multisig failure or compromise.

Certain Threshold Exceptions instead apply as standing exemptions to a defined category of Multisig, without requiring a case-by-case grant. These are specified in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Defines when Multisigs may operate below baseline thresholds, via Core GovOps grants or standing exemptions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes an exception process, but the operative criteria are judgment-based: 'limited circumstances', 'tightly bounded', and a 'defined recovery or replacement mechanism'. No threshold values, deadlines, or metrics are stated, and the baseline and standing exemptions are delegated to other documents.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, third-party review with published outcomes and penalty assessment that could catch Multisigs operating below threshold without a grant or outside a standing exemption. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the paragraph itself states no enforcement path.

assessments.title: Emergency-Response Multisig Threshold Exception
assessments.quote: As a transitionary measure, pending the development of specific threshold requirements for emergency-response Multisigs, a Multisig whose sole capability is an emergency-response function — such as an emergency freeze, pause, or the removal of a compromised Relayer — that cannot move, custody, or allocate assets, is not subject to the minimum signer or signing-threshold requirements specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98). Such a Multisig is configured to optimize for rapid emergency response.
assessments.description: Exempts emergency-only multisigs that cannot move or allocate assets from the standard minimum signer and threshold requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The exemption criteria are concrete: the Multisig's sole capability must be emergency response and it must be unable to move, custody, or allocate assets. However, the 'such as' list is open-ended, 'optimize for rapid emergency response' is qualitative, and the actual threshold magnitudes are delegated to the cross-referenced threshold paragraph and a future specification.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could check whether a Multisig claiming this exemption actually holds only emergency capabilities and cannot move assets, with staged findings and penalty assessment. The consequence is not quantified for this exemption, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the capability restriction.

assessments.title: Additional Use-Case Specific Threshold Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote: Additional threshold requirements and considerations may apply depending on the specific operational use case of the Multisig. These requirements supplement the baseline threshold requirements defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98).
assessments.description: States that additional multisig threshold requirements may apply by use case, supplementing the baseline threshold requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states no threshold, metric, or deadline. It only says requirements 'may apply' and refers to a baseline defined elsewhere, so there is nothing concrete to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph creates no operative requirement that any mechanism would enforce, and the cross-referenced baseline is outside this text.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Control Multisig Threshold Consideration
assessments.quote: Higher signing thresholds should be used for operations involving contract upgrades or significant protocol changes. As a general guideline, thresholds equivalent to at least seven of nine (7/9) signers, or an equivalent supermajority, should be used where feasible. Lower thresholds may be acceptable for highly constrained operations where execution scope is limited by on-chain parameter bounds.
assessments.description: Recommends supermajority signing thresholds, around 7 of 9, for contract upgrades and significant protocol changes, with exceptions for constrained operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete figure (7 of 9 signers) but frames it as a general guideline using 'should', 'where feasible', and 'or an equivalent supermajority'. A defender could argue it does not bind, and 'highly constrained operations' is undefined, so the tie-breaker caps this at 2.
metrics: Signing threshold of at least seven of nine (7/9) signers, or an equivalent supermajority, for contract upgrades and significant protocol changes
Lower thresholds permitted for highly constrained operations with execution scope limited by on-chain parameter bounds
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment, and it could catch a multisig configured below the 7/9 guideline for upgrade operations. The guideline is soft and no consequence is quantified for this specific rule, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: High-Value Asset Multisig Threshold Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisigs managing assets with a value equal to or greater than one million USD ($1,000,000) equivalent must have no fewer than seven (7) signers. This requirement applies to custodial control of assets, not emergency freeze functions.
assessments.description: Requires multisigs holding assets worth $1M or more to have at least seven signers, excluding emergency freeze multisigs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives an exact dollar threshold ($1,000,000) and an exact minimum signer count (7), and clearly scopes custodial control versus freeze functions. Minor gaps remain: the 'equivalent' valuation method and the cadence for re-checking asset value are not defined.
metrics: Asset value >= $1,000,000 USD equivalent
Minimum of 7 signers for custodial multisigs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe contract enforces whatever signer configuration is set, not the stated minimum, so a shortfall is only caught by Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which provides staged findings and penalty assessment. No on-chain mechanism or quantified consequence specific to this signer count was found.

assessments.title: Module Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisigs must not utilize any modules or guards, except those explicitly permitted for the applicable use case in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2 - Use-Case Specific Configuration Requirements And Considerations](f8d0e4df-acca-4f20-a030-584efb4a8695).
assessments.description: Prohibits multisigs from using modules or guards unless the use-case configuration section permits them.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The prohibition is categorical and checkable, with multisigs as the defined actor. However, the permitted exceptions are delegated to a linked section (A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2), so whether a given module or guard is allowed cannot be determined from this paragraph alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can inspect deployed multisig configurations against the permitted-module list and assess penalties, with the reviewer distinct from the multisig operator. No quantified consequence is stated for this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism blocks enabling an unpermitted module or guard.

assessments.title: Treasury Multisig Configuration Requirements
assessments.quote: Treasury Multisigs must use an allowance module that grants the Sky Pause Proxy allowance equal to the maximum amount of each token held by the Multisig.
assessments.description: Requires Treasury Multisigs to use an allowance module granting the Sky Pause Proxy allowance equal to each held token's maximum amount.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Treasury Multisigs), a specific grantee (Sky Pause Proxy), and a formula (allowance equal to the maximum amount of each token held). It lacks a definition or measurement period for "maximum amount" and any verification cadence.
metrics: Sky Pause Proxy allowance equals the maximum amount of each token held by the Multisig
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No on-chain mechanism enforces the allowance configuration. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can catch a non-compliant multisig configuration and assess penalties, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Capital Allocation Multisig Configuration Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote: Capital Allocation Multisigs should implement on-chain constraints wherever feasible, including, but not limited to, smart contract limits or parameter bounds.
assessments.description: Recommends that Capital Allocation Multisigs implement on-chain constraints, such as contract limits or parameter bounds, where feasible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real but non-binding obligation using 'should' and 'wherever feasible' with an open-ended 'including, but not limited to' list. It names no threshold, metric, or deadline, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The text states no rate limit or role requirement that the Rate Limiter or Liquidity Layer roles would reach, and no enforcer or consequence is named. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Control Multisig Configuration Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote:
For Multisigs responsible for smart contract control, the following requirements apply:

- Major contract changes, including, but not limited to, upgrades or significant parameter changes, must be subject to timelock contracts or equivalent delay mechanisms where feasible.
- Protocol parameters controlled by Multisigs must be bounded through smart contract enforcement where feasible.
assessments.description: Requires timelocks or delay mechanisms for major contract changes and smart-contract bounds on parameters controlled by Multisigs, where feasible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names two concrete controls (timelocks for major changes, smart-contract bounds on parameters) but gives no delay duration, parameter bounds, or measurable scope. "Where feasible" appears twice and "including, but not limited to" leaves the covered changes open, so a defender could argue the obligation does not bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check whether multisig configurations and contract-control setups meet these requirements, with penalty assessment. Emergency Spells could freeze or pause when a security rule is violated or threatened. Neither consequence is quantified for this rule, and the "where feasible" qualifiers weaken any finding of breach.

assessments.title: Standard Threshold Recommendations
assessments.quote:
Standard Thresholds refer to recommended Multisig threshold configurations based on use case, Impact Classification level (as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.1 - Impact Assessment](3c0847fe-e117-40f8-86a3-9de56c9a3bba)), and Operational Classification type (as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a)). These standards serve as guidance to the Multisig Administrator during Multisig setup.

| **Use Case** | **Impact Classification Level** | **Operational Classification Type** | **Standard Threshold** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treasury - Large | High | Routine | 4/7 |
| Treasury - Small | Medium | Routine | 3/5 |
| Emergency Freeze | Critical | Emergency | 2/4 |
| Capital Allocation | High | Time-Sensitive | 3/5 |
| Protocol Parameters | High | Routine | 4/7 |
| Constrained DeFi | Medium | Time-Sensitive | 2/3 |
assessments.description: Recommends Multisig threshold configurations by use case, impact level, and operational type, as setup guidance for administrators.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The table gives exact m/n thresholds for six use case, impact, and operational combinations, so the values are quantified. However, the paragraph states they serve only as guidance during setup, so a defender could plausibly argue both compliance and non-binding status, which caps the score at 2.
metrics: Treasury - Large (High, Routine): 4/7
Treasury - Small (Medium, Routine): 3/5
Emergency Freeze (Critical, Emergency): 2/4
Capital Allocation (High, Time-Sensitive): 3/5
Protocol Parameters (High, Routine): 4/7
Constrained DeFi (Medium, Time-Sensitive): 2/3
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Safe enforces whatever threshold is actually configured, not the recommended one, and no artifact review, penalty, or emergency mechanism is tied to deviating from this guidance. Only the misalignment catch-all would reach it.

assessments.title: Backup Interface Setup Recommendations
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator should ensure that alternative Multisig user interfaces are available to signers in the event that the primary interface becomes unavailable. These interfaces should ideally be accessible through independent infrastructure and may include self-hosted or locally runnable alternatives where available.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure alternative signer interfaces exist if the primary interface fails, ideally on independent infrastructure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real obligation (ensure alternative interfaces are available) is stated, but it relies on judgment language such as "should ensure" and "ideally" and "where available". No threshold, count, test, cadence, or verifiable criterion is given, so a defender could argue it does not bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain or contract mechanism enforces interface availability, and no capital-at-risk, penalty, or priced incentive attaches to it. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops reach it.

assessments.title: RPC Redundancy Recommendations
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator should maintain access to multiple RPC providers for each supported network to help preserve operational continuity if a primary provider becomes unavailable. Where possible, RPC providers should be selected to minimize shared infrastructure dependencies.
assessments.description: Recommends the Multisig Administrator keep access to multiple RPC providers per network and diversify their infrastructure where possible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: It names a defined actor and a real obligation, but uses recommendation language ('should', 'where possible') with no provider count, uptime target, or dependency-overlap metric. A defender could argue either compliance or non-binding status on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a non-binding recommendation with no rate limit, role gate, penalty, or artifact review that reaches it. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops could apply.

assessments.title: Communication Setup
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator is responsible for establishing and maintaining communication channels and communication readiness in accordance with the requirements defined in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Assigns the Multisig Administrator responsibility for establishing and maintaining communication channels and readiness, per subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor and an obligation but states no threshold, metric, cadence, or channel specification. Its only operative content is a deferral to subdocuments that are not in the text, so there is nothing concrete to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism directly reaches a duty to establish communication channels; artifact review and misalignment reporting are generic backstops that do not target this obligation.

assessments.title: Primary Communication Channel Requirement
assessments.quote: A dedicated communication channel must be established for Multisig operations. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for ensuring that the channel is restricted to Multisig signers and authorized participants and supports reliable and timely operational communication and coordination between participants.
assessments.description: Requires a dedicated, signer-restricted communication channel for Multisig operations, administered by the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real: a dedicated channel must exist and be restricted to signers and authorized participants. However, 'reliable and timely' communication has no latency, uptime, or response metric, and no cadence or verification method is stated, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could check whether a dedicated, signer-restricted channel exists as part of multisig security guidelines, with the enforcer distinct from the Administrator. No quantified penalty is defined for this rule, and nothing contract-enforced reaches channel restriction or timeliness.

assessments.title: Backup Communication Channel Requirement
assessments.quote: A backup communication channel, established on a different platform from the primary communication channel, must be established to maintain communication continuity in the event the primary channel becomes unavailable. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for ensuring that the backup channel follows the same access and participation constraints as the primary channel.
assessments.description: Requires a backup communication channel on a different platform from the primary, with the Multisig Administrator ensuring matching access and participation constraints.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The different-platform requirement is objectively checkable, and the Multisig Administrator is a named actor. However, there is no deadline, no measure of continuity, and the 'same access and participation constraints' refer to primary-channel constraints that are not defined in this paragraph.
metrics: Backup channel must be established on a different platform from the primary communication channel
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, penalty, or review mechanism is tied to backup channel setup or constraint parity; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Emergency Communication Readiness Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisig Administrators are responsible for ensuring that Multisigs classified with an Emergency or Time-Sensitive Operational Classification level, as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a), maintain communication and alerting mechanisms capable of reliably and rapidly reaching signers, enabling timely execution of required actions in accordance with the operational response expectations of the Multisig. Multisig Administrators must also include Signers in the approved Emergency Response contact mechanisms as specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5).
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to keep alerting channels reaching signers of emergency-classified multisigs and to enroll signers in approved emergency contact mechanisms.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations are named and actors are defined, but no numeric response time, delivery rate, or cadence is stated. 'Reliably and rapidly reaching signers' is judgment language, and the classification and contact-mechanism lists are defined by reference to other paragraphs without values here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps is a scheduled review by a party distinct from the Multisig Administrators, with staged findings and penalty assessment, and it could check whether contact mechanisms and signer enrollment exist. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Communication Access Removal Requirement
assessments.quote: Any signer removed from a Multisig must be promptly removed from all Multisig communication channels and communication systems associated with that Multisig, including primary and backup communication channels. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for ensuring that access is limited to current authorized participants.
assessments.description: Requires prompt removal of departed signers from all Multisig communication channels, with the Multisig Administrator responsible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Multisig Administrator) and scope (primary and backup channels) are defined, but "promptly" has no deadline or measurement, and "current authorized participants" is not verifiable from the text. A defender could plausibly argue either compliance or non-compliance on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can examine whether a Multisig's communication access matches its current signers, with staged findings and penalty assessment, and it is enforced by a body other than the actor. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and the review must be triggered, so it rates mid.

assessments.title: Signer Security Check
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that all Multisig signers comply with the applicable signer security requirements as outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.2 - Signer Security Requirements](3f441562-4c03-429c-8934-f0f87fa0eee7), prior to operational use of the Multisig.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure all signers meet referenced signer security requirements before the Multisig is used operationally.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Multisig Administrator), a gating deadline (prior to operational use), and a cross-referenced requirements document. The operative security criteria are delegated entirely to A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.2, so the rule states what is regulated and when, but not the concrete standards.
metrics: Deadline: prior to operational use of the Multisig
Scope: all Multisig signers must comply with the applicable signer security requirements in A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.2
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a distinct enforcer that could review signer configurations and assess penalties for non-compliance. No quantified consequence attaches to this specific rule, and firing depends on the review being scheduled and the finding escalated, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Multisig Registration
assessments.quote:
All Multisigs currently in use or intended for use within Treasury Management, Emergency Operations (including Freezer or equivalent emergency control Multisigs), Capital Allocation, or Smart Contract Control (including protocol parameter management and constrained DeFi operations) must be registered prior to their inclusion in any Spell or governance execution process.

The Multisig Administrator is responsible for communicating all necessary details about the Multisig to Core GovOps for registration in accordance with the information requirements outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.4 - Multisig Registry](4d80cae1-b28a-4907-8d59-2ebcbba6003d). Core GovOps must coordinate with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to obtain approval prior to completing the registration.
assessments.description: Requires in-scope multisigs to be registered with Core GovOps, with Security Workstream approval, before any Spell use.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors (Multisig Administrator, Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and a verifiable sequencing gate (registration before Spell inclusion). However, the required registration details are delegated to the separate Multisig Registry section, and the approval criteria are unstated.
metrics: Registration must occur prior to inclusion in any Spell or governance execution process
Core GovOps must obtain Protocol Security Workstream Lead approval prior to completing registration
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check whether Spell artifacts reference unregistered multisigs, with an enforcer distinct from the actor and penalty assessment. The consequence for an unregistered multisig is not quantified, and escalation depends on review being triggered.

assessments.title: Signer Verification Process
assessments.quote: Multisig signers must verify their addresses prior to being added to a Multisig. The documents herein define the processes and requirements related to the Signer Verification Process.
assessments.description: Requires multisig signers to verify their addresses before being added to a Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real obligation (verify before addition) but gives no verification method, verifier, or criteria, and defers the process to unspecified 'documents herein'. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain control or named enforcer checks signer verification, and the paragraph defines no process for artifact review or penalty to reach.

assessments.title: Verification Signature
assessments.description: Requires each Multisig signer to cryptographically prove control of their address and state intent, Multisig address, and identity in the signed message.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates four required message components (intent statement, Multisig address, signer address, identifying affiliation), which a third party could check. However, the identity element is only required to be "sufficient to establish accountability," a judgment standard with no defined criteria, and no cryptographic scheme or verification method is specified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can examine Multisig signer onboarding artifacts and assess penalties, so a missing or noncompliant signed message could be surfaced there. The escalation and penalty amount are not defined for this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it.

assessments.title: Verification Submission
assessments.quote: The verification signature must be shared with the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.description: Requires the verification signature to be shared with the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (Multisig Administrator) and a concrete step, but gives no deadline, cadence, or format for sharing. The term 'verification signature' is not defined in the paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, independent review with published findings and penalty assessment, and it can plausibly catch a missing signature share. No quantified consequence attaches to this specific rule, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Signer Security Requirements
assessments.quote:
Multisig signers must comply with the following security requirements:

- All Multisig signers must use hardware wallets for signing operations. The associated seed phrase must be securely backed up using physical, offline storage methods only. Seed phrases must never be stored digitally, including in photographs, files, password managers, cloud storage, email, or messaging applications. Seed phrase backups must be stored on durable offline media and kept in secure physical locations with appropriate access controls to prevent unauthorized access or single-point compromise.
- Signers must use a unique signing address per Multisig and must not reuse the same signing address across Multisigs.
- Signers participating in Multisigs responsible for critical protocol configuration or security-sensitive operations should not use their signing addresses for personal transactions or other unrelated activities and should instead use a dedicated address created specifically for Multisig participation.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig signers to use hardware wallets, offline seed backups, and unique or dedicated signing addresses.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The seed-phrase bullet names concrete prohibited storage media and offline requirements, and the address bullet is objectively checkable. However, "appropriate access controls" is undefined, and the third bullet uses non-binding "should" with an undefined scope ("critical protocol configuration or security-sensitive operations").
metrics: Signers must use hardware wallets for signing operations
Seed phrases must be backed up using physical, offline storage only, never digitally
Signing address must be unique per Multisig and not reused across Multisigs
Signers in critical or security-sensitive Multisigs should use a dedicated Multisig address, not for personal or unrelated activity
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. No mechanism reaches an individual signer's seed-phrase storage or address reuse. Emergency Spells could respond to a threatened security rule, but nothing in the paragraph or catalog detects these off-chain signer practices, so no enforcement path is evident.

assessments.title: Signer Rotation Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisig signers may be rotated as operational or security requirements evolve. All signer rotations must be communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead by the Multisig Administrator, accompanied by clear documentation describing the reason for the change, the outgoing signer, and the incoming signer.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to notify the Protocol Security Workstream Lead of every signer rotation with reason and signer details.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor, recipient, and three required documentation elements, so the obligation is concrete. However, the trigger is qualitative ('as operational or security requirements evolve') and no communication deadline or cadence is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) can check the actual multisig signer roster against the documented rotations and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches an unreported rotation. Nothing on-chain enforces the notification requirement, and no quantified consequence is attached to this rule.

assessments.title: Signer Composition Documentation Requirement
assessments.quote: Any change to Multisig signer composition must be promptly communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead by the Multisig Administrator, including all updated signer addresses.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to promptly notify the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, with updated addresses, of any signer composition change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Multisig Administrator), recipient role, and content (updated signer addresses) are concrete and checkable. The timing is only "promptly", with no numeric deadline, so the operative magnitude is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) could compare the recorded signer set against the on-chain Safe configuration and flag an unreported change, with staged findings and penalty assessment. No mechanism quantifies a consequence specifically for late or missing notification, and the review must be triggered to fire.

assessments.title: Threshold Preservation Requirement
assessments.quote: Signer rotations must not reduce the total number of signers or decrease the signing threshold unless the Multisig Administrator provides a clear operational or security justification that is submitted to and approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.description: Prohibits reducing multisig signer count or signing threshold during rotations unless justified and approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core prohibition is verifiable: total signer count and signing threshold may not decrease during a rotation. The exception depends on a 'clear operational or security justification' with no defined criteria, and there is no cadence or record requirement.
metrics: Total number of signers must not decrease on signer rotation
Signing threshold must not decrease on signer rotation
Exception requires justification submitted to and approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can examine the deployed multisig signer set and threshold against this rule, with a named enforcer distinct from the Multisig Administrator. The consequence for a non-compliant rotation is not quantified for this rule, and review must be triggered.

assessments.title: Signer Offboarding Requirements
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that signers are offboarded in accordance with the procedures outlined in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure signers are offboarded per procedures defined in referenced documents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named actor and a real obligation are stated, but no threshold, deadline, or criteria appear; the operative procedure is delegated to unspecified 'documents herein'. Compliance is arguable on the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can check multisig signer configuration against the offboarding procedures, with staged findings and penalty assessment by a party distinct from the Administrator. The consequence is unquantified for this rule and depends on the review being run, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Signer Removal
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must coordinate with the remaining signers to execute a signer removal transaction in accordance with the Multisig's standard signer rotation procedures. After execution, the Multisig Administrator must verify that the departing signer's address has been removed from the Multisig and that the change is appropriately communicated and documented as outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.1.2 - Signer Composition Documentation Requirement](2d434d95-a892-404f-9e59-216dce97ce89).
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to coordinate and verify removal of a departing signer, then document the change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Multisig Administrator) and the verification step (confirming the departing signer's address is removed) are concrete and checkable on-chain. However, the procedure is delegated to undefined "standard signer rotation procedures", and there is no deadline or cadence. "Appropriately communicated and documented" is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Safe enforces whatever signer set is actually configured, not the documented one, so a removal that was not completed or documented is plausibly caught by Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7). No quantified consequence is attached to this specific rule, so it stops at mid.

assessments.title: Access Revocation And Handover
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the departing signer relinquishes access to all Multisig-related communication channels, shared resources, and sensitive operational systems. Any locally stored sensitive Multisig information must be securely deleted. Departing signers should provide relevant operational context, including any pending actions or responsibilities, to the remaining signers to support a smooth transition.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure departing signers lose access, delete local multisig data, and hand over pending context.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations are real and identifiable (revoke access to all channels, securely delete local data, provide handover context), but no deadline, cadence, or verifiable standard is given. Terms like "securely deleted" and "relevant operational context" are judgment language, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can examine whether the Multisig Administrator revoked access and handed over responsibilities, with staged findings and penalty assessment. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and the review must be triggered, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Multisig Signer Composition Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote:
The signer requirements and considerations applicable to Multisigs classified with a Time-Sensitive or Emergency Operational Classification level, as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a), are as follows:

- Emergency Response Multisigs must maintain 24/7 availability of a number of signers equal to or greater than the Multisig signing threshold.
- Geographic distribution of signers is encouraged for Emergency Response Multisigs where appropriate to support 24/7 operational coverage.
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Multisigs to keep at least as many signers available 24/7 as the signing threshold, and encourages geographic signer distribution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: available signers must be at least the signing threshold, on a 24/7 basis. Gaps include no measurement method or cadence for proving 24/7 availability, and the geographic-distribution bullet is only 'encouraged ... where appropriate'.
metrics: Number of available signers must be greater than or equal to the Multisig signing threshold
Signer availability must be maintained 24/7
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could catch a signer shortfall. Nothing quantifies a consequence for this specific rule, and the Safe itself does not enforce signer availability, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Capital Allocation Multisig Signer Composition Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that all signers participating in Capital Allocation Multisigs (Multisigs responsible for allocating or reallocating capital) possess sufficient protocol expertise.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure Capital Allocation Multisig signers have sufficient protocol expertise.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A defined actor and scope are named, but 'sufficient protocol expertise' is judgment language with no criteria, test, or verification method. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism reaches a subjective expertise standard. Artifact review could check signer composition but has no criteria to test against, and the only general backstop is the misalignment catch-all.

assessments.title: Incident Reporting
assessments.quote: Incident Reporting defines the procedures governing the reporting of security incidents, operational issues, and security-relevant events relating to Multisig operations.
assessments.description: States that procedures will govern reporting of security incidents and operational events for Multisig operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph only asserts that procedures exist and names event categories. It states no reporting deadline, recipient, threshold, or steps, so there is nothing concrete to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism reaches this rule. The only applicable path is the Reports of Misalignment catch-all, which is always weak on its own.

assessments.title: Security Incidents
assessments.quote:
Security incidents must be reported immediately upon discovery, in accordance with the process outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.2 - Emergency Incident Reporting Process](56e44cdc-1ba5-4254-9308-c4cfe189394a). Security incidents include, but are not limited to:

- Signing key compromise or suspected compromise
- Account takeover of email or communication platforms used for Multisig operations
- Device theft or loss involving signing or operational access
- Suspicious or unauthorized activity on Multisig accounts
- Phishing attempts targeting Multisig operations
- Compromise or suspected infiltration of communication channels used for Multisig coordination
assessments.description: Requires immediate reporting of listed Multisig security incidents through the Emergency Incident Reporting Process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names a defined process, but 'immediately upon discovery' has no numeric deadline or cadence. The incident list uses 'include, but are not limited to' with no criteria for what counts as 'suspected' or 'suspicious', so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Report immediately upon discovery
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The in-text Emergency Incident Reporting Process (56e44cdc) routes incidents into the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d), a defined escalation protocol outside the normal governance cycle that can trigger pre-authorized responses. No penalty is quantified for late or missing reports, and escalation depends on someone making the report, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Operational Issues
assessments.quote:
Operational issues must be reported within 24 hours of discovery, in accordance with the process outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.3 - Standard Incident Reporting Process](ec4cd423-74ba-4e74-82d9-46ba5f6cf526). Operational issues include, but are not limited to:

- Loss of access to signing keys or signing devices
- Hardware wallet or backup device failure
- Communication channel failures affecting Multisig coordination
- Verification tool malfunctions
- Operational difficulties preventing adherence to security procedures
assessments.description: Requires operational issues affecting signing and multisig coordination to be reported within 24 hours of discovery.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 24-hour deadline from discovery is concrete and checkable. However, the reporting actor is not named, the list of issues is open-ended ('not limited to'), and the procedure is delegated to a cross-referenced process, so what counts as reportable remains partly judgment-based.
metrics: Operational issues must be reported within 24 hours of discovery
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The cross-referenced Standard Incident Reporting Process (ec4cd423) defines how to report but not any consequence for late or missed reports. Only the generic Reports of Misalignment backstop reaches this duty, and that alone is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Incident Reporting Process
assessments.quote:
When an emergency incident occurs, the following steps must be completed:

- The reporting signer must take immediate actions to secure the situation and prevent further risk, including isolating affected devices or systems where appropriate.
- The reporting signer must notify the Multisig Administrator and other participants through the primary communication channel.
- The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the reporting signer immediately reports the incident to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, following the documentation requirements outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.2.1 - Emergency Incident Documentation Requirements](6d6e7b53-8fcb-4ecb-8428-e07f682d13d4).
- The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the reporting signer follows up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgment is received within 24 hours.
assessments.description: Sets steps after an emergency incident: securing systems, notifying the Multisig Administrator, reporting to the Security Workstream Lead, and following up within 24 hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named and one deadline is stated (24 hours without acknowledgment), but the core obligation to act 'immediately' and isolate systems 'where appropriate' is qualitative. The documentation requirements are delegated to a separate cross-referenced paragraph.
metrics: Follow up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgment is received within 24 hours
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System provides a defined escalation protocol for emergencies, and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could check whether the reporting steps were followed. Neither consequence is quantified for this paragraph, and escalation depends on someone raising the matter.

assessments.title: Emergency Incident Documentation Requirements
assessments.quote:
All emergency incident reports must include sufficient documentation to allow review, follow-up, and operational learning. At minimum, security incident documentation must include:

- Multisig details and classification
- Incident type
- Time of incident occurrence and discovery
- Reporting signer
- Description of the incident
- Immediate actions taken
- Next steps required
- Current Multisig status
- Impact
assessments.description: Requires emergency security incident reports to include nine enumerated documentation fields, including multisig details, timing, and impact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The nine required fields are enumerated and checkable for presence, but the governing standard is "sufficient documentation to allow review, follow-up, and operational learning," which is judgment language. No deadline, reporting cadence, or criteria define "classification" or "sufficient," so a defender could plausibly argue compliance either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can examine incident documentation as artifacts and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches an incomplete incident report. However, the penalty is unquantified for this rule and the review is scheduled rather than triggered per incident.

assessments.title: Standard Incident Reporting Process
assessments.quote:
When a standard incident occurs, the following steps must be completed:

- The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the reporting signer immediately reports the incident to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, following the documentation requirements outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.3.1 - Standard Incident Documentation Requirements](0aec011a-18d2-4945-90b5-8089fa01cefb).
- Follow-up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgment is received within 48 hours.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure signers immediately report standard incidents, with 48-hour follow-up if unacknowledged.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 48-hour acknowledgment follow-up is a concrete, checkable deadline, but "immediately" is unquantified, the incident definition is not in this paragraph, and the documentation content is delegated to a linked section.
metrics: Follow-up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgment is received within 48 hours
Reporting signer reports the incident "immediately"
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or on-chain control attaches to late or missing incident reports; the only generic backstop is the Reports Of Misalignment catch-all, and the Administrator policing the reporting signer is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Standard Incident Documentation Requirements
assessments.quote:
All standard incident reports must include, at minimum, the following information:

- Multisig details and classification
- Incident type
- Time of incident occurrence and discovery
- Reporting signer
- Description of the incident
- Immediate actions taken
- Current Multisig status
- Impact
assessments.description: Requires standard multisig incident reports to include eight specified information fields, at minimum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names eight concrete required fields, so a third party could check whether each appears in a report. It sets no deadline, reporting cadence, or criteria for adequacy, such as what counts as a sufficient description or impact.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Omitting required report fields triggers no contract-enforced, penalty, or review path in the catalog, and the Risk-Capital Incident Response and artifact review mechanisms do not clearly reach multisig incident documentation. Only the misalignment catch-all applies.

assessments.title: Training And Operational Readiness
assessments.quote: Multisig Administrators must ensure that signers maintain sufficient operational expertise through ongoing training and familiarity with the Multisig's procedures. This includes, but is not limited to, training and periodic review of transaction verification practices, operational procedures, and incident response processes applicable to the Multisig's function.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to keep signers trained and familiar with transaction verification, operational, and incident response procedures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names an actor and enumerated training areas, but 'sufficient' expertise, 'periodic' review, and the 'not limited to' catch-all have no cadence, criteria, or verifiable standard. A defender could argue any training program satisfies it.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism verifies signer training or expertise; Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) examines configurations and artifacts, not signer competence, and the catch-all mechanisms alone are weak.

assessments.title: Backup Infrastructure Readiness Requirements
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that signers are prepared to operate using backup infrastructure. This includes providing signers with access to offline or alternative Multisig interfaces, verifying that signers have practiced using backup interfaces, testing backup RPC providers during non-emergency periods, and maintaining documented procedures describing how to switch to backup infrastructure when required.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to prepare signers for backup infrastructure through alternative interfaces, practice, RPC testing, and documented switchover procedures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete actions (alternative interfaces, practice verification, RPC testing, documented procedures) but sets no frequency, threshold, or pass criteria. 'Ensure', 'prepared', and 'verifying that signers have practiced' are judgment language, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: RPC provider testing performed during non-emergency periods
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain, or artifact-review mechanism is tied to Multisig Administrator readiness duties; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops reach it.

assessments.title: Emergency Operations Training And Readiness Requirement
assessments.quote:
Multisig Administrators are responsible for ensuring that Multisigs classified with a Time-Sensitive or Emergency Operational Classification level, as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a), maintain operational readiness appropriate to their function.

To satisfy this requirement, Multisig Administrators must ensure that the following activities are conducted:

- Periodic operational drills
- Quarterly testing of emergency communication and alerting systems to ensure continued reliability
- Semi-annual paging system tests to verify alert functionality
- An annual full emergency simulation involving all signers

The Multisig Administrator must document the completion and outcome of all required readiness activities and provide testing reports and confirmation of completion to Core GovOps.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to run drills and scheduled emergency tests for time-sensitive multisigs and report results to Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Quarterly, semi-annual, and annual cadences are stated for specific activities, but 'periodic operational drills' has no cadence or scope, 'appropriate to their function' is qualitative, and no deadline is set for submitting reports to Core GovOps. The operative obligations are partly quantified and partly delegated.
metrics: Quarterly testing of emergency communication and alerting systems
Semi-annual paging system tests
Annual full emergency simulation involving all signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The required reports to Core GovOps feed the Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7), which is a scheduled review by a distinct enforcer with penalty assessment, and penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly apply to Operational Agents. However, no consequence is quantified for this readiness rule and review firing depends on Core GovOps escalating.

assessments.title: Signer Address Update Process
assessments.quote: Any update to a Multisig signer address must be performed in accordance with the process defined in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Requires any Multisig signer address update to follow the process defined in its subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a cross-reference with no operative criteria, thresholds, steps, or deadlines of its own. The actual process lives in subdocuments that are not part of this text, so there is nothing measurable to comply with here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled, third-party review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could catch a signer change made outside the defined process. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and the review must actually reach signer changes, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Signer Address Update Process If Original Key Is Accessible
assessments.quote:
If the original key of the signer address that needs to be changed remains accessible, the following steps must be completed by the signer:

- The signer authorizes the address change by signing a message with the existing signer address. The signed message must clearly state the intent to replace the existing signer address with the new address.
- The signer must follow the steps defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Signer Verification Process](002821ab-c67c-4eb1-987c-69e759ab7b3c) prior to the new address being added to the Multisig.
assessments.description: Requires a signer with an accessible key to sign an intent message with the existing address and complete signer verification before a replacement address is added.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete steps (signing with the existing address, stating intent, completing the referenced verification process before addition), but the message content is qualitative ("clearly state the intent") and the verification criteria are delegated to another document. No timing or cadence is given.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review multisig signer changes against this process and assess penalties. Nothing on-chain enforces the off-chain signed-message step, and the consequence is not quantified for this rule, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Signer Address Update Process If Original Key Is Lost Or Inaccessible
assessments.quote:
If the original key of the signer address that needs to be changed is inaccessible, the signer must verify their identity to the remaining signers through alternative verification methods such as:

- Authentication through a verified social media or publicly associated account
- Live verification via video call with existing signers
- Other comparable verification methods

Upon successful identity verification, the signer must follow the steps defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Signer Verification Process](002821ab-c67c-4eb1-987c-69e759ab7b3c) and notify the Multisig Administrator once completed.
assessments.description: Requires a signer who lost access to their key to verify identity to remaining signers via alternative methods, then notify the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named (signer, remaining signers, Multisig Administrator) and a process is referenced, but verification methods are open-ended ('such as', 'other comparable methods') and 'successful identity verification' has no defined criteria. No thresholds, quorum, or deadline for notification, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can examine multisig signer changes and their documentation, and could catch a missing verification or notification, with penalty assessment available. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and the identity check itself is off-chain and not contract-enforced.

assessments.title: Transaction Verification And Signing Requirements
assessments.quote: Multisig signers must verify all transaction data prior to signing in order to reduce the risk of malicious or unintended transactions being executed. The procedures defined in the documents herein establish the relevant transaction verification processes for supported execution environments.
assessments.description: Requires multisig signers to verify all transaction data before signing, deferring the specific procedures to other documents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real obligation (signers must verify all transaction data before signing) but gives no checklist, threshold, cadence, or verification criteria. The operative procedures are delegated to unspecified documents, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Signer verification conduct is not observable on-chain, and no listed mechanism reaches it. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could check whether written procedures exist, but it does not verify that individual signers followed them, so it does not reach this rule's violation modes.

assessments.title: EVM Transaction Verification Requirements
assessments.quote: Multisig signers must verify EVM-based Multisig transactions prior to signing to ensure that the transaction being signed matches the intended operation.
assessments.description: Requires multisig signers to verify EVM multisig transactions before signing that they match the intended operation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names a defined actor (multisig signers) and a timing (before signing), but it gives no verification method, checklist, tooling, or evidence standard. Whether a signer complied on given facts is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Pre-signing verification is signer conduct that does not appear on-chain, and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) can check configuration artifacts but not whether a signer verified a transaction before signing. Only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Transaction Hash Verification
assessments.quote: Signers must verify that the transaction hash displayed on the signing device matches the expected transaction hash derived from the transaction parameters. When signing transactions involving nested Multisigs, the hash displayed on the signing device may correspond to an approval hash rather than the underlying transaction. In such cases, signers must verify both the nested transaction and the parent Multisig approval.
assessments.description: Requires signers to verify the signing device's transaction hash against the expected hash, and to verify nested Multisig approvals separately.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete enumerated steps: compare the displayed hash to the expected hash, and for nested Multisigs verify both the nested transaction and the parent approval. It gives no method for deriving the expected hash, no record-keeping requirement, and no timing, so compliance is checkable only through judgment about how verification was done.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review signing practices and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches a signer who approves a mismatched transaction. The paragraph itself sets no consequence, and the review is not per-transaction, so the reach is partial.

assessments.title: SVM Transaction Verification Requirements
assessments.quote: Multisig signers must verify Solana Virtual Machine (SVM) Multisig transactions prior to signing to ensure that the proposal contains the intended instructions and parameters.
assessments.description: Requires multisig signers to verify SVM multisig transactions contain intended instructions and parameters before signing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A defined actor (multisig signers) and a real pre-signing verification obligation exist, but no threshold, cadence, or verification method is stated. 'Verify ... intended instructions and parameters' is judgment language, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Signers verifying their own transactions is self-enforcement. The Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers Agents rather than multisig signers, and no catalog mechanism reaches a signing failure. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Tooling Limitations
assessments.quote: Verification tooling for SVM Multisig transactions is currently more limited than for EVM environments. Signers should exercise additional caution and may cross-verify transactions with other signers prior to execution.
assessments.description: Notes that SVM multisig verification tooling is weaker than EVM and advises signers to exercise caution and may cross-verify.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real but judgment-based expectation: signers 'should exercise additional caution' and 'may cross-verify'. It has no threshold, cadence, metric, or verifiable criterion, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No signing threshold, access role, or on-chain control is stated, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, rate limit, role gate, or artifact review) plausibly reaches a non-verifiable 'exercise caution' note.

assessments.title: Operational Guides
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead must maintain and make available operational guides to support Multisig Administrators in complying with the requirements specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2 - Multisig Security Guidelines](6033699f-1d55-45ba-8eb1-bd8982571cc0). These guides must cover, at minimum, Multisig registration, signer rotation and replacement, signer onboarding and offboarding, incident reporting, and any other processes where standardized documentation is required. The Protocol Security Workstream Lead is responsible for keeping these guides current and accessible to all Multisig Administrators.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to maintain current operational guides for Multisig Administrators covering listed topics.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The named actor and the minimum list of required guide topics are concrete, but there is no measurement cadence, review deadline, or defined standard for what 'current' or 'accessible' means. Compliance could be argued either way.
metrics: Guides must cover, at minimum: Multisig registration, signer rotation and replacement, signer onboarding and offboarding, incident reporting, and other processes requiring standardized documentation
Guides must be kept current and accessible to all Multisig Administrators (no cadence or deadline stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain or named enforcement path reaches the duty to maintain guides; Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers Agent artifacts rather than this workstream deliverable, and the misalignment backstop alone is weak.

assessments.title: Periodic Review Requirement
assessments.quote:
Core GovOps must engage the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and third party providers to conduct periodic reviews of registered Multisigs to verify that Multisig documentation, configuration, and operational classification remain accurate and aligned with current usage. At minimum:

- Multisig documentation and classification must be reviewed on a quarterly basis.
- Reviews must be conducted following major operational, financial, or structural changes affecting the Multisig.
- Reviews must be conducted when significant protocol changes materially affect the Multisig's role, authority, or risk exposure.
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to periodically review registered Multisigs quarterly and after major or significant changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The quarterly review cadence is a concrete, checkable interval, and the actors are named. However, the event-driven triggers rely on undefined qualitative terms such as 'major', 'significant', and 'materially affect' with no criteria.
metrics: Multisig documentation and classification must be reviewed on a quarterly basis
Reviews must be conducted following major operational, financial, or structural changes affecting the Multisig
Reviews must be conducted when significant protocol changes materially affect the Multisig's role, authority, or risk exposure
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The review obligation is the control itself, and no mechanism attaches a consequence to a missed quarterly or trigger-based review. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers agents rather than Multisig review cadence, and Core GovOps is both the obligated actor and the reviewer, so the enforcement is self-policed.

assessments.title: Review Scope
assessments.quote:
Periodic reviews may include, but are not limited to:

- Verification that Multisig documentation in the Multisig Registry remains accurate and up to date.
- Reassessment of Multisig operational purpose where operational patterns change.
- Reassessment of financial exposure or protocol impact where asset exposure or operational scope changes.
- Verification that Multisig configuration and operational practices remain consistent with the Multisig Security Enforcement Framework.
assessments.description: Lists optional topics that periodic reviews of Multisig documentation, purpose, exposure, and configuration may cover.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The four review topics are concrete, but the leading 'may include, but are not limited to' makes the scope permissive and non-mandatory. No cadence, threshold, or pass/fail criterion is stated, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states optional review scope with no consequence attached. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers Agent artifacts rather than this review scope, and the only reachable backstop is the Reports Of Misalignment catch-all, which is weak alone.

assessments.title: Monitoring Outcome
assessments.quote: Where monitoring or review activities identify inconsistencies, outdated documentation, or potential noncompliance, Core GovOps must proceed in accordance with [A.2.11.1.3.5 - Determination And Enforcement Of Multisig Security Noncompliance](2a36aafa-cfe3-4ba5-b549-f341fbb4c666).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to follow the multisig noncompliance determination and enforcement process when monitoring finds inconsistencies or noncompliance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph creates a real mandatory step (Core GovOps must proceed under A.2.11.1.3.5), but the trigger is judgment-based ("inconsistencies", "potential noncompliance") and no thresholds, deadlines, or metrics appear in the text itself.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph routes identified noncompliance to A.2.11.1.3.5 (UUID 2a36aafa, cited verbatim in the text), a determination and enforcement process run by Core GovOps, an enforcer distinct from the multisig actors. Its consequences are not quantified in this paragraph, and the trigger depends on monitoring surfacing the issue, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Multisig Registry
assessments.quote: All Multisigs must be recorded in the Multisig Registry at [A.2.11.1.3.4.2.0.6.1 - Registered Multisigs](7d966e5e-ecb3-4a5b-9111-a70927cfa79a).
assessments.description: Requires all Multisigs to be recorded in the Multisig Registry, linked to the Registered Multisigs document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is binary and checkable: a multisig either appears in the named registry or it does not. However, the paragraph gives no deadline, cadence, required registry fields, or definition of which multisigs count as 'All', so the operative scope is only partly fixed.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check registry completeness against actual multisigs and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches an unregistered multisig. Nothing is quantified for this rule, and the review only fires when a reviewer examines the registry, so the consequence depends on that review.

assessments.title: Multisig Registry Entry Requirements
assessments.quote:
Each Multisig entry in the Multisig Registry must contain the following information:

- Multisig Name
- Administrator Entity
