- Multisig Address
assessments.description: Requires each Multisig Registry entry to include a name, administrator entity, and multisig address.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The three required fields are concrete and a third party could check an entry for their presence. However, the rule sets no format or validity criteria for the address, no update cadence, and no deadline for registration.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps could reach an incomplete or missing registry entry through scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment. The paragraph does not state a consequence for this rule, and firing depends on the review being applied to the registry.

assessments.title: List Of Registered Multisigs
assessments.quote:
The list of registered Multisigs is defined as Active Data in [A.2.11.1.3.4.2.0.6.1 - Registered Multisigs](7d966e5e-ecb3-4a5b-9111-a70927cfa79a).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is Core GovOps.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for 'Direct Edit'.
assessments.description: Makes Core GovOps responsible for updating the registered multisig list, following the Direct Edit protocol, with the list held as Active Data.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The responsible actor is named (Core GovOps) and an update process is referenced, but the list contents, update cadence, and the 'Direct Edit' protocol steps are all delegated to other documents. No threshold, deadline, or verifiable criterion appears in this paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment, and it can plausibly reach an inaccurate multisig registry. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the list.

assessments.title: Determination And Enforcement Of Multisig Security Noncompliance
assessments.quote: When a Multisig is determined to be noncompliant with the Multisig Security Enforcement Framework, a grace period of forty-eight (48) hours is provided to resolve the issue. If the noncompliance is not resolved within this period, Multisig operations must be immediately stopped, unless an exception is granted by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. Core GovOps may then determine whether further actions are required to enforce the halt of operations in relation to such Multisig. These provisions apply only after the effective date specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2 - Multisig Security Guidelines](6033699f-1d55-45ba-8eb1-bd8982571cc0).
assessments.description: Sets a 48-hour grace period, then requires halting a noncompliant Multisig's operations unless the Protocol Security Workstream Lead grants an exception.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 48-hour grace period and immediate halt are concrete, but the noncompliance determination is undefined in this text. Core GovOps' 'may determine whether further actions are required' is discretionary, so the enforcement magnitude is delegated.
metrics: Grace period of 48 hours to resolve noncompliance
Immediate stop of Multisig operations if noncompliance is unresolved after the grace period
Exception granted by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
Applies only after the effective date in A.2.11.1.3.2
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph names distinct enforcers (Workstream Lead, Core GovOps) and a concrete remedy (halt). Firing depends on the noncompliance determination and on Core GovOps volunteering further action, so the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is cited as the escalation path that plausibly reaches it, without a quantified consequence.

assessments.title: Setting Base Rate
assessments.quote: The Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must set the Base Rate to ensure (1) a sufficient level of Cash Stablecoins and (2) price stability of USDS and other Stablecoins produced by the Sky Ecosystem. The subdocuments herein define the process that the Core Executor Agents should follow in setting the Base Rate.
assessments.description: Requires Core Executor Agents, consulting the Core Council Risk Advisor, to set the Base Rate for cash stablecoin sufficiency and USDS price stability.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named actor and a real obligation are stated, but the operative criteria are judgmental: 'sufficient level' of Cash Stablecoins and 'price stability' have no thresholds, metrics, or cadence. The process is deferred to subdocuments, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism in the catalog is triggered by a failure to set the Base Rate correctly: the Peg Stability Module enforces the peg but not the rate-setting process, and the penalty and conservatorship machinery targets Prime and Operational Agent Risk Capital rules rather than Core Executor duties. Only the misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Adjustment Process
assessments.quote: The Core Executor Agents should modify the Base Rate on a daily basis, as necessary, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor. In doing so, the Core Executor Agents should consider the factors specified in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Directs Core Executor Agents to adjust the Base Rate daily as necessary, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A daily cadence is stated, but the trigger is "as necessary" and the factors to consider are only "specified in the documents herein" with no values. The word "should" also makes compliance arguable either way on the same facts.
metrics: Modify the Base Rate on a daily basis
Modify as necessary (no trigger criteria)
Consult the Core Council Risk Advisor
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a Core Executor Agent's base-rate adjustment: the Rate Limiter covers controller rate limits, not the Base Rate; the PSM does not enforce it; and no penalty, review, or emergency path is tied to this duty. Only the catch-all backstop applies.

assessments.title: Level Of Actively Stabilizing Collateral In Lite PSM
assessments.description: Sets non-binding guidance for Core Executor Agents to adjust the Base Rate based on Lite PSM Actively Stabilizing Collateral share.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The PSM ASC metric and its percentage bands are numerically defined, but the operative verb is "consider" and the adjustments are "approximately" sized, so a defender could argue both compliance and non-binding status. Band boundaries also overlap or leave gaps at exact values (30%, 28%, 26%, 24%, 22%, 20%).
metrics: PSM ASC = Actively Stabilizing Collateral in Lite PSM as a percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio
PSM ASC above 30%: consider decreasing Base Rate by approximately 2%
PSM ASC between 28% and 30%: consider decreasing Base Rate by approximately 1%
PSM ASC between 26% and 28%: consider decreasing Base Rate by approximately 0.3%
PSM ASC between 24% and 26%: consider maintaining Base Rate at approximately its current level
PSM ASC between 22% and 24%: consider increasing Base Rate by approximately 0.3%
PSM ASC between 20% and 22%: consider increasing Base Rate by approximately 1%
PSM ASC below 20%: consider increasing Base Rate by approximately 2%
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The guidelines are expressly non-binding, and no on-chain control, capital-at-risk, priced incentive, or named enforcer attaches to Base Rate decisions based on PSM ASC. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could reach it.

assessments.title: External Rate Environment
assessments.quote: The Core Executor Agents should consider the external interest-rate environment, including the interest rates offered by competitors and funding rates in decentralized finance and traditional finance markets.
assessments.description: Directs Core Executor Agents to consider external interest-rate conditions, including competitor and DeFi/TradFi funding rates, when setting the base rate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names a defined actor and enumerated inputs (competitor rates, DeFi and TradFi funding rates), but uses the non-binding phrase "should consider" with no threshold, metric, cadence, or criteria for how the inputs affect the base rate. Compliance is arguable on any facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The duty is a judgment-based consideration with no on-chain control, penalty, or review path reaching it; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, and self-policing by the executors does not count.

assessments.title: Tools Development
assessments.quote: The Core Executor Agents must develop automated tools to monitor the external interest-rate environment to improve the rate-setting process.
assessments.description: Requires Core Executor Agents to develop automated tools monitoring the external interest-rate environment for rate-setting.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph imposes a real obligation on a named actor to build automated monitoring tools, but gives no specification of tool scope, coverage, deadline, or completion criteria. Compliance is arguable either way, since 'develop' and 'improve' are judgment terms.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or contract-enforced mechanism reaches a failure to develop the tools. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, which are weak alone.

assessments.title: Other Factors
assessments.quote: The Core Executor Agents should consider other factors such as supporting long-term market stability, user stability, system sustainability, and growth. In addition, the Core Executor Agents should consider constraints on Primes, including their cost of capital and reaction time, to avoid creating unnecessary volatility in rates.
assessments.description: Directs Core Executor Agents to weigh stability, user, sustainability, growth, and Prime cost and reaction-time constraints when setting the base rate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: It names a real obligation and enumerates factors for the Core Executor Agents to consider, but uses only judgment language ('should consider') with no thresholds, metrics, cadence, or criteria. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The obligation is non-quantified consideration by Core Executor Agents with no on-chain check, and no penalty, review, or emergency path has a defined test that could reach a failure to weigh these factors. Only the misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Setting Other Core Stability Parameters
assessments.quote: When setting the Base Rate, the Core Executor Agents must also set all other Core Stability Parameters so that they maintain their specified relationship to the Base Rate. See [A.3.1.2 - Parameters](86c75c9c-3803-48c1-a897-88d2be7aeb0e). The only exception is the Dai Savings Rate, which must be gradually reduced to 0% as specified in [A.3.1.2.4.1 - Dai Savings Rate Modification](238d8932-633d-44df-a7ed-0ec5a423cc53).
assessments.description: Requires Core Executor Agents to set other Core Stability Parameters relative to the Base Rate, with the Dai Savings Rate reduced to 0%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor, the Base Rate, and the DSR end state of 0% are concrete, but the required 'specified relationship' between parameters and the Base Rate is delegated to A.3.1.2, and the 'gradual' DSR reduction schedule is defined only in A.3.1.2.4.1 with no cadence stated here.
metrics: Dai Savings Rate must be reduced to 0%
Other Core Stability Parameters maintain their specified relationship to the Base Rate (relationship defined in A.3.1.2, not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check whether Core Executor Agents' parameter-setting artifacts match the required relationships and staged findings could follow, but no quantified penalty is attached to this specific rule. Parameter changes are not contract-enforced against the stated relationship, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Implementation Of Rate Changes
assessments.quote: The smart contracts that implement all of the Core Stability Parameters must be configured to allow the Core Executor Agents to modify the Core Stability Parameters using the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).
assessments.description: Requires Core Stability Parameter contracts to let Core Executor Agents modify parameters through the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actors (Core Executor Agents), the parameter set, and the access mechanism are named, and the configuration requirement is binary and checkable. However, the operative bounds on what can be modified and by how much are delegated to the cross-referenced module, and no cadence or metric is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The bounded access module (UUID cited in the text) is the contract-level access path that the rule depends on, but the rule itself only requires a configuration to exist. Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is the plausible check that a misconfigured contract would be caught, but no quantified consequence is attached to this specific rule.

assessments.title: Relationship To Base Rate
assessments.quote: The Sky Savings Rate is equal to the Base Rate minus the sum of (1) the Distribution Reward Fee (see [A.2.2.9.1.2.1.2 - Distribution Reward Rate](57384c49-e499-4c69-b22c-8e1f1dd34759)) and (2) the Sky Spread (see [A.3.1.2.6 - Sky Spread](e1b694de-1ee3-4502-a9c9-52eea9539804)).
assessments.description: Defines the Sky Savings Rate as the Base Rate minus the Distribution Reward Fee and the Sky Spread.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is explicit and computable, with defined components and linked definitions. However, the Base Rate, Distribution Reward Fee, and Sky Spread have no values here, and no update cadence or edge-case handling is stated.
metrics: Sky Savings Rate = Base Rate − (Distribution Reward Fee + Sky Spread)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a definitional formula with no rate limit, penalty, or contract-enforced constraint on the resulting rate. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Sky Savings Rate Modification
assessments.quote: The Sky Savings Rate can be modified through either Executive Votes or the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).
assessments.description: States that the Sky Savings Rate may be modified via Executive Votes or the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names two permitted change channels and a parameter, but gives no bounds, magnitudes, cadence, or criteria for a change. The text only describes who may modify the rate, not how much or when.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The cross-referenced Bounded External Access Module (47b8b035) may limit changes, but this paragraph does not state its enforcement, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, role-based access, or emergency spell) is triggered by this text.

assessments.title: Sky Savings Rate Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Parameters
assessments.quote:
The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module parameters for the Sky Savings Rate are:

- `max` - 3,000 basis points,
- `min` - 200 basis points,
- `step` - 400 basis points,
- `tau` - Globally defined in [A.3.7.1.3.1.4.1 - Tau Current Value](dd9472e5-9796-4aff-a2b1-7a847e008c9b).

These basis-point values are expressed as annual percentage yields, as specified in [A.3.1.2.7 - Rate Conventions](154c3b5d-7a87-4dae-85f3-7d26deab9a31).
assessments.description: Sets max, min, and step bounds in basis points (APY) for the Sky Savings Rate's bounded external access module, with tau defined elsewhere.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Concrete values are given for max (3,000 bps), min (200 bps), and step (400 bps), with units defined by a linked convention. Tau is delegated to another document and its value is not stated here, so one input is unresolved.

min = 200 basis points (APY)
step = 400 basis points (APY)
tau = globally defined in A.3.7.1.3.1.4.1 (value not stated in paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps artifact review could compare deployed bounded-access parameters against these stated values and assess penalties, but no quantified consequence attaches to this rule. No penalty or conservatorship mechanism targets Sky Core parameter settings, and the paragraph does not state that the bounds are contract-enforced.

assessments.title: Sky Savings Rate Current Value
assessments.quote:
The current value of the Sky Savings Rate can be obtained by calling the `ssr()` function on the sUSDS contract located on the Ethereum Mainnet at `0xa3931d71877C0E7a3148CB7Eb4463524FEc27fbD`. The value returned is the per-second compounding factor; the Sky Savings Rate is the annual percentage rate, as specified in [A.3.1.2.7 - Rate Conventions](154c3b5d-7a87-4dae-85f3-7d26deab9a31), whose accrual over one (1) year is equivalent to compounding that factor every second.

The `ssr()` function returns a per-second compounding rate in RAY precision (10^27). The Sky Savings Rate expressed as an annual percentage rate is given by the formula:

`annual percentage rate = 12 * ((ssr() / 1E27)^2628000 - 1)`

where 2,628,000 is the number of seconds in one (1) month of a 365-day year. The result is a decimal rate (e.g., 0.0346 represents 3.46% per year); the annual percentage yield equivalent is obtained by the conversion specified in [A.3.1.2.7 - Rate Conventions](154c3b5d-7a87-4dae-85f3-7d26deab9a31).
assessments.description: Defines how to read the current Sky Savings Rate from sUSDS `ssr()` and convert the per-second factor to an annual percentage rate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The contract address, RAY (10^27) precision, exact conversion formula, and 2,628,000-second month exponent are all stated, so the calculation can be checked from the text. The final APY conversion is delegated to A.3.1.2.7 without a value stated here, which is a minor gap.

ssr() returns per-second compounding factor in RAY precision (10^27)
annual percentage rate = 12 * ((ssr() / 1E27)^2628000 - 1)
2,628,000 seconds per month (365-day year)
APY conversion per A.3.1.2.7 (not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. This paragraph is a measurement and calculation definition that binds no actor to a behaviour; no on-chain control, penalty, or named enforcer reaches it.

assessments.title: Agent Rate
assessments.quote: The Agent Rate is the rate that Prime Agents earn on USDS, Dai, and sUSDS balances. Except as specified in [A.3.1.2.3.4 - Spark](e15caed7-276c-4489-95dc-9ba628566bf4), the Agent Rate applies only to such balances held in the Prime Agent's SubProxy.
assessments.description: Defines the Agent Rate paid to Prime Agents on USDS, Dai, and sUSDS, limited to SubProxy balances except as the Spark section specifies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter, the eligible tokens, and a scope limit to the Prime Agent's SubProxy, which is checkable. It states no rate value, and the Spark exception is incorporated by reference, so the operative magnitude is delegated to other sections.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No cited mechanism reaches the rate-setting or SubProxy-scope obligation: the Rate Limiter governs controller operations, not earned rates, and the penalty and conservatorship machinery is not tied to this definition.

assessments.title: Relationship To Base Rate
assessments.quote: The Agent Rate is equal to the Base Rate minus the Sky Spread (see [A.3.1.2.6 - Sky Spread](e1b694de-1ee3-4502-a9c9-52eea9539804)), and thus is equal to the Sky Savings Rate plus the Distribution Reward Fee (see [A.2.2.9.1.2.1.2 - Distribution Reward Rate](57384c49-e499-4c69-b22c-8e1f1dd34759)).
assessments.description: Defines the Agent Rate as Base Rate minus Sky Spread, equivalently Sky Savings Rate plus Distribution Reward Fee.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact arithmetic identity, so the relationship is fully formula-based. Its inputs (Base Rate, Sky Spread, Sky Savings Rate, Distribution Reward Fee) are defined in linked sections without values here, and it sets no cadence or bounds.
metrics: Agent Rate = Base Rate - Sky Spread
Agent Rate = Sky Savings Rate + Distribution Reward Fee
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph is a definitional identity rather than an obligation on an actor, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, PSM, Liquidation Penalty, Penalty Mechanisms) reaches a violation of it.

assessments.title: Treatment Of USDS and Dai Balances
assessments.quote: Prime Agents receive the full Agent Rate on USDS and Dai balances held in their SubProxy through the Monthly Settlement Cycle, as specified in [A.3.1.2.3.6 - Settlement](eed3d922-7bb8-4cee-97a4-47e902a1c937).
assessments.description: Requires Sky to pay Prime Agents the full Agent Rate on USDS and Dai held in their SubProxy, settled monthly.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Prime Agents), the balances (USDS and Dai in SubProxy), and the monthly cadence are stated, but the payment magnitude is delegated to the Agent Rate parameter, which has no value here, and settlement mechanics are deferred to the linked Settlement doc.
metrics: Full Agent Rate on USDS and Dai balances held in SubProxy
Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain control, penalty, or escalation path in the catalog reaches a failure to pay the Agent Rate, so only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Treatment Of sUSDS Balances
assessments.quote: Prime Agents earn the Agent Rate on sUSDS balances held in their SubProxy. Because sUSDS balances already earn the Sky Savings Rate, only the remaining 0.20% — the Distribution Reward Rate (see [A.2.2.9.1.2.1.2 - Distribution Reward Rate](57384c49-e499-4c69-b22c-8e1f1dd34759)) — is paid through the Monthly Settlement Cycle, as specified in [A.3.1.2.3.6 - Settlement](eed3d922-7bb8-4cee-97a4-47e902a1c937), bringing the total up to the Agent Rate.
assessments.description: Sets Prime Agents' Agent Rate on sUSDS balances, with the remaining 0.20% paid via Monthly Settlement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete 0.20% residual rate and a monthly settlement cadence, and the total is defined as reaching the Agent Rate. The Agent Rate and Sky Savings Rate are referenced without values here, and the settlement mechanics are deferred to another section.
metrics: Remaining reward rate of 0.20% (Distribution Reward Rate)
Payment through the Monthly Settlement Cycle
Total brought up to the Agent Rate
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. This is a payment entitlement rather than a constraint on Prime behaviour, and no penalty, on-chain, or escalation mechanism reaches a failure to pay or a misstatement of the rate.

assessments.title: Spark
assessments.quote: Spark is entitled to an Agent Rate equal to the Base Rate on USDS and sUSDS balances held in Peg Stability Modules. See [A.3.3.2.1.1 - Peg Stability Module](0082c12d-f1a7-46ff-a4aa-5fe42ece1a4d). The Agent Rate earned by Spark is still subject to the limitations set forth in [A.3.1.2.3.5 - Limitations For Prime Agents Receiving Subsidized Rate](7f6c1ab6-7674-41b0-9522-7e7e5a1cab3d).
assessments.description: Entitles Spark to an Agent Rate equal to the Base Rate on USDS and sUSDS held in Peg Stability Modules.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rate is stated as a formula (Agent Rate equals Base Rate) and the scope is named (USDS and sUSDS balances in PSMs), but the Base Rate has no value here and the operative limitations are delegated to A.3.1.2.3.5. No measurement cadence or balance calculation method is given.
metrics: Agent Rate equal to the Base Rate on USDS and sUSDS balances held in Peg Stability Modules
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Peg Stability Module (0082c12d) is cited but enforces peg arbitrage, not the payment of an Agent Rate, and the Rate Limiter reaches controller operations rather than rate entitlements. Only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Limitations For Prime Agents Receiving Subsidized Rate
assessments.quote: If a Prime Agent is borrowing funds from Sky at a Subsidized Rate, as defined in [A.3.1.2.5.2 - Subsidized Rate](ceceb90b-57d1-43db-9e52-133532c373fd), then the Agent Rate earned by that Prime Agent shall be limited. Specifically, if the standard Agent Rate would exceed the Prime Agent’s Subsidized Rate, the Prime Agent will earn the Subsidized Rate on those balances. The difference between what would have been the standard Agent Rate earnings and the earnings at the Subsidized Rate is effectively retained by Sky. This adjustment is processed as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, as specified in [A.3.1.2.3.6 - Settlement](eed3d922-7bb8-4cee-97a4-47e902a1c937). If the standard Agent Rate is less than or equal to the Subsidized Rate, the standard Agent Rate applies.
assessments.description: Caps a Prime Agent's earned Agent Rate at its Subsidized Rate when it borrows from Sky at a Subsidized Rate, with the difference retained by Sky.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is a clear min() formula: earnings equal the lower of the standard Agent Rate and the Subsidized Rate, settled monthly. The Subsidized Rate is defined in another paragraph and its value is not stated here, and the standard Agent Rate is not given a value in this text.
metrics: Earned rate = lesser of standard Agent Rate and Subsidized Rate
Adjustment processed in the Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog mechanism reaches this rate-cap rule. The cap is applied inside the monthly settlement computation, which is the rule's own implementation rather than an enforcer with defined escalation. Penalty and conservatorship machinery target Risk Capital rules, not subsidized-rate settlement, so only the generic misalignment backstop remains.

assessments.title: Settlement
assessments.quote: To the extent Prime Agents are entitled to payments for the Agent Rate, those payments are made through the Monthly Settlement Cycle. See [A.2.4 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle](6f8d5065-d6ff-4add-9a28-eadeffa7ed1a).
assessments.description: Routes any Agent Rate payments to Prime Agents through the Monthly Settlement Cycle, conditional on entitlement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: States a monthly settlement cadence and cross-references A.2.4, but gives no payment amount, formula, or deadline. The 'to the extent entitled' qualifier leaves it arguable whether any payment obligation binds.
metrics: Agent Rate payments settled through the Monthly Settlement Cycle (monthly cadence)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph attaches no penalty, escalation, or contract-enforced control to settlement timing or amounts; the cross-referenced A.2.4 cycle is a payment process, not an enforcement mechanism in the catalog.

assessments.title: No Double Counting
assessments.quote: A Prime Agent's total reward on a USDS, Dai, or sUSDS balance shall not exceed the Agent Rate, which for the Spark balances specified in [A.3.1.2.3.4 - Spark](e15caed7-276c-4489-95dc-9ba628566bf4) is the Base Rate. The Agent Rate is therefore never paid on top of an existing base reward: an sUSDS balance earning the Sky Savings Rate is topped up to the Agent Rate as specified in [A.3.1.2.3.3 - Treatment Of sUSDS Balances](b1cc2cb1-aff6-4b7a-bb32-bdf56fc7fd2f), not paid the full Agent Rate in addition; and a balance receiving Integration Boost or USDS Token Rewards does not earn the Agent Rate.
assessments.description: Caps a Prime Agent's total reward on USDS, Dai, or sUSDS balances at the Agent Rate and bars stacking the Agent Rate on existing rewards.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is a formula, total reward ≤ Agent Rate, with the Spark case fixed as equal to Base Rate and explicit top-up and exclusion rules for sUSDS, Integration Boost and USDS Token Rewards balances. The Agent Rate and Base Rate values are defined elsewhere and no measurement cadence is stated, so compliance is checkable but depends on inputs not in this paragraph.
metrics: Total reward on a USDS, Dai, or sUSDS balance shall not exceed the Agent Rate
Agent Rate equals the Base Rate for the Spark balances specified in A.3.1.2.3.4
sUSDS balance earning the Sky Savings Rate is topped up to the Agent Rate, not paid the full Agent Rate in addition
Balances receiving Integration Boost or USDS Token Rewards do not earn the Agent Rate
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check the reward configuration against this cap and publish staged findings with penalty assessment, so an overpayment is reachable by an enforcer distinct from the Prime. assessments.quote: The Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate is equal to the Base Rate unless variable pricing has been activated pursuant to [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.2.1 - Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Prime Agent Credit Rating System](4c165fcc-59e5-45c8-866d-c5c68192e591). Upon activation, the rate varies by Prime Agent according to its Credit Rating

assessments.title: Subsidized Rate
assessments.quote: Prime Agents may temporarily be able to borrow specified amounts from Sky Core at a Subsidized Rate below the Base Rate under the terms of an Ecosystem Accord entered into between Sky and the Prime Agent.
assessments.description: Permits Prime Agents to temporarily borrow specified amounts from Sky Core at a Subsidized Rate below the Base Rate under an Ecosystem Accord.
