assessments.title: Use Of Funds
assessments.quote: Funds borrowed by Agents from Sky at the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate must be deposited into the Agent’s Allocation Vault and used to invest in Allocation System Instances. See [A.2.2.10.1 - Allocation System Primitive](9db14ab7-bb4b-4751-8084-843bd4359f2a). These funds may not be transferred to the Agent’s SubProxy account or otherwise outside of the Agent’s designated accounts for its Allocation System Primitive.
assessments.description: Requires Agents to deposit borrowed Sky funds into their Allocation Vault for investment and bars transfers to SubProxy or other non-designated accounts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete actors and accounts (Agent Allocation Vault, designated Allocation System accounts, SubProxy) and prohibits specific destinations. It states no amount, ratio, or deadline, and "used to invest in Allocation System Instances" is not defined operationally, so compliance is only partly checkable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps plausibly reach misuse of borrowed funds, but no consequence is quantified for this rule. The paragraph does not state that the vault's outflows are role-gated or rate-limited, so no contract-enforced mechanism is cited.

assessments.title: Accrued Interest
assessments.quote: Interest accrues on borrowed funds and is reflected in the Allocation Vault balance. Prime Agents must regularly transfer interest payments to the Allocation Vault to pay down accrued interest, ensuring the Allocation Vault balance returns to the principal amount only. Any accrued but unpaid interest reduces the Prime Agent's available Total Risk Capital. See [A.3.2.1.2.1 - Total Risk Capital Definition](6f6b25d6-f73c-4733-ba37-12a0a411433c).
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to regularly pay accrued interest to the Allocation Vault, reducing available Total Risk Capital by any unpaid amount.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation to pay interest is named with an actor and a verifiable end state (vault balance equals principal), but "regularly" gives no cadence or deadline. The effect on Total Risk Capital is stated directionally without a formula or magnitude.
metrics: Allocation Vault balance returns to the principal amount only
Any accrued but unpaid interest reduces the Prime Agent's available Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Reduced available Total Risk Capital can push a Prime into a capital-requirement breach, which the Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements could reach. No consequence is quantified for late interest, and firing requires someone to detect the unpaid amount, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Credit Rating System
assessments.quote: After the development of a Prime Agent Credit Rating System, the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate will vary based on the Credit Rating of each Prime Agent. The Credit Rating for a Prime Agent will take into account factors including the Encumbrance Ratio and the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry.
assessments.description: Future rule: Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate will vary by Prime Agent credit rating, using Encumbrance Ratio and security incident factors.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is conditional on a system that has not been developed yet and gives no formula, weights, or thresholds. It names factors (Encumbrance Ratio, Prime Spell Security Incident Registry) but nothing a Prime could be held to today.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism reaches this rule today because the credit rating system does not exist and the paragraph sets no operative limit. The Risk-Based Pricing mechanism (fd1f682c) prices insurance from the security registry, not the borrow rate, so it does not reach this rule.

assessments.title: Sky Spread
assessments.quote: The Sky Spread is a margin Sky retains for facilitating the ecosystem’s financing. Together with the Distribution Reward Fee, it constitutes the difference between the Base Rate and the Sky Savings Rate. The Sky Spread is 0%.
assessments.description: Sets the Sky Spread, the margin Sky retains for ecosystem financing, at 0%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Sky Spread is stated as an exact value (0%), which is objectively verifiable. It is defined as the gap between Base Rate and Sky Savings Rate with the Distribution Reward Fee, but those inputs have no values in this paragraph.
metrics: Sky Spread = 0%
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No mechanism in the catalog or the paragraph text directly enforces the Sky Spread value. It is a governance-set parameter with no on-chain rate limit or penalty tied to it, so only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Rate Conventions
assessments.quote:
Unless otherwise specified, all rates defined in the Atlas are expressed as annual percentage rates with a monthly compounding frequency. The annual percentage yield equivalent of a rate is given by the formula:

`annual percentage yield = (1 + annual percentage rate / 12)^12 - 1`

A spread between two rates defined in the Atlas is the arithmetic difference between their annual percentage rates. Where the Atlas specifies one rate as another rate plus or minus a spread, that spread is added to or subtracted from the annual percentage rate directly. A rate specified as an annual percentage yield is first converted to its equivalent annual percentage rate before any such arithmetic is performed.

Rates may be displayed as their annual percentage yield equivalents in user-facing interfaces and communications. Where a rate is implemented by a smart contract that compounds at a different frequency, the technical parameter is set such that the accrual produced by the smart contract over one (1) year equals the accrual of the stated rate. Basis-point rate parameters, and the bounds on them, set through Bounded External Access Modules are expressed as annual percentage yields, matching the conversion enforced by the module contracts. A rate applied through periodic payments that are not added to an accruing balance is applied at the annual percentage rate divided by the number of payment periods in each year.
assessments.description: Sets how Atlas rates are interpreted: APR with monthly compounding, APY conversion formula, spread arithmetic, and periodic-payment division.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The compounding frequency (monthly), the APY formula, the periodic-payment divisor, and the spread arithmetic are all explicit and checkable. Gaps remain: "unless otherwise specified" and "matching the conversion enforced by the module contracts" defer to text and contracts outside the paragraph.
metrics: annual percentage yield = (1 + annual percentage rate / 12)^12 - 1
compounding frequency: monthly (12 periods per year)
accrual over one (1) year of smart-contract rate equals accrual of stated rate
periodic payment rate = annual percentage rate divided by number of payment periods per year
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a definitional convention with no violation consequence. The Bounded External Access Modules' conversion is referenced but not cited by UUID, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty) reaches a conversion convention.

assessments.title: Risk Capital
assessments.quote: Prime Agents who invest capital from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio using the Allocation System Primitive must hold Risk Capital to protect Sky from potential losses on these investments. This Article sets forth the framework governing Risk Capital.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents investing Collateral Portfolio capital via the Allocation System to hold Risk Capital against potential losses, and introduces the framework.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a regulated actor (Prime Agents) and a real obligation (holding Risk Capital for allocations), but states no threshold, formula, or metric. Compliance cannot be checked from this text alone, and 'to protect Sky from potential losses' is a purpose rather than a measurable standard.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The obligation to hold Risk Capital is the subject of the Penalty Mechanisms, which can escalate to Conservatorship by Core GovOps for breach of capital requirements. These reach failure to hold Risk Capital, but this intro sets no quantified consequence itself and depends on the operative Article sections that follow.

assessments.title: Capital Ratio Requirement
assessments.quote:
The Capital Ratio Requirement (CRR) with respect to one or more Instances is the Required Risk Capital with respect to such Instances divided by the amount of capital from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in such Instances.

Risk Capital requirements in the Risk Framework may be specified either as an amount of RRC or as a CRR. If a CRR is specified, then the RRC is equal to the amount of capital from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in the relevant Instances times the CRR.

For example, if a certain Instance has a CRR of 5% and 100,000,000 USDS is invested in the Instance, then the RRC is 5,000,000 USDS.

CRR may be specified in aggregate (Aggregate CRR), for a particular Instance (Instance CRR), or for a particular type of risk with respect to an Instance (Instance Financial CRR, Instance Smart Contract CRR, or Instance Administrative CRR).
assessments.description: Defines the Capital Ratio Requirement as Required Risk Capital divided by capital invested in an Instance, and how CRR converts to RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula RRC = invested capital × CRR and the worked example (5% of 100,000,000 USDS = 5,000,000 USDS) are exact and checkable. Gaps remain: no CRR values are set here, and terms such as Instance and invested capital are defined elsewhere.
metrics: CRR = Required Risk Capital / capital from Sky's Collateral Portfolio invested in the Instances
RRC = invested capital × CRR when a CRR is specified
Example: CRR of 5% on 100,000,000 USDS invested gives RRC of 5,000,000 USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is a definition and imposes no duty itself. Breaches of the RRC or CRR requirements it defines would reach the Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements, but the escalation is not quantified for this paragraph and depends on the requirements that use it.

assessments.title: Aggregate RRC
assessments.quote: The Aggregate RRC that a Prime Agent must maintain is equal to the sum of the Instance Total RRC for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive that the Prime Agent has deployed.
assessments.description: Defines a Prime's Aggregate Required Risk Capital as the sum of Instance Total RRC across its active Allocation System instances.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is exact: Aggregate RRC equals the sum of Instance Total RRC over each Active Instance the Prime has deployed. Instance Total RRC is an input defined elsewhere, and this paragraph gives no measurement cadence.
metrics: Aggregate RRC = sum of Instance Total RRC for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive deployed by the Prime Agent
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a Risk Capital requirement, so a shortfall against it reaches the Penalty Mechanisms (quantified penalties) and escalates to Conservatorship for Breach of Capital Requirements, where Sky Core takes direct control of the Prime. The consequence path is defined, though not quantified for this specific formula.

assessments.title: Instance Total RRC
assessments.quote: The Instance Total RRC for an Instance is equal to the sum of the Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract RRC, and Instance Administrative RRC for that Instance. See [A.3.2.1.1.4 - Instance Financial RRC](ba1d5c0e-399f-47a6-b5d4-b3f5477d5787), [A.3.2.1.1.5 - Instance Smart Contract RRC](4b4ea578-28b4-481c-9abd-d34c5a4f383c), and [A.3.2.1.1.6 - Instance Administrative RRC](c2b60f0d-6555-463c-9ad3-2a9746be77c5).
assessments.description: Defines Instance Total RRC as the sum of the Instance Financial, Smart Contract, and Administrative RRC components for an Instance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The aggregation formula is exact and verifiable as a pure sum of three named components. The component values are not stated here and are delegated to the linked sub-paragraphs, which are outside this text.
metrics: Instance Total RRC = Instance Financial RRC + Instance Smart Contract RRC + Instance Administrative RRC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a definitional computation, not a standalone requirement. A miscalculated Total RRC would surface as a Risk Capital shortfall, which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can address, and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) can catch a misstated calculation, but no consequence is quantified for this paragraph itself.

assessments.title: Inability To Calculate Types Of RRC
assessments.quote: If Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract RRC, or Instance Administrative RRC for an Instance cannot be calculated then the Instance Total CRR is 100%.
assessments.description: When any Instance Financial, Smart Contract, or Administrative RRC cannot be calculated, the Instance Total RRC is set to 100%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The consequence is a concrete value (Instance Total RRC = 100%) with a defined trigger covering three named RRC components. The trigger "cannot be calculated" has no operational test, and the text says "CRR" where it means RRC, so a minor gap remains.
metrics: Instance Total RRC = 100% if Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract RRC, or Instance Administrative RRC cannot be calculated
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship for breach of capital requirements (5c3dd35a) plausibly reach a Prime that fails to compute its RRC. The 100% default is a built-in capital cost, but no penalty is quantified for this specific rule, and escalation depends on someone detecting the uncalculated component.

assessments.title: Perpetual Positions
assessments.quote: The model for perpetual positions uses a modified Credit Risk model to evaluate the risk of tokenized delta-neutral positions, such as Ethena and Resolv. The implementation of the model for perpetual positions is specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2 - Perpetual Positions](69fac7fa-6168-4b74-99cc-28b557826556).
assessments.description: Describes a modified Credit Risk model for evaluating tokenized delta-neutral perpetual positions, with implementation deferred to another section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a model and points to another section for its implementation, but states no thresholds, formulas, parameters, or deadlines. Nothing here can be checked for compliance on its own, so it reads as a pointer rather than an operative rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph contains no operative obligation or violation mode that a mechanism could reach. The referenced implementation section (69fac7fa) is not itself an enforcement mechanism in the catalog.

assessments.title: Direct Exposures
assessments.quote: The model for direct exposures combines Market Risk and Liquidity Risk to evaluate the risk of direct asset holdings of volatile cryptoassets, such as ETH, stETH, and WBTC. The implementation of the model for direct exposures is specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.3 - Direct Exposures](69d0776b-786c-408b-b76a-860ea60b6b9a).
assessments.description: Describes a market and liquidity risk model for direct volatile cryptoasset holdings, with implementation deferred to another section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a model combining Market Risk and Liquidity Risk but states no formula, threshold, or parameter. Its only operative content is a pointer to another section for the implementation, so there is nothing a regulated party could be checked against here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no obligation for an actor to meet, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Penalty Mechanisms, etc.) reaches it. The referenced implementation doc is a model specification, not an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: Cash Stablecoins
assessments.quote: The model for Cash Stablecoins is based on identifying stablecoins, such as USDC and USDT, that do not present significant Market Risk, Credit Risk, or Liquidity Risk. The implementation of the model for Cash Stablecoins is specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.6 - Cash Stablecoins](3c0a9e8b-4a0b-4059-87a4-155deaee0486).
assessments.description: Defines the Cash Stablecoins model as stablecoins lacking significant market, credit, or liquidity risk, with implementation deferred to another section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The criterion is qualitative: 'do not present significant' Market, Credit, or Liquidity Risk, with no threshold, metric, or test for significance. The operative details are delegated to A.3.2.2.1.1.1.6, and this paragraph names no concrete value.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This paragraph only classifies stablecoins; no on-chain control, capital-at-risk consequence, or named enforcer reaches a misclassification here, and the catch-all backstops alone are weak.

assessments.title: Risk Rating
assessments.quote: The determination of Smart Contract Risk should initially be based on an evaluation of the risk that the investment could experience losses due to a bug or technical exploit. This determination should take into account factors such as (1) the technical complexity of the code base (e.g. cyclomatic complexity, decision points, number of external calls, lines of code), (2) the number, quality, and recency of audits, and (3) the "Lindiness" of the relevant smart contracts.
assessments.description: Directs that Smart Contract Risk be initially assessed from bug or exploit loss potential, considering code complexity, audits, and Lindiness.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates real assessment factors (code complexity, audit count, quality and recency, Lindiness) but gives no weights, scoring scale, thresholds, or output values. Its 'should' and 'take into account' language leaves compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The 'should' wording is advisory, and no consequence is tied to the rating methodology itself. Penalty and conservatorship mechanisms attach to breaches of capital requirements, not to how a risk rating is derived.

assessments.title: Required Risk Capital
assessments.quote: The risk of a technical exploit in one protocol is unlikely to be correlated with the risk of a technical exploit in an unrelated protocol. Therefore, the risks from small exposures to even relatively risky protocols are likely to be diversified away. In contrast, very large exposures to even relatively safe protocols can create a risk to a Prime Agent and potentially to Sky itself if there is a technical exploit, especially if multiple Prime Agents have the same exposure. To account for this, the calculation of Instance Smart Contract RRC should take into account the risk rating, the level of exposure of the Prime, and the level of exposure of the Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Directs that Instance Smart Contract RRC account for protocol risk rating and Prime and Sky Ecosystem exposure levels.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is mainly rationale. Its only operative language is that the RRC calculation 'should take into account' three factors, with no formula, weights, thresholds, or cadence. The calculation it refers to is not defined here, so nothing can be checked against this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: RRC feeds the Prime's Risk Capital requirement, so a Risk Capital shortfall plausibly reaches the Penalty Mechanisms. The consequence is not quantified for this calculation-method paragraph, and the mechanism does not name a specific remedy for mis-specified RRC inputs, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Risk Rating
assessments.quote: The determination of Administrative Risk should initially be based on an evaluation of the risk that an investment could experience losses due to an abuse of privileged access. This determination should take into account factors such as (1) the level of privileged access that exists, (2) the security delay that such access is subject to, and (3) the "Lindiness" of the system.
assessments.description: Directs that administrative risk for an investment be initially assessed from privileged-access abuse, considering access level, security delay, and Lindiness.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names three real factors (privileged access level, security delay, Lindiness) but gives no scale, threshold, or formula for rating them. The operative verb is 'should' and the determination is 'initially based on' an evaluation, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a methodology for an initial risk determination, not a violable limit, and no contract, penalty, or escalation path is tied to how the rating is derived. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Required Risk Capital
assessments.quote: The risk of an abuse of privileged access in one protocol is unlikely to be correlated with the risk of an abuse of privileged access in an unrelated protocol. Therefore, the risks from small exposures to even relatively risky protocols are likely to be diversified away. In contrast, very large exposures to even relatively safe protocols can create a risk to a Prime Agent and potentially to Sky itself if there is an abuse of privileged access, especially if multiple Prime Agents have the same exposure. To account for this, the calculation of Instance Administrative RRC should take into account the risk rating, the level of exposure of the Prime, and the level of exposure of the Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Explains that Instance Administrative RRC should account for risk rating, Prime exposure, and Sky Ecosystem exposure, without specifying how.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names three concrete inputs (risk rating, Prime exposure level, Sky Ecosystem exposure level) but gives no formula, weighting, or thresholds, and 'should take into account' is judgment language. Compliance could be argued either way on the same calculation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a conceptual rationale with no testable calculation or threshold to breach, so no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism reaches it today; the Penalty Mechanisms could only attach once a concrete RRC formula is specified.

assessments.title: Implementation
assessments.quote: The implementation of the calculation of Instance Administrative RRC is specified in [A.3.2.2.1.3 - Instance Administrative RRC Calculation](277d6712-25ff-4566-a42b-38d7e860ae76).
assessments.description: Points to the section specifying how Instance Administrative RRC is calculated; states no operative requirement itself.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph contains no threshold, formula, metric, or actor. It only cross-references A.3.2.2.1.3, so nothing is verifiable from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The only UUID cited (277d6712) is a cross-reference to the calculation section, not an enforcement mechanism, and no catalog mechanism reaches a pure pointer paragraph.

assessments.title: Total Risk Capital
assessments.quote: The documents herein define the conceptual framework for types of capital that contribute to a Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital (TRC). Prime Agents must maintain at all times a level of TRC that exceeds their Aggregate RRC or be subject to penalties.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to keep Total Risk Capital above Aggregate RRC at all times, or face penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is a verifiable comparison (TRC must exceed Aggregate RRC) with a defined actor and an "at all times" standard. The components TRC and Aggregate RRC are defined elsewhere and no numeric margin or measurement cadence is stated here, so it is not fully quantified.
metrics: TRC exceeds Aggregate RRC
maintained at all times
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph itself makes a breach subject to penalties, which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) quantify for Risk Capital rule violations. Breach of capital requirements also escalates to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), where Core GovOps and an expedited Executive Vote can take direct control of the Prime, giving a named enforcer and concrete remedy.

assessments.title: Total Risk Capital Definition
assessments.quote: Total Risk Capital is capital that is currently eligible, available, and verifiably under the Prime’s control. For capital to be included in a Prime Agent's TRC, it must be currently deployable towards covering its Required Risk Capital obligations. Consequently, in-flight capital (e.g., assets being bridged) does not contribute towards a Prime’s TRC. Similarly, commitments for future capital, such as Ecosystem Accords for renting Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) or Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) that have been agreed upon by counterparties but are not yet formally codified within the Atlas, cannot contribute towards a Prime’s TRC until such formalization is complete.
assessments.description: Defines Total Risk Capital as currently eligible, available, verifiably controlled capital, excluding in-flight assets and uncodified future commitments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete inclusion and exclusion criteria, including in-flight capital and uncodified Ecosystem Accord commitments. It gives no numeric threshold, and key terms such as "currently deployable" and "verifiably under the Prime's control" are qualitative and unmeasured.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Overstating TRC would undermine Required Risk Capital compliance, which reaches the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could catch a miscounted TRC, but the penalty is not quantified for this definition and review must be triggered.

assessments.title: Junior Risk Capital
assessments.quote: Junior Risk Capital (JRC) is the first capital to absorb losses on investments under the Allocation System. Junior Risk Capital must experience 100% losses before any losses are absorbed by Senior Risk Capital.
assessments.description: Defines Junior Risk Capital as first-loss capital that must absorb 100% of losses before Senior Risk Capital is hit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loss-ordering threshold is quantified (100% of JRC losses before any Senior Risk Capital absorption), which a third party could check against a loss waterfall. It lacks a defined responsible actor and does not specify how losses are measured or when they are recognized.
metrics: JRC must experience 100% losses before any losses are absorbed by Senior Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Capital Incident Response governs losses to Risk Capital and can impose penalties up to conservatorship to make losses whole, and Penalty Mechanisms incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific loss-ordering rule, and firing depends on incident escalation, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)
assessments.quote:
Internal Junior Risk Capital is capital owned by the Prime Agent itself. It serves as the foundation for the Prime’s risk capacity: the amount of IJRC directly dictates the maximum External JRC the Prime can source (governed by the External Per Internal ratio) and provides the primary capacity for enabling Senior Risk Capital (via the Senior Per Junior ratio), while also bearing the initial impact of any losses (the Tip JRC mechanism). IJRC must be eligible assets held in the Prime Agent’s designated treasury account (e.g., SubProxy), controlled by the Prime’s root governance.

See [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.1 - External Per Internal Ratio](ff374833-920c-40f6-ae6c-a71d33d99b82), [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2 - Senior Per Junior Ratio](fbc9a273-d217-4d52-8b3e-b496580f27a2), and [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.2 - JRC Loss Allocation Rules](c201122a-75d2-44fa-b221-4e7c09bf42f2).
assessments.description: Defines Internal Junior Risk Capital as Prime-owned capital that must be eligible assets held in the Prime's designated treasury account under root governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete parameters: the Prime as owner, a designated treasury account (e.g., SubProxy), and root governance control. The operative magnitudes are delegated to linked ratio and loss-allocation docs, and "eligible assets" is undefined here, so the IJRC amount and asset criteria are not stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship for capital-requirement breaches plausibly reach a Prime that holds IJRC outside eligible assets or the designated account. The consequence is not quantified for this definitional rule, and escalation depends on enforcement being triggered.

assessments.title: Types Of Eligible Assets For IJRC
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define the types of assets that qualify as Internal Junior Risk Capital.

These types will be specified in a future iteration of the Risk Framework.
assessments.description: States that eligible asset types for Internal Junior Risk Capital will be specified in a future framework iteration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph contains no thresholds, asset types, or criteria. Its only operative content is a deferral to a future iteration, which makes it a stub with nothing to comply with yet.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No obligation exists to enforce, and no mechanism such as the Rate Limiter, Penalty Mechanisms, or Liquidation Penalty reaches a rule that defines no assets.

assessments.title: Initial Loss Absorption By "Tip JRC"
assessments.quote:
The Tip JRC mechanism dictates that losses from a distinct risk event are first absorbed entirely by the Prime Agent's Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), up to a specific threshold amount. This threshold amount is calculated as a percentage of Total JRC and is specified in [A.3.2.2.2.1 - JRC Loss Allocation Parameters](b718459e-57e0-414f-9c99-fbc82685cc0f).

Only losses exceeding this threshold amount trigger absorption by other Junior Risk Capital components - specifically, the remaining IJRC and External Junior Risk Capital. This initial absorption solely by IJRC ensures that Prime Agents are highly incentivized to prevent losses and avoids the need to resolve disputes regarding the allocation of small losses to EJRC providers.
assessments.description: Requires IJRC to absorb losses up to a threshold, a percentage of Total JRC, before other Junior Risk Capital is drawn.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Prime Agent IJRC), the allocation order, and the threshold basis (a percentage of Total JRC). The percentage itself is delegated to A.3.2.2.2.1 and is not stated here, so the operative magnitude is missing.
metrics: Threshold amount expressed as a percentage of Total JRC (value specified in A.3.2.2.2.1, not stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: IJRC is first-loss capital at risk for the Prime, which is a real incentive, and the Penalty Mechanisms and Risk-Capital Incident Response reach Risk Capital rule breaches. However, no penalty or escalation is quantified for this specific allocation rule, and the threshold is not given, so the rating stops at mid.

assessments.title: Post-Tip JRC Loss Allocation
assessments.quote: If a loss event exceeds the Tip JRC amount, the remaining loss is allocated pro-rata across the rest of the JRC capital. This includes the remaining Internal Junior Risk Capital (Total IJRC minus the Tip amount) and all External Junior Risk Capital (Prime External Junior Risk Capital plus Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital).
assessments.description: Allocates losses exceeding the Tip JRC amount pro-rata across remaining internal and external junior risk capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives a pro-rata allocation formula over named components (remaining IJRC, Prime External JRC, Tokenized External JRC) with a defined trigger. It lacks explicit pro-rata weights, a measurement cadence, and the Tip JRC amount's value, which is defined elsewhere.
metrics: Trigger: loss event exceeds the Tip JRC amount
Remaining loss allocated pro-rata across (Total IJRC minus Tip amount) plus Prime External JRC plus Tokenized External JRC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Capital Incident Response governs loss events and lets Sky Core impose penalties up to conservatorship to make losses whole, which plausibly reaches how losses are allocated. Consequences are not quantified for this specific allocation rule, and the escalation must be triggered.

assessments.title: Per-Event Basis
assessments.quote:
The JRC loss allocation rules are applied independently based on the total losses attributed to each distinct risk event. The concept of "per-event basis" is crucial; the classification of a distinct risk event (classifying losses as one large event versus multiple smaller ones) can dictate whether the Tip JRC threshold is breached.

Breaching the threshold activates the pro-rata sharing mechanism for any losses exceeding the Tip JRC amount, distributing such excess losses between both the remaining Internal JRC (IJRC) and all External JRC (EJRC). Conversely, if the threshold is not breached for an event, the loss is contained entirely within the Tip layer and absorbed solely by IJRC.

The operational process for the determination of distinct risk events will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Specifies JRC loss allocation per distinct risk event: pro-rata sharing above the Tip JRC threshold, IJRC-only absorption below it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The allocation logic is stated, but the Tip JRC threshold has no value and the classification of distinct risk events is explicitly deferred to a future iteration. Compliance cannot be checked from the text alone.
metrics: Tip JRC threshold breach per distinct risk event (threshold value not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes a loss-allocation outcome rather than a violable actor duty, and no penalty, rate-limit, or contract mechanism reaches the per-event classification, which is deferred.

assessments.title: Senior Risk Capital
assessments.quote:
Senior Risk Capital (SRC) is protected from losses relative to Junior Risk Capital. Senior Risk Capital only begins to absorb losses after Junior Risk Capital has experienced 100% losses and absorbs 100% of losses thereafter.

Senior Risk Capital can be originated from Sky Core on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle; Prime Agents can also rent Senior Risk Capital from each other via the [A.2.2.10.2 - Risk Capital Rental Primitive](d8086dc0-7e77-4c6b-98c7-5fc41337a1ce).
assessments.description: Defines Senior Risk Capital as loss-protected relative to Junior Risk Capital, with monthly origination by Sky Core and Prime-to-Prime rental.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loss waterfall is fully quantified: SRC absorbs losses only after JRC has suffered 100% losses, then absorbs 100%. Origination cadence is monthly, but origination amounts and sizing are not stated, and rental terms are deferred to the linked primitive.
metrics: SRC absorbs losses only after Junior Risk Capital has experienced 100% losses
SRC absorbs 100% of losses thereafter
Senior Risk Capital originated from Sky Core on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The loss ordering is applied through the Risk-Capital Incident Response framework, which lets Sky Core impose penalties up to conservatorship to make losses whole. That reaches losses allocated against this waterfall, but the paragraph sets no quantified consequence of its own, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: External Per Internal Ratio
assessments.quote: The External Per Internal (EPI) ratio determines the maximum amount of External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC and TEJRC combined) that a Prime Agent can source directly based on its held Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC). This acts as the primary constraint ensuring a baseline level of the Prime’s own capital backs its external JRC sourcing. The required External Per Internal ratio is specified in [A.3.2.2.2.2.1 - External Per Internal (EPI) Ratio Value](3ed32706-c072-42b5-b1e5-187bddf8dc37).
assessments.description: Caps a Prime's external junior risk capital sourcing by a ratio of its internal junior risk capital, with the ratio value deferred elsewhere.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the EPI ratio and states the constraint form (maximum external JRC relative to held IJRC), but gives no numeric value and delegates the magnitude to section A.3.2.2.2.2.1. It also has no measurement cadence or defined calculation basis.
metrics: Maximum External JRC (PEJRC + TEJRC combined) that a Prime may source, determined by the External Per Internal ratio applied to held IJRC
EPI ratio value (specified in A.3.2.2.2.2.1, not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The EPI ratio is a Risk Capital sourcing requirement, so breach plausibly triggers the Penalty Mechanisms, with escalation to Conservatorship for breach of capital requirements, where Sky Core takes direct control of the Prime. The consequence is not quantified in this paragraph, and the ratio's value is not stated here.

assessments.title: Senior Per Junior Ratio
assessments.quote:
The Senior Per Junior (SPJ) ratio defines the effectiveness of each type of Junior Risk Capital (IJRC, PEJRC, TEJRC) in supporting Senior Risk Capital (SRC). Specifically, it quantifies how many units of SRC (whether Originated or Rented) can be activated or "enabled" per unit of a given JRC type.

A Prime Agent's overall "SPJ capacity" is calculated by summing the potential enablement contributed by each type of JRC it holds (IJRC, PEJRC or TEJRC), where each contribution equals the amount of that JRC type multiplied by its specific SPJ ratio.

Since SRC only absorbs losses after JRC is depleted, the SPJ enablement mechanism validates that sufficient JRC backing exists, allowing enabled SRC to be counted as part of the Prime Agent's total eligible Risk Capital. Therefore, a Prime Agent might hold a certain amount of OSRC or rented SRC, but only the portion that is successfully "enabled" by its JRC according to the SPJ ratios is accounted by the system as eligible capital contributing towards the Prime’s satisfaction of its Required Risk Capital. The required ratio of Senior Per Junior is specified in [A.3.2.2.2.2.2 - Senior Per Junior (SPJ) Ratio Values](8578e240-3fe8-41c0-8b2c-15ec9a7181ab).
assessments.description: Defines the Senior Per Junior ratio and how JRC backing enables SRC to count toward a Prime's Required Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an operative formula: SPJ capacity equals the sum of each JRC type's amount multiplied by its SPJ ratio. The ratio values themselves are delegated to A.3.2.2.2.2.2, so the magnitudes that determine eligible capital are not stated here.
metrics: SPJ capacity = sum over JRC types (IJRC, PEJRC, TEJRC) of JRC amount × that type's SPJ ratio
Required SPJ ratio per JRC type specified in A.3.2.2.2.2.2 (Senior Per Junior (SPJ) Ratio Values), not stated in this paragraph
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph determines which SRC counts toward Required Risk Capital, so a miscalculated SPJ enablement would be a capital-requirement breach reachable by the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship. No consequence is quantified for this definitional rule, so it stays mid.

assessments.title: Alternative Use Of SPJ Capacity To Source External Junior Risk Capital
assessments.quote:
A Prime Agent may optionally choose to deploy all or some portion of its calculated SPJ capacity not to enable Senior Risk Capital, but instead to source additional External Junior Risk Capital. This provides a secondary mechanism to increase the total JRC potentially beyond the amount initially constrained by the EPI ratio applied solely to IJRC.

Crucially, the EJRC tranche acquired through utilizing SPJ capacity is permanently accounted for as having an SPJ ratio of zero (0). It contributes to the JRC buffer but provides no capacity itself for enabling SRC in any subsequent calculations. This contrasts with EJRC sourced normally via the EPI ratio, which retains its standard SPJ capacity.
assessments.description: Lets Primes use SPJ capacity to source External Junior Risk Capital, which is then permanently assigned an SPJ ratio of zero.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The SPJ ratio of zero for EJRC sourced via SPJ capacity is a concrete, checkable value, and it is contrasted with the standard SPJ capacity for EPI-sourced EJRC. However, the amount deployed is left as 'all or some portion' with no cap, formula, or threshold.
metrics: EJRC acquired via SPJ capacity has an SPJ ratio of 0, permanently
EJRC sourced via the EPI ratio retains its standard SPJ capacity
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Miscounting SPJ capacity would misstate Risk Capital compliance, which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could plausibly reach. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific accounting rule, and the optional deployment decision is not itself contract-enforced.

assessments.title: Interaction Between Ratios And SPJ Capacity
assessments.quote:
The sourcing of External Junior Risk Capital and enablement of Senior Risk Capital involves a sequential application of the Risk Capital sourcing ratios in conjunction with the Prime Agent’s deployment of its SPJ capacity.

First, the EPI ratio sets the initial limit for sourcing standard, SPJ-bearing EJRC based solely on the Prime Agent’s IJRC.
Second, the total SPJ capacity is calculated from the Prime Agent’s resulting JRC pool (IJRC + any EPI-sourced EJRC).

Finally, this total calculated SPJ capacity can be allocated by the Prime Agent to enable SRC (standard use), and/or to source additional, non-SPJ-bearing EJRC using the mechanism described under [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2.1 - Alternative Use Of SPJ Capacity To Source External Junior Risk Capital](03029174-91b4-4974-af1e-52438556a70b). Any specific portion of the total SPJ capacity allocated towards sourcing EJRC cannot simultaneously be allocated towards enabling SRC.
assessments.description: Sequences EPI-based EJRC sourcing, total SPJ capacity calculation, and allocation of that capacity to SRC or EJRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an ordered procedure and a hard exclusivity constraint: SPJ capacity allocated to EJRC cannot also enable SRC. However, the EPI ratio value and the SPJ capacity formula are not stated here and are delegated to other paragraphs.
metrics: EPI ratio sets the initial limit on SPJ-bearing EJRC, based solely on IJRC (value defined elsewhere)
Total SPJ capacity is calculated from the JRC pool (IJRC + EPI-sourced EJRC); formula not stated here
Any portion of total SPJ capacity allocated to sourcing EJRC cannot simultaneously enable SRC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a Risk Capital sourcing rule, so breaches fall under the Penalty Mechanisms (quantified penalties on Primes) and escalate to Conservatorship for Breach of Capital Requirements, where Sky Core takes direct control of the Prime. The paragraph itself states no consequence; the rating relies on these mechanisms reaching it.

assessments.title: Calculate Probability Of Default
assessments.quote:
The first step is calculating the Probability Of Default $PD$. $PD$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\text{PD} = N(-d_1) + N(-d_2) \left( \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{j=1}^m D_0^j} \right)^{-2a}
$$

Here $N$ is the normal cumulative probability distribution function.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Probability of Default formula, a first step in calculating Required Risk Capital, with inputs deferred to subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core formula for PD is fully written with exact operators and exponent structure, so the calculation is objectively reproducible. However, N(-d1), N(-d2), the exponent parameter a, and the LT_i, V_0^i, and D_0^j inputs are defined only in subdocuments and carry no values here.
metrics: N is the normal cumulative probability distribution function
Exponent is -2a, with a defined in subdocuments
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This PD step is part of Required Risk Capital under A.3.2.2. An understated PD yields understated capital, which is a capital-requirement breach. That breach reaches the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship escalation by Core GovOps to an expedited Executive Vote.

assessments.title: Leverage Adjusted Drift To Risk Ratio
assessments.quote:
The Leverage Adjusted Drift To Risk Ratio $a$ is calculated as follows:

$$
a = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) - \sum_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j) + \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D - \sigma_U^2}{\sigma_U^2 + \sigma_D^2 - 2 \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the Leverage Adjusted Drift To Risk Ratio as a formula over drift, volatility, correlation and weight inputs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with exact operators and terms, so the ratio is computable as written. The inputs (returns r_c, r_s, r_d, weights, volatilities, correlation) are not defined or valued in this paragraph, and no measurement cadence is given.
metrics: a = (Σ_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) − Σ_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j) + ρ_UD σ_U σ_D − σ_U²) / (σ_U² + σ_D² − 2 ρ_UD σ_U σ_D)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The ratio feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a miscomputed or non-compliant value could breach Risk Capital requirements, which reach the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship escalation. Those consequences are not quantified for this formula, and no mechanism checks the calculation itself, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Distance To Default
assessments.quote:
The Distance To Default $d_1$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
d_1 = \frac{\ln\left( \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{j=1}^m D_0^j} \right) + \left( \sum_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) - \sum_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j) + \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D - \sigma_U^2 \right) T}{\sqrt{\sigma_U^2 + \sigma_D^2 - 2 \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D} \sqrt{T}}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the Distance To Default d1 as a log-based formula over asset and debt values, drifts, volatilities, and correlation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The full closed-form formula for d1 is stated, so the calculation is objectively reproducible. Inputs such as the volatilities, correlation, rates, weights, and horizon T are referenced without values, sources, or measurement cadence.
metrics: d1 computed by the stated formula using LT_i V_0^i, D_0^j, w_U^i, w_D^j, r_c^i, r_s^i, r_d^j, sigma_U, sigma_D, rho_UD, and T
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Distance To Default feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculated d1 could cause a capital shortfall that the Penalty Mechanisms would reach. The consequence is not quantified for this formula, and no contract enforces the calculation itself.

assessments.title: Downward Adjusted Distance To Default
assessments.quote:
The Downward Adjusted Distance To Default $d_2$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
d_2 = \frac{\ln\left( \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{j=1}^m D_0^j} \right) - \left( \sum_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) - \sum_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j)+ \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D - \sigma_U^2 \right) T}{\sqrt{\sigma_U^2 + \sigma_D^2 - 2 \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D} \sqrt{T}}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the formula for the Downward Adjusted Distance To Default d_2 used in the Instance Financial RRC calculation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with an explicit mathematical expression, so the calculation is objectively reproducible. However, inputs such as LT_i, V_0, D_0, the weights w, the rates r, the volatilities sigma, the correlation rho, and the horizon T are defined elsewhere and given no values or measurement cadence in this paragraph.
metrics: d_2 = [ln(sum LT_i V_0^i / sum D_0^j) - (drift terms) T] / (sqrt(sigma_U^2 + sigma_D^2 - 2 rho sigma_U sigma_D) sqrt(T))
assessments.enforcementReasoning: d_2 sets the Required Risk Capital, so a miscalculation would be caught by Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) and could trigger the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) that enforce Risk Capital rules. The consequence is not quantified for this formula itself, and no contract enforces the calculation on-chain.

assessments.title: Total Variance Of Underlying Asset Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The Total Variance Of Underlying Asset Portfolio $\sigma_U^2$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\sigma_U^2 = \sum_{i,k=1}^n w_U^i w_U^k \sigma_V^i \sigma_V^k \rho_{V,ik}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the total variance of the underlying asset portfolio via a weighted pairwise covariance formula.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified, but its inputs (weights w_U, volatilities sigma_V, and correlations rho_V) are referenced without values or sourcing rules in this paragraph. No measurement cadence or edge-case handling is stated.
metrics: sigma_U^2 = sum over i,k=1..n of w_U^i * w_U^k * sigma_V^i * sigma_V^k * rho_{V,ik}
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The variance feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a misstated variance would understate required capital and breach Risk Capital requirements. Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach that breach, but no consequence is quantified for this formula itself.

assessments.title: Total Variance Of Debt Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The Total Variance Of Debt Portfolio $\sigma_D^2$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\sigma_D^2 = \sum_{j,l=1}^m w_D^j w_D^l \sigma_D^j \sigma_D^l \rho_{D,jl}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the total variance of the debt portfolio as a double sum over asset weights, volatilities and correlations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is exact and fully specified as a computation. However, its inputs (weights w_D^j, volatilities sigma_D^j, correlations rho_{D,jl}) and the summation bound m are defined elsewhere, with no values or sourcing stated in this paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The variance feeds the Risk Capital requirement, so a miscalculated value that understates required capital could breach Risk Capital rules, which carry Penalty Mechanisms. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could catch a divergent implementation, but no consequence is quantified for this formula specifically, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Correlation Between Asset Portfolio And Debt Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The Correlation Between Asset Portfolio And Debt Portfolio $\rho_{UD}$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\rho_{UD} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^m w_U^i w_D^j \sigma_V^i \sigma_D^j \rho_{VD,ij}}{\sqrt{\sigma_U^2 \sigma_D^2}}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the correlation between a Prime's asset portfolio and debt portfolio via a weighted covariance formula.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully explicit, with summation bounds and a defined calculation. However, the weights, volatilities, and asset-debt correlation inputs are defined elsewhere without values here, and the denominator's sigma_U and sigma_D are not defined in this paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The correlation feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculation can lead to under-capitalization that the Penalty Mechanisms would reach. The consequence is not quantified for this formula, and no artifact review or direct enforcement is named.

assessments.title: Weight Of Asset In Underlying Asset Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The weight of asset $i$ in the underlying asset portfolio $w_U^i$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
w_U^i = \frac{\text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{k=1}^n \text{LT}_k V_0^k}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the weight of each asset in the underlying portfolio as its liquidation-threshold-weighted value share.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified and mechanically computable. The inputs LT_i, V_0^i and the summation bound n are not defined or valued in this paragraph, so the supporting parameters must be found elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This weight feeds the Risk Capital requirement calculation, so a miscalculation would be caught by Core GovOps artifact review, and a resulting Risk Capital shortfall would fall under the Penalty Mechanisms. Neither reaches this formula directly, and no consequence is quantified for it specifically.

assessments.title: Weight Of Debt Instrument In Debt Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The weight of debt instrument $j$ in the debt portfolio $w_D^j$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
w_D^j = \frac{D_0^j}{\sum_{l=1}^m D_0^l}
$$
assessments.description: Defines each debt instrument's weight in the debt portfolio as its share of total portfolio debt.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact formula, w_D^j = D_0^j / sum over l=1..m of D_0^l, so the calculation is fully determined. The input D_0 and the instrument count m are not defined in this paragraph, so a reviewer must look elsewhere for their values.
metrics: w_D^j = D_0^j / sum_{l=1}^{m} D_0^l (debt weight of instrument j as share of total debt across m instruments)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is an input definition within the Risk Capital RRC calculation, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a miscalculation that breaches Risk Capital requirements. No consequence is quantified for this weight calculation specifically, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it.

assessments.title: Correlation Coefficient
assessments.quote: The correlation coefficient $\rho$ between two instruments is the correlation of block-weighted log returns of those assets over the last 365 days. In the documents herein, the correlation coefficient is followed by subscripts indicating the relevant instruments. For example, $\rho_{UD}$ is the correlation between the underlying asset portfolio $U$ and the debt portfolio $D$ as specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.6 - Correlation Between Asset Portfolio And Debt Portfolio](ae1dbcb9-828d-40c0-8ad8-96b3072dad4e). The subscript may begin with $V$ or $D$ to indicate whether the relevant instruments are part of the asset portfolio or debt portfolio. For example, $\rho_{VD,ij}$ is the correlation coefficient between the asset $i$ and the debt instrument $j$.
assessments.description: Defines the correlation coefficient between two instruments as correlation of block-weighted log returns over 365 days, with subscript notation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 365-day lookback window and the log-return basis are concrete and checkable. The block-weighting scheme is named but not specified here, so it is defined elsewhere without a value. The paragraph is a definition rather than an operative obligation.
metrics: Lookback window of 365 days
Block-weighted log returns of the two instruments
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The coefficient feeds the Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculated correlation could cause a capital shortfall. The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) would plausibly reach that breach, but no consequence is quantified for this definition itself.

assessments.title: Time Horizon
assessments.quote: The Time Horizon $T$ is the time horizon in years over which the Probability Of Default is being estimated. The value of the $T$ parameter is `1`.
assessments.description: Fixes the time horizon parameter T at 1 year for the probability-of-default estimate in the required risk capital calculation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states an exact value (T = 1, in years) for a named parameter with a defined meaning. A third party can verify the value from the text alone, though the formula that consumes T is not in this paragraph.
metrics: Time Horizon T = 1 year
assessments.enforcementReasoning: T feeds the Risk Capital requirement, so a Prime using a different horizon under-capitalizes and would breach Risk Capital rules, which reach Penalty Mechanisms. Artifact Review by Core GovOps could catch a mismatched RRC implementation, but no consequence is quantified for this parameter and firing depends on review.

assessments.title: Calculate Loss Given Default
assessments.quote:
The second step is calculating the Loss Given Default $LGD$. $LGD$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
LGD = min(1 - \frac{(1 - LP) * (1 - S)}{LT}, 0)
$$

Here $min$ is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lower of the two specified parameters.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein. All of these parameters should be specified as decimal numbers. For example, 3% should be specified as `0.03`.
assessments.description: Specifies the formula for calculating Loss Given Default, floored at zero, with parameters expressed as decimals.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The LGD formula and the zero floor via min() are fully specified and computable. The inputs LP, S and LT are defined only in subdocuments, with no values stated in this paragraph, so the rule cannot be checked from this text alone.
metrics: LGD floored at 0 (minimum function)
Parameters expressed as decimals (e.g., 3% = 0.03)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a calculation step in the Risk Capital requirement. A miscalculated LGD understates required capital, so Penalty Mechanisms and Agent Artifact Review could plausibly reach a violation. No consequence is quantified for this formula specifically, and enforcement depends on review or escalation being triggered.

assessments.title: Slippage
assessments.quote: The Slippage $S$ is the estimated slippage for liquidating the entire position in one block. The estimated slippage should not exceed 25%.
assessments.description: Caps the estimated one-block liquidation slippage used in Risk Capital calculation at 25%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 25% ceiling on estimated slippage is an explicit numeric threshold with a defined scope (entire position, one block). However, the estimation method, the estimating party, and the measurement cadence are not specified, so a third party cannot independently verify the estimate.
metrics: Estimated slippage for liquidating the entire position in one block must not exceed 25%
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is an input to the Required Risk Capital calculation under A.3.2.2.x, so an understated slippage that leads to insufficient Risk Capital falls under Risk Capital requirements. Those breaches trigger the Penalty Mechanisms and can escalate to Conservatorship, with Sky Core taking direct control of the Prime.

assessments.title: Calculate Asset Correlation Coefficient
assessments.quote:
The third step is to calculate the Asset Correlation Coefficient $R$. $R$ is calculated as follows:

$$
R = a \times \left(1 - e^{-K \times PD}\right) + b \times \left(1 - \left(1 - e^{-K \times PD}\right)\right)
$$

Here $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Specifies the formula for the Asset Correlation Coefficient R in the Risk Capital calculation, with its parameters deferred to subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully written out, so the calculation structure is defined. However, the magnitudes of a, b and K are not stated, PD is not defined here, and the paragraph defers all parameters to subdocuments.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A miscalculated Risk Capital requirement would breach Prime capital rules, which reach the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship. The consequence is not quantified for this formula step, and firing depends on detection through review.

assessments.title: Lower Bound
assessments.quote: The Lower Bound $a$ is an estimate of the correlation between assets during "calm" periods. It is set of `0.13`.
assessments.description: Sets the Lower Bound parameter a to 0.13, an estimated asset correlation during calm market periods.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact value (0.13), so compliance with the stated value is directly checkable. It does not say how a enters the Risk Capital calculation or how often it is reviewed or updated, which are defined elsewhere.
metrics: Lower Bound a = 0.13
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Because a feeds the Risk Capital calculation, an incorrect value would breach Risk Capital requirements, which the Penalty Mechanisms can reach. Agent Artifact Review can catch a mismatch between the stated 0.13 and the implemented value, but no consequence is quantified for this parameter specifically.

assessments.title: Upper Bound
assessments.quote: The Upper Bound $b$ is an estimate of the correlation between assets during "stressful" market environments. It is set to `0.33`.
assessments.description: Sets the Upper Bound correlation parameter for stressful markets to 0.33 in the Financial RRC calculation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact value (b = 0.33), so the core parameter is quantified. It lacks a defined stressful-market window, an estimation method, and any update cadence for the estimate.
metrics: Upper Bound b = 0.33
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A Prime or Operational Agent that uses a different b in the RRC calculation is not blocked on-chain. Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) could catch the mismatch, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could then apply, but no consequence is quantified for this specific parameter.

assessments.title: Sensitivity Coefficient
assessments.quote: The Sensitivity Factor `K` is a tuning parameter indicating how quickly the correlations transition between $a$ and $b$. It is set to `10`.
assessments.description: Sets the Sensitivity Factor K, which controls how quickly correlations transition in the required risk capital calculation, to 10.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete value (K = 10), which a third party can verify against the calculation parameters. It does not state the formula in which K is used, and the transition function it tunes is defined elsewhere, so the parameter's effect is not fully specified here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: K sits within the Risk Capital requirement calculation, so a Prime using a different K breaches Risk Capital rules, which reach the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship. Nothing enforces K itself on-chain, and the consequence is not quantified for this parameter, so detection depends on someone reviewing the calculation.

assessments.title: Calculate Capital Requirement Without Buffers
assessments.quote:
The fourth step is to calculate the Capital Requirement Without Buffers $K$. $K$ is calculated as follows:

$$
K = \left[ LGD \times N\left( \frac{N^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{R} \cdot N^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1-R}} \right) - PD \times LGD \right]
$$

Here $N$ is the cumulative normal probability distribution function and $N^{-1}$ is the inverse cumulative normal probability distribution function.
assessments.description: Defines the formula for Capital Requirement Without Buffers K from LGD, PD, asset correlation R, and a 0.999 confidence level.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified and the 0.999 confidence level is stated. The inputs PD, LGD and R are not given values or sourcing in this paragraph, and the rounding and measurement cadence are not stated.
metrics: K = LGD × N((N^-1(PD) + sqrt(R) × N^-1(0.999)) / sqrt(1-R)) - PD × LGD
confidence level 0.999

assessments.title: Reference Implementation
assessments.quote:
A reference implementation of the calculation of Instance Financial RRC for lending markets is included herein.

```python
import math

from scipy.stats import norm

# Constants
RISK_FREE_RATE = 0.04  # SOFR
TIME_HORIZON = 1  # 1 year


class FinancialRRCModel:
    def __init__(self):
        # For demo purposes, we hardcode a dummy correlation map
        self.token_correlation_map = {
            "TOKENA": {"TOKENB": 0.5},
            "TOKENB": {"TOKENA": 0.5},
        }

    def _calculate_effective_volatility(self, list_1, list_2):
        """
        Calculate the effective variance between two sets of positions.
        """
        effective_variance = 0.0
        for sym1, pos1 in list_1.items():
            for sym2, pos2 in list_2.items():
                if sym1 == sym2:
                    corr = 1.0
                else:
                    corr = self.token_correlation_map.get(sym1, {}).get(
                        sym2, self.token_correlation_map.get(sym2, {}).get(sym1, 0.0)
                    )
                effective_variance += (
                    pos1["share"]
                    * pos2["share"]
                    * pos1["volatility_30d"]
                    * pos2["volatility_30d"]
                    * corr
                )
        return effective_variance

    def _estimate_rrc_for_position(self, wallet_data):
        """
        Estimate the required-risk capital (RRC) for a given wallet_data dict.
        """
        # 1) compute effective volatilities
        var_coll = self._calculate_effective_volatility(
            wallet_data["collateral_positions"],
            wallet_data["collateral_positions"],
        )
        var_debt = self._calculate_effective_volatility(
            wallet_data["debt_positions"],
            wallet_data["debt_positions"],
        )
        vol_coll = math.sqrt(var_coll)
        vol_debt = math.sqrt(var_debt)

        # 2) correlation collateral↔debt
        cov_cd = self._calculate_effective_volatility(
            wallet_data["collateral_positions"],
            wallet_data["debt_positions"],
        )
        corr_cd = cov_cd / (vol_coll * vol_debt) if vol_coll * vol_debt > 0 else 0.0

        # 3) drift terms
        eff_coll_rate = sum(
            p["share"] * p["supply_apy_30d"]
            for p in wallet_data["collateral_positions"].values()
        )
        eff_borrow_rate = sum(
            p["share"] * p["borrow_apy_30d"]
            for p in wallet_data["debt_positions"].values()
        )
        eff_stake_rate = sum(
            p["share"] * p["staking_apy_30d"]
            for p in wallet_data["collateral_positions"].values()
        )

        drift_cd = (
            eff_coll_rate + eff_stake_rate - eff_borrow_rate + (var_debt - var_coll) / 2
        )

        vol_cd = math.sqrt(
            max(var_coll + var_debt - 2 * corr_cd * vol_coll * vol_debt, 0)
        )

        # 4) Black-Cox inputs
        a = (drift_cd - vol_cd**2 / 2) / (vol_cd**2) if vol_cd > 0 else 0.0
        L = wallet_data["collateral_usd_lt"]
        D = wallet_data["debt_usd"]
        log_term = math.log(L / D) if L > 0 and D > 0 else float("-inf")
        denom = vol_cd * math.sqrt(TIME_HORIZON) if vol_cd > 0 else 1e-10

        d1 = (log_term + (drift_cd - vol_cd**2 / 2) * TIME_HORIZON) / denom
        d2 = (log_term - (drift_cd - vol_cd**2 / 2) * TIME_HORIZON) / denom

        # 5) Probability of Default
        try:
            pd = norm.cdf(-d1) + norm.cdf(-d2) * (L / D) ** (-2 * a)
        except OverflowError:
            pd = 1.0
        pd = max(0.0, min(pd, 1.0))

        # 6) Loss Given Default
        recovery = sum(
            p["share"]
            * (1 - p["liquidation_penalty"])
            * (1 - p["slippage"])
            / p["liquidation_threshold"]
            for p in wallet_data["collateral_positions"].values()
        )
        lgd = max(0.0, min(1 - recovery, 1.0))

        # 7) Exposure at Default
        ead = sum(
            debt["debt_usd"]
            * math.exp((RISK_FREE_RATE + debt["borrow_apy_30d"]) * TIME_HORIZON)
            for debt in wallet_data["debt_positions"].values()
        )

        # 8) Asset Correlation Coefficient
        a_acc, b_acc, c_acc = 0.13, 10, 0.33
        exp_term = math.exp(-b_acc * pd)
        acc = a_acc * (1 - exp_term) / (1 - math.exp(-b_acc)) + c_acc * (
            1 - (1 - exp_term) / (1 - math.exp(-b_acc))
        )

        # 9) Credit risk weight
        default_threshold = (
            norm.ppf(max(pd, 1e-10)) + math.sqrt(acc) * norm.ppf(0.999)
        ) / math.sqrt(1 - acc)
        credit_risk = max(lgd * norm.cdf(default_threshold) - lgd * pd, 0)

        # 10) RRC
        rrc = credit_risk * ead
        return rrc


# -------- DEMO USAGE --------

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # 1) Build a dummy wallet_data structure
    wallet_data = {
        "collateral_positions": {
            "TOKENA": {
                "share": 0.6,
                "volatility_30d": 0.2,
                "supply_apy_30d": 0.05,
                "staking_apy_30d": 0.02,
                "liquidation_penalty": 0.1,
                "liquidation_threshold": 0.8,
                "slippage": 0.01,
            },
            "TOKENB": {
                "share": 0.4,
                "volatility_30d": 0.25,
                "supply_apy_30d": 0.04,
                "staking_apy_30d": 0.015,
                "liquidation_penalty": 0.12,
                "liquidation_threshold": 0.85,
                "slippage": 0.015,
            },
        },
        "debt_positions": {
            "TOKENA": {
                "share": 0.7,
                "volatility_30d": 0.2,
                "borrow_apy_30d": 0.06,
                "debt_usd": 100_000,
            },
            "TOKENB": {
                "share": 0.3,
                "volatility_30d": 0.25,
                "borrow_apy_30d": 0.07,
                "debt_usd": 50_000,
            },
        },
        "collateral_usd_lt": 200_000,
        "debt_usd": 150_000,
    }
```

assessments.title: Citations To Basel Framework
assessments.quote:
Citations are made throughout the process for calculating Instance Financial RRC for Real World Assets to relevant provisions from the Basel Framework.

These citations follow the standard format of `[Prefix][Chapter Number].[Paragraph Number]`, where `Prefix` is a three letter prefix indicating the regulatory standard area or chapter family. For example, a citation to `CRE20.1` refers to Credit Risk Standards, Chapter 20 regarding "Standardised Approach: Individual Exposures", paragraph 1.

When reference is made to a range of documents, a hyphen may be used. For example, `CRE20.1-93` refers to Credit Risk Standards, Chapter 20 regarding "Standardised Approach: Individual Exposures", paragraphs 1 through 93.

Similarly, discrete sets of documents may be referenced using a comma. For example, `CRE40-41, 45` refers to Credit Risk Standards, Chapters 40 to 41 and 45.
assessments.description: Defines the citation format for referencing Basel Framework provisions when calculating Instance Financial RRC for Real World Assets.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The citation grammar is concrete: a three-letter prefix, chapter.paragraph numbering, hyphen ranges, and comma-separated sets, with worked examples. However, the operative obligation to cite is not quantified, and the text sets no cadence, verification method, or defined checker.
metrics: Citation format: [Prefix][Chapter Number].[Paragraph Number]
Prefix is a three-letter code for the regulatory standard area
Hyphen denotes an inclusive range of chapters or paragraphs (e.g., CRE20.1-93)
Comma denotes a discrete set of chapters or paragraphs (e.g., CRE40-41, 45)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism in the catalog or cited in the paragraph reaches citation formatting in Instance Financial RRC calculations. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply, so the rating is weak with none found.

assessments.title: Funds / Collective Investment Undertakings / Exchange Traded Funds

Risk Weights for Funds / Collective Investment Undertakings / Exchange Traded Funds (see `CRE60`) are calculated as follows:

- If look-through is feasible, apply the Look Through Approach (see `CRE60.2-5`)
- If look-through is not feasible but the mandate information is available, apply the Mandate Based Approach (see `CRE60.6-7`)
- If look-through is not feasible and the mandate information is not available, apply the fallback conservative approach (see `CRE60.8`)
assessments.description: Sets a three-tier waterfall for risk weights on fund exposures: look-through, then mandate-based, then a fallback conservative approach.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Risk Rating Calculation
assessments.quote:
The second step in calculating the Instance Smart Contract RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Smart Contract Risk Rating $SCRR$ for the covered smart contracts identified in [A.3.2.2.1.2.1 - Defining Relevant Smart Contracts](162cfc93-77bd-4878-a8be-370d8862d792). The $SCRR$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{SCRR} = min[\text{CAP}, (\text{SR} + \text{CCR}) \times \text{LAF} \times {AF}]
$$

Here $min$ is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters.
The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Smart Contract Risk Rating as the minimum of a cap and a formula combining SR, CCR, LAF and AF for covered contracts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact formula with a min function, which a third party could recompute. The inputs (CAP, SR, CCR, LAF, AF) are delegated to subdocuments and no values are stated here, so the magnitudes are not fixed in this text.
metrics: SCRR = min[CAP, (SR + CCR) × LAF × AF]
SCRR calculated for covered smart contracts identified in A.3.2.2.1.2.1
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SCRR feeds the Instance Smart Contract RRC, a Risk Capital requirement under A.3.2.2. An understated SCRR is a capital requirement breach, which reaches the Penalty Mechanisms and escalates to conservatorship with the Sky Core Facilitator taking control of the Prime. The paragraph does not state this path itself, so it is implicit.

assessments.title: Code Complexity Rating
assessments.quote:
The Code Complexity Rate $CCR$ is a measure of the complexity of the code of the smart contracts used by the protocol. The $CCR$ is calculated as follows:

$$
CCR = \text{CCRMax} \times min(1, \frac{\text{RawCCR} + 1}{\text{CCRUpperBound} + 1})
$$

Here the $min$ function is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines a Code Complexity Rate formula, capping it at CCRMax using RawCCR and CCRUpperBound, with parameters deferred to subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The capped min-formula is exact, but CCRMax, RawCCR and CCRUpperBound have no values or measurement method here, and the paragraph explicitly delegates them to subdocuments. Compliance can be checked against the formula but not the magnitudes.
metrics: CCR = CCRMax × min(1, (RawCCR + 1) / (CCRUpperBound + 1))
Parameter values (CCRMax, RawCCR, CCRUpperBound) delegated to subdocuments
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The CCR feeds the Risk Capital requirement calculation, so a miscalculated CCR could understate required capital that Primes must hold. Penalty Mechanisms plausibly reach that, but no consequence is quantified for this formula and firing requires review.

assessments.title: Raw Code Complexity Rating
assessments.quote:
The Raw Code Complexity Rating $\text{RawCCR}$ is an unnormalized measure of the complexity of the code of the smart contracts that implement the protocol. The $\text{RawCCR}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{RawCCR}=(\text{TCC} \times \text{CCweight}) + (\text{TDP} \times \text{DPweight}) + (\text{TEC} \times \text{ECweight}) + (\text{ID} \times \text{IDweight}) + (\frac{\text{CS}}{\text{CSfactor}} \times \text{CSweight})
$$

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with named terms and operators, so the calculation structure is exact. However, every weight, the CSfactor, and the input values (TCC, TDP, TEC, ID, CS) are deferred to subdocuments, so no magnitude is stated in this paragraph.

assessments.title: Lindy Adjustment Factor
assessments.quote:
The Lindy Adjustment Factor $\text{LAF}$ is a measure of the "Lindiness" of the smart contracts and is based on the idea that vulnerable smart contracts with large TVL for a significant period of time would have already been hacked. Therefore, protocols with a greater time integrated TVL are safer, all other things equal, than protocols with a lower time integrated TVL. The $\text{LAF}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{LAF} = max(0, 1 - \frac{ln(1 + \lambda \times \text{AGEeff})}{ln(1 + \lambda \times \text{max})})
$$

Here $max$ is the mathematical maximum function that returns the greater of the specified parameters and $ln$ is the natural logarithm.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Lindy Adjustment Factor formula, which reduces risk capital for smart contracts with longer time-integrated TVL.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The LAF formula is fully specified with an exact expression and a max floor at zero. The inputs λ, AGEeff and max have no values in this paragraph and are deferred to subdocuments.
metrics: LAF = max(0, 1 − ln(1 + λ × AGEeff) / ln(1 + λ × max))
λ, AGEeff and max defined in subdocuments without values here
assessments.enforcementReasoning: LAF is an input to the Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculation would breach Risk Capital rules, which the Penalty Mechanisms reach. No consequence is quantified for this formula, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it.
