assessments.quote: The Decay Factor $lambda$ is a tuning parameter that represents an estimate of how quickly the risk of a set of smart contracts decreases as its effective age increases. The value of $lambda$ is set to `0.1`.
assessments.description: Sets the Decay Factor lambda, a tuning parameter for how fast smart-contract risk falls with effective age, to 0.1.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states an exact value (lambda = 0.1), so the parameter is objectively checkable. It does not say how lambda enters the RRC calculation, when it may be revised, or who approves a change, so those gaps keep it below 5.
metrics: lambda (Decay Factor) = 0.1
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The value is embedded in the Instance Smart Contract RRC Implementation, so a deployed lambda that differs from the stated 0.1 would be caught only by Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7). A resulting under-stated risk capital requirement for a Prime would fall under the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), but no consequence is quantified for this parameter itself.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: A deployed value other than 60 would be a Required Risk Capital calculation error, which Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could catch and which falls under Risk Capital Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). assessments.title: Effective Age
assessments.quote:
The Effective Age $\text{AGEeff}$ is the age of the contracts adjusted for the TVL of the contracts. The $\text{AGEeff}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{AGEeff}=\text{CA} \times ln(1 + \frac{\text{gmTVL}}{\text{TVLthreshold}})
$$

Here $ln$ is the natural logarithm.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines Effective Age as contract age CA scaled by the natural log of one plus gmTVL over TVLthreshold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is explicit, but CA, gmTVL and TVLthreshold have no values here and are delegated to subdocuments. Its operative magnitudes are therefore not stated in this paragraph.
metrics: AGEeff = CA × ln(1 + gmTVL / TVLthreshold)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a definitional formula that imposes no compliance obligation of its own. Any consequence would attach to the Risk Capital calculation paragraphs that consume it, not to this definition.

assessments.title: Contract Age

However, "relevant contracts" is not defined in this paragraph, and the operative verb is "should," leaving the measurement obligation soft.

assessments.title: Audit Factor
assessments.quote:
The Audit Factor $AF$ is a measure of the extent to which the Base Risk is reduced by audits. The $AF$ is calculated as:

$$
AF = \Pi{[1 - \text{effAuditValue} \times \text{decayFactor}]}
$$

The audit from each audit firm with the highest product of Effective Audit Value and Delay factor should be included in this calculation.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

Selection of audits (highest product per firm) is stated but depends on the undefined Delay factor.

assessments.title: Effective Audit Value
assessments.quote:
The Effective Audit Value $\text{effAuditValue}$ measures the effectiveness of a single audit in reducing the risk of a set of smart contracts and is a function of the percent of the code covered by the audit and the reputation of the audit firm. The $\text{effAuditValue}$ is calculated as:

$$
\text{effAuditValue} = \text{effectivenessCoefficient} \times \text{coverage}
$$

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states an explicit formula, but effectivenessCoefficient and coverage are defined only in subdocuments, and audit-firm reputation is named without any measurement method or value. The operative magnitudes are delegated, so the rule is not fully verifiable from this text.
metrics: effAuditValue = effectivenessCoefficient × coverage

The consequence is not quantified for this formula, and no mechanism directly enforces the calculation itself.

The Coverage $\text{coverage}$ is a measure of the percent of a set of smart contracts that were covered in the scope of an audit. The $\text{coverage}$ is calculated as:

\text{coverage} = \frac{\text{LinesOfCodeCovered}}{\text{TotalLinesOfCode}}
$$

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

The paragraph sets no minimum coverage threshold or deadline, so it defines a metric without stating an operative requirement.

assessments.title: Decay Factor
assessments.quote:
The Decay Factor $decayFactor$ is a parameter indicating how rapidly the effectiveness of audits in reducing risk decreases over time. The $decayFactor$ is calculated as follows:

$$

assessments.title: Piecewise Function
assessments.quote:
The Piecewise Function $CRR(x)$ calculates a percentage risk capital requirement based on an input $x$ and is defined as follows:

$$
\text{CRR}(x) =\begin{cases}a & \text{if } x \le x_{\text{start}}, \\[8pt]b \times \dfrac{x - x_{\text{start}}}{x_{\text{kink}} - x_{\text{start}}} & \text{if } x_{\text{start}} < x \le x_{\text{kink}}, \\[8pt]b \;+\; c \;\dfrac{x - x_{\text{kink}}}{x_{\text{max}} - x_{\text{kink}}}& \text{if } x_{\text{kink}} < x < x_{\text{max}}, \\[8pt]d& \text{if } x \ge x_{\text{max}}.\end{cases}
$$
assessments.description: Defines a piecewise function mapping an input x to a percentage risk capital requirement CRR(x), with parameters a, b, c, d and thresholds x_start, x_kink, x_max.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The piecewise formula and its branch boundaries are exact and mechanically computable. However, the parameters a, b, c, d and the thresholds x_start, x_kink, x_max, and the meaning of input x, are symbolic here with no values, so the operative magnitudes are delegated elsewhere.
metrics: CRR(x) = a for x <= x_start
CRR(x) = b * (x - x_start)/(x_kink - x_start) for x_start < x <= x_kink
CRR(x) = b + c * (x - x_kink)/(x_max - x_kink) for x_kink < x < x_max
CRR(x) = d for x >= x_max
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph defines the calculation feeding Risk Capital requirements, and the Smart Contract RRC implementation can diverge from this formula. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly catches a mismatch with staged findings and penalty assessment, but no consequence is quantified for this formula specifically.

assessments.title: Reference Implementation
assessments.quote:
The document herein contains a reference implementation of the calculation of Instance Smart Contract RRC based on the Smart Contract Risk Rating.

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Function Definition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def piecewise_coverage(x, x_start, x_kink, x_max):
    """
    Returns a coverage fraction in [0.0 ... 1.0] given x
    and piecewise linear thresholds:
      - 0% coverage if x < x_start
      - linear 0%→25% from x_start to x_kink
      - linear 25%→100% from x_kink to x_max
      - 100% if x > x_max
    """
    # Safely handle edge cases
    if x <= x_start:
        return 0.0
    if x >= x_max:
        return 1.0

    # If between x_start and x_kink -> map linearly from 0% to 25%
    if x_start < x <= x_kink:
        span = x_kink - x_start
        # fraction of the way through that segment
        frac = (x - x_start) / span
        # coverage goes 0 -> 0.25 (25%)
        return 0.25 * frac

    # If between x_kink and x_max -> map linearly from 25% to 100%
    else:  # x_kink < x < x_max
        span = x_max - x_kink
        frac = (x - x_kink) / span
        # coverage goes 0.25 -> 1.0
        return 0.25 + (0.75 * frac)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Thresholds
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating):
    """
    Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
    in % terms, e.g. 5%, 23.75%, 30%, etc.
    """
    x_start = (50 - rating) * 0.01  # e.g. rating=0 -> 0.5 (50%)
    x_max = x_start + 0.50  # always a 50% gap to max
    # kink is 75% of the way from start to max
    x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start)
    return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)


def f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating):
    """
    Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
    in fraction form (0.50, 0.875, 1.00, etc).
    """
    # starting threshold = (75 - rating) * 2%:
    x_start = (75 - rating) * 0.02
    x_max = x_start + 0.50
    x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start)  # 75% of the way
    return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# RRC Calculation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def calculate_rrc_coverage(
    rating,
    exposure_internal,
    exposure_total,
    liquid_surplus_internal,
    total_exposure_beyond_surplus,
    total_collateral,
):
    """
    Returns the coverage fraction (0 - 1) for a given rating & scenario.
    For the absolute coverage amount, multiply coverage_fraction
    by `exposure_internal`.
    """

    # 1) Compute the two driver ratios
    f1 = max(
        0.0, total_exposure_beyond_surplus / total_collateral
    )  # Ensuring it is non-negative when surplus > exposure
    f2 = (
        exposure_internal + 0.1 * (exposure_total - exposure_internal)
    ) / liquid_surplus_internal

    # 2) Determine which category the rating is in
    if rating <= 25:
        # TRR Category 1 (Low Risk)  => use only f1 piecewise
        x_start, x_kink, x_max = f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating)
        coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

    elif rating <= 50:
        # TRR Category 2 (Medium Risk) => blend coverage from f1-curve and f2-curve
        # First get coverage from the "f1 low-risk"
        x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1 = f1_thresholds_low_risk(25)
        cov_f1 = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1)

        # Then get coverage from the "f2 high-risk"
        x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2 = f2_thresholds_high_risk(50)
        cov_f2 = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2)

        # Blend factor alpha
        alpha = (rating - 25) / (50 - 25)
        coverage_fraction = (1 - alpha) * cov_f1 + 0.15 * alpha * cov_f2

    elif rating <= 75:
        # TRR Category 3 (High Risk) => use only f2
        x_start, x_kink, x_max = f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating)
        coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

    else:
        # TRR Category 4 (Extreme Risk) => special piecewise lumps.
        if rating > 75:
            return 1.0

    return coverage_fraction
```

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The piecewise formulas, slopes (0 to 25% then 25 to 100%), threshold offsets (50 and 75 rating anchors, 0.50 gap, 75% kink), 0.1 exposure weighting, and 0.15 blend factor are all exact. Scope is slightly unclear because the paragraph calls itself a reference implementation, and inputs such as the rating and liquid_surplus_internal are defined elsewhere.

assessments.title: Administrative Risk Rating Calculation
assessments.quote:
The first step in calculating the Instance Administrative RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Administrative Risk Rating $\text{ARR}$ for the protocol being invested in. The $\text{ARR}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{ARR} = min[\text{CAP}, \text{SR} \times \text{DF} \times \text{LAF}]
$$

Here $min$ is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Administrative Risk Rating as the minimum of CAP and the product SR×DF×LAF, with inputs specified in subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula ARR = min[CAP, SR × DF × LAF] is exact, but none of the four parameters (CAP, SR, DF, LAF) has a value or range in this paragraph, and the text explicitly defers them to subdocuments. The magnitudes are delegated, so the rule names what is regulated but not how much.
metrics: ARR = min[CAP, SR × DF × LAF]
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The ARR feeds the Instance Administrative RRC, which sets Risk Capital requirements. Penalty Mechanisms reach Risk Capital rule violations, so a miscalculated or non-compliant ARR could trigger them. No consequence is quantified for this calculation step itself, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Delay Factor
assessments.quote:
The Delay Adjustment Factor $\text{DF}$ is a factor indicating the extent to which the risk associated with backdoor access is mitigated by a security delay between the time that a change using backdoor access is approved and the time that such a change becomes effective. This delay gives users time to raise issues or withdraw funds in the event of malicious or undesirable use of backdoor access.

The Delay Factor is `1` if there is no security delay and `0` if the security delay is 48 hours or greater. For security delays between 0 hours and 48 hours, the Delay Factor is linearly reduced for each hour of security delay. So a security delay of 24 hours would result in a Delay Factor of `0.5`.
assessments.description: Defines the Delay Adjustment Factor as a linear function of security delay hours, from 1 at zero hours to 0 at 48 hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact piecewise formula: DF is 1 at zero delay, 0 at 48 hours or more, and linear between, with 24 hours yielding 0.5. A third party can compute the factor from the stated inputs. The only unstated element is the source of the security delay value, which is defined elsewhere.

Delay Factor = 0 if security delay is 48 hours or greater
Delay Factor reduced linearly per hour for security delays between 0 and 48 hours
Example: 24 hours of security delay yields a Delay Factor of 0.5
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Delay Factor is an input to Required Risk Capital, so a miscomputed factor understates capital and is a Risk Capital violation that the Penalty Mechanisms can reach. assessments.title: Deposit And Redemption Queues
assessments.quote:
The srUSDS contract utilizes distinct queues for managing conversions. Users can add USDS to the deposit queue for conversion into srUSDS; or add srUSDS to the redemption queue for conversion back into USDS at any point during the month.

Assets placed in either queue can be withdrawn by the user at any time before the Monthly Settlement Cycle begins.

At the Monthly Settlement Cycle, all assets remaining in the queues are processed: queued USDS is converted into srUSDS, and queued srUSDS is converted into USDS based on the prevailing Conversion Rate. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.3 - Conversion Rate](2220b1b5-f2f6-4325-9bb5-43cca84e184c).

assessments.title: Conversion Rate
assessments.quote:
The conversion rate represents the amount of USDS redeemable per unit of srUSDS. This rate increases or decreases over time, reflecting the net return earned by the ESRC pool. The rate is updated at the conclusion of each Monthly Settlement Cycle based on the performance of the ESRC pool during the preceding month, according to the following standard compounding formula:

`New srUSDS Conversion Rate = Previous Conversion Rate * (1 + Monthly srUSDS Yield)`

The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein.

The Monthly srUSDS Yield input is defined elsewhere with no value given in this paragraph, so the magnitude of the update is not verifiable from this text alone.

assessments.title: Monthly srUSDS Yield
assessments.quote:
`Monthly srUSDS Yield` represents the net percentage return earned solely by the ESRC pool during the concluded monthly cycle, distributable to srUSDS holders via the conversion rate adjustment. It directly reflects the risk-adjusted performance of the capital deployed and is calculated as:

`[(Total Interest Paid by Stars on ESRC Portion - Losses Allocated to ESRC) / ESRC Principal at start of month - Sky Spread] * (1 - ESRC Earnings Fee)`

The Sky Spread and ESRC Earnings Fee are specified in [A.3.2.2.4.2.3.3.1 - Sky Spread](c160f99c-c3d8-41e9-a3d1-cde514b7a2da) and [A.3.2.2.4.2.3.3.2 - ESRC Earnings Fee](559f6fb6-daf6-41b2-9882-53a91aaf132f), respectively.
assessments.description: Defines the monthly srUSDS yield as ESRC net return after losses, Sky Spread, and earnings fee, distributed via conversion rate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core formula is fully specified with explicit operands and a monthly cycle, and the principal is tied to start-of-month. However, Sky Spread and ESRC Earnings Fee are defined only by reference to other paragraphs with no values here, and 'Losses Allocated to ESRC' is undefined in this text.

assessments.title: Senior Risk Capital (SRC) Origination Process
assessments.quote: This document defines the operational details of the recurring monthly process allowing Prime Agents to originate Senior Risk Capital (Originated Senior Risk Capital or OSRC) from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool. The process involves determining the available TSRC supply, a bidding phase, an allocation auction, and settlement aligned with the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.description: Outlines the recurring monthly process by which Prime Agents originate Senior Risk Capital from the TSRC pool via supply determination, bidding, auction, and settlement.

The paragraph itself states no consequence and the penalty magnitude for this specific process is unquantified, so it rates mid.

assessments.title: Process Timing and Schedule
assessments.quote: The SRC origination process operates monthly, synchronized with the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The bidding window occurs during the current month for SRC that is usable in the next month; the bidding window closes before settlement processing begins. Additional operational details, including timelines, will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

metrics: Origination process operates monthly

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain control, or escalation path is tied to SRC origination scheduling; the only generic backstop is the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls, which alone are weak.

assessments.title: Available Total Senior Risk Capital Pool Determination
assessments.quote: Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) is the amount of Senior Risk Capital that is available each Monthly Settlement Cycle for Primes to originate and thus turn into Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) through the monthly origination process. TSRC is the sum of designated Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) (see [A.2.3.1.3 - Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital](ac7a6636-acbc-40c9-abc1-4543c0beb300)) and available External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) from the srUSDS contract. Prior to each monthly bidding window, the TSRC is calculated and publicly announced. Additional operational details will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Defines Total Senior Risk Capital as internal plus available external capital, calculated and announced monthly before each bidding window.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a summation formula (ISRC plus available ESRC from the srUSDS contract) and a monthly cadence with public announcement before bidding. However, what counts as 'available' ESRC and the operational calculation details are deferred to a future iteration, so a defender could argue the obligation does not yet bind.
metrics: TSRC = designated ISRC + available ESRC from the srUSDS contract
TSRC calculated and publicly announced prior to each monthly bidding window
Applies each Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No cited mechanism reaches the calculation or announcement duty; Agent Artifact Review and the misalignment backstop are not tied to this definitional rule, and the ESRC availability input is not contract-enforced here.

assessments.title: Bidding Process
assessments.quote: Participating Prime Agents submit bids via the Powerhouse interface during the defined bidding window. Each bid must specify: (1) The quantity of SRC the Prime seeks to originate, and (2) The maximum price the Prime is willing to pay (expressed in basis points above the Base Rate) for using the OSRC during the upcoming monthly period. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Requires Participating Primes to submit bids via Powerhouse specifying SRC quantity and a maximum basis-point spread over Base Rate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names required bid fields and a unit (basis points above Base Rate) but gives no numeric limits, window duration, or submission deadline. The defining details are deferred to a future iteration, so a defender could argue the rule does not yet bind.
metrics: Each bid specifies the quantity of SRC the Prime seeks to originate
Each bid specifies a maximum price in basis points above the Base Rate
Bids are submitted during the defined bidding window
Bids apply to the upcoming monthly period

assessments.title: Allocation & Clearing Price Determination
assessments.quote: Bids are ranked descending by price. TSRC is allocated sequentially to the highest bids until the pool is exhausted or all bids are filled. The price of the lowest successful bid that receives an allocation (even partial) sets the uniform clearing price for the month. All winning bidders pay this clearing price per unit of OSRC allocated, regardless of their original bid price. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Allocates SRC by descending bid rank and sets a uniform monthly clearing price at the lowest successful bid.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The allocation algorithm and clearing-price rule are enumerated and checkable, but TSRC pool size, bid timing, unit definitions, and tie-breaking are undefined. The paragraph also explicitly defers operational details to a future iteration.
metrics: Bids ranked descending by price
TSRC allocated sequentially until pool exhausted or all bids filled
Clearing price = price of lowest successful bid receiving allocation (even partial)
Clearing price applies per unit of OSRC allocated, monthly
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a Risk Capital origination rule, so Penalty Mechanisms could reach misapplication of the auction, and Agent Artifact Review could catch a deviating implementation. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific allocation or pricing rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the auction logic.

assessments.title: Settlement Of Origination
assessments.quote: During the Monthly Settlement Cycle following allocation, the cost (Allocated OSRC Quantity * Clearing Price) is deducted from each winning Prime Agent’s operational account. Concurrently, the allocated OSRC amount is credited to the Prime Agent’s Risk Capital account as OSRC for the upcoming monthly period.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The cost formula (Allocated OSRC Quantity * Clearing Price), the named actor (winning Prime Agent), and the Monthly Settlement Cycle timing are all stated. Clearing Price is an input defined elsewhere with no value given here, and the paragraph does not say how an unpaid settlement is handled.
metrics: Cost = Allocated OSRC Quantity * Clearing Price, deducted from each winning Prime Agent's operational account

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules, and this settlement is part of the Senior Risk Capital origination process. No consequence is quantified for non-payment or late settlement, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: OSRC Duration and Renewal
assessments.quote: OSRC is valid only for the single monthly period following the settlement cycle in which it was originated. Renewal requires successful participation in the next monthly origination process; there is no automatic rollover.

assessments.title: Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) Rental Implementation

assessments.title: Ecosystem Accord Requirements
assessments.quote:
Rental of Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) requires a registered Ecosystem Accord specifying: Amount, Duration, and Price/Terms. As the system permits sub-renting (allowing a Prime to rent out OSRC it has previously rented), the Accord must explicitly state if the borrower is granted this permission. In regards to Duration, the Ecosystem Accord must specify the rental period, which cannot extend beyond the end of the current Monthly Settlement Cycle. Primes may agree on any Duration within this limit.

Standardized Ecosystem Accord templates will be provided in a future iteration of the Atlas.

assessments.title: SRC Accounting & Enablement

The borrowing Prime Agent must possess sufficient Junior Risk Capital (IJRC, PEJRC, TEJRC) and corresponding Senior Per Junior (SPJ) capacity to enable the rented OSRC, such that it counts towards their own Risk Capital requirements. Rented OSRC that is not successfully enabled by the borrower pursuant to the SPJ ratio does not contribute to their Risk Capital calculation.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms in the Risk Capital regime plausibly reach a Prime that fails to supply or maintain the feeds that update its Risk Capital parameters. The penalty is not quantified for this specific obligation, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it.

assessments.title: High Severity Breach Definition
assessments.quote: A High Severity Breach is one in which the Encumbrance Ratio is greater than 103%.

Those consequences are not quantified for this tier here, and firing requires the breach to be identified and escalated.

assessments.title: Length Of Breaches
assessments.quote:
The length of a breach refers to the duration measured between its defined start and end points, which depend on the specific aspect of the breach being considered.

If a breach is initially a Low Severity Breach and subsequently becomes a High Severity Breach, then (1) the length of the Low Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a Low Severity Breach until it became a High Severity Breach; and (2) the length of the High Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a High Severity Breach until that high-severity period concludes (e.g., upon final resolution of the breach or a transition to a different severity level).

Likewise, if a breach is initially a High Severity Breach and subsequently becomes a Low Severity Breach, then (1) the length of the High Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a High Severity Breach until it became a Low Severity Breach; and (2) the length of the Low Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a Low Severity Breach until that low-severity period concludes (e.g., upon final resolution of the breach or a transition to a different severity level).
assessments.description: Defines how the duration of a Risk Capital breach is measured, including how low and high severity periods are timed when severity changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The start and end points for each severity period are defined, so the duration method is verifiable. assessments.title: Financial Penalties For First 30 Minutes
