assessments.title: Collection Of Penalties
assessments.quote: Penalties are calculated by the Core Executor Agents as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. See [A.2.4 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle](6f8d5065-d6ff-4add-9a28-eadeffa7ed1a). Once calculated, penalties are transferred from the Prime Agent’s SubProxy Account to Sky by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Core Executor Agents calculate Prime penalties in the monthly settlement; Sky Governance transfers them from the Prime SubProxy Account.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors (Core Executor Agents, Sky Governance) and a monthly cadence via the referenced settlement cycle are stated, but no penalty amount, formula, or transfer deadline appears in this paragraph. The magnitudes are delegated to the settlement cycle doc.
metrics: Penalties calculated as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle (monthly cadence)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is the collection step of the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which provide quantified financial penalties against Primes that breach Risk Capital rules. Collection is not automatic, though: it depends on Sky Governance acting on the calculated amount, so the consequence is not self-executing.

assessments.title: Alternative Enforcement Mechanisms
assessments.quote:
In the event that the Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital is less than its Required Risk Capital at the time of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, or the collection of the penalty would cause the Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital to fall below its Required Risk Capital, then Sky may exercise the alternative enforcement mechanism described below.

In this instance Sky, at its discretion, may issue additional tokens of the Prime Agent and sell them on the open market until it has collected proceeds equal to the calculated penalty. Any proceeds above the calculated penalty shall be refunded to the Prime Agent SubProxy account.

Alternatively, Sky may convert the penalty into a debt owed by the Prime Agent to Sky Core at terms mutually agreed between Sky Core and the Prime Agent.
assessments.description: Lets Sky collect a Prime Agent's capital-shortfall penalty by issuing and selling Prime tokens or converting it into debt.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger is concrete (Total Risk Capital below Required Risk Capital at the Monthly Settlement Cycle) and the collection methods are named. However, the penalty amount is only referenced as 'calculated penalty' with no formula here, Sky's use of the mechanism is discretionary, and the debt terms are 'mutually agreed'.
metrics: Total Risk Capital less than Required Risk Capital at the time of the Monthly Settlement Cycle
Token sales continue until proceeds equal the calculated penalty
Proceeds above the calculated penalty refunded to the Prime Agent SubProxy account
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is the alternative collection path of the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which reach capital-shortfall violations with a named enforcer (Sky) and concrete remedies. It is rated mid because Sky must volunteer its discretionary use of the mechanism and the penalty amount is calculated elsewhere.

assessments.title: Short-Term Exemption
assessments.quote: While the Risk Framework undergoes refinement, penalties for any Prime Agent breaches of Required Risk Capital will be calculated by Core GovOps once the infrastructure is in place to do so. This calculation serves the purposes of system monitoring, data gathering, and framework calibration. However, throughout this interim phase, such calculated penalties will not be formally assessed against Prime Agents, and consequently, Prime Agents will not be required to make payment for these penalties. Notwithstanding this temporary exemption from penalty payment, Prime Agents are expected to maintain a Encumbrance Ratio of less than or equal to 90%. See [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9).
assessments.description: Suspends formal penalty payments for Required Risk Capital breaches while expecting Primes to keep Encumbrance Ratio at or below 90%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 90% Encumbrance Ratio ceiling is a concrete value, with the metric defined in a linked paragraph. However, the obligation is framed as 'expected' rather than required, penalty calculation is tied to undefined infrastructure readiness, and payment is expressly waived, so a Prime could plausibly argue the rule does not yet bind it.
metrics: Encumbrance Ratio less than or equal to 90%
Penalties calculated by Core GovOps once infrastructure is in place (no date or trigger defined)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) are expressly disapplied for this interim phase, so no financial consequence attaches to a breach. No on-chain or structural mechanism is cited that reaches the 90% Encumbrance Ratio expectation, so only the generic misalignment backstop remains.

assessments.title: Additional Token Issuance For Breach Of Capital Requirements
assessments.quote: In the event that financial penalties are not sufficient to address the shortfall because payment of the penalties would exacerbate an existing capital shortfall, Core GovOps may require the Prime Agent to issue additional tokens and sell them to the extent it deems necessary. Operational GovOps will assist Core GovOps in executing any such transaction. Future iterations of the Risk Capital framework will specify a more detailed methodology for required token issuance.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps require a Prime Agent to issue and sell additional tokens when penalties cannot cover a capital shortfall.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Core GovOps, Operational GovOps, Prime Agent) but gives no threshold, formula, trigger metric, or deadline. It defers discretion with "to the extent it deems necessary" and explicitly leaves the methodology to future iterations, so there is nothing measurable to comply with yet.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps is a distinct enforcer, and the Risk-Capital Incident Response and Penalty Mechanisms can escalate a capital breach toward conservatorship. However, this token-issuance step is unquantified and only fires if Core GovOps chooses to invoke it, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Restrictions On Investments For Breach Of Capital Requirement
assessments.quote: Core GovOps may impose whatever restrictions it deems necessary on the usage of the Allocation System Primitive by the Prime Agent, including limiting the Prime Agent’s exposure to certain Instances (conduits) or prohibiting the Prime Agent from using certain Instances. These restrictions may extend for a period of time that Core GovOps deems fit.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps impose discretionary restrictions on a Prime Agent's use of the Allocation System, including exposure limits or prohibited Instances.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is entirely discretionary ("whatever restrictions it deems necessary", duration "that Core GovOps deems fit"). It names an actor and example remedy types, but gives no thresholds, durations, or criteria for triggering or sizing restrictions.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a penalty within the Penalty Mechanisms framework, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) reach a Prime's breach of capital requirements. Core GovOps is a distinct enforcer with concrete remedies, but the restriction is discretionary ("may") and unquantified, so escalation depends on Core GovOps acting.

assessments.title: Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements
assessments.quote: In the event that less extreme measures are not adequate to address the capital shortfall, Core GovOps may seek to put the Prime Agent into conservatorship, in which case the Sky Core Facilitator takes direct control of the Prime Agent to maximize value for Sky and other Prime Agent stakeholders. Seeking to put a Prime Agent into conservatorship requires immediate escalation to Sky Core Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48).
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps seek conservatorship of a Prime Agent after lesser measures fail to cure a capital shortfall, transferring control to the Facilitator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Core GovOps, Sky Core Facilitator, Sky Core Governance) and the escalation path are named, but the trigger is judgment language ("not adequate", "less extreme measures") with no capital-shortfall threshold. "May seek" and "immediate"/"expedited" have no cadence or deadline, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph is itself the Conservatorship mechanism (5c3dd35a), a named enforcer distinct from the Prime with a concrete remedy, and Risk-Capital Incident Response (12b7d480) supplies the framework. Firing depends on Core GovOps volunteering the escalation, so it is mid rather than strong, and no quantified penalty is stated for this rule.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For Operational Executor Agents
assessments.quote: In the near term there are no penalties for Operational Executor Agents for failure of the Prime Agents they supervise to maintain appropriate levels of capital. In future iterations of the Risk Framework, Operational Executor Agents will be required to put up collateral and act as "insurers" of all activities by the Prime Agents they supervise with regard to the Sky Primitives. At that point Core GovOps will be able to seize this collateral in the event of failure to obtain compensation for breaches of the Risk Capital requirement by the Prime Agent.
assessments.description: States Operational Executor Agents face no penalties for Prime capital failures now, with a future collateral regime deferred.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states no current obligation, threshold, or deadline. Its only concrete content is that no penalties apply near term, and the collateral and seizure regime is explicitly deferred to unspecified future iterations.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The text expressly disclaims penalties for Operational Executor Agents in the near term, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) it sits under do not reach this paragraph's current, unpenalized state. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Termination Of Executor Accord
assessments.quote: In the event that Core GovOps determines that the Operational Executor Agent is not appropriately supervising the activities of the Prime Agent, Core GovOps may terminate the respective Executor Accord. This requires an immediate escalation to Sky Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48). Core GovOps must arrange for another Operational Executor Agent to stand in until the Prime Agent can Invoke the Executor Accord Primitive to enter into a new Executor Accord. The Prime Agent must suspend all operations until a new Executor Accord is voted on and formally integrated into the Agent’s Artifact.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps terminate an Executor Accord when the Operational Executor is judged to inadequately supervise the Prime, with escalation and operations suspension.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The remedy steps are concrete: immediate escalation, an expedited Executive Vote, a stand-in executor, and suspension until a new accord is integrated. The trigger, 'not appropriately supervising', is a qualitative judgment with no defined criteria, metric, or cadence.
metrics: Immediate escalation to Sky Governance upon termination determination
Expedited Executive Vote per A.1.9.1.5.4.1 (3f5f79fa)
Core GovOps must arrange a stand-in Operational Executor Agent
Prime Agent must suspend all operations until a new Executor Accord is voted on and formally integrated into its Artifact
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) under which this paragraph sits, plus the Known And Uncontentious Remedies executive vote (3f5f79fa), reach the executor's supervision failure with a named enforcer (Core GovOps) distinct from the actor. Termination and suspension are concrete remedies, but the rule is discretionary ('may') and quantified penalties are not stated for this violation, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Triggers For Escalation
assessments.quote: In the event of a disagreement regarding the penalties for a violation of Risk Capital requirements, either party may escalate the matter to Sky Governance. In addition, the extraordinary remedies of Prime Agent Conservatorship and Executor Accord Termination must always be escalated to a Sky Governance Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Lets either party escalate Risk Capital penalty disputes to Sky Governance and requires Executive Vote for conservatorship or termination.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete actors and a mandatory route: either party may escalate, and conservatorship or Executor Accord Termination must go to an Executive Vote. It gives no criteria for what counts as a disagreement and no timeline for escalation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Sky Governance is a named enforcer distinct from the Prime, and the mandatory Executive Vote path leads to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), a concrete remedy. The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) supply the penalties that the disputes concern.

assessments.title: Sky Governance Process
assessments.quote: Once a matter has been escalated to Sky Governance, the Sky Core Facilitator may request any information they deem necessary from Core GovOps, Operational GovOps, and the Prime Agent. Sky Governance then acts through a Governance Poll to determine its resolution of the matter.
assessments.description: Lets the Sky Core Facilitator request information from GovOps and the Prime, then Sky Governance resolves escalated matters by Governance Poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A defined process and actors exist (Sky Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, Operational GovOps, Prime Agent, Governance Poll), but the information request is discretionary ("any information they deem necessary") with no deadline, scope, or response obligation. No thresholds or outcomes are specified, so compliance is judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is the Sky Governance escalation step inside the Penalty Mechanisms, which supply quantified penalties for Prime breaches. The paragraph itself does not quantify a consequence, and a Governance Poll must be initiated to reach one, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management
assessments.quote: The Asset Liability Management framework establishes universal rules for Prime Agents deploying Sky’s Collateral Portfolio to maintain the stability of the USDS peg through highly liquid assets. The Asset Liability Management framework governs collateral allocation across all Agents, via the Allocation System Primitive, and replaces Sky Core’s historical Asset Liability Management mechanisms which will be offboarded entirely or transitioned to Prime Agents.
assessments.description: Introduces the Asset Liability Management framework for Prime Agents deploying Collateral Portfolio assets to stabilize USDS via the Allocation System.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a scope and posture statement. It names actors (Prime Agents, Sky Core) and the Allocation System, but states no threshold, formula, cadence, or verifiable condition. It only says the framework will govern allocations and that legacy mechanisms will be offboarded or transitioned.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no rate limit, role requirement, or penalty. Controller rate limits and role gates would reach specific allocation paragraphs, not this framing statement, and no mechanism is triggered by its text.

assessments.title: Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: The "Sky Collateral Portfolio" consists of all assets backing USDS, whether deployed by Prime Agents or Sky Core. The Asset Liability Management framework is based on ensuring that a certain percentage of Sky Collateral Portfolio is invested in Actively Stabilizing Collateral, highly liquid market making non-USDS assets that trade for close to 1 USD per USDS. In this way, if there is ever downward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to buy USDS to maintain the peg.
assessments.description: Defines the Sky Collateral Portfolio and frames an unquantified share of it to be held as Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real obligation to keep a share of the Sky Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral, but the magnitude is only "a certain percentage", so no threshold, metric, cadence, or actor-level test appears. A defender could argue it does not yet bind anyone to a specific level.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found that reaches this paragraph's text. With no stated percentage, no breach is determinable, so penalty machinery and artifact review have nothing to act on; the numeric 5% minimum sits in a separate paragraph (475fe222), not this one.

assessments.title: Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.quote: The Asset Liability Management also ensures that a certain percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio is invested in a Demand Absorption Buffer, highly liquid market making USDS assets that trade for close to 1 USD per USDS. In this way, if there is ever upward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to sell USDS to maintain the peg.
assessments.description: Requires an unstated percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio to be held in a Demand Absorption Buffer of liquid USDS market-making assets.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real obligation to hold a share of the Sky Collateral Portfolio in a buffer, but the magnitude is only "a certain percentage" with no number, cadence, or measurement method. A party could argue it has not yet been given a binding level.
metrics: Percentage of Sky Collateral Portfolio invested in Demand Absorption Buffer (value not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, penalty, or review mechanism in the catalog is tied to the buffer allocation percentage, so only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Application To Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Each Prime Agent investing a portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio must maintain, with respect to its portion of same, the percentage of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer specified in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8). By ensuring that every Prime Agent maintains these levels, Sky as a whole remains compliant with the required thresholds of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer.
assessments.description: Requires each Prime Agent to hold the Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer percentages set in A.3.3.2.2.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (each Prime Agent) and the obligation, but states no numeric threshold itself and delegates the percentage to the cross-referenced A.3.3.2.2. No measurement cadence or verification method appears in this text.
metrics: Actively Stabilizing Collateral percentage specified in A.3.3.2.2 (deferred; not stated here)
Demand Absorption Buffer percentage specified in A.3.3.2.2 (deferred; not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) cover Prime compliance with Risk Capital rules and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could catch a shortfall against the referenced levels. No consequence is quantified for this specific paragraph, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Actively Stabilizing Collateral is collateral that actively supports the peg of USDS by market-making and providing buy support at a price close to 1 USD per USDS. The implementation of the Asset Liability Management framework specifies the downside spread that is allowed for collateral to qualify as Actively Stabilizing Collateral. See [A.3.3.2 - Implementation](bf1a1991-1c2b-457c-b1ca-6147049e93c5).
assessments.description: Defines Actively Stabilizing Collateral as collateral that market-makes and provides buy support near 1 USD per USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a qualitative definition using the judgment phrase "close to 1 USD per USDS" and states no numeric threshold. The downside spread that governs qualification is deferred to the Implementation section (bf1a1991), so the operative magnitude is not stated here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a definitional paragraph with no violation mode of its own; any consequence attaches to the downstream Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral rule, not to this definition. Artifact review could arguably reach misclassification, but nothing in the text routes this paragraph to it.

assessments.title: Application To Sky Core
assessments.quote: While its legacy ALM infrastructure is being transferred to Prime Agents, Sky Core manages the portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio not deployed by Prime Agents ("Sky Core Collateral Portfolio"). During this transitional period, Sky Core allocates the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral as specified in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf).
assessments.description: During the ALM transition, Sky Core allocates its unassigned collateral portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral per a cross-referenced rule.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Sky Core), the portfolio (Sky Core Collateral Portfolio), and the target asset class (Actively Stabilizing Collateral), but states no allocation percentage, threshold, or deadline. The operative criteria are delegated entirely to A.3.3.2.6, so compliance cannot be verified from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph references A.3.3.2.6 but describes no enforcement path, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Penalty Mechanisms, Liquidation Penalty, PSM) reaches a Sky Core-internal allocation decision. Only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event
assessments.quote: In addition to the requirement for Prime Agents to hold a certain percentage of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral and the Demand Absorption Buffer, Prime Agents have special responsibilities in extraordinary situations where the stability of the peg is threatened. The definition of these events and the obligations for Prime Agents are specified in the implementation of the framework. See [A.3.3.2 - Implementation](bf1a1991-1c2b-457c-b1ca-6147049e93c5).
assessments.description: States that Prime Agents have extra responsibilities during peg-threatening events, with the definitions and obligations deferred to another section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines no event, threshold, or obligation. It says the definitions and obligations are specified elsewhere and refers to 'a certain percentage' without stating it, so there is nothing enforceable in this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no consequence and no operative obligation, and no mechanism doc reaches a rule that is only a deferral to A.3.3.2.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management Rental
assessments.quote: To allow the Asset Liability Management obligation of Prime Agents to be satisfied in the most efficient way possible, Prime Agents may enter into Asset Liability Management Rentals between each other, as specified in the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive. This allows one Prime Agent to hold a greater amount of Actively Stabilizing Collateral to offset another Prime Agent holding a lesser amount. Thus, the overall level of Actively Stabilizing Collateral is unaffected but the Actively Stabilizing Collateral can be held by a Prime Agent that is able to more efficiently hold it.
assessments.description: Permits Prime Agents to satisfy Asset Liability Management obligations by renting Actively Stabilizing Collateral from each other.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real permission and mechanism (inter-Prime rentals offsetting ASC holdings) but gives no thresholds, limits, or cadence. It defers all operative terms to the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive, so compliance is hard to judge from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is permissive and sets no violation modes; the underlying ASC obligation has penalty machinery (b8ee2d12) and artifact review (d4bf73e7), but nothing in this text reaches a rental-specific breach.

assessments.title: All Asset Liability Management Obligations Are Rented Together
assessments.quote: When Asset Liability Management obligations are rented, the associated obligations with regard to Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Demand Absorption Buffer, and Peg Defense Events are all transferred together.
assessments.description: Requires that rented Asset Liability Management obligations transfer together with their Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Demand Absorption Buffer, and Peg Defense Event obligations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names three concrete obligation categories and a binary all-or-nothing transfer condition, which is checkable in principle. However, it gives no thresholds, metrics, cadence, or defined mechanics for what 'transferred together' requires, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a transfer of ALM obligations on rental: the Rate Limiter and role controls govern controller calls, and the Penalty Mechanisms target Risk Capital rule breaches, not this co-transfer condition.

assessments.title: Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Prime Agents must maintain at least 5% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to keep at least 5% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Prime Agents), a numeric floor (5%), and a verifiable portfolio share (Collateral Portfolio held as Actively Stabilizing Collateral). A third party could check compliance from the text alone. No measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: At least 5% of Collateral Portfolio held in Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) can check the 5% floor against Prime portfolio artifacts with an enforcer distinct from the Prime, and Penalty Mechanisms (A.3.2.2.7.2) could plausibly apply to a breach. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on review being run, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the sum of (1) Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral and (2) Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Defines Actively Stabilizing Collateral as the sum of Resting and Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an explicit additive formula with two named components, so the term is measurable in principle. It states no threshold, and both inputs are defined elsewhere without values, so it is a definition rather than an operative quantified obligation.
metrics: Actively Stabilizing Collateral = Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral + Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a definition with no obligation for a party to breach, and no citable mechanism (penalty, rate limit, liquidation, or review) reaches a definitional sum. The minimum-ASC rule that gives this term its purpose is a separate paragraph.

assessments.title: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements.
assessments.description: Requires resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral to provide buy support at or above 0.999 USD per USDS, with listed eligible asset types.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 0.999 USD per USDS price floor and 10bps downside spread are concrete and checkable. However, the quantity of buy support, measurement cadence, and the 'redemption price and transparency requirements' that gate eligibility are not defined in this paragraph, so compliance cannot be fully verified from the text.
metrics: Buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS
10bps downside spread
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a sub-obligation of Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral, a Risk Capital requirement, so Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps and the Penalty Mechanisms could plausibly reach a shortfall in buy support. No consequence is quantified for this specific price-floor rule, and the on-chain PSM does not enforce buy support by market makers, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations
assessments.description: Defines Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral as the sum of six listed USDC and Cash Stablecoin balances across PSMs, Curve, GUNI, and Uniswap.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The calculation is an explicit six-term sum with named venues and assets, so the formula is fully specified. The term 'Cash Stablecoins' is not defined here, and the paragraph gives no measurement cadence or reporting deadline.
metrics: Resting ASC = sum of: USDC in LitePSM; USDC in PSM3 (Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism); Cash Stablecoins in Curve paired with USDS; USDC in GUNI 0.01%; USDC in GUNI 0.05%; Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap paired with USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This calculation feeds the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral rule. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could catch a misstated sum, and the Penalty Mechanisms could follow, but no consequence is quantified for this paragraph specifically. The PSM and GUNI balances are on-chain, yet the paragraph's own sum is not contract-enforced.

assessments.title: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote:
Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins.

Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral:

1. The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles;
2. The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and
3. The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels.
assessments.description: Defines Latent ASC as convertible Cash Stablecoins and sets eligibility conditions: verifiability, 15-minute conversion, and automated triggering.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 15-minute conversion window is a concrete, checkable threshold. "Normal market conditions," "reputable APIs or oracles," and "specified levels" for the automatic trigger are undefined, so compliance is partly delegated.
metrics: Conversion into Resting ASC within 15 minutes under normal market conditions
Automatic conversion triggered when ASC falls below specified levels
Assets verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could check whether assets counted as Latent ASC meet the three requirements, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could reach a breach of Prime capital rules. No consequence is quantified for this specific paragraph, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the 15-minute window or the trigger.

assessments.title: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations
assessments.description: Defines Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral as a sum of stablecoin holdings across six listed protocols, subject to discretionary exposure limits.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The calculation is an enumerated sum of six named components, but 'Cash Stablecoins' is not defined here and the Core Executor limitation power has no threshold, cap, or criteria. The discretionary limit is delegated, so the magnitude is unstated.
metrics: Sum of cash stablecoins in Curve (not paired with USDS)
Sum of cash stablecoins in Uniswap (not paired with USDS)
Sum of cash stablecoins in SparkLend
Sum of cash stablecoins in Aave
Sum of cash stablecoins in Morpho
Sum of cash stablecoins in a Prime ALM Proxy
Exposure limits on these protocols or specific pools, set by Core Executor Agents in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor (no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is an input definition with no consequence attached. The exposure-limit power is self-enforced by the Core Executor Agents, and the only generic backstop is the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls. Artifact review and penalties reach the downstream Minimum ASC rule, not this calculation text.

assessments.title: Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Caps Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral at 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete numeric ceiling (25%) on a ratio between two defined collateral metrics, so it is verifiable from the portfolio. It does not name the regulated actor or a measurement cadence, and it relies on the parent section to identify who must comply.
metrics: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral ≤ 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check a Prime's collateral composition against the ratio and assess penalties, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach breaches of Risk Capital rules. No consequence is quantified for this specific ratio, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failing To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement
assessments.quote: In the near term there will be no penalties for Prime Agents for failing to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Instead, failures to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral will be detected and reported as specified in [A.3.3.2.2.2.1 - Reporting Of Failures To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement](b74ba49a-de9e-4c4c-866c-b04d9dd208f7).
assessments.description: States that Prime Agents face no penalties near term for missing Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral; failures are reported under a linked section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states no numeric threshold, deadline, or penalty magnitude. It disclaims penalties for now and defers all detection and reporting mechanics to another document (A.3.3.2.2.2.1), so there is nothing concrete to comply with here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph expressly disables penalties near term, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) do not reach this rule. The reporting pathway it cites (b74ba49a) detects and reports failures but attaches no consequence, and no other catalog mechanism reaches it; none found.

assessments.title: Reporting Of Failures To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement
assessments.description: Requires a Core Council Risk Advisor tool to detect Prime Agent ASC shortfalls and report each violation within 24 hours to named parties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 24-hour reporting deadline and the five named recipients are concrete and checkable. The detection tool has only a "near term" deadline, and the violation test (Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral) is inherited from another section rather than stated here.
metrics: Each violation by a Prime Agent reported within 24 hours
Recipients: Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for the Prime Agent, and the Prime Agent
Tool to detect failures to maintain Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral to be developed "in the near term" (no date)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Mandatory reporting to Core Facilitator and Core GovOps (enforcers distinct from the Prime) feeds the Penalty Mechanisms, which plausibly reach ASC shortfalls. The paragraph itself sets no penalty amount and does not name an escalation path, so the consequence is unquantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Near Term Exemption For Keel
assessments.quote: In the near term, due to limitations in the infrastructure on Solana, Keel is exempt from the requirement to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral. This exemption will be removed in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management Framework.
assessments.description: Exempts Keel from the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement in the near term, pending a future framework revision.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The exemption is a clear, named actor-level carve-out, but its duration is undefined: 'near term' has no date or trigger, and removal is deferred to an unspecified 'future iteration'. No threshold or metric is stated, so a defender could argue the exemption does not yet have a fixed end.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph grants an exemption rather than imposing an obligation, and no catalogued mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, Rate Limiter, Liquidity Layer roles) reaches an exemption from the Minimum ASC requirement.

assessments.title: Near Term Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive
assessments.quote: In the near term, Prime Agents are eligible for an Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive for fulfilling Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirements.
assessments.description: Makes Prime Agents eligible for an Actively Stabilizing Collateral incentive for meeting ASC requirements in the near term.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Prime Agents) and a condition (fulfilling ASC requirements), but states no incentive amount, ASC threshold, measurement method, or defined period beyond the undefined phrase 'near term'. Compliance is arguable because the requirement is referenced rather than stated here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a reward for eligibility rather than imposing a consequence for non-compliance. The ASC requirement it references is not enforced by any citable mechanism within this text, and the catch-all backstops alone are weak.

assessments.title: Calculation
assessments.quote:
The Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive is calculated on a per block basis as follows:

`Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive = Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral * (Base Rate - SOFR)`

The parameters of this formula are defined in [A.3.3.2.2.4.1.1 - Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral](e0b95f42-2021-44ab-a979-491a113ccbc1), and SOFR is specified in [A.3.3.2.2.4.1.3 - Secured Overnight Financing Rate](2edd1333-6ca6-4c10-9d71-80b85d4a4265).
assessments.description: Defines a per-block Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive as eligible collateral multiplied by the spread between a Base Rate and SOFR.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula and per-block cadence are stated exactly, but Base Rate is not defined or valued in this paragraph. Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral and SOFR are delegated to linked sections, so the inputs must be looked up elsewhere.
metrics: Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive = Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral * (Base Rate - SOFR)
Calculated on a per block basis
Base Rate (value not stated in this paragraph)
SOFR (defined in A.3.3.2.2.4.1.3)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is an incentive calculation rather than a compliance obligation, and no citable mechanism (on-chain enforcement, penalty, or conservatorship) reaches it. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: The Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the lesser of (1) the Prime Agent’s Actively Stabilizing Collateral and (2) the Prime Agent’s Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral specified in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8).
assessments.description: Defines Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral as the lesser of a Prime Agent's ASC and its minimum ASC requirement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an explicit min() formula with both inputs identified, and the minimum is linked to A.3.3.2.2, which states the 5% threshold. The paragraph itself does not define how ASC is measured, so the text is precise but depends on linked definitions.
metrics: Eligible ASC = min(Prime Agent's Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Prime Agent's Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a definitional formula for incentive eligibility and creates no violation mode. Enforcement attaches to the linked Minimum ASC rule (A.3.3.2.2), not to this definition.

assessments.title: Payment
assessments.quote: The Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive is paid on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.description: Requires the Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive to be paid monthly as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete cadence (monthly) and ties payment to a named process (Monthly Settlement Cycle). The incentive amount, eligibility, and payee are not stated here and are delegated to other sections.
metrics: Payment frequency: monthly
Process: Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a payment-timing obligation: the Rate Limiter and Role Definitions cover controller calls, and the Penalty Mechanisms and Liquidation Penalty do not govern incentive disbursement. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.quote: Every Prime Agent must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer equal to 25% of their required Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Requires Primes to maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer equal to 25% of required Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is quantified (buffer equal to 25% of required ASC) and the actor is defined as Prime Agent. The 'required Actively Stabilizing Collateral' base is defined elsewhere, and there is no measurement cadence or definition of the buffer's composition in this paragraph.
metrics: Demand Absorption Buffer equal to 25% of required Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a Prime that under-holds the buffer, since it is a Risk Capital-adjacent requirement on Primes. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, so it is mid rather than strong, matching the Minimum ASC calibration.

assessments.title: Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.quote: To further stabilize USDS during periods of excess supply, Prime Agents must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer (DAB), a subset of ASC consisting of USDS that is for sale for at most 1.001 USD per USDS. The Demand Absorption Buffer includes USDS or DAI in PSMs. The Demand Absorption Buffer can also be fulfilled by autonomous systems that generate USDS dynamically through the allocation as needed.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to hold a Demand Absorption Buffer of USDS offered for sale at no more than 1.001 USD.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The sale-price ceiling of 1.001 USD per USDS is a concrete threshold, but the required size of the buffer is never quantified, and no measurement cadence is stated. Whether the obligation is met can be argued either way without a minimum buffer amount.
metrics: USDS offered for sale at most 1.001 USD per USDS
DAB is a subset of ASC
Required buffer size: not specified
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Artifact review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can catch a Prime whose buffer falls short or is priced above 1.001, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could then apply. Neither is quantified for this rule, and the PSM's fixed-rate swaps (0082c12d) enforce the peg but not the buffer obligation itself, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failing To Satisfy Demand Absorption Buffer Requirement
assessments.quote: Penalties for failing to maintain the Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer will be specified in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management framework.
assessments.description: States that penalties for failing to maintain the Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer will be specified later.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a pure stub deferring penalty definitions to a future iteration. It states no threshold, metric, cadence, or consequence for the buffer requirement.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph specifies no penalty, and no catalogued mechanism is tied to this paragraph's text; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply, which are weak by themselves.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event Definition
assessments.quote: A Peg Defense Event is a situation where the average price of USDS on DEXes that are connected via LayerZero falls below 0.999 USD per USDS.
assessments.description: Defines a Peg Defense Event as average USDS DEX price across LayerZero-connected venues falling below 0.999 USD.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger is quantified: an average price metric and a 0.999 USD threshold. Gaps remain: no averaging window, no sampling cadence, and the set of LayerZero-connected DEXes is not enumerated.
metrics: Average price of USDS across DEXes connected via LayerZero
Price below 0.999 USD per USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a definition with no actor obligation to breach. The Peg Stability Module (0082c12d) makes peg deviation arbitrageable, but it operates independently of this definition and does not enforce it, so none found.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event Alert Tool
assessments.quote: The Core Council Risk Advisor, in consultation with Core GovOps, will develop a tool that calculates the average price of USDS on DEXes that are connected via LayerZero in real time. This tool must be made available to all Prime Agents and functionality must be developed that notifies Sky and Prime Agents in real time when a Peg Defense Event has been triggered.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council Risk Advisor to build a real-time LayerZero DEX USDS average price tool and Peg Defense Event alerts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actors and a concrete metric (average USDS price across LayerZero-connected DEXes, in real time), but gives no numeric threshold, no deadline, and no definition of the Peg Defense Event trigger here. It is also a development obligation with no completion date, so a defender could argue it does not yet bind.
metrics: Average price of USDS on DEXes connected via LayerZero, calculated in real time
Real-time notification to Sky and Prime Agents when a Peg Defense Event is triggered
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a tool-development duty with no consequence for failing to build it or deliver alerts. Emergency Response System and Peg Stability Module do not reach this development obligation, and the catch-all mechanisms alone are weak.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.quote: In a Peg Defense Event, all Prime Agents must immediately begin to buy USDS at a rate of at least 6.25% of their Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement every six (6) hours. The six (6) hour periods run consecutively from the onset of the Peg Defense Event, and the Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement is measured as of the start of each period. Each Prime Agent is responsible for monitoring its Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement and maintaining sufficient capacity to satisfy this obligation for the duration of the Peg Defense Event.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents in a Peg Defense Event to buy USDS at 6.25% of their ASC requirement every six hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a 6.25% buy rate of the ASC requirement, a six-hour cadence, and measurement at each period's start. The Peg Defense Event trigger and the definition of ASC requirement are defined elsewhere and not restated here, so a supporting input is missing a value in this text.
metrics: Buy USDS at a rate of at least 6.25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement
Every six (6) hours, in consecutive periods from onset of Peg Defense Event
ASC requirement measured as of the start of each six-hour period
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a Prime's failure to meet the ASC-based buying obligation, but no consequence is quantified for this specific paragraph. Nothing on-chain enforces the buy rate or cadence, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Alternatives For Satisfying Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.quote: Peg Defense can be performed through a combination of (1) selling other types of collateral for USDS, or (2) by using USDS, or generating new USDS via the Allocation System, that is then used as collateral to borrow other types of assets (e.g. USDC or USDT on Aave) and buy USDS with it.
assessments.description: Lists two alternative methods Sky may use to perform peg defense: selling other collateral for USDS, or borrowing other assets against USDS and buying USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates two concrete peg-defense methods but gives no thresholds, amounts, timing, or eligibility criteria. It is permissive ("can be performed"), so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The second method mints or generates USDS through the Allocation System and uses it as collateral for borrowing, which are controller operations. The Rate Limiter contracts revert any such operation above its current limit, so on-chain enforcement plausibly reaches it, though the paragraph states no limit and the first method has no clear enforcer.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failure To Satisfy Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.quote: Penalties for failing to fulfill the Peg Defense Obligations will be specified in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management framework.
assessments.description: States that penalties for failing Peg Defense Obligations will be specified in a future framework iteration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a pure stub deferring all penalty terms to a future iteration; it states no threshold, metric, penalty amount, or deadline. Nothing is currently verifiable or compliable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph itself defines no penalty, and no cited mechanism is tied to Peg Defense Obligations specifically; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops could reach it, which alone is weak.

assessments.quote: Pursuant to [A.3.3.1.4 - Application To Sky Core](6e050b66-0bc8-43f1-b32d-2220c9df466b), Sky Core manages the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio by allocating capital to the Lite PSM (see [A.3.3.2.7.1.1 - Lite Peg Stability Module](39473e1a-63f8-433b-a850-08f53b2dcf02)).

The verb "manages" is judgment language, and the reference to A.3.3.1.4 defers scope without stating values, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Lite PSM's fixed-rate swaps (0082c12d) self-enforce the peg, but nothing in the paragraph is enforced by them, and no rate limit, role gate, or penalty attaches to the allocation obligation itself.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module

Until this transition is complete, the Lite PSM continues to be controlled by Sky Core, subject to the requirements specified in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf). Post-transition, Grove will manage the Lite PSM as an ASC asset pursuant to the rules defined in this Article.
assessments.description: Transfers control of the Lite PSM from Sky Core to Grove and states that Grove will then treat it as an ASC asset.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Sky Core, Grove) and a classification (ASC asset) but gives no thresholds, deadlines, or completion criteria for the transition. Whether the transition is complete is undefined, so the Sky Core-to-Grove handover is not verifiable from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a control-assignment transition: the Rate Limiter and Role Definitions bind specific controller calls and roles, which this paragraph does not state. Cross-referenced A.3.3.2.6 is not a catalog mechanism and its enforcement is not verified here.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Buffer Definition
assessments.quote: `buf` is a fixed-sized amount of pre-minted Dai which LitePSM is designed to maintain in most situations. Note, however, that when a user calls `buyGem`, the amount of Dai available can be temporarily larger than `buf`.
assessments.description: Defines the LitePSM buffer as a fixed-size pre-minted Dai amount it aims to maintain in most situations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the buffer parameter and calls it fixed-sized, but states no amount, formula, or cadence. 'Most situations' and 'temporarily larger' are judgment language, so compliance with the buffer level is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph itself allows the available Dai to exceed buf temporarily, so no contract reverts or penalizes a buffer shortfall. The Peg Stability Module mechanism enforces peg deviation through arbitrage on swaps, not the buffer level.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Modification
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, may recommend changes to any of the parameters specified in the subdocuments of [A.3.3.2.7.1.1.1 - Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Definitions](9196786a-18b6-4dea-b4e2-852090371dd7). These changes will be subject to an Executive Vote through the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator recommend changes to Lite PSM parameters, subject to an Executive Vote in the weekly cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Core Facilitator, Core Council Risk Advisor), a process (recommend, then Executive Vote) and a cycle (Operational Weekly Cycle). However, the 'may recommend' wording is discretionary and no criteria, thresholds or limits on the changes are stated, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Executive Vote is an approval gate on recommendations, not a consequence for breaching the rule. No penalty, rate limit, or artifact review reaches an unauthorized or improper parameter change. Only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Andromeda
assessments.quote: Historically, Andromeda balanced Sky Core’s Cash Stablecoin liquidity by allocating excess into low-risk treasury strategies and replenishing shortages. Control of the Andromeda RWA Arranged Structure is currently being transitioned to Grove. Until the transition to Grove is complete, Andromeda continues to be controlled by Sky Core, subject to the requirements defined in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf). Post-transition, Grove will manage Andromeda as a non-ASC asset within its Collateral Portfolio, subject to JRC requirements. Andromeda is not currently operational and its debt ceiling has been reduced to zero.
assessments.description: Describes Andromeda's legacy status: transfer of control to Grove, interim Sky Core control, and a zero debt ceiling.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states one verifiable value, a debt ceiling of zero. The operative controls are delegated: interim obligations point to A.3.3.2.6 and post-transition treatment is 'subject to JRC requirements' with no stated magnitudes.
metrics: Andromeda debt ceiling reduced to zero
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The zero debt ceiling is a maximum on an Allocation System controller, which the Rate Limiter reaches; a call above it would revert on-chain. The paragraph does not state a rate limit explicitly, and the transition control itself has no citable enforcer.

assessments.title: Other RWA Offboarding
assessments.quote: Other than Andromeda, all old RWA exposure that was added before Endgame must stay for as long as necessary, and optimized for yield if possible. When it is possible, the Core Facilitator should take action to wind down and offboard all such Legacy RWA. Governance actions related to optimizations, wind down and offboardings can be done directly in Executive Votes with no prior Governance Poll needed.
assessments.description: Requires keeping pre-Endgame legacy RWA exposure (except Andromeda) and winding down and offboarding it when possible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: It names an actor (Core Facilitator) and a process (Executive Votes without a prior Poll), but the operative obligations are judgment language: 'as long as necessary', 'if possible', 'should take action'. No threshold, deadline, or metric exists, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No penalty, rate limit, or contract-enforced control reaches this wind-down duty. Executive Votes are the ordinary governance path, and only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, so none found.

assessments.title: Agent Owner For Arranged Structures
assessments.quote: Arranged Structures must have an Agent owner. The Agent owner assigns instructions to the Arranged Structure on behalf of Sky, and determines if and how other Agents can access the Conduit of the Arranged Structure.
assessments.description: Requires every Arranged Structure to have an Agent owner who instructs it for Sky and controls other Agents' access to its Conduit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete actor (the Agent owner) and a binary existence requirement that can be checked. It gives no numeric thresholds, and the scope of 'determines if and how' access is delegated to the owner's discretion without stated criteria.
metrics: Each Arranged Structure has an Agent owner (existence requirement, no numeric threshold)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a named enforcer distinct from the actor that can check owner assignment and assess penalties, but the consequence is not quantified for this rule. Liquidity Layer Role Definitions (2ae4b91a) would revert unauthorized Conduit calls if owner-granted access is implemented as roles, though the rule itself never states a role and does not enforce owner existence.

assessments.title: Arrangers
assessments.quote: This Section defines procedures related to Arrangers, Ecosystem Actors that assist in the design and operation of Arranged Structures. Every Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger responsible for conducting ongoing reporting. All aspects of this relationship, including the Arranger's duties, must be defined in this Section.
assessments.description: Requires every Arranged Structure to have a designated Arranger responsible for ongoing reporting.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph imposes a real obligation (each Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger), but "ongoing reporting" has no cadence, content, or metric. It defers all duties to unspecified content elsewhere in the Section, so a defender could argue the reporting duty does not yet bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a missing Arranger or a reporting failure, and the paragraph cites no enforcement path. Artifact review could in principle reach it, but with no defined reporting standard there is no violation mode to review.

assessments.title: Introduction
assessments.quote:
Arrangers are Ecosystem Actors who specialize in sourcing, negotiating, structuring, and reporting on Real World Assets, as well as maintaining and monitoring the underlying Arranged Structures used by the Sky Protocol. The Arrangers manage a restricted function on the Arranged Structure Conduit that allows them to send assets onwards to the predetermined blockchain account of the Arranged Structure.

Arrangers are generally prohibited from occupying any position where they could cause damage or loss to the Sky Ecoystem, notwithstanding delays or inconveniences.

After the Arranged Structures are established and assets are allocated, Arrangers must not have the capability to operate or influence the legal and operational structure’s asset operations in any manner that could cause significant harm or losses to the stability of USDS.

Arrangers are directly approved by SKY voters, and all LRA collateral exposure must be structured by an approved Arranger.
assessments.description: Defines Arrangers' role over Real World Assets and sets qualitative prohibitions on harmful influence, plus a requirement that LRA exposure use approved Arrangers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations rely on judgment terms such as "generally prohibited", "significant harm or losses" and "notwithstanding delays or inconveniences", with no thresholds or cadence. The requirement that all LRA exposure be structured by an approved Arranger is concrete, but "approved" is defined by SKY voters elsewhere and no criteria are given here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Liquidity Layer Role Definitions (2ae4b91a) make the Arrangers' restricted conduit function contract-gated, so calls from addresses without the role revert. The prohibitions on harmful influence and the rule on approved-Arranger structuring have no identified mechanism that reaches them, so enforcement is only partial.

assessments.title: Onboarding And Offboarding of Arrangers
assessments.quote: When they deem it necessary, the Core Facilitator may initiate a Governance Poll to onboard or offboard Arrangers. The list of current active Arrangers is maintained in [A.3.4.3.2.1 - List Of Active Arrangers](b8791aaa-84b7-4012-8a4f-053595ec232a).
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator initiate a Governance Poll to onboard or offboard Real World Asset Arrangers, with the active list maintained separately.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Core Facilitator, Governance Poll) and a referenced list, but the trigger is purely discretionary ("when they deem it necessary") with no criteria, thresholds, or cadence. A regulated party could argue both compliance and non-applicability on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph only permits a poll; no penalty, conservatorship, or automatic control reaches a failure to onboard or offboard properly, and governance voting is not an enforcement path for this rule.

assessments.title: Reporting And Stress Test Requirements
assessments.quote:
Arrangers must publish monthly reporting on each Arranged Structure they have arranged.

Every six (6) months, Arrangers are also required to publish a stress test analysis that demonstrates how the structures would perform under historical financial crisis scenarios and other hypothetical scenarios.

The Core Facilitator must periodically fund independent Ecosystem Actors to review and verify the quality and the results of the stress tests. Should an independent review produce an unfavorable result, the Core Facilitator must propose a Governance Poll for warning, temporarily deactivating, or permanently offboarding the Arranger and/or the Asset Managers connected to the discovered issue.

To be considered compliant, Arrangers’ monthly reports must satisfy the requirements of one of the following documents:

- [A.3.4.3.3.1 - Monthly Arranger Report Requirements](7b902bb1-68b4-477d-a575-29aaa02e9e7b)
- [A.3.4.3.3.2 - Access To Accounts](47eedd39-5bb9-492f-a4aa-9405bb5d196f)
assessments.description: Requires Arrangers to publish monthly reports and six-monthly stress tests, with Core Facilitator-funded reviews triggering possible governance action.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Monthly reporting and six-month stress-test cadences are concrete, but the stress-test content and the 'unfavorable result' trigger are undefined, the review funding is 'periodic', and report content is delegated to linked specifications.
metrics: Monthly reporting on each Arranged Structure
Stress test analysis every six (6) months
Independent reviews funded periodically by the Core Facilitator
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The text names the Core Facilitator as enforcer and lists remedies (warning, temporary deactivation, offboarding) via Governance Poll, but the trigger is undefined and the poll is not automatic. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) is the plausible review path, but it does not clearly reach the monthly reporting duty.

assessments.title: Monthly Arranger Report Requirements
assessments.quote:
The following information must be included in the monthly Arranger report. Each item must be reported for at least the start and end date of the reporting period. If these dates fall on days when markets are closed, the first business day after the start date and the last business day before the end date may be used instead.

- Cash balance.
- Cash income over the reporting period. Any income over $20,000 in value should be broken out as its own line item, and an explanation provided for any non-recurring or non-ordinary expenses.
- Cash expenses over the reporting period. Any expense over $20,000 in value should be broken out as its own line item, and an explanation provided for any non-recurring or non-ordinary expenses.
- Market value of publicly traded equities, ETFs, and mutual funds.
- Market value (the closing price) of publicly traded debt securities. Debt securities that are investment grade and less than 12 months from maturity may alternatively be reported at cost basis + linearly recognizing scheduled interest income.
- A valuation for illiquid or privately traded assets. This should utilize a valuation from a reputable third party with relevant expertise or follow a well-defined methodology that is explained in detail in the report.
- CUSIPs, date of purchase, date of maturity, coupon, cost basis, and face value of all publicly traded debt securities in the portfolio for the last day of the reporting period.
- USDS inflows from the Sky Protocol during the reporting period.
- Total repayments on-chain to the Sky Protocol either to a vault or for surplus. If repayments are derived from multiple sources, they should be broken out into line items for each source.
- Vault debt to the Sky Protocol.
- Copies of original statements for all bank, brokerage, exchange, custodial, or other accounts. The Arranger may redact the names for non-Arranger service providers if and only if that is a requirement of confidentiality agreements with the non-Arranger service providers.

The Core Facilitator must publicly confirm on the Sky Forum that they have reviewed the original account documentation and verified that it supports the Arranger’s summary.
assessments.description: Specifies monthly Arranger report contents, including cash, income and expense thresholds, valuations, debt details, and Core Facilitator verification.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Core reporting obligations are quantified: a $20,000 breakout threshold for income and expenses, a 12-month maturity cutoff, and investment-grade criteria for alternative debt reporting. Gaps remain in judgment terms such as "reputable third party," "well-defined methodology," and "non-ordinary," which lack objective criteria.
metrics: Reporting must include the start and end date of the reporting period, or the nearest business days if markets are closed
Income over $20,000 broken out as its own line item
Expenses over $20,000 broken out as its own line item
Debt securities investment grade and less than 12 months from maturity may use cost basis plus linearly recognized scheduled interest income
CUSIPs, purchase date, maturity date, coupon, cost basis, and face value of all publicly traded debt securities as of the last day of the reporting period
