assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can review submitted reports, issue staged findings, and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches missing or inaccurate monthly report items. However, no consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and the paragraph's own Core Facilitator confirmation is a verification step rather than a defined penalty path.

assessments.title: Access To Accounts
assessments.quote:
As an alternative to the requirements set out in [A.3.4.3.3.1 - Monthly Arranger Report Requirements](7b902bb1-68b4-477d-a575-29aaa02e9e7b), the Arranger can provide the following information through public read-only access to all accounts:

- All asset balances
- All transaction amounts (non-Arranger service provider names may be redacted)
- Hold-to-maturity yields (for assets with maturity) or current yield (for assets with no maturity)

In addition, Makerburn.com ([https://makerburn.com/#/](https://makerburn.com/#/)), Daistats.com ([https://daistats.com/#/](https://daistats.com/#/)), or another dashboard must be publicly available to summarize USDS inflows and outflows from the Sky vault.
assessments.description: Lets Arrangers replace monthly reporting with public read-only account access and requires public USDS vault flow dashboards.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The three disclosed data categories and the named dashboards are concrete, and public availability is checkable. However, "all accounts" and "another dashboard" are undefined, and no cadence or deadline appears in this paragraph; it relies on the monthly cadence of the referenced A.3.4.3.3.1.
metrics: Public read-only access to all accounts
Reported items: all asset balances, all transaction amounts, hold-to-maturity or current yield
Dashboard (Makerburn.com, Daistats.com, or another) publicly available, summarizing USDS inflows and outflows from the Sky vault
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps is a scheduled review by a party distinct from the Arranger, with staged findings and penalty assessment, and could check whether the public account access and dashboards exist. No quantified consequence is attached to this specific reporting rule, and nothing in the paragraph triggers the review.

assessments.title: Agent Owner Can Change Arrangers
assessments.quote: The Agent owner of the Arranged Structure can change the blockchain account of the Arranged Structure and change the Arranger.
assessments.description: Lets the Agent owner of an Arranged Structure change its blockchain account and its Arranger.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph identifies a defined actor (the Agent owner) and a concrete permission, but gives no conditions, notice period, approval step, or criteria for when a change is allowed. Compliance cannot be verified from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The text does not say the change is gated by a role-restricted contract function, so the Liquidity Layer Role Definitions do not clearly reach it. No penalty, emergency, or review mechanism is tied to this right, and the owner's own choice is self-enforcement only.

assessments.title: Implemented By Core Facilitator
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator can implement various perpetual yield strategies, including on-chain and off-chain mechanisms, that enable the Sky Protocol to take advantage of high risk-adjusted return on perpetual yield strategies in the crypto markets.

Exposure targets specified in this document override requirements defined by other Articles of the Stability Scope.
assessments.description: Permits the Core Facilitator to implement on-chain and off-chain perpetual yield strategies, and states that this document's exposure targets override other Stability Scope articles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph grants a permission with qualitative terms like 'various' and 'take advantage of' and gives no threshold, limit, or metric. The override clause refers to 'exposure targets specified in this document' that do not appear in this paragraph, so nothing here is measurable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches this permissive rule, which sets no limit that could be breached. The override clause depends on exposure targets stated elsewhere, and the only generic backstop is the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls.

assessments.title: Perpetual Exposure Direct Accumulation
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator can trigger Executive Votes that instruct Arranged Structures to set up mechanisms that allow them to take direct exposure to Ethena sUSDe, or use legal rails to get direct exposure through custodians.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator trigger Executive Votes directing Arranged Structures to gain direct sUSDe exposure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Core Facilitator, Arranged Structures) and a process (Executive Vote), but gives no limits, amounts, criteria, or deadlines. It states a permission rather than a measurable obligation, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants authority without a consequence for misuse, and none of the catalogued mechanisms (penalties, rate limits, role gating, emergency spells) reaches this authorization. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Current Value
assessments.quote:
The current value of the Surplus Buffer can be calculated using the Vat contract, Sky’s central accounting contract, located on the Ethereum Mainnet at `0x35D1b3F3D7966A1DFe207aa4514C12a259A0492B`. The current value of the Surplus Buffer is the difference between:

1. The assets of the Vow contract obtained by calling the `dai` function on the Vat contract with the address of the Vow contract, and
2. The liabilities of the Vow contract obtained by calling the `sin` function on the Vat contract with the address of the Vow contract.
assessments.description: Defines the Surplus Buffer's current value as Vat dai minus Vat sin for the Vow contract.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact formula, a named contract and mainnet address, and specific function calls (dai and sin with the Vow address), so a third party can reproduce the value from the text alone. It states no threshold or cadence because it is a measurement definition, not a limit.
metrics: Surplus Buffer current value = Vat.dai(Vow address) − Vat.sin(Vow address)
Vat contract address on Ethereum Mainnet: 0x35D1b3F3D7966A1DFe207aa4514C12a259A0492B
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines a calculation and imposes no compliance obligation, so there is no violation for an enforcement mechanism to reach. The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is the buffer this value measures, but it is not an enforcement path for this text.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Parameters
assessments.quote:
The current Smart Burn Engine parameters are:

- kicker.khump: -200 million USDS (Threshold of Surplus Buffer for Splitter to activate)
- kicker.kbump: 6,000 USDS
- splitter.hop: 2,693 seconds
- burn (the percentage of the kicker.kbump to be moved to the underlying flapper): set as specified in [A.2.3.1.4.1 - Staking Rewards Rate Adjustment](de233df4-34cc-4e88-a065-9a9dde9add3c); the current value can be read by calling `burn()` on the Splitter contract
- LSEV2-SKY-A USDS rewardsDuration: 2,693 seconds

The rewardsDuration for the LSEV2-SKY-A USDS rewards contract must be set such that it is equal to the splitter.hop parameter.
assessments.description: Sets current Smart Burn Engine parameters and requires the LSEV2-SKY-A USDS rewardsDuration to equal the splitter.hop value.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Khump, kbump, hop and rewardsDuration carry explicit values and the equality constraint is objectively checkable. The burn parameter is delegated to another document and to an on-chain read, so no value is stated here.
metrics: kicker.khump = -200,000,000 USDS (Surplus Buffer threshold for Splitter activation)
kicker.kbump = 6,000 USDS
splitter.hop = 2,693 seconds
LSEV2-SKY-A USDS rewardsDuration = 2,693 seconds
LSEV2-SKY-A USDS rewardsDuration must equal splitter.hop
burn set per A.2.3.1.4.1 and readable via burn() on the Splitter contract
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No contract enforces the rewardsDuration equal-to-hop constraint. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could catch a mismatch between the stated parameters and deployed configuration, but escalation depends on the review being run and the penalty is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Splitter Module
assessments.quote: The Splitter Module splits funds transferred to it from the Surplus Buffer between accumulating SKY and paying USDS rewards to SKY stakers.
assessments.description: Describes the Splitter Module dividing Surplus Buffer funds between SKY accumulation and USDS rewards to SKY stakers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real function (splitting Surplus Buffer funds between two uses) but states no split ratio, formula, or allocation criteria. Compliance is arguable because nothing says how funds are divided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is the context, but it is a protocol-level loss-absorption backstop, not a control on how the Splitter divides funds. With no ratio stated, no mechanism reaches a split-ratio violation.

assessments.title: Splitter Interval Parameter
assessments.quote: The `hop` parameter is the time interval between `kicker.kbump` funds being transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter. Together with the `kicker.kbump` parameter, it controls the rate at which funds are transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter.
assessments.description: Defines the hop parameter as the time interval between kicker.kbump transfers from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the hop parameter and its role in setting transfer rate with kbump, but gives no value, unit, or bounds. Rate control is described only qualitatively, so the operative magnitude is undefined.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is a protocol-level loss-absorption backstop, not an actor-level enforcer of this parameter. No penalty, escalation, or contract-enforced limit on the hop value is stated, and the paragraph regulates a system parameter rather than an actor's conduct.

assessments.title: SKY Accumulation Percentage Parameter
assessments.quote: The `burn` parameter is the percentage of each transfer from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter that is sent to the Flapper contract, which accumulates SKY. The remainder of each transfer is sent to the contract for USDS rewards for SKY stakers.
assessments.description: Defines the burn parameter as the share of Surplus Buffer-to-Splitter transfers sent to the Flapper for SKY accumulation, with the remainder going to USDS staker rewards.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the burn parameter and the two-way split (Flapper versus USDS staker rewards), but states no value, range, or update cadence for the percentage. Compliance cannot be checked from the text, and a defender could argue it is only a definition.
metrics: burn: percentage of each Surplus Buffer-to-Splitter transfer sent to the Flapper (no value stated)
remainder of each transfer sent to the USDS staker rewards contract
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Splitter executes whatever burn value is set, but no mechanism punishes a deviation from the stated split. The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is a loss-absorption backstop that does not reach a misconfigured burn parameter, so only the catch-all applies.

assessments.title: Kicker Module
assessments.quote: The Kicker Module allows funds to be transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter as long as the Surplus Buffer is above a specified signed threshold. This allows funds to be transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter even when the Surplus Buffer is negative, as long as the Surplus Buffer is above the specified threshold.
assessments.description: Permits transfers from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter when the buffer exceeds an unspecified signed threshold, even if negative.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The governing condition is concrete (Surplus Buffer above a signed threshold), but the threshold's value is not stated and is delegated to a specified parameter. The paragraph gives no cadence, bounds, or transfer amounts.
metrics: Surplus Buffer must be above a specified signed threshold (value not stated in paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a permission rather than an actor obligation with a violation mode. The Surplus Buffer itself (3eb6f099) is the regulated resource, not an enforcer, and no penalty, rate-limit, or review mechanism is shown to reach a threshold breach.

assessments.title: Kicker Threshold Parameter
assessments.quote: The `khump` parameter is the minimum value of the Surplus Buffer for funds to be transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter contract. It is a signed integer with `RAD` precision.
assessments.description: Defines the khump parameter as the minimum Surplus Buffer value required before funds transfer to the Splitter, with RAD precision.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete parameter, its role as a transfer threshold, and its type and precision (signed integer, RAD). It states no operative magnitude, so a third party cannot check a value from this text alone, and a defender could argue it does not yet bind any particular amount.
metrics: khump: minimum Surplus Buffer value for transfer to the Splitter contract
signed integer with RAD precision
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) governs when buffer funds flow to the Splitter, so the khump gate plausibly applies to those transfers. It is an economic backstop rather than an actor-level penalty, and no consequence is quantified for this parameter, so the rating is capped at mid.

assessments.title: Kicker Lot Size Parameter
assessments.quote: The `kbump` parameter is the amount of funds transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter every `splitter.hop` interval when the Surplus Buffer is greater than `kbump`. Together with the `splitter.hop` parameter, it controls the rate at which funds are transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter.
assessments.description: Defines kbump as the amount moved from the Surplus Buffer to the Splitter each splitter.hop interval when the buffer exceeds kbump.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the concrete parameters kbump and splitter.hop and states a transfer condition (buffer greater than kbump). It gives no values, units, or cadence, so the operative magnitudes are delegated to parameter values defined elsewhere.
metrics: Transfer amount equals kbump, sent every splitter.hop interval
Transfer occurs only when Surplus Buffer is greater than kbump
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The transfer is executed by the Smart Burn Engine contracts, but the paragraph describes a parameter's effect rather than an actor obligation that can be breached. The Surplus Buffer mechanism (3eb6f099) is a protocol-level loss-absorption backstop and does not police how kbump is set or applied, so no citable mechanism reaches a violation mode.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, can modify the `kbump`, `hop`, and `burn` parameters of the Smart Burn Engine. Such a modification can be enacted either by proposing it for inclusion in an Executive Vote pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, or by executing it directly through the SBE-BEAM within its bounds, as specified in [A.3.5.2.4 - Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module](b57ac61b-f6b1-4025-bd44-569d0f2afe2f). LSEV2-SKY-A-USDS rewardsDuration should always match the value of the `hop` parameter without requiring prior governance authorization.

The Core Facilitator must modify all parameters of the Smart Burn Engine as necessary to implement the allocation specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121). Such a modification can be enacted either by proposing it for inclusion in an Executive Vote pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, or by executing it directly through the SBE-BEAM within its bounds.

Except as provided in the preceding paragraphs, modifications to the parameters of the Smart Burn Engine require a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module
assessments.quote:
The Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module (SBE-BEAM) enables a designated, Governance-whitelisted Operator to adjust the Kicker Lot Size (`kbump`), the SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`), and the Splitter Interval (`hop`) parameters of the Smart Burn Engine, as specified in [A.3.5.2.2.1.2 - Kicker Lot Size Parameter](fc9cece1-84bf-4133-a2ef-ef2182a23a35), [A.3.5.2.1.1.2 - SKY Accumulation Percentage Parameter](e16d6215-c2f1-4140-affd-30e52a17fd43), and [A.3.5.2.1.1.1 - Splitter Interval Parameter](39a67e65-33f0-4f2c-917d-efff544cf5ab). Adjustments are governed by the SBE-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance.

The SBE-BEAM Operator can raise or lower these parameters within the bounds set by Sky Governance. Those bounds are one-sided guardrails on the rate of accumulation: the Kicker Lot Size cannot be set above `maxKbump`, the Splitter Interval cannot be set below `minHop`, and the combined throughput, expressed as the Kicker Lot Size divided by the Splitter Interval, cannot exceed `maxRate`. The rate of accumulation therefore cannot be raised beyond the maximum that Sky Governance has sanctioned, while no corresponding bound limits reductions to it. The SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`) is not subject to these bounds, which limit only the rate of accumulation, and the only technical constraint on it is the maximum specified in [A.3.5.2.4.4 - Technical Limitations](42ea8a7b-fb28-455e-8038-5fcf25250f17). The `tau` parameter separately requires a minimum interval between operations, applying to any operation regardless of whether it raises or lowers the parameters. The SBE-BEAM holds the following bounding parameters: (i) `maxKbump`, (ii) `minHop`, (iii) `maxRate`, and (iv) `tau`. The bases on which these parameters may be modified are specified in [A.3.5.2.3 - Modification](499570de-9fae-4009-be34-c3330266030a).
assessments.description: Lets a whitelisted Operator adjust Smart Burn Engine kicker size, burn percentage and splitter interval within Governance-set bounds and a minimum operation interval.

The text does not state that out-of-bound calls revert, and the tau and burn constraints are not shown to be enforced, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Max Kbump Definition
assessments.quote: The `maxKbump` parameter defines the maximum permitted value of the `kbump` parameter when set using the SBE-BEAM. The SBE-BEAM can set `kbump` to any value at or below `maxKbump`, whether that raises or lowers the current value, but cannot set `kbump` above `maxKbump`.

The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine doc is an economic backstop that alone reaches this bound at most as mid, and no cited mechanism is shown to revert or penalize a kbump set above maxKbump.

assessments.title: Min Hop Definition
assessments.quote: The `minHop` parameter defines the minimum permitted value of the `hop` parameter when set using the SBE-BEAM. The SBE-BEAM can set `hop` to any value at or above `minHop`, whether that raises or lowers the current value, but cannot set `hop` below `minHop`.

However, no numeric value or formula for minHop is given, and its magnitude is defined elsewhere, so the operative quantity is delegated.

Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could catch a configuration that sets hop below minHop, with penalty assessment, but no consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Tau Definition
assessments.quote:
The `tau` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive uses or operations of the SBE-BEAM.

A SBE-BEAM operation may adjust one or more parameters. Once a SBE-BEAM operation is executed, the `tau` duration must expire before any subsequent SBE-BEAM operation can be performed. This interval applies to every operation regardless of whether it raises or lowers the affected parameters.
assessments.description: Defines tau as the minimum seconds that must elapse between consecutive SBE-BEAM operations, applying to all operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The cooldown rule is fully specified: consecutive SBE-BEAM operations must be separated by at least tau seconds, with no exemption for raising or lowering parameters. The numeric value of tau is defined elsewhere and not stated here, which is a supporting gap.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph does not state an on-chain revert or other enforcer for the cooldown. The Rate Limiter reaches Allocation System controller limits, not SBE-BEAM timing, and the Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine doc is an economic backstop that does not enforce operation spacing.

assessments.title: Parameters
assessments.quote:
The bounding parameters set by Sky Governance for the SBE-BEAM are as follows:

- The value of the `maxKbump` parameter is 12,000 USDS.
- The value of the `minHop` parameter is 550 seconds.
- The value of the `maxRate` parameter is 350,000,000 USDS per year.
- The value of the `tau` parameter is 1,800 seconds.

assessments.title: Parameter Adjustments
assessments.quote: All SBE-BEAM bounding parameters can be modified by Sky Governance, through the Operational Weekly Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. Such changes are proposed by the Core Facilitator, on behalf of the Core Council and in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor.

assessments.title: Technical Limitations
assessments.quote:
The SBE-BEAM enforces technical limitations, including the following, that apply independently of the bounding parameters set by Sky Governance. An attempt to use the SBE-BEAM in a manner that exceeds these limitations will revert.

The `hop` parameter cannot be set higher than five (5) years. This limitation prevents the Smart Burn Engine from being placed in a state in which its reward stream — the staking rewards funded by the non-burned portion of surplus and streamed out over the Splitter Interval — can no longer be revived through the SBE-BEAM.

The `burn` parameter cannot be set higher than 100%, the point at which the entire surplus is directed to SKY accumulation. A higher value would cause the Smart Burn Engine to halt.

The `kbump` parameter must be set to a whole multiple of `RAY` (10²⁷). A value that is not an exact multiple of `RAY` will revert, ensuring the Kicker Lot Size is always expressed in the protocol's standard fixed-point precision.
assessments.description: Sets hard technical limits on SBE-BEAM parameters: hop at most 5 years, burn at most 100%, and kbump a whole multiple of RAY.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each of the three limits is a numeric or formula-based constraint with an explicit bound (hop ≤ 5 years, burn ≤ 100%, kbump an exact multiple of 10^27), and the text states that violations revert. A third party could check compliance directly from the text.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph says out-of-limit calls revert, which is contract-enforced, but no catalog or in-text mechanism UUID covers SBE-BEAM parameter bounds. The Rate Limiter targets Allocation System controller limits and the role definitions target access control, so neither reaches these checks. None found.

assessments.title: Operators
assessments.quote: The SBE-BEAM Operator is a Governance-whitelisted entity that can use the SBE-BEAM to alter the three Smart Burn Engine parameters within its control — the Kicker Lot Size (`kbump`), the SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`), and the Splitter Interval (`hop`). Changes to the `kbump` and `hop` parameters, and to their combined throughput, are limited by the `maxKbump`, `minHop`, and `maxRate` parameters, and every change is subject to the `tau` cadence. The `burn` parameter is not subject to the `maxKbump`, `minHop`, or `maxRate` bounds, which limit only the rate of accumulation, and the only technical constraint on it is the maximum specified in [A.3.5.2.4.4 - Technical Limitations](42ea8a7b-fb28-455e-8038-5fcf25250f17). The Operator can be changed by an Executive Vote.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameters and the bounding variables (maxKbump, minHop, maxRate, tau) and points to a technical maximum for burn in another section. It states no numeric values, cadence or deadlines, so the operative magnitudes are delegated.

assessments.title: Circulating USDS Supply
assessments.quote:
The Circulating USDS Supply is the total supply of USDS and Dai less the Non-Circulating Balances. Dai is exchangeable for USDS at a rate of 1:1, as specified in [A.4.1.1.1 - USDS Launch](3e00cf4d-8b10-4182-bb3d-08b63bc55aeb), and is counted as USDS.

The total supply of USDS and Dai is the sum of:

1. The total supply of the USDS token on the Ethereum Mainnet;
2. The total supply of the Dai token on the Ethereum Mainnet; and
3. Dai deposited in the Dai Savings Rate (see [A.3.1.2.4 - Dai Savings Rate](d220731b-35db-4803-8a74-1c470a5ad693)), which is held as an internal balance of the Sky Protocol rather than as Dai tokens.

Tokens that represent USDS or Dai on other blockchains are not counted separately from the USDS and Dai locked on the Ethereum Mainnet that back them.

Non-Circulating Balances are the following balances, each of which is controlled by the Sky Protocol, Sky Core, or an Agent and has not been placed into circulation with users:

1. Dai minted to the Lite PSM (see [A.3.3.2.7.1.1 - Lite Peg Stability Module](39473e1a-63f8-433b-a850-08f53b2dcf02)) that has not been swapped for collateral;
2. USDS and Dai held in the SubProxy of an Agent, including Genesis Capital (see [A.3.7.1.6.6 - Genesis Capital](18f3de06-064b-4b08-a855-4720240e37f5));
3. USDS and Dai held by an Agent in its ALM Proxy on any blockchain, or deployed by an Agent from its ALM Proxy into Peg Stability Modules, Basins, lending protocols, or liquidity pools;
4. USDS and Dai held in the Core Council Buffer (see [A.2.3.1.2.2.2.1 - Core Council Buffer](8b6781d7-f35c-4ffe-b8ed-299fa98e3da7)) and the Aligned Delegates Buffer (see [A.2.3.1.2.2.2.2 - Aligned Delegates Buffer](05fa5c41-26ca-4c25-94dd-834ef72c318a)); and
5. sUSDS and stUSDS held in the positions specified in items 2 through 4, each counted as the USDS it represents.

Where an Agent has deployed USDS or Dai into a lending protocol or liquidity pool, the Non-Circulating Balance is the share of the USDS and Dai held by that protocol or pool that is attributable to the Agent's deposit. USDS and Dai that have been borrowed from a lending protocol are in circulation and are not Non-Circulating Balances, regardless of whose deposit funded the loan.

All other USDS and Dai are in circulation, including USDS deposited in the Sky Savings Rate or staked as stUSDS by users, and USDS and Dai bridged to other blockchains.

The positions that hold Non-Circulating Balances are specified in [A.3.5.3.2.1.1.1 - Non-Circulating Balance Positions](cf00c6be-78da-4053-9630-8931318d412e).

For the purpose of calculating the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, the Circulating USDS Supply is measured at the same time as the Aggregate Backstop Capital with which it is compared.

The Core Council Risk Advisor must publish the Circulating USDS Supply and the balance of each position on a publicly available dashboard. The dashboard is located at [https://financial.skyeco.com/usds/supply](https://financial.skyeco.com/usds/supply).

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no penalty or escalation, and the cited artifact review and penalty machinery target Agents and Primes, not the Core Council Risk Advisor's publication duty. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Turbo-Fill Floor
assessments.quote: The current Turbo-Fill Floor for the Aggregate Backstop Capital is 150 million USDS. The Turbo-Fill Floor is the level below which an accelerated retention rate applies, as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.description: Sets the Turbo-Fill Floor for Aggregate Backstop Capital at 150 million USDS, below which accelerated retention applies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete numeric floor (150 million USDS) for a named capital aggregate. The accelerated retention rate that applies below the floor is deferred to a linked section, and no measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: Turbo-Fill Floor for Aggregate Backstop Capital: 150 million USDS
Accelerated retention applies when Aggregate Backstop Capital is below the floor
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine governs protocol-level retention and loss absorption, so it plausibly reaches a breach of the floor. The consequence is not quantified in this paragraph and the rate sits in the linked section, and the engine is an economic backstop rather than an actor-level penalty.

assessments.title: Capital Retention To Achieve Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.quote: When Aggregate Backstop Capital is below Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, a portion of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital, as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.description: When aggregate backstop capital is below target, retains a portion of Step 2 capital to grow it, per a cross-referenced spec.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger (aggregate backstop capital below target) is verifiable, but the retained portion is not quantified here and is delegated entirely to the cross-referenced Step 2 document. A defender could argue the obligation does not yet bind on its own text.
metrics: Trigger: Aggregate Backstop Capital is below Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (no numeric target or retention share stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph governs a capital-retention mechanic, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limit, or role gating) reaches a failure to retain. The Surplus Buffer is the regulated subject, not an enforcer, and the catch-all backstops alone are weak.

assessments.title: SKY Backstop
assessments.quote: This Article governs the SKY Backstop. If the USDS Stablecoin becomes undercollateralized, the Sky Protocol will automatically generate and sell SKY to recapitalize the system. The period when the recapitalization mechanism is actively minting and selling SKY to close the shortfall is termed a "SKY Backstop Event."
assessments.description: Specifies that when USDS is undercollateralized, the protocol automatically mints and sells SKY to recapitalize the system.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The automatic mint-and-sell action is concrete, but the trigger 'undercollateralized' has no threshold, formula, or measurement cadence. Whether a given shortfall activates the backstop is left open to interpretation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is a dilutive last-resort recapitalization that economically disciplines governance, and the Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) absorbs losses first. Both are protocol-level rather than actor-level, and no quantified consequence attaches to this rule, so the rating is capped at mid.

assessments.title: Emission Rate
assessments.quote: An emissions rate for the SKY backstop function that prevents risk of sudden failure must be defined. This must be continuously assessed and improved to maximize stability of the system in worst case scenarios.
assessments.description: Requires an SKY backstop emission rate to be defined to prevent sudden failure, and continuously assessed and improved for worst-case stability.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph imposes real obligations to define and continuously assess an emission rate, but states no numeric threshold, formula, cadence, or metric. Whether the rate has been 'defined' or 'improved' adequately is a judgment call, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is a dilutive last-resort recapitalization that disciplines outcomes, but nothing reaches a failure to define or continuously assess the emission rate. No artifact review, penalty, or emergency path is tied to this rule, and the only generic backstop is misalignment reporting.

assessments.title: Limitless
assessments.quote: The SKY Backstop is temporarily limitless.
assessments.description: States that the SKY Backstop's emission rate is temporarily unlimited.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a single posture statement with no threshold, cap, formula, duration, or actor-level obligation. It gives no measurable value for 'temporarily' or for the emission rate, so there is nothing a third party could verify for compliance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes a parameter state rather than imposing a duty on any actor, and no catalog mechanism constrains or penalizes a 'limitless' emission rate. The SKY Backstop itself (4d8b0d82) is the subject being described, not an enforcer of this statement.

assessments.title: Maximum Level Of Emission
assessments.quote: A maximum level of SKY emission per undercollateralization event must be defined. This must be continuously assessed and improved to maximize stability of the system in worst-case scenarios.
assessments.description: Requires a maximum SKY emission level per undercollateralization event to be defined and continuously improved.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a metric (maximum SKY emission per undercollateralization event) but states no value, formula, or deadline for it. It defers the operative magnitude entirely, leaving nothing concrete to comply with.
metrics: Maximum level of SKY emission per undercollateralization event (no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is a dilutive last resort that disciplines governance economically, but no mechanism enforces a cap that has not been defined. The rule has no cited enforcer or automatic limit reaching it.

assessments.title: Override Mechanism
assessments.quote: The Protocol must include an override mechanism that allows Sky Governance to continue emitting SKY beyond the maximum level. This Section must specify research processes and principles to guide when and how the override mechanism can be safely used.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol to include an override allowing Sky Governance to emit SKY beyond the maximum level, with principles to be specified.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to include an override that exceeds the maximum SKY emission level is clearly stated. However, there is no threshold, cap value, or verifiable condition, and the rules for safe use are deferred to a section that is not yet written.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a design requirement on the Protocol with no consequence attached to a violation. The SKY Backstop (A.3.6) is the subject of the rule, not an enforcer, and no catalog mechanism reaches the requirement to include an override.

assessments.title: Halt Mechanism
assessments.quote: The Protocol must contain a SKY backstop halt mechanism that immediately halts the backstop event in case of severe risk of total failure.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol to have a SKY backstop halt mechanism that immediately stops a backstop event under severe risk of total failure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real (a halt mechanism must exist) but the trigger, severe risk of total failure, is undefined judgment language with no metric or threshold. 'Immediately' gives no deadline or measurement.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) and the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) describe halting capability, but nothing attaches a consequence to the Protocol lacking this mechanism or failing to trigger it. The rule is a design requirement with no enforcer or penalty path.

assessments.title: Mitigate Worst Case Scenario
assessments.quote: In case the backstop limit is reached and not overridden, or in case the backstop is halted during the event, the USDS target price receives a haircut to settle the remaining bad debt of the system. This Section must define elements and infrastructure to address this worst-case scenario, including research concerning ways to mitigate damage.
assessments.description: Specifies a USDS target price haircut to settle remaining bad debt if the SKY backstop limit is reached or halted.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger conditions (backstop limit reached and not overridden, or backstop halted during an event) and the haircut consequence are identifiable, but the haircut magnitude, the backstop limit value, and the elements to address the scenario are not quantified. The sentence requiring the section to define elements and mitigation research defers the operative details.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop is the triggering context, but no citable mechanism enforces the haircut, and the haircut is an undefined systemic outcome rather than an actor-level consequence. Surplus Buffer is not invoked by this text, and the catch-all mechanisms alone are always weak.

assessments.title: Relation To Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.quote: The SKY Backstop may not be invoked unless the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)) has been applied and USDS remains undercollateralized.
assessments.description: Bars invoking the SKY Backstop unless the Genesis Capital Backstop has been applied and USDS remains undercollateralized.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a concrete sequencing gate with two named conditions, so compliance can be checked as a yes/no question. However, "undercollateralized" has no stated threshold, metric, or measurement method, and the Genesis Capital Backstop's application is not defined here.
metrics: Genesis Capital Backstop has been applied before SKY Backstop invocation

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The gate governs a governance invocation decision with no on-chain check, named enforcer, or penalty tied to it. The SKY Backstop's dilution applies once it is invoked, not as a consequence of invoking it early, and the Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication catch-alls alone are weak.

assessments.title: Native Vault Engine

During the transition period, the Core Vaults will have a limited set of collateral types and risk parameters that Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must implement according to the following subdocuments.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Liquidation Penalty reaches collateral violations in vaults, not Core GovOps' duty to implement the transition parameters, and penalty and artifact-review machinery target Primes and Agents rather than this Sky Core implementation duty.

assessments.title: Liquidation Ratio
assessments.quote:
The Liquidation Ratio parameter limits the maximum amount of Dai debt that a vault user can draw from their vault given the value of their collateral locked in that vault. In practice, it expresses the minimum collateral in percentage terms that can support a given Dai debt. If the ratio of a Vault user's collateral to their debt drops below this value, their vault can be liquidated. Each vault type has its own Liquidation Ratio. The Liquidation Ratio for each vault type is expressed as a percentage value of the collateral that must be present in the vault to support its debt.

Changes to the Liquidation Ratio are subject to the Operational Weekly Cycle, requiring a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Defines the Liquidation Ratio as the minimum collateral percentage per vault type, and sets its change process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter, its per-vault-type scope, and the collateral-to-debt trigger, but gives no numeric Liquidation Ratio value for any vault type. The magnitude is absent from the text, and the change cadence is only a weekly cycle label.

assessments.quote:
The Debt Ceiling Limit is numerically provided and acts as an upper limit. Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, can propose changes within this limit.

Debt Ceiling Limit = Unlimited is defined as large enough to avoid being reached in the near future.

The DC-IAM methodology contained in [A.3.7.1.1.2.4 - Debt Ceiling Instant Access Module (DC-IAM)](93c9f662-4e0d-477e-8fc9-e3726877e842) acts as a risk mitigation tool. It limits the rate at which exposure can increase in a short period of time in the event of an unexpected emergency.
assessments.description: Sets the Debt Ceiling Limit as an upper bound on exposure, lets Core GovOps propose changes, and references the DC-IAM rate-limiting module.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The ceiling is named as a numerically provided upper limit, but no value appears in the text. The 'Unlimited' value is defined only as 'large enough to avoid being reached in the near future,' which is judgment language. Proposal changes have no criteria, cadence, or magnitude.

Debt Ceiling Limit = Unlimited, defined as large enough to avoid being reached in the near future
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The DC-IAM (cited verbatim in the text) is an automated limit on how fast exposure can rise, which plausibly reaches ceiling breaches in the Native Vault Engine. The paragraph does not state a consequence for exceeding the ceiling itself, and the DC-IAM's own mechanics are defined in a separate paragraph, so the enforcement is only mid.

assessments.title: Stability Fee
assessments.quote:
The Stability Fee parameter is an annual percentage fee charged on the Dai generated on Vaults. It is expressed as an annual percentage yield but it is charged on a per-block basis in Dai. The Dai from this fee is minted, added to the Dai debt for the vault, and then transferred into the Surplus Buffer which is under the control of Sky Governance. Each vault type has its own Stability Fee that can be adjusted independently.

The Stability Fees can be modified through either Executive Votes or the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).

The Stability Fees must be gradually increased over time to incentivize users to migrate to SparkLend and other borrowing platforms offered by Prime Agents.
assessments.description: Defines the Stability Fee on vault Dai, its per-block charging and Surplus Buffer destination, and says it must rise gradually.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter, its per-block charging basis, its destination, and the two modification paths, but gives no fee magnitude, bound, or step size. The core obligation that fees 'must be gradually increased over time' uses judgment language with no rate, cadence, or deadline, so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Stability Fee expressed as an annual percentage yield
Fee charged on a per-block basis in Dai
Fees must be gradually increased over time (no rate or cadence stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph cites the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module, but it does not state that the module enforces any bound on fee changes, and that module is not a catalog enforcement mechanism. No penalty, rate limiter, or emergency spell in the catalog is shown to reach the 'gradually increased' duty, so only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Maximum Debt Ceiling (line)
assessments.quote:
The `line` parameter refers to the maximum value for the Debt Ceiling that the DC-IAM will allow in the given vault type. When using the DC-IAM to manage the Debt Ceiling of a vault type, the `line` parameter essentially replaces the Debt Ceiling parameter for that vault type. Rather than Sky Governance setting the Debt Ceiling directly, they will need to set the Maximum Debt Ceiling `line` in the DC-IAM. The `line` parameter is defined in Dai.

The Maximum Debt Ceiling is defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2.2 - Debt Ceiling Limit](b490d4d0-8eb8-4dc6-9ef3-c85d357f1f4b) and is currently unlimited.
assessments.description: Defines the DC-IAM line parameter as the maximum Debt Ceiling per vault type, currently unlimited.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter, the actor (Sky Governance), and the system (DC-IAM), but gives no numeric cap; the only stated value is 'currently unlimited', with the actual limit deferred to A.3.7.1.1.2.2. A defender could argue both that the unlimited ceiling imposes no binding obligation and that governance must set a line, so the score is capped at 2.
metrics: Maximum Debt Ceiling line: currently unlimited (defined by reference to A.3.7.1.1.2.2 Debt Ceiling Limit)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The DC-IAM would enforce a line once set, but the paragraph states no cap today and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Penalty Mechanisms, etc.) is cited or clearly reaches a violation of the line parameter.

assessments.title: Target Available Debt (gap)
assessments.quote: The `gap` parameter controls how much of a gap the DC-IAM aims to maintain between the current debt usage and the Debt Ceiling of the vault type. The higher this value, the more risk there is from large collateral drops in very short amounts of time. The smaller this value, the more vault use is negatively affected. The `gap` parameter is defined in Dai.
assessments.description: Defines the gap parameter, the buffer the DC-IAM aims to keep between vault debt usage and the Debt Ceiling, in Dai.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real parameter and its unit (Dai) and describes a maintained buffer, but gives no numeric value, default, bounds, or measurement cadence. The risk trade-off is stated only in qualitative terms (higher or smaller values increase or reduce risk).
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states a tuning target ('aims to maintain') rather than a rule a call can violate, and no catalog mechanism (Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Penalty Mechanisms, PSM) reaches a debt-ceiling gap target.

assessments.title: Ceiling Increase Cooldown (ttl)
assessments.quote: The Ceiling Increase Cooldown (`ttl`) parameter controls how frequently the Debt Ceiling can be increased by the DC-IAM. If a user attempts to use the DC-IAM to increase the Debt Ceiling of a vault type before this time expires, the transaction will fail to execute and the Debt Ceiling will remain unchanged. The `ttl` parameter in combination with the `gap` parameter enforces a maximum rate at which debt usage can increase over time using a given vault type. These parameters should be set such that the maximum increase over time can accommodate all reasonable usage of the vault type in question. The `ttl` parameter is defined in seconds.
assessments.description: Sets a per-vault-type cooldown in seconds between DC-IAM Debt Ceiling increases, with early attempts reverting.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative behavior is verifiable: an increase attempted before ttl expires reverts and the ceiling stays unchanged, and ttl is in seconds. The magnitude is never stated, and the sizing guidance ("accommodate all reasonable usage") is qualitative.
metrics: ttl is defined in seconds (no numeric value stated)
Debt Ceiling increase via DC-IAM blocked until ttl expires after the prior increase
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph states a maximum rate of debt-ceiling increase, which the Rate Limiter reaches; the DC-IAM transaction reverts before ttl expires, so the limit is contract-enforced with no actor in the loop.

assessments.title: Auction Parameters
assessments.quote: A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the parameters specified in this document. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must obtain approval through a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, has the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. The parameters contained herein must be regularly monitored and updated if needed.
assessments.description: Requires justification and analysis for parameter changes, Governance Poll approval before Executive Vote, an emergency bypass, and regular monitoring of Native Vault Auction parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The approval path is concrete, with named actors (Core GovOps, Core Council Risk Advisor) and ordered steps (Governance Poll, then Executive Vote). However, "clear justification and analysis," "emergency," and "regularly monitored" have no criteria, thresholds, or cadence.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Governance Poll gate depends on Core GovOps self-policing, and the emergency bypass is discretionary with no penalty or named enforcer. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, and no catalog mechanism reaches these parameter-change steps.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (calc)
assessments.quote:
The Auction Price Function is the mathematical function that determines how the collateral price changes over time during a collateral auction. Collateral auctions use a falling price auction, where the price starts high and decreases according to the function defined in this parameter.

The Exponential Stair Step function contains two key parameters, `cut` and `step`, defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2.5.1.1 - Auction Price Function (cut)](1ff3ceac-abd0-4195-9a60-a4aaf48c3d31) and [A.3.7.1.1.2.5.1.2 - Auction Price Function (step)](4b46633c-4d6c-4a9c-9be0-93d242ce9db9), respectively.
assessments.description: Defines the Auction Price Function that sets how collateral auction prices decline over time, naming its Exponential Stair Step form and two parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the function type and its cut and step parameters, but states no formula, values, or cadence. The operative magnitudes are delegated to sub-parameter pages, so compliance cannot be checked from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) governs the penalty on liquidated positions, not the decline curve of the auction price, and no catalog mechanism reaches this definitional paragraph's violation modes.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (cut)
assessments.quote: The `cut` parameter controls the ‘depth’ of each step in the function. A smaller `cut` means a smoother line; a large one means more pronounced steps. The `cut` parameter is defined as a multiplicative factor. For example, 0.99 equated to a 1% price drop.
assessments.description: Defines the auction price function's cut parameter as a multiplicative step-depth factor, illustrated with 0.99 as a 1% drop.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines cut as a multiplicative factor and gives one worked example (0.99 equals a 1% drop), which is a formula-like illustration. It states no operative value, permitted range, or update procedure, so it describes the parameter rather than imposing a checkable requirement.
metrics: Illustrative example only: cut of 0.99 equates to a 1% price drop per step
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states a definition with no obligation or violation mode. The auction contract applies the parameter on-chain, but the Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) covers vault collateral violations, not auction price-function definitions, so no catalog mechanism reaches a breach here.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (step)
assessments.quote: The `step` parameter controls the length of time between price drops. A smaller step means a smoother line; a large one means more pronounced steps. The `step` parameter is defined in seconds.
assessments.description: Defines the auction price function's step parameter as the time between price drops, measured in seconds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete parameter and its unit (seconds) but states no value, range, or formula. Its smoothness-versus-steepness language is qualitative, so nothing can be checked for compliance.
metrics: step: length of time between auction price drops, defined in seconds (no numeric value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph is descriptive and imposes no obligation, and no catalog mechanism or UUID in the text reaches it.

assessments.title: Auction Price Multiplier (buf)
assessments.quote: The `buf` parameter is a multiplier that is applied to the starting price of a collateral auction. Each vault type has its own Auction Price Multiplier that can be adjusted by Sky Governance separately. This multiplier is intended to be greater than 1.0x because Liquidations 2.0 uses falling price auctions. This means that it is generally preferable for the auction price to begin above the market price and then fall to the correct value over some amount of time. The `buf` parameter is defined as a multiplicative factor.
assessments.description: Describes the buf auction price multiplier, which is set per vault type and intended to exceed 1.0x for falling-price collateral auctions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter and gives a soft bound, 'intended to be greater than 1.0x', but frames it as intent ('generally preferable') with no enforceable threshold, cadence, or range. A defender could reasonably argue the text does not bind a specific value.
metrics: buf intended to be greater than 1.0x
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Liquidation Penalty and Rate Limiter do not reach a governance-set auction multiplier, and no mechanism enforces the intended >1.0x bound; only the catch-all backstops apply.

assessments.title: Max Auction Drawdown (cusp)
assessments.quote:
The Max Auction Drawdown is the maximum percentage drop in collateral price during a collateral auction before the auction is reset. 'Collateral price' in this context refers to the collateral auction price rather than the collateral market price.

The Max Auction Drawdown parameter overlaps with the Max Auction Duration parameter in that an auction will need to be reset once either maximum is exceeded.
assessments.description: Defines Max Auction Drawdown as the maximum collateral auction price drop before reset, and its overlap with Max Auction Duration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a metric (maximum percentage drop in collateral auction price) and a reset trigger, but states no numeric threshold, value, or cadence. A defender could argue no operative limit exists yet, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Maximum percentage drop in collateral auction price before the auction is reset
Auction reset when either Max Auction Drawdown or Max Auction Duration is exceeded
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The reset is part of the on-chain vault liquidation auction machinery, which the Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) governs for Sky Core vaults. That mechanism quantifies liquidation cost rather than enforcing this drawdown parameter, and no stated magnitude exists, so enforcement is only mid.

assessments.title: Max Auction Duration (tail)
assessments.quote:
The Max Auction Duration parameter sets the maximum time that can elapse before an auction needs to reset for a particular vault type. Expressed in seconds, this parameter determines when an auction can no longer settle and must be reset.

The Max Auction Duration parameter overlaps with the Max Auction Drawdown parameter in that an auction will need to be reset once either maximum is exceeded.
assessments.description: Defines Max Auction Duration, a seconds-based limit after which a vault-type auction must reset, and its overlap with Max Auction Drawdown.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The parameter's unit (seconds) and reset trigger (either this maximum or Max Auction Drawdown being exceeded) are stated, but no numeric value or per-vault-type figure appears. A defender could argue there is no operative threshold yet to comply with.
metrics: Maximum auction duration in seconds, per vault type (value not stated)
Auction must reset once Max Auction Duration or Max Auction Drawdown is exceeded
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The liquidation machinery that would run auctions is on-chain, but no unset-value timer is enforced today, and the Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) covers position penalties rather than auction timers. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Proportional Kick Incentive (chip)
assessments.quote: The Proportional Kick Incentive parameter represents a reward in Dai paid to the keepers that trigger collateral liquidation auctions in the Sky Protocol. The Proportional Kick Incentive is set as a percentage and represents a portion of Dai based on the debt of the vault that is being liquidated. The Dai is rewarded for each liquidation auction at the point the auction is triggered. Each vault type has its own Proportional Kick Incentive that may be adjusted separately by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Defines the Proportional Kick Incentive, a percentage-of-debt Dai reward paid to keepers who trigger liquidation auctions, set per vault type by Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The reward is defined as a percentage of the liquidated vault's debt and paid at auction trigger, but no actual percentage value or bounds are stated, and the magnitude is left to Sky Governance. Keeper eligibility and the timing of the kick are described qualitatively.
metrics: Proportional Kick Incentive set as a percentage of the vault's debt
Reward paid at the point each liquidation auction is triggered
Each vault type has its own parameter, adjustable separately by Sky Governance
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with no consequence for misconfiguration or misuse. The Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) governs vault collateral violations, not the kick reward, so it does not reach this rule; only the catch-all misalignment reporting applies.

assessments.title: Flat Kick Incentive (tip)
assessments.quote: The Flat Kick Incentive parameter represents a reward in Dai paid to the keepers that trigger collateral liquidation auctions in the Sky Protocol. The Flat Kick Incentive is a fixed amount of Dai that is rewarded for each liquidation auction at the point the auction is triggered. Each vault type has its own Flat Kick Incentive that may be adjusted separately by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Defines the Flat Kick Incentive as a fixed Dai reward paid to keepers per collateral liquidation auction, set separately per vault type.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes a real payout mechanism but states no fixed amount, per-vault values, or trigger timing beyond 'at the point the auction is triggered'. The magnitude is delegated to Sky Governance, so compliance cannot be verified from the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with no violation mode for an actor to breach. The Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) covers vault collateral violations, not keeper rewards, and no listed mechanism reaches a wrong Flat Kick amount.

assessments.title: Liquidation Penalty (chop)
assessments.quote: The Liquidation Penalty parameter controls the fee vault owners must pay when their position is liquidated due to insufficient collateral. For a vault holder to receive any collateral back from the liquidations process, the debt and Liquidation Penalty must be covered by the collateral auction. Each vault type has its own Liquidation Penalty that can be adjusted by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Defines the Liquidation Penalty fee charged to liquidated vault owners and requires auction proceeds to cover debt plus penalty.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter, its per-vault-type scope, and a verifiable coverage condition (debt plus penalty covered by the collateral auction). No penalty magnitude is stated; the value is left to Sky Governance adjustment.
metrics: Debt and Liquidation Penalty must be covered by the collateral auction before a vault holder receives any collateral back
Each vault type has its own Liquidation Penalty, adjustable by Sky Governance
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Liquidation Penalty is applied automatically on-chain when a Sky Core vault is liquidated, so the fee and the auction coverage condition are contract-enforced with no human in the loop. The mechanism applies to Sky Core vaults only.

assessments.title: Local Liquidation Limit (hole)
assessments.quote: The Local Liquidation Limit sets the maximum amount of Dai debt for which collateral auctions can be active at any one time within a particular vault type. When the total Dai value of auctions exceeds this maximum for a particular vault type, no more collateral can be auctioned using that vault type until others are completed. Each vault type has a separate Local Liquidation Limit.
assessments.description: Caps total Dai debt in active collateral auctions per vault type and halts new auctions for a type when the cap is exceeded.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative behavior is clear: a per-vault-type cap on active auction value, with new auctions halted once it is exceeded. No numeric value or measurement cadence is stated, so the magnitude is delegated to the parameter's configured value.
metrics: Total Dai value of active collateral auctions per vault type must not exceed the Local Liquidation Limit
Each vault type has a separate Local Liquidation Limit
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The cap governs the same Sky Core vault liquidation machinery as the Liquidation Penalty, which is contract-enforced for vaults, so auction halting is plausibly reached by that machinery. The paragraph does not state an on-chain enforcement path for the cap itself, and no catalog mechanism directly enforces the auction ceiling, so this is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Debt Floor (dust)
assessments.quote: The Debt Floor parameter controls the minimum amount of Dai that can be minted using a specific vault type for an individual vault. If a user tries to mint Dai and the amount of Dai minted would not put the vault's amount of Dai minted above its Debt Floor, the transaction will fail and no DAi will be minted. Likewise, if a user attempts to pay back debt such that their debt will equal less than the Debt Floor and greater than zero, the transaction will fail and no Dai will be paid back. Each vault type has its own Debt Floor that can be adjusted by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Sets a per-vault-type minimum Dai debt, enforced by reverting mints or repayments that leave debt below it but above zero.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The revert conditions are concrete: a mint must leave vault debt above the Debt Floor, and a repayment cannot leave debt between zero and the floor. The floor's magnitude is not stated and is delegated to Sky Governance per vault type.
metrics: Debt Floor per vault type (value not stated; adjustable by Sky Governance)
Post-mint vault debt must exceed the Debt Floor
Post-repayment vault debt must not fall between zero and the Debt Floor
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The vault contract reverts non-compliant mints and repayments, which is on-chain enforcement, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the text documents this check. The Liquidation Penalty covers collateral shortfalls rather than the debt floor, so none found.

assessments.title: Offboarding Low Usage Collateral
assessments.quote: To protect the Protocol from unnecessary complexity, the Core Facilitator must offboard collateral types specified in [A.3.7.1.1.1 - Vault Types](64971463-0650-4462-b9c4-1eecb704fa1a) if they fall below a total debt of 20 million.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to offboard listed collateral types whose total debt falls below 20 million.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 20 million total-debt threshold and the named actor (Core Facilitator) are concrete and checkable. Gaps remain: no measurement cadence, no statement of whether the threshold applies per collateral type or in aggregate, and the Vault Types list is only cross-referenced.
metrics: Total debt below 20 million for a collateral type triggers offboarding
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The obligation falls on the Core Facilitator, and no penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review in the catalog reaches a failure to offboard. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Offboarding WBTC Collateral
assessments.quote: WBTC-A, WBTC-B and WBTC-C are defined in [A.3.7.1.1.1 - Vault Types](64971463-0650-4462-b9c4-1eecb704fa1a) only for the purpose of Stability Fee consistency. These are otherwise not considered Native Vault Engine collateral and should be offboarded according to [A.3.7.1.1.3.3 - Offboarding Other Collateral](fe6595fc-173a-4d75-83ca-9f29dbbb63a3).
assessments.description: Declares WBTC-A/B/C not Native Vault Engine collateral and directs their offboarding under another section's procedure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a real directive to offboard the WBTC vault types, but the 'should' wording is non-binding and the procedure is delegated to another section. It states no deadline, cadence, or threshold, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Liquidation Penalty reaches collateral-requirement violations in live vaults, not the decision to offboard a collateral type. No catalog mechanism reaches this offboarding directive, so only the catch-all backstop applies.

assessments.title: Offboarding Other Collateral
assessments.quote: All other collateral types should be offboarded when the Core Facilitator deems it appropriate and when new mechanisms are in place to take over the roles previously covered by the offboarded collateral.
assessments.description: Sets conditions for offboarding other collateral types: Core Facilitator discretion and replacement mechanisms in place.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real but expressed in judgment language: offboarding depends on the Core Facilitator deeming it appropriate, and 'new mechanisms are in place' is undefined with no criteria, metric, or deadline. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants discretionary authority to the Core Facilitator rather than imposing a violable obligation, and no penalty, rate limit, role gate, or emergency mechanism reaches the conditions for offboarding.

assessments.title: Collateral Offboarding Process
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must use the Operational Weekly Cycle to offboard Native Vault Engine collateral pursuant to [A.3.7.1.1.3 - Collateral Offboarding](05f29c65-4d92-43b3-aacb-3dd75b9f6794) and its subdocuments.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator, consulting the Core Council Risk Advisor, to offboard Native Vault Engine collateral weekly via the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actors and a weekly cadence, but the offboarding criteria, thresholds and pace are delegated to the referenced A.3.7.1.1.3 subdocuments. A defender could argue compliance simply by running the weekly cycle, while another could argue the rule does not yet bind without those criteria, so it is capped at 2.
metrics: Offboarding is executed using the Operational Weekly Cycle (weekly cadence)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator is the regulated actor and no catalog mechanism checks whether the weekly cycle is used for NVE offboarding. Artifact review and penalty machinery are not shown to reach this Core role, so only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Oracles
assessments.quote:
The Native Vault Engine collateral types of ETH, STETH, WBTC will specifically use the Chronicle v3 oracle solution, until at least January 1st 2026. The Native Vault Engine collateral types must be migrated to the new version of the Chronicle v3 oracle when it is feasible to do so.

Other oracle solutions, including diversified oracles, will only be considered until January 1st, 2026, and only if there are unresolvable security concerns with the Chronicle v3 oracles.
assessments.description: Requires Native Vault Engine ETH, STETH and WBTC collateral to use Chronicle v3 oracles until 2026, restricting alternative oracles to security exceptions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The collateral types and the January 1st 2026 date are concrete, but the Chronicle v3 floor is 'at least' that date, migration is due 'when feasible', and alternatives are allowed only on 'unresolvable security concerns', which are undefined judgment terms. Compliance is therefore delegated in key respects.
metrics: Collateral types: ETH, STETH, WBTC
Chronicle v3 oracle used until at least January 1st 2026
Other oracles considered only until January 1st 2026
Other oracles only if unresolvable security concerns with Chronicle v3 exist
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The oracle choice is a Sky Core configuration decision with no on-chain check that the feeds match the stated oracle, and the Agent Artifact Review and Emergency Spells mechanisms do not clearly reach Sky Core's own Native Vault Engine configuration. Only the catch-all misalignment reporting applies.

assessments.title: Updates
assessments.quote: If not otherwise specified, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, has the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2 - Risk Parameter Definitions](8eb26d06-d2b3-493f-a79f-e3509326ddc6) for any of the Vault Types in [A.3.7.1.1.1 - Vault Types](64971463-0650-4462-b9c4-1eecb704fa1a). As a general rule, the modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll. Exceptions to this general rule must be clearly stated in the relevant Atlas document.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps, consulting the Risk Advisor, modify vault-type risk parameters via weekly Executive Vote without a Governance Poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete actors (Core GovOps, Core Council Risk Advisor), a cadence (Operational Weekly Cycle), and a vote path (Executive Vote, not Governance Poll). It states no numeric bounds on parameter changes and leaves exceptions to other documents, so the magnitude of permitted change is undefined.
metrics: Parameter modifications are pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle
Modifications effected via Executive Vote without requiring a Governance Poll
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Rate Limiter and Liquidity Layer roles govern Allocation System controllers, not vault risk parameters. Liquidation Penalty applies to vault positions, not to who may change parameters. Core GovOps is both the actor and the approving body, so enforcement is self-policing and reduces to the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: ALLOCATOR-SPARK-A Parameters
assessments.quote:
The parameters for the Spark Allocator Vault are:

- `duty`: set by the SP-BEAM specified in [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).
- `line`: controlled by DC-IAM
- DC-IAM parameters:
    - `gap`: 1.5 billion USDS
    - `line`: 10 billion USDS
    - `ttl`: 12 hours
assessments.description: Sets Spark Allocator Vault parameters: DC-IAM gap of 1.5B USDS, line of 10B USDS, 12-hour ttl; duty set by SP-BEAM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The DC-IAM gap (1.5 billion USDS), line (10 billion USDS) and ttl (12 hours) are stated as exact values, and the line is named as DC-IAM-controlled. The duty value is deferred to the SP-BEAM module, which is not given here, so that input has no value in this text.
metrics: DC-IAM gap: 1.5 billion USDS
DC-IAM line: 10 billion USDS
DC-IAM ttl: 12 hours
duty: set by SP-BEAM (no value stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The line, gap and ttl are maximum-amount and rate-style limits on a vault draw, which the contract-enforced Rate Limiter reaches; a draw above the limit reverts. The rating assumes the Prime Allocator Vault sits within the Allocation System controller layer, which the paragraph does not state.

assessments.title: ALLOCATOR-BLOOM-A Parameters
assessments.quote:
The parameters for the Grove Allocator Vault are:

- `duty`: set by the SP-BEAM specified in [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).
- `line`: controlled by DC-IAM
- DC-IAM parameters:
    - `gap`: 500 million USDS
    - `line`: 5 billion USDS
    - `ttl`: 24 hours
assessments.description: Sets Grove Allocator Vault parameters: duty via SP-BEAM, line via DC-IAM, with gap 500M, line 5B USDS, ttl 24 hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The DC-IAM gap (500 million USDS), line (5 billion USDS), and ttl (24 hours) are stated as exact values with named parameters. The duty parameter is delegated to the SP-BEAM module without a stated value in this paragraph, which leaves a minor gap.
metrics: gap: 500 million USDS
line: 5 billion USDS
ttl: 24 hours
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The duty parameter is bounded by the SP-BEAM Bounded External Access Module, cited verbatim in the text, which plausibly constrains changes to the stated value. The gap, line, and ttl values are controlled by DC-IAM, but no mechanism doc for that module is cited here, and the paragraph does not quantify a consequence for breaching them.

assessments.title: ALLOCATOR-GROVE-A Parameters

assessments.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module
assessments.quote: The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the Stability Fees of supported vault types, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), and the Sky Savings Rate (SSR). Adjustments are governed by the SP-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. SP-BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each vault type or savings rate: (i) `min`, (ii) `max`, (iii) `step`, and (iv) `tau`.
assessments.description: Lets Governance-whitelisted operators adjust vault Stability Fees, DSR and SSR within per-parameter min, max, step and tau bounds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names four concrete bound parameters (min, max, step, tau) and the adjustable targets, but gives no values, formulas or cadence. Operative magnitudes are delegated to 'specific parameters set by Sky Governance' and the unspecified SP-BEAM contract logic.
metrics: Four parameters per vault type or savings rate: min, max, step, tau (values not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SP-BEAM contract logic may bound adjustments on-chain, but no catalog mechanism reaches it: the Rate Limiter covers Allocation System controllers, not SP-BEAM, and no UUID is cited in the text.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter and its unit (basis points) and says each rate parameter has its own min, but gives no minimum values or formula. assessments.title: Max Technical Upper Limit
assessments.quote: Although the `max` parameter can be set higher, the SP-BEAM cannot be used to set a rate higher than 50% (5,000 basis points) due to technical limitations. Attempts to use the SP-BEAM in this manner will revert. To avoid confusion, `max` should not be set to a value higher than 50% (5,000 basis points).
assessments.description: Caps rates set through the SP-BEAM at 50% (5,000 basis points), with attempts above that reverting, and advises against setting max above that value.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text states an exact numeric cap (50% / 5,000 basis points) and a verifiable outcome (calls above it revert). The final sentence's 'should not' is advisory, but the revert makes the hard limit checkable from the text alone.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The 50% ceiling is enforced on-chain: calls exceeding it revert automatically, as the Rate Limiter does for controller rate limits. The cited Rate Limiter is the closest catalog analogue, since it is not explicitly documented as governing SP-BEAM.

assessments.description: Defines the step parameter as the per-transaction limit on rate changes in basis points, bounded by tau, for each SP-BEAM rate parameter.

assessments.title: Tau Definition
assessments.quote:
The `tau` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive uses or operations of the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.

An SP-BEAM operation may adjust one or more parameters. Once an SP-BEAM operation is executed, the `tau` duration must expire before any subsequent SP-BEAM operation can be performed.
assessments.description: Defines the tau parameter as the minimum seconds between consecutive SP-BEAM operations, which may each adjust one or more parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives a unit (seconds) and a clear operative constraint: no subsequent SP-BEAM operation until tau expires. The tau value itself is not stated anywhere in the paragraph, so the magnitude is delegated.
