assessments.title: Legacy Context
assessments.quote:
Periodically, collateral and vault types (ilks) are re-evaluated, which sometimes results in an offboarding of that collateral or vault type.

There have been several instances where users entered official Sky forums/chats to understand why they had been suddenly liquidated, despite historically comfortable collateralization ratios ([https://forum.skyeco.com/t/an-assessment-first-hand-experience-and-recommendations-from-the-aave-offboarding/11836](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/an-assessment-first-hand-experience-and-recommendations-from-the-aave-offboarding/11836)). This is, understandably, a poor user experience.

Even with liquidation penalties set to 0%, the forced unwinding of levered positions conceivably can result in user losses, as well as potentially taxable events.

This Section defines procedures concerning the dissemination of information about upcoming collateral offboarding on a best-effort basis. The objective is to minimize the number of users who are unaware of the offboarding prior to getting their positions liquidated.
assessments.description: Gives background on collateral offboarding and states a best-effort goal of informing users before liquidation.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The only enforcement-adjacent element is the on-chain Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b), but the paragraph imposes no notification duty that a penalty or contract check would reach. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop could apply.

1. Codify a series of good-faith communication efforts.
2. Provide an easy-to-follow process for Sky contributors to follow without significant burden.
3. Minimize the number of users unaware of a collateral offboarding.
4. Provide a method to bypass these requirements in the event a collateral is being offboarded due to serious security or solvency concerns.

assessments.title: Immediate Actions
assessments.quote:
Upon approval by Sky Governance to offboard a permissionless collateral type or vault type, the following actions are taken as soon as is practicable:

- Set debt ceiling to zero (0) Dai or USDS.
- Make an initial public announcement on all communication channels listed in [A.3.7.1.5.3.0.6.1 - Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing](9ac8a70b-8b6a-4825-a5e0-5e9019e50bc4).
- Make a second public announcement on all communication channels in the above cited document no later than 14 calendar days after the initial public announcement.
- Once the second public announcements have been made, set the liquidation penalty to 0%.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The debt ceiling value (zero), the 14-calendar-day gap between announcements, and the 0% liquidation penalty are all stated. The initial announcement has no deadline beyond "as soon as is practicable", and the announcement channels are defined by external reference.

assessments.title: Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing
assessments.quote:
The following channels should be used for initial and second public announcements of collateral offboarding. The order of announcement publication is as follows:

1. The author of the collateral offboarding notice shall post to the Sky Forum detailing the recommended offboarding. This forum thread is used to inform downstream announcements on other channels.
2. Core GovOps publishes the associated notices to:
    - All public Sky Calendars
    - The Sky Official Discord’s Announcement channel.
    - The official Sky subreddit.
3. Partner Relationship Leads from relevant Ecosystem Actors reach out to:
    - Affected collateral partners (e.g., Aave)
    - Affected frontend service providers (e.g., Oasis, DeFi Saver)

Additionally, outreach may be done to cover more channels not listed here. These may include other Ecosystem Actor or Facilitator owned Twitter accounts, communication channels, and platforms.

Unless otherwise noted in [A.3.7.1.5 - Offboarding Process](3da8a0fd-952c-4f80-b674-f60c9a293cb9) and its subdocuments, Core GovOps will take the lead in coordinating channels announcements.

It gives no deadlines, announcement intervals, or definition of 'second' announcement, and outreach is optional ('may be done'), so the operative timing and scope are left open.

Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could in principle examine such notices, but the paragraph states no review trigger or consequence, so it does not reliably reach this rule. Core GovOps coordinating its own announcements is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Requirements
assessments.quote:
When a collateral type threatens the security or solvency of the Sky Protocol, an expedited offboarding is in order. Expedited offboardings override the timeline specified in [A.3.7.1.5.2 - Technical Process](305e2bd6-a594-4aec-8713-adbe7bc87120) and allow the immediate modification of all relevant parameters.

Expedited offboardings must proceed pursuant to the following requirements:

- The Offboarding Proposal must state that the offboarding should be expedited due to an emergency or urgent concern, as defined in [A.1.9.1.1 - Definition Of Emergency Situations](5eafb29e-84a0-4a53-a798-3f958c880225)**.**
- The Offboarding Proposal must explicitly reference this Atlas document.
assessments.description: Requires expedited collateral offboarding proposals to state an emergency or urgent concern and reference the Atlas document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The two drafting obligations (state the emergency basis, cite this Atlas document) are concrete and checkable from the proposal text. The trigger ("threatens the security or solvency") and the override ("immediate modification of all relevant parameters") are qualitative with no thresholds or deadlines.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. A proposal omitting the emergency statement or the Atlas reference would simply fail to meet the content requirements in governance. The Emergency Response System definition is referenced but does not itself penalize a non-compliant proposal, and only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Announcements
assessments.quote: The public announcements defined in [A.3.7.1.5.2 - Technical Process](305e2bd6-a594-4aec-8713-adbe7bc87120) must still be carried out. However, the timing of these announcements no longer constrains the modification of parameters. These announcements must also state that the offboarding is being expedited and explain the reasons for this accelerated process.
assessments.description: Requires offboarding announcements during expedited offboarding to state the acceleration and its reasons, and lifts their timing constraint on parameter changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives concrete obligations: announcements must be made, must state the offboarding is expedited, and must explain the reasons. It sets no numeric threshold, deadline, or measurable standard for the explanation, and the announcement content and timing are delegated to A.3.7.1.5.2 without values here. Compliance with the reasons requirement is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches a missing or deficient expedited-offboarding announcement; the Penalty Mechanisms, Rate Limiter, and Liquidity Layer roles do not apply to this duty. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops remain, which are always weak.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.quote: If losses exceed a Prime Agent’s capital and cannot be absorbed by the Sky Surplus Buffer, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized to cover the portion of the loss that exceeds what the Prime Agent’s capital and the Sky Surplus Buffer can absorb, up to a maximum of the Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)).
assessments.description: Specifies a pro-rata haircut on Genesis Agents' capital, sized to cover Prime Agent losses beyond the Prime's capital and the Surplus Buffer, capped at Aggregate Backstop Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The haircut sizing formula is stated (cover the loss exceeding Prime capital and Surplus Buffer) and the allocation is pro-rata across Genesis Agents. The cap depends on Aggregate Backstop Capital, defined elsewhere (6dbead44) with no value here, and eligible assets and measurement timing are not specified.
metrics: Haircut sized to the portion of loss exceeding Prime Agent capital plus Sky Surplus Buffer
Haircut allocated pro-rata across each Genesis Agent's Genesis Capital
Maximum haircut equals Aggregate Backstop Capital (defined in 6dbead44, no value stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Surplus Buffer and SKY Backstop are the loss-absorption layers this haircut sits behind, and Genesis Agents bear their own capital as first-loss exposure. These are economic backstops rather than actor-level compliance enforcement, and the haircut is not itself a penalty for a rule violation, so mid at most.

assessments.title: Implementation
assessments.quote:
In the near term, transfers are made through Executive Votes and may be made through Emergency Spells (see [A.1.10.5 - Emergency Spells](b8266c11-3a84-4bbe-abe2-de9474f74ffd)) as part of the Emergency Response System (see [A.1.9.1 - Emergency Response](20dcf582-8862-48b3-9ca9-c3703871bd14)).

A solution must be developed to allow these transfers to be accomplished on an automated basis without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay (see [A.1.10.3 - Governance Security Delay Requirements](c5f0e955-0441-42e0-a6fc-eab875bba568)).
assessments.description: Sets near-term transfers via Executive Votes or Emergency Spells; requires an automated transfer solution bypassing GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The current process (Executive Votes, possibly Emergency Spells) is named, but no thresholds, amounts, or deadlines are given. The automation requirement is a bare instruction to develop a solution with no defined criteria, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Spells and Emergency Response System mechanisms govern intervention in security violations, not the transfer process itself. Nothing reverts or penalizes a failure to develop the automated solution.

assessments.title: Post Backstop Settlement
assessments.quote: If, after the haircut, losses still exceed the combined capacity of the Prime Agent’s capital and Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)), the SKY Backstop (see [A.3.6 - SKY Backstop](4d8b0d82-97da-4041-b185-4b98c2779cbe)) is activated. The SKY mint must be sized to cover the remaining loss. If losses still exceed what the SKY Backstop can absorb, Sky will adjust the USDS target price below $1 to the extent necessary to settle the remaining deficit; Sky will then distribute 24 billion SKY to USDS holders via an airdrop.
assessments.description: Defines the post-haircut loss waterfall: SKY Backstop mint sizing, a sub-$1 USDS target price adjustment, and a 24 billion SKY airdrop to USDS holders.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 24 billion SKY airdrop is a concrete value, but the SKY mint is only 'sized to cover the remaining loss' and the target price is adjusted 'to the extent necessary', so the operative magnitudes are delegated. The haircut and combined capacity are referenced without values.
metrics: Airdrop of 24 billion SKY to USDS holders
USDS target price adjusted below $1 to the extent necessary to settle the remaining deficit
SKY mint sized to cover the remaining loss (no formula given)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found that reaches this settlement sequence. The SKY Backstop and Aggregate Backstop Capital are the loss-absorbing substance of the rule rather than enforcement against a violation, and the actor executing the waterfall is Sky itself, which is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Genesis Agent Capital Shortfalls
assessments.quote: Transfers of capital from Genesis Agents may cause capital shortfalls for Genesis Agents under the Risk Framework (see [A.3.2 - Risk Capital](55999acf-75fe-4adf-8584-9746ef50d3e4)). Sky will work in good faith with such Agents to waive penalties for a reasonable period of time to allow the Agents to rebuild their capital.
assessments.description: Sky commits to work in good faith with Genesis Agents facing transfer-caused capital shortfalls to waive penalties temporarily.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative duty is an effort-based commitment ('work in good faith') with no defined waiver period, eligibility test, or penalty scope; 'reasonable period' is undefined, so compliance is arguable either way. No numeric thresholds or deadlines appear.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a discretionary waiver commitment that reduces penalty exposure, and no mechanism polices Sky's good-faith effort; only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls would apply, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Relation To SKY Backstop
assessments.quote: The Genesis Capital Backstop must be applied before the SKY Backstop (see [A.3.6 - SKY Backstop](4d8b0d82-97da-4041-b185-4b98c2779cbe)).
assessments.description: Requires the Genesis Capital Backstop to be applied before the SKY Backstop during loss absorption.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a sequencing obligation (Genesis Capital Backstop before SKY Backstop) that is checkable in principle. It gives no trigger, threshold, amount, or defined actor responsible for applying either backstop, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is a dilutive last resort that disciplines governance economically, but it does not enforce the ordering of backstops, and no mechanism polices the sequence itself.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital
assessments.quote: The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the Eligible Genesis Capital of the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. The Eligible Genesis Capital of an Agent is the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.1 - Amount Of Capital Contributed By Sky To Agents](0331556e-e7ae-48a2-a693-75468c416321)) minus the Phased-Out Genesis Capital of the Agent (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3.0.6.1 - Current Phased-Out Genesis Capital](41bf89b5-dae5-47f3-bd6b-73b5598d9a0d)).
assessments.description: Defines an Agent's Genesis Capital as the lesser of its Eligible Genesis Capital and total capital, with Eligible Genesis Capital net of phased-out amounts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The governing formulas are fully specified: Genesis Capital is the minimum of two quantities, and Eligible Genesis Capital is Sky-contributed capital minus Phased-Out Genesis Capital. The input values are defined in the linked sub-paragraphs (A.3.7.1.6.6.1 and A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3.0.6.1) rather than stated here, which is a minor gap.
metrics: Genesis Capital = min(Eligible Genesis Capital, total capital of the Agent)
Eligible Genesis Capital = Sky-contributed capital to the Agent minus Phased-Out Genesis Capital of the Agent
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This paragraph is a calculation definition rather than a conduct obligation, and none of the catalogued mechanisms (Penalty Mechanisms, Rate Limiter, Liquidation Penalty, Risk-Capital Incident Response, etc.) reaches a miscalculation of Genesis Capital. Only the misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Phase-Out
assessments.quote:
As the ecosystem matures and Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) reaches a sufficient level, Genesis Capital will phase out. The documents herein define the eligibility conditions and phase-out amounts.

Phase-out is effected by increasing an Agent's Phased-Out Genesis Capital (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3 - Phased-Out Genesis Capital](8f813186-1317-41b1-86d1-47fce7f42af5)), which reduces the Agent's Eligible Genesis Capital and therefore its Genesis Capital, progressively reducing the Genesis Capital subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)). Phase-out does not involve any repayment or transfer of capital from the Genesis Agents to Sky.
assessments.description: Describes Genesis Capital phase-out, which reduces Agents' eligible Genesis Capital as Aggregate Backstop Capital grows, with amounts deferred elsewhere.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The phase-out mechanism is described (Phased-Out Genesis Capital reduces Eligible Genesis Capital), but the trigger ('sufficient level') is unquantified and the eligibility conditions and phase-out amounts are explicitly deferred to other documents. A defender could argue that no binding obligation exists yet.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes a parameter-driven phase-out rather than an obligation an actor can breach, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limit, role gating) reaches it.

assessments.title: Sky Phase-Out Eligibility Conditions
assessments.quote: Genesis Capital phase-out is active when Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above 125 million USDS. If Aggregate Backstop Capital falls below 125 million USDS at any point, phase-out pauses for all Genesis Agents until Aggregate Backstop Capital is once again at or above the threshold.
assessments.description: Makes Genesis Capital phase-out active only while Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above 125 million USDS, pausing it otherwise.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core trigger is a numeric threshold of 125 million USDS with a clear pause/resume rule. Gaps: no measurement cadence or source for Aggregate Backstop Capital, and the phrase 'at any point' is not tied to a verification method.

Phase-out pauses for all Genesis Agents when Aggregate Backstop Capital falls below 125 million USDS

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a phase-out eligibility condition with no consequence for misstatement, and no citable mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limit, or on-chain control) reaches it; only the catch-all backstop applies.

It leaves 'liquid token' undefined and does not specify the trading venues, the measurement source, or how the average is calculated.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is an eligibility gate for a governance-driven phase-out, not a conduct rule with a violation mode. assessments.title: Phase-Out Amount
assessments.quote: For each eligible Genesis Agent whose eligibility conditions are satisfied, the phase-out amount per month (the Total Phase-Out Amount) is the sum of the Base Phase-Out Amount and the Additional Phase-Out Amount, as specified in the documents herein. Following each Monthly Settlement Cycle, the Current Phased-Out Genesis Capital (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3.0.6.1 - Current Phased-Out Genesis Capital](41bf89b5-dae5-47f3-bd6b-73b5598d9a0d)) for each Agent must be increased by the Total Phase-Out Amount for that Agent, but must not exceed the amount of capital contributed by Sky to that Agent (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.1 - Amount Of Capital Contributed By Sky To Agents](0331556e-e7ae-48a2-a693-75468c416321)).
assessments.description: Caps each eligible Genesis Agent's accumulated phased-out Genesis Capital at Sky's contributed capital, adding a monthly Total Phase-Out Amount after each settlement cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The monthly cadence and the cap at Sky's contributed capital are concrete and checkable. The Base and Additional Phase-Out Amounts that make up the monthly increment are delegated to 'the documents herein' with no values stated in this paragraph.

Current Phased-Out Genesis Capital must not exceed capital contributed by Sky to that Agent

assessments.title: Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote:
The Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or its users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit).

The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior.

The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with these requirements.
assessments.description: Restricts use of the Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig to urgent or emergency situations and specified purposes, with Core Council oversight.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Defines a named actor (Core Council), a controlled system, and two conditions for use, but the criteria are judgment language such as 'urgent or emergency', 'potential to harm', and 'generally aligned', with no thresholds, cadence, or verification method. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The only enforcement is the Core Council's duty to ensure alignment, which has no defined consequence path. Misuse of the multisig would fall to the generic Reports of Misalignment backstop, which is weak alone. Emergency Spells and Emergency Response System govern invoking emergency action, not penalizing misuse of the multisig.

assessments.title: Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote:
The Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or its users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit).

The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior.

The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with these requirements.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps is a scheduled review by a body distinct from the multisig signers, with staged findings and penalty assessment, and could catch use outside the urgency and purpose criteria. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the Core Council's own oversight of usage is largely self-policing.

assessments.title: stUSDS Holders’ Risk Bearing
assessments.quote: Holders of stUSDS accept the risk associated with providing capital for SKY-backed borrowing. In the event that the liquidation of a borrower’s staked SKY collateral does not cover the outstanding debt, stUSDS balances will be subject to a haircut proportional to the shortfall. This mechanism ensures that the Sky Protocol is isolated from losses originating from the SKY-backed borrowing facility.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loss-allocation mechanism and its trigger (liquidation shortfall) are named, but the haircut is only "proportional to the shortfall" with no coefficient, formula, cap, or measurement cadence. The magnitude is qualitative and the execution path is unstated.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is itself a loss-allocation rule rather than a conduct requirement with a violation to deter. The Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) absorbs protocol-level losses and is not an actor-level incentive, and no on-chain or named enforcer is stated for executing the haircut.

assessments.title: Debt Ceiling
assessments.quote: The Debt Ceiling is the maximum amount of USDS that can be borrowed against staked SKY. It is determined dynamically and is equal to the lower of (1) the `line` parameter set through the stUSDS BEAM and (2) the total value of stUSDS (the USDS owed to stUSDS holders, including accrued yield) less the debt currently in liquidation auctions, or zero if that difference is negative.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is explicit: min(line, total stUSDS value including accrued yield minus debt in liquidation auctions), floored at zero. The `line` parameter is set through the stUSDS BEAM with no value given here, and the accrued-yield and liquidation-debt inputs are not quantified in this paragraph.

assessments.title: Usage Standards
assessments.quote:
The signers of the Freezer Multisig should exercise their authority to freeze the Spark Liquidity Layer in the event that Spark is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management, or in the event of another emergency. The signers should consult with Operational GovOps Soter Labs before exercising such authority, unless such consultation would cause a delay that could result in a loss of user funds or harm to Sky or Spark. Operational GovOps Soter Labs may also ask the signers to exercise the Freezer Multisig in an emergency. The signers will work with Operational GovOps Soter Labs and, if necessary, other Ecosystem Actors, in good faith in determining whether to exercise their authority based on such request.

Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum.
assessments.description: Governs when Freezer Multisig signers should freeze Spark's Liquidity Layer, consultation with Soter Labs, and post-action reporting to the Sky community.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Freezer Multisig signers) and triggers (Risk Capital or ALM non-compliance, emergencies) are named, but the operative terms are judgment language: 'should exercise', 'good faith', and 'reasonable time frame' for reporting. No numeric threshold or measurable deadline is given, so compliance is arguable.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps is a scheduled, externally enforced review that could catch missing or late reports of Freezer Multisig actions, and it has penalty assessment. The penalty is not quantified for this rule, and no mechanism reaches the discretionary freeze decision itself.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.
assessments.description: Requires Governance Poll approval for Freezer Multisig signer changes, with exceptions for lost keys or voluntary removal, and escalation for suspected malicious changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors (Core Facilitator, Sky Governance, signers) and enumerated steps such as Governance Poll, Sky Forum post, and expedited Executive Vote are concrete. However, timing is qualitative ('as soon as possible', 'immediately') and 'should be questioned' gives no criteria for what counts as suspected malicious activity.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can pre-authorize executive intervention when security rules are violated, and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) can surface unauthorized signer changes, but the remedy (removal of external security access) is not quantified and the expedited Executive Vote depends on the Core Facilitator volunteering the escalation. No contract enforces the Governance Poll requirement on signer changes.

assessments.title: Allocator Role
assessments.quote:
The `ALLOCATOR_ROLE` is authorized to call functions on the Controller contract to perform operations on behalf of the ALM Proxy contract. The Allocator Role is held by the AdministeredAgent contract, as specified in [A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.3.1.5 - AdministeredAgent Contract](3afc0502-e0ba-45a1-ae05-fe539053cf07), which mediates access for the Spark Liquidity Layer relayer system. This role was granted at deployment; actor changes do not transfer the Allocator Role to those actors.

Actors submit allocation operations through the AdministeredAgent. The Arbitrum Diamond PAU actors are:

- ALM Relayer Multisig: `0x8a25A24EDE9482C4Fc0738F99611BE58F1c839AB`.
- Spark hot wallet: `0x062cE42caE04c51D04E77e3D64cc8953a2296FfE`.

Actors can initiate `cctp_transfer` through the Controller within its configured limits and to the Ethereum ALM Proxy only. If the Spark hot wallet is an EOA, a single key can exercise this operational access.

An actor may be removed from the AdministeredAgent by an address holding the Freezer Role, as specified in [A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.5.1.4 - Freezer Role](bd20f786-b4af-4d5b-b29a-d84050a8fa2d).
assessments.description: Grants the ALLOCATOR_ROLE to the AdministeredAgent for Controller operations on the ALM Proxy, and limits cctp_transfer to the Ethereum ALM Proxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Ethereum ALM Proxy destination restriction and the Freezer Role removal path are concrete, and the actor addresses are listed. The cctp_transfer limits are only 'configured limits' with no value stated here, so the operative magnitude is delegated.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Liquidity Layer Role Definitions (2ae4b91a) make calls from addresses without ALLOCATOR_ROLE revert, and the Rate Limiter (a578830d) reverts cctp_transfer operations above the configured limits. The destination restriction and the EOA single-key risk are not covered by these contracts alone.

assessments.title: Approve PSM Spend
assessments.quote:
The operator must approve the PSM to spend the newly acquired DAI. The approval is needed for the PSM to be able to `swap` DAI for USDC.

```
proxy.doCall(
    address(dai),
    abi.encodeCall(dai.approve, (address(psm), usdsAmount))
);
```
assessments.description: Requires the operator to approve the PSM to spend newly acquired DAI through a proxy approve call for usdsAmount.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (operator), the target (PSM), the token (DAI), and the exact call are specified in code. The approved amount is the variable usdsAmount, defined elsewhere without a stated value, and no cadence or deadline is given.
metrics: Approval amount equals usdsAmount (variable; value not stated in paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Rate Limiter does not cover this approval, and no role-gating language is stated. The PSM's on-chain swap would fail without approval, but that is a functional precondition, not a consequence attached to violating this rule. Compliance rests on operator self-enforcement.

```
    address(usdc),

```

assessments.title: Calculate Swap Limit
assessments.quote:
The operator must calculate the `swap` `limit` per transaction. The maximum amount of USDC that can be swapped to DAI in one transaction is calculated based on the DAI balance held by the PSM. `psmTo18ConversionFactor` converts DAI’s 18 token decimals to USDC’s 6 token decimals.

`uint256 limit = dai.balanceOf(address(psm)) / psmTo18ConversionFactor;`
assessments.description: Requires the operator to compute a per-transaction USDC-to-DAI swap limit from the PSM's DAI balance, using a decimal conversion factor.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula `limit = dai.balanceOf(psm) / psmTo18ConversionFactor` is exact and the operator is named, so a third party could recompute the value. The conversion factor is referenced but its value (10^12) is not stated in this paragraph, and the calculation cadence is only 'per transaction'.
metrics: Swap limit per transaction
limit = dai.balanceOf(address(psm)) / psmTo18ConversionFactor
psmTo18ConversionFactor converts 18-decimal DAI to 6-decimal USDC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check a Prime Agent's published swap-limit calculation against this formula and assess penalties, with the enforcer distinct from the operator. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the PSM's own DAI balance check is a physical constraint rather than a rule enforcing the calculation.

assessments.title: Split Into Multiple Swaps If Limit Exceeded
assessments.quote:
If the `usdcAmount` exceeds the limit, the operator must split the swap into multiple smaller swaps as follows.

1. The operator must refill the PSM with DAI by calling `psm.fill()`.
2. The operator must recalculate the limit to see how much USDC can be swapped after the refill.
3. The operator must swap the maximum possible USDC amount that doesn't exceed the limit.
4. The operator must update `remainingUsdcToSwap` by subtracting the amount just swapped.
5. The operator must repeat the process until the full `usdcAmount` is swapped.
assessments.description: Requires operators to split USDC-to-DAI PSM swaps exceeding the limit into repeated refill-and-swap steps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The five steps are enumerated and name a concrete function (psm.fill()) and state variables, but the limit itself is referenced without a value and no cadence or per-iteration swap size is given. The magnitudes are derived from a limit defined elsewhere.
metrics: Swap amount must not exceed the limit on each iteration
Repeat until the full usdcAmount is swapped
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter reverts any controller swap above the current limit, so an oversized single swap is contract-enforced. It does not reach the fill, recalculation, or subtraction sequence, and no quantified consequence attaches to deviating from those steps.

assessments.title: Split Into Multiple Swaps If Limit Exceeded
assessments.description: Splits a USDC-to-DAI PSM swap into repeated fills capped by the PSM's available DAI balance, reverting if nothing can be filled.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loop logic is fully specified: each chunk is the lesser of the remaining amount and the PSM's DAI balance divided by the 18-decimal conversion factor. The fill-availability check and the psm.fill() behaviour are defined elsewhere, and the if-branch condition is missing from the excerpt.
metrics: Revert with `DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill` if the PSM cannot be filled
swapAmount = min(remainingUsdcToSwap, dai.balanceOf(psm) / psmTo18ConversionFactor)
Loop continues while remainingUsdcToSwap > 0
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Each chunk is a controller swap, so the Rate Limiter reverts any operation above the current limit on-chain. The PSM fixed-rate swap also reverts when no fill is possible (`nothing-to-fill`), so the splitting logic is bounded by contract code rather than by any actor's discretion.

assessments.title: Remove Compromised Relayer As Freezer
assessments.quote:
In the event of a compromised Relayer, the `FREEZER_ROLE` can call the function to `removeRelayer` from the Controller contract. This function takes an address, and then the Freezer can remove the compromised Relayer, thereby preventing it from doing any harm to the system. The backstop relayer can then take over. This function should only be used if the keys to the relayer multisig have been leaked or compromised, and the relayer is now in the hands of an external bad actor.

`mainnetController.removeRelayer(compromisedRelayer)`
assessments.description: Lets the FREEZER_ROLE remove a compromised Relayer from the Controller only when its multisig keys are leaked or compromised.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the FREEZER_ROLE, the removeRelayer function, its address parameter, and a concrete call example. The operative trigger, that the relayer multisig keys have been leaked or compromised, is a qualitative judgment with no verification method or threshold.
metrics: Use only if the relayer multisig keys have been leaked or compromised and the relayer is in the hands of an external bad actor
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Liquidity Layer Role Definitions contract-enforce that only the FREEZER_ROLE can call removeRelayer, so unauthorized callers revert. The 'only if compromised' usage condition is not contract-enforced, and no penalty or escalation path reaches a misuse by an authorized Freezer.

assessments.title: Compromised Key Response
assessments.quote:
If a Delegate suspects key compromise, the following steps must be taken:

- The Delegate must notify the Spark Foundation as soon as the breach is discovered.
- The Spark Foundation flags the Delegate in Registry of Delegates as "Suspended - Security Review" and notifies the governance community on the Sky Forum. All voting power to the suspended address is annulled.
- The Delegate may submit a new verified address; upon Spark Foundation approval, suspensions are lifted and delegations migrate at the next snapshot-block.
assessments.description: Sets steps a Delegate and the Spark Foundation must follow when key compromise is suspected, including suspension and voting-power annulment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors, a registry flag, and the annulment of voting power are concrete, and the snapshot-block migration is a defined point in time. However, the trigger "suspects" is subjective, "as soon as" sets no deadline, and the criteria for Spark Foundation approval are unstated.

assessments.title: SparkLend Risk Parameters Cap Automators
assessments.quote:
Cap Automators allow the Supply Cap defined in [A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.1.9 - Supply Cap Definition](e222b8da-abda-42f5-8106-20c6f2881dc7) and the Borrow Cap defined in [A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.1.10 - Borrow Cap Definition](a2d6a99e-c63a-4f30-87f3-a3d66b1eda92) to be dynamically adjusted.

The cap automator is defined in terms of three parameters:

1. `gap` - the target available exposure
2. `ttl` - the cooldown period for cap increases
3. `max` - the absolute maximum exposure

Authorized parties can update a covered Supply Cap or Borrow Cap so the available exposure is equal to the target, as long as the resulting exposure does not exceed the specified maximum limit and the cooldown period has elapsed in the case of increases to the Supply Cap or Borrow Cap.
assessments.description: Lets authorized parties auto-adjust SparkLend supply and borrow caps toward a target gap, bounded by a maximum and an increase cooldown.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the gap, ttl and max parameters and states a formula (available exposure equals target, capped at max, with cooldown on increases). However, no parameter values or cooldown duration are given, and the actor is only "authorized parties", which is undefined.
metrics: gap: target available exposure (no value stated)
ttl: cooldown period for cap increases (no duration stated)
max: absolute maximum exposure (no value stated)

assessments.title: SparkLend Risk Parameters Kill Switch
assessments.quote:
The kill switch disables all borrowing across SparkLend markets in the event of a depeg on key collateral assets.

The kill switch is defined in terms of a threshold for specified pegged assets. If the ratio of the price of a specified asset to its peg is equal to or less than the threshold, then any user can trigger the kill switch to disable borrowing across all SparkLend markets.

After the kill switch is triggered, markets can be reactivated by Sky Governance after resetting the kill switch. Resetting the kill switch is subject to the Governance Security Delay specified in [A.1.10.3 - Governance Security Delay Requirements](c5f0e955-0441-42e0-a6fc-eab875bba568).
assessments.description: Requires borrowing across all SparkLend markets to be disabled via a kill switch when a specified pegged collateral asset's price-to-peg ratio falls to or below a threshold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger formula (price-to-peg ratio ≤ threshold) and the actors (any user to trigger, Sky Governance to reset) are defined. However, the threshold value and the list of specified pegged assets are not stated in the text, and reset timing depends on an external Governance Security Delay whose value is not given here.
metrics: Ratio of the price of a specified asset to its peg must be ≤ threshold to permit triggering (threshold value not stated)
Reset of the kill switch subject to the Governance Security Delay in A.1.10.3 (duration not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (b8266c11) provide pre-authorized pause/freeze intervention when security conditions such as a depeg are threatened, which plausibly reaches a failure to halt borrowing. The referenced Governance Security Delay (c5f0e955) constrains only reset, not the trigger, and no quantified penalty or on-chain enforcement of the threshold itself is stated.

assessments.title: SparkLend Risk Parameters Modification
assessments.quote:
The modification of SparkLend parameters is temporarily controlled by Sky Core, but will be transitioned to Spark in the future. Currently, the Core Council Risk Advisor, in consultation with Phoenix Labs, may recommend changes to any of the parameters specified in the subdocuments of [A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.1 - SparkLend Risk Parameters Definitions](667abf8c-64a3-4029-b218-e7a6e7000bbd) or [A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.1 - SparkLend Risk Parameters Cap Automator Parameter Definitions](e6bc54e6-91df-4095-a032-0e1128c2cab7).

As a general rule, the modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll.

assessments.title: Definition
assessments.quote: The Encumbrance Ratio is defined as the ratio of Spark's Required Risk Capital (RRC) to Total Risk Capital (TRC), as these terms are defined in the Sky Atlas Stability Scope ([A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9)). Spark will seek to maintain a Encumbrance Ratio not greater than the Target Risk Tolerance Ratio specified in [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.1.3 - Parameters](d65a06a6-1426-4af2-978c-cd4f7bac79b7).
assessments.description: Defines Spark's Encumbrance Ratio as Required Risk Capital over Total Risk Capital and states an aspirational cap set by a Parameters paragraph.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The ratio is defined by an explicit formula, but the operative obligation is that Spark 'will seek to maintain' the ratio, which is judgment language and arguably non-binding. The cap value is delegated to the Parameters paragraph and no value appears here.
metrics: Encumbrance Ratio = Required Risk Capital (RRC) / Total Risk Capital (TRC)
Encumbrance Ratio not greater than the Target Risk Tolerance Ratio (value specified in A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.1.3)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Encumbrance Ratio is a Risk Capital metric, so Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a breach, and Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could surface one. Because the 'seek to maintain' wording is soft and no consequence is quantified for this rule, escalation depends on review findings.

assessments.title: Operational Process
assessments.quote:
Spark governance and contributors must take immediate action to reduce the Encumbrance Ratio when it exceeds the Target Encumbrance Ratio level. These actions may fall into two categories, risk capital actions or allocation system actions.

Risk capital actions are actions Spark takes to increase Total Risk Capital, including increasing Internal Junior Risk Capital, sourcing External Junior Risk Capital from other Prime Agents or tokenized sources, or sourcing External Senior Risk Capital from Sky or tokenized sources.

Allocation system actions involve adjusting the capital allocations within the Spark instance of the Allocation System to reduce Required Risk Capital, such as unwinding or disposing of assets requiring higher levels of risk capital as a percent of exposure.

The operational processes implemented at Spark will meet or exceed the requirements specified in the Sky Atlas at [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management](3af8a3a2-25e5-44b3-87a4-7df1f2712685).
assessments.description: Requires Spark to take immediate action to reduce its Encumbrance Ratio when it exceeds the target, via risk capital or allocation actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real but expressed in judgment language: "immediate action" has no deadline, and the Encumbrance Ratio and Target Encumbrance Ratio are referenced without values. The two action categories are enumerated without criteria, and compliance is delegated to the cross-referenced TRC Management section.
metrics: Encumbrance Ratio exceeds Target Encumbrance Ratio (both values defined elsewhere, not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph is a Risk Capital management duty that the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) are designed to incentivize, and the Risk-Capital Incident Response framework (12b7d480) could escalate a failure to act toward penalties or conservatorship. Neither is quantified for this specific obligation, and firing requires the incident process to be invoked, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: RRC Lookback Period Definition
assessments.quote: The Target SubProxy Value evaluation method ([A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.2.2 - Evaluation Method](99d4b8da-fa5c-49ce-b93c-70d07334d7aa)) considers the higher of current Required Risk Capital (RRC) or highest RRC incurred within a trailing period. RRC Lookback Period defines the amount of time to review for the trailing period when evaluating the RRC component of Target SubProxy Value.
assessments.description: Defines the RRC Lookback Period used when evaluating the RRC component of Target SubProxy Value, without stating its duration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a concrete max-based rule (higher of current RRC or highest RRC in a trailing period) but never states the lookback duration. The key parameter is undefined here, so a Prime could argue the rule does not yet bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Target SubProxy Value feeds Risk Capital requirements, which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) reach. The consequence is not quantified for this definition, and no mechanism fires automatically on the lookback itself.

assessments.title: Spark Product Backstop Definition
assessments.quote: The Spark Product Backstop is a fixed value of USDS, updated from time to time by Spark governance via the Spark SubProxy Policy Changes process ([A.6.1.1.1.3.4.1.1 - Spark SubProxy Policy Changes](90240e75-6e5f-4a54-8999-ee430cfcf20d)), meant to cover the anticipated risk exposures to Spark products that are not covered under Sky’s Required Risk Capital framework.
assessments.description: Defines the Spark Product Backstop as a governance-updated fixed USDS amount covering Spark product risks outside Sky's Required Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a fixed USDS backstop and an update process via SubProxy Policy Changes, but states no amount, formula, cadence, or deadline. Coverage is described only as 'anticipated risk exposures', a judgment standard with no defined scope.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a definition with no violation mode. Updates run through Spark governance itself, which is self-enforcement, and no penalty, emergency, or on-chain mechanism reaches it. Surplus Buffer and SKY Backstop are protocol-level and are not tied to this rule.

assessments.title: Evaluation Method
assessments.quote:
Target SubProxy Value is computed as the greater of Required Risk Capital (RRC) plus Spark Product Backstop, or Operational Expense Reserve.

RRC is calculated as the higher of current RRC or highest RRC incurred within the RRC Lookback Period, divided by Risk Tolerance Ratio ([A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](9995ba51-1de7-4b32-8b76-a71462dc4c5b)).

Spark Product Backstop is set manually by Spark governance per [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.2.1.3 - Spark Product Backstop Definition](ac10196b-18b2-4bc4-8627-0cacac8a3524).

Operational expense reserve is calculated as the higher of past month’s operating expenses multiplied by Target Runway (in months), or total operating expenses incurred in trailing period equal to Target Runway.
assessments.description: Defines how Spark's SubProxy target value is computed from risk capital, product backstop, and operating expense reserve.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified as a max() of two terms, with RRC defined as a lookback maximum divided by Risk Tolerance Ratio. However, Target Runway, RRC Lookback Period, and Risk Tolerance Ratio have no values in this text, and Spark Product Backstop is set manually by governance, leaving that input undefined.
metrics: Target SubProxy Value = greater of (RRC + Spark Product Backstop) or Operational Expense Reserve
RRC = higher of current RRC or highest RRC within RRC Lookback Period, divided by Risk Tolerance Ratio
Operational Expense Reserve = higher of past month's operating expenses × Target Runway (months) or total operating expenses over trailing period equal to Target Runway
Target Runway (months) and RRC Lookback Period (no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SubProxy target is a risk-capital funding requirement, so Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a miscalculation or shortfall. No consequence is quantified for this computation rule itself, and enforcement depends on artifact review or escalation.

assessments.title: Operational Process
assessments.quote:
The Spark Prime Relayer Multisig will execute transactions to ensure liquidity within Spark Savings vaults is aligned with the Target Liquidity configurations specified in Target Liquidity Current Configuration, up to the total amount of user deposits in a given Spark Savings vault. This will be implemented via control of the taker role in the vault and transferAsset rate limit from Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy to the vault.

In normal conditions, this will be automated via the ALM Planner software. If the Prime Relayer Multisig fails to maintain Spark Savings vault liquidity in alignment with the Target Liquidity configurations, the Core Operator Relayer Multisig is empowered to effectuate transactions to achieve this.
assessments.description: Spark Prime Relayer Multisig must execute transactions aligning Spark Savings vault liquidity with Target Liquidity configurations, with Core Operator fallback.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors, the taker role, and the transferAsset rate limit are named, and transfers are capped at total user deposits. The Target Liquidity values are defined elsewhere, the rate-limit magnitude is not stated, and no cadence or definition of 'fails to maintain' is given.
metrics: Vault liquidity aligned with Target Liquidity Current Configuration
Transfers up to total user deposits in a given Spark Savings vault
transferAsset rate limit from Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy to the vault
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter (a578830d) reverts any transferAsset above its limit, and Liquidity Layer role definitions (2ae4b91a) revert vault taker-role calls from unauthorized addresses, so both bound the controllable actions on-chain. The alignment target itself is not contract-enforced, and the Core Operator fallback has no quantified remedy.

assessments.title: Counterparty Requirements
assessments.quote:
Borrowers funded via Arkis Infrastructure must be duly registered by competent authorities in their primary jurisdiction, and must not be subject to sanctions by the US, UK, EU, or UN. Responsibility for verifying KYC/KYB and meeting related compliance requirements is handled by Arkis during the borrower onboarding process.

Borrowers must not be insolvent at the time of loan origination or renewal. Borrowers will self-certify their solvency as part of loan agreements. If a borrower becomes insolvent or enters administration while having an active loan, the entire loan amount becomes due and payable and Arkis may immediately liquidate collateral to recover the loan balance.
assessments.description: Sets borrower eligibility rules for Arkis-funded loans: registration, sanctions exclusion, solvency at origination and renewal, and loan recall on insolvency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the sanctions regimes (US, UK, EU, UN) and a concrete trigger for recall, but "duly registered" and "insolvent" are undefined, KYC/KYB is delegated to Arkis, and there is no verification cadence or evidentiary standard. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review Spark's Omni documents, including these counterparty rules, with penalty assessment, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach Prime risk-capital lapses. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific rule, and the on-chain Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) does not reach off-chain Arkis lending.

assessments.title: Exposure Limit
assessments.quote: The maximum aggregate gross exposure to a given asset permitted within Spark funded instances of the Arkis protocol. When calculating gross exposure, we use the higher of the sum of long exposure across all positions or short exposure across all positions, without offsetting long and short exposure within each position.
assessments.description: Sets a maximum aggregate gross asset exposure for Spark-funded Arkis instances, computed as the higher of total long or short exposure without netting.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The gross exposure calculation is formulaically specified (higher of summed long or summed short, no per-position offset), but the maximum permitted exposure is never stated and is referenced only as a 'maximum' with no value or source. The cap's magnitude is missing, so a third party cannot verify compliance from this text alone.

assessments.title: Borrower Insolvency
assessments.quote: If a borrower becomes insolvent or enters administration, any outstanding debts facilitated via the Arkis protocol become due and payable immediately. If the borrower does not repay the debt promptly, collateral may be liquidated to protect the interests of the lender.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger (insolvency or administration) and the consequences are clear, but no threshold, cadence, or value is given. "Promptly" has no deadline and "may be liquidated" leaves the decision to discretion, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A Prime that mishandles a defaulted Arkis loan creates a Risk-Capital loss, which the Risk-Capital Incident Response (penalties up to conservatorship) and Penalty Mechanisms could plausibly reach. Neither is quantified for this specific rule, and no contract enforces the debt-acceleration or liquidation step. The Liquidation Penalty is excluded because it covers only Sky Core vaults, not off-chain or third-party lending.

assessments.title: Parameter Updates in Non Emergency Situations
assessments.quote: Spark may update approved assets and products, risk parameters, and other details of the Arkis Infrastructure product or allocation strategy into the Arkis protocol via governance. If a previously issued loan no longer conforms with Spark’s current operational mandate due to a non-emergency parameter update, Spark will recall the loan at the earliest possible opportunity, while respecting the agreed loan duration.
assessments.description: Lets Spark update Arkis product and risk parameters via governance and requires recalling non-conforming loans at the earliest opportunity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The recall obligation is real, but its timing is judgment language ("earliest possible opportunity") and is qualified by an unquantified "agreed loan duration" defined elsewhere. No numeric threshold, cadence, or verifiable trigger for "no longer conforms" is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Spark's Omni Documents are Prime Agent artifacts, so Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can assess whether loans were recalled and apply penalty assessment. That reach is general and unquantified for this rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the recall timing.

assessments.title: Emergency Parameter Updates
assessments.quote: If market conditions or other factors create an immediate and severe risk of capital impairment, Spark and Arkis are empowered to implement immediate changes to risk parameters and configuration to mitigate risk. Actions taken may include preventing new loans or draws on existing loans, adjusting risk parameters of existing positions including increasing margin requirements or haircuts, demanding immediate repayment, up to and including liquidating high risk positions.
assessments.description: Lets Spark and Arkis immediately tighten risk parameters, halt draws, demand repayment, or liquidate high-risk positions when capital impairment risk is severe.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger ('immediate and severe risk of capital impairment') and the remedies ('other factors', 'high risk positions') are undefined judgment language, with no thresholds, metrics, or time limits. The enumerated actions are real but carry no magnitudes, so compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Spark and Arkis actors self-determine whether the trigger is met, which is self-enforcement and weak on its own. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps is a distinct enforcer that could examine whether emergency powers were used appropriately, with staged findings and penalty assessment. That path is scheduled rather than real-time and its consequence is not quantified for this rule, so mid at most.

assessments.title: Counterparty Requirements
assessments.quote:
Borrowers funded via Offchain Collateralized Lending must be duly registered by competent authorities in their primary jurisdiction, and must not be subject to sanctions by the US, UK, EU, or UN. Responsibility for verifying KYC/KYB and meeting related compliance requirements is handled by venues (custodians and/or collateral agents) during the borrower onboarding process.

Borrowers must not be insolvent at the time of loan origination or renewal. Borrowers will self-certify their solvency as part of loan agreements. If a borrower becomes insolvent or enters administration while having an active loan, the entire loan amount becomes due and payable and the collateral agent or custodian may immediately liquidate collateral to recover the loan balance.
assessments.description: Restricts off-chain collateralized loan borrowers to registered, non-sanctioned, solvent entities, and allows immediate collateral liquidation on insolvency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Sanctions regimes (US, UK, EU, UN) and the administration trigger are named, but there is no numeric threshold or verification method. Solvency rests on borrower self-certification and KYC is delegated to venues, so a defender could argue compliance either way.

assessments.title: Exposure Limit
assessments.quote: The exposure limit is the maximum amount of account value, defined in USD based on current value of assets and positions, inclusive of collateral, idle liquidity pending loan issuance, and repaid loan proceeds pending withdrawal or reinvestment, that may be held within each approved venue or under management of each collateral agent.
assessments.description: Defines the exposure limit as a maximum USD account value per approved venue or collateral agent, with no numeric value stated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The metric is well defined: USD account value, including collateral, idle liquidity, and repaid proceeds, measured per venue or collateral agent. No limit magnitude, measurement cadence, or deadline is stated, and the text reads as a definition rather than a binding cap, so a Prime could argue it does not yet bind.
metrics: Maximum USD account value held within each approved venue or under management of each collateral agent (the limit value itself is not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no rate limit, maxAmount, or controller cap, so the Rate Limiter does not clearly reach it, and no penalty, conservatorship, or artifact-review path is tied to this definition. assessments.title: Collateral Agent
assessments.quote: The collateral agent performs certain critical loan servicing functions on behalf of Spark Asset Foundation as lender, including issuing margin calls, performing liquidations, returning loan proceeds to the lender and excess collateral or liquidation proceeds to borrowers. This service may be provided by an affiliate of the venue/custodian, or by a third party. One venue may have multiple approved collateral agents, each with their own maximum exposure limit.

assessments.title: Borrower Insolvency
assessments.quote: If a borrower becomes insolvent or enters administration, any outstanding debts facilitated via Offchain Collateralized Lending arrangements become due and payable immediately. If the borrower does not repay the debt promptly, collateral may be liquidated to protect the interests of the lender.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) is contract-enforced only for Sky Core vaults and expressly excludes a Prime's off-chain collateralized lending. Penalty Mechanisms and artifact review could reach Spark's documentation, but nothing reaches a failure to call the debt or liquidate collateral, and the clause is a permissive lender-protection term.

assessments.title: Cross Default
assessments.quote: If a borrower defaults on or is liquidated in one Offchain Collateralized Loan funded by Spark, Spark may accelerate any other outstanding loans from the same borrower.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger events (default or liquidation on one Spark-funded loan) are verifiable, but the consequence is discretionary: 'may accelerate' with no criteria, threshold, or procedure for choosing whether to accelerate. A defender could argue either compliance or non-applicability on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph grants Spark a discretionary right rather than imposing a constraint on Spark, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, rate limiter, liquidation penalty) reaches this off-chain lending action. assessments.title: Parameter Updates in Non Emergency Situations
assessments.quote: Spark may update approved assets, risk parameters, and other details of the Offchain Collateralized Lending program via governance. assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can review Spark's Offchain Collateralized Lending program and assess penalties, which could reach a failure to recall non-conforming loans. assessments.title: Emergency Parameter Updates
assessments.quote: If market conditions or other factors create an immediate and severe risk of capital impairment, Spark is empowered to implement immediate changes to risk parameters and configuration to mitigate risk. Actions taken may include preventing new loans or draws on existing loans, adjusting configurable parameters, or requesting accelerated repayment and return of capital.
assessments.description: Lets Spark immediately change risk parameters and halt or recall loans when capital impairment risk is immediate and severe.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger ('immediate and severe risk of capital impairment') and the permitted responses are judgment-based with no numeric threshold, metric, or deadline. The listed actions are enumerated, but nothing defines when they must be used or how far they may go.

Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, third-party review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could catch misuse or non-use of the emergency powers, but no consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Polling Requirement
assessments.quote:
Except for risk-reduction actions approved in advance under [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.3 - Risk-Reduction Actions](8fcbbe4b-51be-4150-896e-ffbb80373507), all curator-executed changes must be approved by Spark governance through a polling process before they are implemented.

A Curator may queue a proposed change before the related governance poll is created or approved, provided that the onchain timelock for the pending change will expire no earlier than twenty-four (24) hours after the expected closing time of that poll. Queueing means submitting a change to the onchain timelock without implementing it. All applicable timelock delays continue to apply.

The twenty-four (24) hour condition applies when the change is queued. Once the related poll is created, its actual closing time, including any subsequent change to that time, must be used to assess the remaining period before the pending change becomes executable. Cancellation on timing grounds is required only if that period is less than twenty (20) hours.

The pending change must match the change submitted for approval. If the poll does not approve that change, or the actual poll closing time leaves less than twenty (20) hours before the pending change becomes executable, the pending change must be cancelled in accordance with [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.2 - Cancellation Reasons](0e572cad-bdf2-437f-b272-0cd634424b19).
assessments.description: Requires Spark curator changes to get polling approval, with timelock timing and cancellation rules around poll closing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Two concrete thresholds are stated: queued changes must expire at least 24 hours after expected poll close, and cancellation is required if less than 20 hours remain after actual close. Remaining gaps are that the expected closing time and poll outcome rely on definitions elsewhere, and the cancellation mechanics sit in a cross-referenced doc.
metrics: Pending change's onchain timelock expires no earlier than 24 hours after the expected poll closing time, at queue time
Remaining period from actual poll closing time to executability must be at least 20 hours, or the change is cancelled
Pending change must match the submitted change and be approved by the poll, or be cancelled
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can detect curator changes executed without poll approval or with timing violations and assess penalties, with enforcer distinct from the Spark actor. Emergency Spells could pause a pending change that threatens security rules, but no quantified consequence attaches to this specific rule and no on-chain mechanism enforces the poll or 24/20-hour conditions.

assessments.title: Execution Authority
assessments.quote: The Curator is authorized to submit the onchain transactions needed to queue a change before governance approval only under the conditions in [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.1 - Polling Requirement](218f889f-6a5d-46a8-b8a3-cb0a075825c2). Following successful governance approval, the approved change or changes may be implemented only after the applicable timelock has expired. Queueing a change does not authorize its implementation.
assessments.description: Limits Spark's Curator to queueing changes before approval only under the polling conditions, and implementation only after timelock expiry.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Curator), the governance-approval precondition, and the timelock-expiry gate are concrete and checkable. The timelock duration is only "the applicable timelock", and the queueing conditions are delegated to the cross-referenced Polling Requirement, which is not stated here.
metrics: Implementation only after the applicable timelock has expired
Queueing before governance approval only under the conditions in A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.1
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pause or freeze queued or approved changes if security rules are threatened, which plausibly reaches premature queueing or implementation. The timelock is a structural delay, but it is not a catalogued mechanism and its duration is unquantified in this text, so the rating stays mid.

assessments.title: Timelock Requirement
assessments.quote:
All admin or privileged controls managed by curator roles must be subject to a minimum timelock delay of three (3) days between scheduling and execution, except as set out below.

For any function for which [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3.1 - Vault Timelock Requirements](14aba6cb-eb34-4780-84c1-908666835569) or [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3.2 - Adapter Timelock Requirements](91ba9acf-6ed7-4214-8b6b-adfb03427ae1) sets a requirement, that requirement applies in place of the minimum in this section.

The minimum in this section does not apply to cancelling a pending change, reducing a cap or deallocating funds.
assessments.description: Requires a minimum three-day timelock between scheduling and execution of curator-managed privileged controls, with overrides and exemptions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified as a three-day minimum delay between scheduling and execution. Gaps: the 'admin or privileged controls' scope is not enumerated, and the vault and adapter timelock requirements that override the minimum are defined elsewhere without values in this text.
metrics: Minimum timelock delay of three (3) days between scheduling and execution
Exempt actions: cancelling a pending change, reducing a cap, deallocating funds
Per-function overrides set by the Vault Timelock Requirements and Adapter Timelock Requirements
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A timelock delays execution at the contract level, so a shorter-delay execution could be blocked on-chain, but the paragraph does not name the enforcing contract. The cited Vault and Adapter Timelock Requirements are rule specifications rather than enforcement machinery, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Visibility
assessments.quote: Pending changes subject to the timelock must be publicly visible onchain for the duration of the delay period.
assessments.description: Requires pending timelocked changes to be publicly visible onchain for the entire delay period.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete (onchain public visibility of queued changes) and checkable against a timelock queue, but the delay period it refers to has no stated duration or reference value. The magnitude of the visibility window is delegated to the timelock's own configuration.
