Nothing automatically enforces visibility, and firing depends on someone detecting the violation and escalating it, so the rating stays at mid with no quantified consequence.

assessments.title: Authorized Cancellers
assessments.quote: Pending changes within the timelock must be able to be cancelled by any of the following: the Spark SubProxy, a designated guardian or sentinel role, or the Curator. On Morpho Vaults v1 the Spark SubProxy and the Guardian each cancel directly; on Morpho Vaults v2, where revocation is restricted to the curator and sentinel roles, the Spark SubProxy exercises this authority through a Sentinel it appoints.
assessments.description: Requires pending timelocked changes on Spark Morpho vaults to be cancellable by the SubProxy, a guardian or sentinel, or the Curator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors and per-version cancellation paths are specified and verifiable against role configuration. The timelock duration it depends on is not given a value in this paragraph, so the rule has a minor input gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) is an enforcer distinct from Spark that can detect a Morpho vault configuration lacking the required cancel paths, with staged findings and penalty assessment. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could pause a vault when a security rule is threatened, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule. The Rate Limiter and role-definition mechanisms do not reach Morpho's external role configuration.

assessments.title: Cancellation Reasons
assessments.quote:
Pending changes may be cancelled for the following reasons: misalignment or conflict with the Sky Atlas or Spark Artifact; excessive or unacceptable risk, as identified by the Sky Core Council; emergency situations, as defined in the Sky Atlas in [A.1.9 - Emergency Response System](1d940c6d-02ce-4c17-8057-cef13c1cc7ad); or cancellation requested by the Curator.

For a change queued before governance approval, the Curator and the cancellation authority holders for the relevant smart contract instance are responsible for ensuring that the pending change is cancelled before it becomes executable if the related poll does not approve the exact pending change, including where the poll is not held, is withdrawn or cancelled, or closes without a valid approval result. The same responsibility applies on timing grounds only if the actual poll closing time, including any subsequent change to that time, leaves less than twenty (20) hours before the pending change becomes executable. A period of twenty (20) hours or more does not require cancellation on timing grounds; the other cancellation reasons and the duty to cancel unapproved changes remain applicable. Any actor authorized under [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.1 - Authorized Cancellers](f87333c8-ec5e-4483-83a9-791e1f9f9634) may fulfil this responsibility by cancelling the pending change; once it has been cancelled, no duplicate cancellation is required.
assessments.description: Lists reasons pending changes may be cancelled and requires cancelling unapproved queued changes before execution, with a 20-hour timing threshold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative duty is quantified: cancel before execution if the exact change is not approved, and treat less than 20 hours before executability as a timing trigger. The permissive cancellation reasons, such as misalignment and risk identified by the Sky Core Council, remain qualitative.
metrics: Pending change must be cancelled before it becomes executable if the related poll does not approve the exact pending change
Timing-based cancellation duty applies if actual poll closing time leaves less than twenty (20) hours before the pending change becomes executable
A period of twenty (20) hours or more does not require timing-based cancellation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a named enforcer distinct from the Spark actor that could review Omni documents and assess penalties for failing to cancel unapproved changes. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could pre-authorize intervention if the unapproved-change security rule is violated. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific duty, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the cancellation duty itself.

assessments.title: Cancellation Authority
assessments.quote:
A Guardian is a specific admin role defined within the Morpho smart contract system. In Morpho Vaults v1 this role is named Guardian; in Morpho Vaults v2 it is named Sentinel. Within this framework, the two are together referred to as the cancellation authority. In Morpho Vaults v2, multiple addresses may hold the Sentinel role. The vault owner may remove a Sentinel role holder without a timelock; where the vault owner is the Spark SubProxy, removal requires a Sky Executive Vote.

In addition to cancelling pending changes, a cancellation authority holder may reduce an absolute or relative cap, or deallocate funds from a market or adapter, where its role permits that action at the smart contract level. It may do so only for one of the reasons set out in [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.2 - Cancellation Reasons](0e572cad-bdf2-437f-b272-0cd634424b19), other than a request by the Curator.
assessments.description: Defines cancellation authority roles in Morpho vaults and limits when they may reduce caps or deallocate funds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named (Guardian/Sentinel, vault owner, Spark SubProxy) and Spark-specific removal requires a Sky Executive Vote, but the permitted reasons are delegated to another paragraph. No cap magnitudes, deallocation limits, or deadlines are stated.
metrics: Removal of a Sentinel by the Spark SubProxy requires a Sky Executive Vote
Removal of a Sentinel role holder by the vault owner occurs without a timelock (non-Spark owners)
Cap reductions or deallocations only for reasons in A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.2 Cancellation Reasons
Cancellation authority may not act on a request by the Curator
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is a Spark agent artifact, so Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) can check use of cancellation authority against the stated reasons, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could apply to a Prime's misuse. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the Morpho role permissions are not contract-enforced against the reason limits.

assessments.title: Cancellation Authority Independence
assessments.quote:
The cancellation authority holder controlled by the Operational Executor Agent must use a signer set separate from the signer set of the Curator multisig for the same smart contract instance, and at least one cancellation authority holder must be fully independent of every entity serving in the Curator role. Compromise or misalignment of the Curator role must not in itself remove the ability of the cancellation authority to cancel pending changes.

The requirements of this section do not apply to the independence of the Curator from a cancellation authority holder controlled by the Operational GovOps of an Operational Executor Agent or by another actor expressly designated by Sky Governance to exercise cancellation authority for the relevant smart contract instance. This section does not require such a holder to use a signer set separate from the Curator’s, and does not require an additional independent cancellation authority holder for an instance with such a holder.
assessments.description: Requires a separate Curator signer set and one fully independent cancellation authority holder, with exemptions for GovOps-controlled or designated holders.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The separate-signer-set requirement is objectively checkable, but 'fully independent of every entity serving in the Curator role' is undefined and the 'must not in itself remove the ability to cancel' clause states an outcome with no test. No numeric thresholds or cadence appear.
metrics: Cancellation authority holder must use a signer set separate from the Curator multisig signer set for the same smart contract instance
At least one cancellation authority holder must be fully independent of every Curator entity
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) can catch a signer-set overlap or lack of independence, with published findings and penalty assessment. The Safe enforces only the threshold configured, not the independence requirement, and no quantified consequence is stated for this rule.

assessments.title: Permitted Actions
assessments.quote:
Designated Contributors are permitted to take any actions reasonably necessary to facilitate the deployment, configuration, testing, maintenance, and operational readiness of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment. Such actions may include deployment and configuration of smart contracts, establishment of multisigs or administrative control systems, deployment and configuration of Spark Savings or Morpho vault infrastructure, operation of relayer or frontend infrastructure, and related implementation activities.

Confidential Strategic Integrations and Deployments may remain undisclosed while applicable confidentiality obligations remain in effect, provided that the governance acceptance and disclosure requirements set forth in this section are satisfied.

For the avoidance of doubt, this authorization does not permit deployment or allocation of Spark treasury assets, Spark Liquidity Layer assets, governance-controlled capital, or other protocol-owned funds, except as otherwise expressly authorized through Spark governance processes. Nothing herein prohibits the movement or allocation of assets voluntarily deposited by users into a Confidential Strategic Partnership and Deployment through preconfigured product functionality established prior to public launch, provided that such functionality remains subject to the limitations and governance acceptance requirements set forth in this section.
assessments.description: Authorizes Designated Contributors to deploy and operate Confidential Strategic Integrations, while excluding treasury and Liquidity Layer asset allocation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates permitted activity types and a clear exclusion for treasury and Liquidity Layer assets, but gives no numeric thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria. 'Reasonably necessary' and the deferred 'governance acceptance and disclosure requirements set forth in this section' leave compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Liquidity Layer Role Definitions (2ae4b91a) make calls from addresses lacking the required role revert, which plausibly blocks unauthorized allocation of Liquidity Layer assets. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could freeze activity if a security rule is threatened. Neither reaches the confidentiality or disclosure requirements, and the paragraph itself adds no consequence.

assessments.title: Disclaimers
assessments.quote: Protocol deployments and products launched under the Confidential Strategic Integrations and Deployments framework are not covered by Spark or Sky insurance, and users bear all risk associated with the deployments and products, including but not limited to hacks, operational or key management failures, illiquidity, insolvency, or failure of a collateral asset. Spark protocol coverage will only be conveyed if Spark governance explicitly votes to extend coverage to a specific deployment or products after public launch and full disclosure of the deployment or product details.
assessments.description: Disclaims Spark and Sky insurance for Confidential Strategic deployments and sets a governance-vote condition for any later Spark coverage extension.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete condition: coverage requires an explicit Spark governance vote after public launch. However, 'full disclosure' is undefined and unquantified, and as a user-facing disclaimer it is arguable whether it binds any actor, so the tie-breaker caps it at 2.
metrics: Coverage extension requires an explicit Spark governance vote
Vote occurs only after public launch of the deployment or product
Requires full disclosure of deployment or product details (undefined)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, penalty, or escalation mechanism reaches this disclaimer; users bear risk by statement only, and the governance vote is a voluntary decision rather than an enforcement path.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The stub states no operative value, so no rate limiter, on-chain check, or penalty path reaches it. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could apply.

- `slope`: 500,000,000 USDC per day

assessments.title: USDS For USDC Swap Maximum
assessments.quote:

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible.

Any changes to the Multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the Multisig.

The `PAUSER_ROLE` is held by the [A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.4 - Freezer Multisig](99bc2dd5-5573-4bb9-9210-5af299d058d9) across all Tokenized Treasury Instances.

assessments.title: Deposit To PSM
assessments.quote:
The operator, acting as a Relayer, calls `depositPSM` to deposit `amount` of `asset` from the ALM Proxy into the PSM, receiving the corresponding PSM `shares` in return. The function approves the PSM to spend the `asset` from the ALM Proxy and then deposits it, crediting the shares to the ALM Proxy. Only an address holding the `RELAYER` role may call this function, and the deposit is rate limited per asset by `LIMIT_PSM_DEPOSIT`.

```
function depositPSM(address asset, uint256 amount)
        external
        onlyRole(RELAYER)
        rateLimitedAsset(LIMIT_PSM_DEPOSIT, asset, amount)
        returns (uint256 shares)
```
assessments.description: Lets a RELAYER-role operator deposit an asset from the ALM Proxy into the PSM, rate limited per asset.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (RELAYER role), function signature, and per-asset rate limit identifier LIMIT_PSM_DEPOSIT are all specified. The numeric limit value is defined elsewhere and not stated in this paragraph, so the quantity is not verifiable from this text alone.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter reverts any depositPSM call exceeding LIMIT_PSM_DEPOSIT, and the Liquidity Layer role definitions revert any call from an address without RELAYER. Both are contract-enforced, with no human in the loop.

assessments.title: Remove Compromised Relayer As Freezer
assessments.quote:

assessments.title: swapUSDSToUSDC Function
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDS to USDC via the PSM. To do so, they must call the swapUSDSToUSDC function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the equivalent amount of USDS for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC) for the PSM.
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to an 18-decimal format using psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the converted amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap USDS to DAI at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending DAI to the proxy.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the DAI.
- The contract will swap DAI to USDC at a 1:1 ratio with no fee via psm.buyGemNoFee, sending USDC to the proxy.

The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
function swapUSDSToUSDC(uint256 usdcAmount) external
```
assessments.description: Restricts USDS-to-USDC PSM swaps to relayer-role operators, enforced by a rate limit, a balance check, and a 1:1 no-fee conversion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The function signature, 1e6 USDC precision, 1:1 swap ratio, zero fee, and named rate-limit key LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC are all stated, and the actor is defined as a relayer-role holder. The rate-limit magnitude is delegated to external configuration and not given as a value.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Rate Limiter reverts any swap above LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC, and Liquidity Layer role definitions revert calls from non-relayer addresses, both contract-enforced. The PSM's fixed-rate swap also makes any peg deviation arbitrageable on-chain.

The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the amount of USDC specified for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDC_TO_USDS) for the PSM.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the USDC from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will calculate the swap limit per transaction based on the DAI balance held by the PSM, converting with psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- If the usdcAmount is less than or equal to the limit, the contract will perform a direct swap of USDC to DAI.
- If the usdcAmount exceeds the limit, the contract will split the swap into multiple smaller swaps: refill the PSM with DAI via psm.fill, recalculate the limit, swap the maximum allowed amount, update the remaining amount, and repeat until complete (reverting with "DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill" if PSM cannot be filled).
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to a DAI amount, accounting for token decimal differences.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the DAI amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap DAI to USDS at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending USDS to the proxy.

The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
function swapUSDCToUSDS(uint256 usdcAmount) external
```

assessments.title: swapUSDSToUSDC Function
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDS to USDC via the PSM. To do so, they must call the `swapUSDSToUSDC` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the equivalent amount of USDS for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC) for the PSM.
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to an 18-decimal format using psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the converted amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap USDS to Dai at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending Dai to the proxy.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the Dai.
- The contract will swap Dai to USDC at a 1:1 ratio with no fee via psm.buyGemNoFee, sending USDC to the proxy.

The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
function swapUSDSToUSDC(uint256 usdcAmount) external
```
assessments.description: Restricts USDS-to-USDC swaps via the PSM to relayer-role operators calling swapUSDSToUSDC, subject to a rate limit and balance check.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states concrete parameters: the relayer role, 1e6 USDC precision, a 1:1 USDS/Dai conversion, no PSM fee, and the LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC rate-limit identifier. The rate limit's magnitude and any cadence are not stated in this text, so one supporting element is left undefined.

assessments.title: swapUSDCToUSDS Function
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDC to USDS via the PSM. To do so, they must call the `swapUSDCToUSDS` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the amount of USDC specified for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDC_TO_USDS) for the PSM.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the USDC from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will calculate the swap limit per transaction based on the Dai balance held by the PSM, converting with psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- If the usdcAmount is less than or equal to the limit, the contract will perform a direct swap of USDC to Dai.
- If the usdcAmount exceeds the limit, the contract will split the swap into multiple smaller swaps: refill the PSM with Dai via psm.fill, recalculate the limit, swap the maximum allowed amount, update the remaining amount, and repeat until complete (reverting with "DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill" if PSM cannot be filled).
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to a Dai amount, accounting for token decimal differences.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the Dai amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap Dai to USDS at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending USDS to the proxy.

The function signature is as follows:

```solidity
function swapUSDCToUSDS(uint256 usdcAmount) external
```
assessments.description: Restricts USDC-to-USDS PSM swaps to relayer-role operators, using rate-limited, balance-capped, split-swap execution through the Controller.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph fixes the caller role, the 1e6 USDC precision, the revert conditions, and the 1:1 Dai-to-USDS conversion. The rate limit is named (LIMIT_USDC_TO_USDS) but its value is defined elsewhere, and the per-transaction limit is described by formula rather than a stated number.
